radial-nerve-injury.caption: The radial nerve winds around the shaft of the humerus.
radial-nerve-injury.body:
In short: The radial nerve winds around the shaft of the humerus.

Spiral Groove

The radial nerve winds around the shaft of the humerus. A fracture there can injure it and cause wrist drop.

Pressure from tourniquets or from tight positioning on the arm board can also affect it.

Why it matters in theatre

Anatomy is the map surgeons and theatre staff work from. Knowing landmarks and structures at risk explains why operations are done the way they are.

Check hand function before and after surgery.

stages-of-anaesthesia.title: Stages of anaesthesia
stages-of-anaesthesia.caption: A quick list on stages of anaesthesia: Stage 1: analgesia; Stage 2: excitement, with the risk of laryngospasm and vomiting.
stages-of-anaesthesia.body:
In short: A quick list on stages of anaesthesia: Stage 1: analgesia; Stage 2: excitement, with the risk of laryngospasm and vomiting.

Stages of anaesthesia

  • Stage 1: analgesia
  • Stage 2: excitement, with the risk of laryngospasm and vomiting
  • Stage 3: surgical anaesthesia
  • Stage 4: too deep, with failure of breathing and circulation

Why it matters in theatre

Anaesthesia removes pain and awareness but also takes over protective reflexes and breathing. Understanding the basics lets theatre staff support the anaesthetic team and notice problems early.

Avoid stimulating the patient in stage 2.

minimum-alveolar-concentration.title: Minimum alveolar concentration
minimum-alveolar-concentration.caption: MAC is the concentration of a gas at which half of patients do not move in response to a surgical incision.
minimum-alveolar-concentration.body:
In short: MAC is the concentration of a gas at which half of patients do not move in response to a surgical incision.

Mac

MAC is the concentration of a gas at which half of patients do not move in response to a surgical incision. A lower MAC means a more potent gas.

Age, temperature, pregnancy and other drugs change MAC.

Why it matters in theatre

Anaesthesia removes pain and awareness but also takes over protective reflexes and breathing. Understanding the basics lets theatre staff support the anaesthetic team and notice problems early.

Remember

MAC measures potency, not depth of anaesthesia.

MAC measures potency, not depth of anaesthesia.

rapid-sequence-induction.title: Rapid sequence induction
rapid-sequence-induction.caption: A quick list on rapid sequence induction: Pre-oxygenate the patient; Give the induction drug and a fast-acting relaxant together.
rapid-sequence-induction.body:
In short: A quick list on rapid sequence induction: Pre-oxygenate the patient; Give the induction drug and a fast-acting relaxant together.

Rapid sequence induction

  • Pre-oxygenate the patient
  • Give the induction drug and a fast-acting relaxant together
  • Avoid bag-mask ventilation if possible to limit air in the stomach
  • Intubate quickly, then confirm with capnography

Why it matters in theatre

Anaesthesia removes pain and awareness but also takes over protective reflexes and breathing. Understanding the basics lets theatre staff support the anaesthetic team and notice problems early.

Remember

Used when the stomach may not be empty.

predicting-a-difficult-airway.title: Predicting a difficult airway
predicting-a-difficult-airway.caption: The Mallampati score grades how much of the throat can be seen with the mouth open (class I to IV).
predicting-a-difficult-airway.body:
In short: The Mallampati score grades how much of the throat can be seen with the mouth open (class I to IV).

Mallampati And More

The Mallampati score grades how much of the throat can be seen with the mouth open (class I to IV). Class III and IV suggest difficulty.

Other signs: a short distance from chin to thyroid (less than about 6 cm), poor neck movement, small mouth opening, loose teeth or a large tongue.

Why it matters in theatre

Anaesthesia removes pain and awareness but also takes over protective reflexes and breathing. Understanding the basics lets theatre staff support the anaesthetic team and notice problems early.

Remember

No single test is perfect. Always have a plan B.

Check yourself

Safe extubation

  • Obeying commands and breathing well

  • Suction, oxygen and a face mask ready

nitrous-oxide-effects.title: Nitrous oxide effects
nitrous-oxide-effects.caption: When nitrous oxide is turned off, it rushes out of the blood into the lungs and dilutes the oxygen there.
nitrous-oxide-effects.body:
In short: When nitrous oxide is turned off, it rushes out of the blood into the lungs and dilutes the oxygen there.

Diffusion Hypoxia

When nitrous oxide is turned off, it rushes out of the blood into the lungs and dilutes the oxygen there. Giving 100 percent oxygen for several minutes prevents low oxygen.

Nitrous oxide also expands air-filled spaces and is avoided with pneumothorax or bowel obstruction.

Why it matters in theatre

Anaesthesia removes pain and awareness but also takes over protective reflexes and breathing. Understanding the basics lets theatre staff support the anaesthetic team and notice problems early.

Remember

Give oxygen after turning nitrous oxide off.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about nitrous oxide effects?

Give oxygen after turning nitrous oxide off.

awareness-under-anaesthesia.title: Awareness under anaesthesia
awareness-under-anaesthesia.caption: Awareness means a patient remembers being awake during surgery.
awareness-under-anaesthesia.body:
In short: Awareness means a patient remembers being awake during surgery.

Rare But Serious

Awareness means a patient remembers being awake during surgery. Risks include paralysis without enough anaesthetic, light anaesthesia in emergencies and equipment failure.

Checking drug delivery and using depth monitors help prevent it.

Why it matters in theatre

Anaesthesia removes pain and awareness but also takes over protective reflexes and breathing. Understanding the basics lets theatre staff support the anaesthetic team and notice problems early.

Remember

Take every report of awareness seriously.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about awareness under anaesthesia?

Take every report of awareness seriously.

total-intravenous-anaesthesia.title: Total intravenous anaesthesia
total-intravenous-anaesthesia.caption: In TIVA, drugs such as propofol are given by infusion, often with a pump, instead of using inhaled gas.
total-intravenous-anaesthesia.body:
In short: In TIVA, drugs such as propofol are given by infusion, often with a pump, instead of using inhaled gas.

Tiva

In TIVA, drugs such as propofol are given by infusion, often with a pump, instead of using inhaled gas.

Benefits include less nausea and no trigger for malignant hyperthermia. The cannula must be secure and visible because disconnection can wake the patient.

Why it matters in theatre

Anaesthesia removes pain and awareness but also takes over protective reflexes and breathing. Understanding the basics lets theatre staff support the anaesthetic team and notice problems early.

Remember

Check the IV line often during TIVA.

pre-oxygenation.caption: Breathing 100 percent oxygen through a tight-fitting mask for about three minutes of quiet breathing, or eight deep breaths, fills the lungs with oxygen.
pre-oxygenation.body:
In short: Breathing 100 percent oxygen through a tight-fitting mask for about three minutes of quiet breathing, or eight deep breaths, fills the lungs with oxygen.

More Time Before Low Oxygen

Breathing 100 percent oxygen through a tight-fitting mask for about three minutes of quiet breathing, or eight deep breaths, fills the lungs with oxygen.

It gives extra time before oxygen levels fall when breathing stops.

Why it matters in theatre

Anaesthesia removes pain and awareness but also takes over protective reflexes and breathing. Understanding the basics lets theatre staff support the anaesthetic team and notice problems early.

A good mask seal makes all the difference.

halsted-s-principles.body:

Halsted's principles

  • Gentle handling of tissue
  • Careful haemostasis
  • Preserve the blood supply
  • Strict aseptic technique. No tension, and obliterate dead space

Why it matters in theatre

Basic surgical principles apply to almost every operation. They explain why surgeons control bleeding, handle tissue gently and remove dead material.

Remember

The principles still guide modern surgery.

wound-healing-by-intention.title: Wound healing by intention
wound-healing-by-intention.caption: A quick list on wound healing by intention: Primary: wound edges are closed and heal directly; Secondary: wound is left open and fills in from the base.
wound-healing-by-intention.body:
In short: A quick list on wound healing by intention: Primary: wound edges are closed and heal directly; Secondary: wound is left open and fills in from the base.

Wound healing by intention

  • Primary: wound edges are closed and heal directly
  • Secondary: wound is left open and fills in from the base
  • Tertiary (delayed primary): closed after a few days once the risk of infection has fallen
  • Contaminated wounds often heal by secondary or tertiary intention

Why it matters in theatre

Basic surgical principles apply to almost every operation. They explain why surgeons control bleeding, handle tissue gently and remove dead material.

The wound type decides the closure plan.

dead-space-and-seroma.title: Dead space and seroma
dead-space-and-seroma.caption: Dead space is an empty pocket left in tissues.
dead-space-and-seroma.body:
In short: Dead space is an empty pocket left in tissues.

Close The Gaps

Dead space is an empty pocket left in tissues. Fluid collects there as seroma, haematoma or abscess.

Surgeons reduce it by closing layers, using drains and applying pressure dressings.

Why it matters in theatre

Basic surgical principles apply to almost every operation. They explain why surgeons control bleeding, handle tissue gently and remove dead material.

Remember

Report swelling at the wound after surgery.

debridement-and-source-control.title: Debridement and source control
debridement-and-source-control.caption: Dead tissue and pus must be removed because antibiotics cannot reach them.
debridement-and-source-control.body:
In short: Dead tissue and pus must be removed because antibiotics cannot reach them.

Remove The Cause

Dead tissue and pus must be removed because antibiotics cannot reach them. Source control means draining abscesses, removing infected tissue or fixing a perforation.

In sepsis, source control should happen as soon as practical, usually within hours.

Why it matters in theatre

Basic surgical principles apply to almost every operation. They explain why surgeons control bleeding, handle tissue gently and remove dead material.

Remember

Antibiotics alone cannot solve a collection of pus.

Check yourself

Antibiotics alone cannot solve a collection of pus.

damage-control-surgery.title: Damage control surgery
damage-control-surgery.caption: In a very sick or unstable patient, damage control surgery stops bleeding and contamination quickly, leaves the abdomen temporarily open and sends the patient for resu...
damage-control-surgery.body:
In short: In a very sick or unstable patient, damage control surgery stops bleeding and contamination quickly, leaves the abdomen temporarily open and sends the patient for resuscitation.

Survive First

In a very sick or unstable patient, damage control surgery stops bleeding and contamination quickly, leaves the abdomen temporarily open and sends the patient for resuscitation.

Definitive repair happens later, when they are warmer and clotting better.

Why it matters in theatre

Basic surgical principles apply to almost every operation. They explain why surgeons control bleeding, handle tissue gently and remove dead material.

Remember

Warm, correct clotting, then repair.

skin-edges-and-tension.title: Skin edges and tension
skin-edges-and-tension.caption: Skin edges should meet gently, slightly everted, without tight sutures.
skin-edges-and-tension.body:
In short: Skin edges should meet gently, slightly everted, without tight sutures.

Closing The Skin

Skin edges should meet gently, slightly everted, without tight sutures. Too much tension causes ischaemia and wide scars.

Deep layers carry the strength. Skin stitches are the final touch.

Why it matters in theatre

Basic surgical principles apply to almost every operation. They explain why surgeons control bleeding, handle tissue gently and remove dead material.

Do not tie stitches tight.

removing-drains.body:

When To Pull

Drains stay until the output is low, usually small daily volumes, and the fluid looks right. Policies differ by drain type and surgeon.

Watch for leaks, infection or blockage. Record the amount and appearance each day.

glasgow-coma-scale.title: Glasgow Coma Scale
glasgow-coma-scale.caption: The GCS adds three scores: eye opening (1 to 4), verbal response (1 to 5) and motor response (1 to 6).
glasgow-coma-scale.body:
In short: The GCS adds three scores: eye opening (1 to 4), verbal response (1 to 5) and motor response (1 to 6).

Eye, Verbal, Motor

The GCS adds three scores: eye opening (1 to 4), verbal response (1 to 5) and motor response (1 to 6). The total is 3 to 15.

A score of 8 or less often means the airway needs protection.

Why it matters in theatre

Trauma care prioritises the most life-threatening problems first. A structured approach keeps teams from missing injuries.

Remember

Record the three components separately.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about glasgow coma scale?

Record the three components separately.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

haemothorax-or-tension-pneumothorax.title: Haemothorax or tension pneumothorax
haemothorax-or-tension-pneumothorax.caption: Tension pneumothorax: air trapped under pressure.
haemothorax-or-tension-pneumothorax.body:
In short: Tension pneumothorax: air trapped under pressure.

Two Chest Emergencies

Tension pneumothorax: air trapped under pressure. Resonant chest, absent breath sounds, low blood pressure. Release the air at once.

Haemothorax: blood in the pleural space. Dull to percussion. A chest drain is inserted and bleeding assessed.

Why it matters in theatre

Trauma care prioritises the most life-threatening problems first. A structured approach keeps teams from missing injuries.

Remember

Do not wait for imaging if the patient is collapsing.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about haemothorax or tension pneumothorax?

Do not wait for imaging if the patient is collapsing.

fast-scan.title: FAST scan
fast-scan.caption: FAST looks for free fluid (usually blood) in four places: around the heart, around the liver, around the spleen and in the pelvis.
fast-scan.body:
In short: FAST looks for free fluid (usually blood) in four places: around the heart, around the liver, around the spleen and in the pelvis.

Focused Ultrasound

FAST looks for free fluid (usually blood) in four places: around the heart, around the liver, around the spleen and in the pelvis.

It is quick and used at the bedside, but a negative scan does not exclude all injuries.

Why it matters in theatre

Trauma care prioritises the most life-threatening problems first. A structured approach keeps teams from missing injuries.

Remember

It supports the decision. It does not replace the exam.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about fast scan?

It supports the decision. It does not replace the exam.

pelvic-fracture.title: Pelvic fracture
pelvic-fracture.caption: Severe pelvic fractures can bleed heavily.
pelvic-fracture.body:
In short: Severe pelvic fractures can bleed heavily.

Binder And Bleeding

Severe pelvic fractures can bleed heavily. A pelvic binder wrapped around the hips at the level of the greater trochanters reduces pelvic volume and bleeding.

Avoid log rolling and rocking the pelvis.

Why it matters in theatre

Trauma care prioritises the most life-threatening problems first. A structured approach keeps teams from missing injuries.

Remember

Do not repeatedly spring the pelvis.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about pelvic fracture?

Do not repeatedly spring the pelvis.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

head-injury-and-brain-pressure.title: Head injury and brain pressure
head-injury-and-brain-pressure.caption: Rising pressure inside the skull can cause high blood pressure, a slow heart rate and irregular breathing.
head-injury-and-brain-pressure.body:
In short: Rising pressure inside the skull can cause high blood pressure, a slow heart rate and irregular breathing.

Cushing'S Triad

Rising pressure inside the skull can cause high blood pressure, a slow heart rate and irregular breathing.

In head injury the priorities are oxygen, blood pressure and ventilation. Both low oxygen and low pressure worsen brain injury.

Why it matters in theatre

Trauma care prioritises the most life-threatening problems first. A structured approach keeps teams from missing injuries.

Remember

Avoid hypoxia and hypotension.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about head injury and brain pressure?

Avoid hypoxia and hypotension.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

rule-of-nines-for-burns.title: Rule of nines for burns
rule-of-nines-for-burns.caption: A quick list on rule of nines for burns: Head and neck: 9 percent; Each arm: 9 percent.
rule-of-nines-for-burns.body:
In short: A quick list on rule of nines for burns: Head and neck: 9 percent; Each arm: 9 percent.

Rule of nines for burns

  • Head and neck: 9 percent
  • Each arm: 9 percent
  • Front of trunk 18, back of trunk 18, each leg 18
  • Groin: 1 percent

Why it matters in theatre

Trauma care prioritises the most life-threatening problems first. A structured approach keeps teams from missing injuries.

Remember

A rough guide for adults. Children have larger heads.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Rule of nines for burns".

Head and neck: 9 percent; Each arm: 9 percent; Front of trunk 18, back of trunk 18, each leg 18; Groin: 1 percent.

impaled-objects.title: Impaled objects
impaled-objects.caption: Do not remove an object that is stuck in the body outside the operating theatre.
impaled-objects.body:
In short: Do not remove an object that is stuck in the body outside the operating theatre.

Leave It In

Do not remove an object that is stuck in the body outside the operating theatre. It may be plugging a damaged vessel.

Secure it in place and remove it under controlled conditions with the surgical team ready.

Why it matters in theatre

Trauma care prioritises the most life-threatening problems first. A structured approach keeps teams from missing injuries.

Remember

Pad around the object. Do not pull.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about impaled objects?

Pad around the object. Do not pull.

tetanus-prophylaxis.title: Tetanus prophylaxis
tetanus-prophylaxis.caption: Tetanus-prone wounds include dirty, deep, crushed or old wounds.
tetanus-prophylaxis.body:
In short: Tetanus-prone wounds include dirty, deep, crushed or old wounds.

Wound Care

Tetanus-prone wounds include dirty, deep, crushed or old wounds. Patients with unknown or incomplete immunisation may need a tetanus vaccine and tetanus immunoglobulin.

Follow national guidelines. Clean wound care is vital.

Why it matters in theatre

Trauma care prioritises the most life-threatening problems first. A structured approach keeps teams from missing injuries.

Remember

Ask about vaccination history.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tetanus prophylaxis?

Ask about vaccination history.

crush-injury.title: Crush injury
crush-injury.caption: Crushed muscle releases myoglobin and potassium.
crush-injury.body:
In short: Crushed muscle releases myoglobin and potassium.

Rhabdomyolysis

Crushed muscle releases myoglobin and potassium. Myoglobin can block the kidneys and potassium can reach dangerous levels, especially after release of the limb.

Early large-volume fluids and heart monitoring are central.

Why it matters in theatre

Trauma care prioritises the most life-threatening problems first. A structured approach keeps teams from missing injuries.

Remember

Give fluids before the limb is released.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about crush injury?

Give fluids before the limb is released.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

the-4-2-1-rule.title: The 4-2-1 rule
the-4-2-1-rule.caption: The 4-2-1 rule gives maintenance fluid per hour: 4 mL per kg for the first 10 kg, 2 mL per kg for the next 10 kg and 1 mL per kg for the rest.
the-4-2-1-rule.body:
In short: The 4-2-1 rule gives maintenance fluid per hour: 4 mL per kg for the first 10 kg, 2 mL per kg for the next 10 kg and 1 mL per kg for the rest.

Maintenance Fluids In Children

The 4-2-1 rule gives maintenance fluid per hour: 4 mL per kg for the first 10 kg, 2 mL per kg for the next 10 kg and 1 mL per kg for the rest.

A 25 kg child needs about 40 + 20 + 5 = 65 mL per hour.

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Add losses and deficits to maintenance.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about the 4-2-1 rule?

Add losses and deficits to maintenance.

low-sodium.title: Low sodium
low-sodium.caption: Sodium below about 135 mmol/L.
low-sodium.body:
In short: Sodium below about 135 mmol/L.

Hyponatraemia

Sodium below about 135 mmol/L. Mild cases may cause few signs. Severe cases cause confusion, vomiting and seizures.

Sodium is corrected slowly. Too fast a rise can cause brain damage (osmotic demyelination).

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Do not correct sodium faster than the plan.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about low sodium?

Do not correct sodium faster than the plan.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

treating-high-potassium.title: Treating high potassium
treating-high-potassium.caption: A quick list on treating high potassium: Protect the heart with calcium; Shift potassium into cells with insulin and glucose, and salbutamol.
treating-high-potassium.body:
In short: A quick list on treating high potassium: Protect the heart with calcium; Shift potassium into cells with insulin and glucose, and salbutamol.

Treating high potassium

  • Protect the heart with calcium
  • Shift potassium into cells with insulin and glucose, and salbutamol
  • Remove potassium with dialysis, diuretics or binders
  • Repeat the potassium level and monitor the ECG

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Calcium protects the heart but does not lower potassium.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Treating high potassium".

Protect the heart with calcium; Shift potassium into cells with insulin and glucose, and salbutamol; Remove potassium with dialysis, diuretics or binders; Repeat the potassium level and monitor the ECG.

low-potassium.title: Low potassium
low-potassium.caption: Low potassium causes weakness and heart rhythm problems.
low-potassium.body:
In short: Low potassium causes weakness and heart rhythm problems.

Hypokalaemia

Low potassium causes weakness and heart rhythm problems. Replacement is given orally when possible, or by slow intravenous infusion.

IV rates are limited, commonly about 10 mmol per hour through a peripheral line unless local policy allows more with monitoring.

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Never give concentrated potassium as a bolus.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about low potassium?

Never give concentrated potassium as a bolus.

calcium-in-surgery.title: Calcium in surgery
calcium-in-surgery.caption: Low calcium can follow thyroid or parathyroid surgery and massive blood transfusion (citrate binds calcium).
calcium-in-surgery.body:
In short: Low calcium can follow thyroid or parathyroid surgery and massive blood transfusion (citrate binds calcium).

When Calcium Falls

Low calcium can follow thyroid or parathyroid surgery and massive blood transfusion (citrate binds calcium). Signs include tingling, muscle spasm and a positive Chvostek or Trousseau sign.

Treatment is intravenous calcium and finding the cause.

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Check calcium during massive transfusion.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about calcium in surgery?

Check calcium during massive transfusion.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

magnesium.title: Magnesium
magnesium.caption: Low magnesium can cause muscle twitching, low potassium and dangerous rhythms such as torsades de pointes.
magnesium.body:
In short: Low magnesium can cause muscle twitching, low potassium and dangerous rhythms such as torsades de pointes.

Hypomagnesaemia

Low magnesium can cause muscle twitching, low potassium and dangerous rhythms such as torsades de pointes.

Intravenous magnesium is used to treat both low magnesium and certain arrhythmias.

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Check magnesium in rhythm problems.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about magnesium?

Check magnesium in rhythm problems.

signs-of-dehydration.title: Signs of dehydration
signs-of-dehydration.caption: A quick list on signs of dehydration: Dry mouth and reduced skin elasticity; Fast heart rate and low blood pressure.
signs-of-dehydration.body:
In short: A quick list on signs of dehydration: Dry mouth and reduced skin elasticity; Fast heart rate and low blood pressure.

Signs of dehydration

  • Dry mouth and reduced skin elasticity
  • Fast heart rate and low blood pressure
  • Low urine output and dark urine
  • Sunken eyes in infants, and a sunken fontanelle

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Correct dehydration before elective surgery.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Signs of dehydration".

Dry mouth and reduced skin elasticity; Fast heart rate and low blood pressure; Low urine output and dark urine; Sunken eyes in infants, and a sunken fontanelle.

signs-of-fluid-overload.title: Signs of fluid overload
signs-of-fluid-overload.caption: A quick list on signs of fluid overload: Crackles in the lungs and breathlessness; Swollen legs or puffy eyelids.
signs-of-fluid-overload.body:
In short: A quick list on signs of fluid overload: Crackles in the lungs and breathlessness; Swollen legs or puffy eyelids.

Signs of fluid overload

  • Crackles in the lungs and breathlessness
  • Swollen legs or puffy eyelids
  • Raised neck veins
  • Weight gain and a falling oxygen level

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Review fluids in heart and kidney patients.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Signs of fluid overload".

Crackles in the lungs and breathlessness; Swollen legs or puffy eyelids; Raised neck veins; Weight gain and a falling oxygen level.

refeeding-syndrome.title: Refeeding syndrome
refeeding-syndrome.caption: After a long period of starvation, restarting feeding causes a shift in phosphate, potassium and magnesium into cells.
refeeding-syndrome.body:
In short: After a long period of starvation, restarting feeding causes a shift in phosphate, potassium and magnesium into cells.

Danger Of Feeding Too Quickly

After a long period of starvation, restarting feeding causes a shift in phosphate, potassium and magnesium into cells.

Low levels can lead to heart failure, rhythm problems and confusion. Start feeding slowly and replace electrolytes.

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Check electrolytes daily when refeeding.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about refeeding syndrome?

Check electrolytes daily when refeeding.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

dextrose-fluids.title: Dextrose fluids
dextrose-fluids.caption: Dextrose solutions provide sugar and free water.
dextrose-fluids.body:
In short: Dextrose solutions provide sugar and free water.

What Dextrose Does

Dextrose solutions provide sugar and free water. Dextrose 5 percent is a way to give water, not much salt.

In the brain-injured or in those with hyperglycaemia, they can cause harm. Use them with a clear reason.

Why it matters in theatre

Fluids and electrolytes keep the circulation and cells working. Imbalances can cause dangerous problems that are often easy to treat when spotted.

Remember

Do not use dextrose for resuscitation.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about dextrose fluids?

Do not use dextrose for resuscitation.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

how-x-rays-work.title: How X-rays work
how-x-rays-work.caption: X-rays pass through the body.
how-x-rays-work.body:
In short: X-rays pass through the body.

Density And Shadows

X-rays pass through the body. Dense tissue such as bone absorbs more and looks white. Air looks black. Fat and muscle are shades of grey.

Radiation exposure should be as low as reasonably achievable (ALARA).

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Use only the exposure that is needed.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about how x-rays work?

Use only the exposure that is needed.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

ct-scan-basics.title: CT scan basics
ct-scan-basics.caption: CT uses many X-ray images to build slices of the body.
ct-scan-basics.body:
In short: CT uses many X-ray images to build slices of the body.

Slices

CT uses many X-ray images to build slices of the body. It is fast and good for trauma, bleeding and bones. The radiation dose is higher than a plain X-ray.

Intravenous contrast improves detail but needs kidney checks and an allergy history.

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Ask about allergies and kidney function.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ct scan basics?

Ask about allergies and kidney function.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

mri-safety.title: MRI safety
mri-safety.caption: MRI uses a strong magnet.
mri-safety.body:
In short: MRI uses a strong magnet.

Magnets

MRI uses a strong magnet. Ferromagnetic items such as some scissors, oxygen cylinders and monitors can become dangerous missiles. Some implants and pacemakers are unsafe.

Use MRI-compatible equipment and follow the screening checklist.

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Always screen the patient and everyone entering the room.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about mri safety?

Always screen the patient and everyone entering the room.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

contrast-reactions.title: Contrast reactions
contrast-reactions.caption: Reactions range from nausea and a rash to severe anaphylactoid reactions.
contrast-reactions.body:
In short: Reactions range from nausea and a rash to severe anaphylactoid reactions.

Be Prepared

Reactions range from nausea and a rash to severe anaphylactoid reactions. Kidney injury is another risk. Hydration and dose limits help.

The team should know where the emergency drugs and equipment are before the injection.

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Check allergies and kidney function first.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about contrast reactions?

Check allergies and kidney function first.

ultrasound-physics-in-short.title: Ultrasound physics in short
ultrasound-physics-in-short.caption: Higher frequency sound waves give sharper images but do not travel as far.
ultrasound-physics-in-short.body:
In short: Higher frequency sound waves give sharper images but do not travel as far.

Frequency And Depth

Higher frequency sound waves give sharper images but do not travel as far. Lower frequencies reach deeper but with less detail.

Superficial nerves and veins use high-frequency probes. Abdominal imaging uses lower frequencies.

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Pick the probe for the depth.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ultrasound physics in short?

Pick the probe for the depth.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

reading-a-normal-ecg.title: Reading a normal ECG
reading-a-normal-ecg.caption: A quick list on reading a normal ecg: P wave: atrial activity; QRS complex: ventricular contraction.
reading-a-normal-ecg.body:
In short: A quick list on reading a normal ecg: P wave: atrial activity; QRS complex: ventricular contraction.

Reading a normal ECG

  • P wave: atrial activity
  • QRS complex: ventricular contraction
  • T wave: ventricular recovery
  • Check rate, rhythm, and any ST changes

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Always compare with the patient's baseline.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Reading a normal ECG".

P wave: atrial activity; QRS complex: ventricular contraction; T wave: ventricular recovery; Check rate, rhythm, and any ST changes.

chest-x-ray-tube-positions.title: Chest X-ray tube positions
chest-x-ray-tube-positions.caption: An endotracheal tube tip should lie about 2 to 4 cm above the carina.
chest-x-ray-tube-positions.body:
In short: An endotracheal tube tip should lie about 2 to 4 cm above the carina.

Where Lines Should End

An endotracheal tube tip should lie about 2 to 4 cm above the carina. A central line tip should lie near the junction of the superior vena cava and right atrium. A nasogastric tube should sit below the diaphragm in the stomach.

Confirm before using any tube.

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Never feed through an unconfirmed tube.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about chest x-ray tube positions?

Never feed through an unconfirmed tube.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

alara-and-staff-protection.title: ALARA and staff protection
alara-and-staff-protection.caption: Reduce radiation by limiting time, increasing distance and using shielding.
alara-and-staff-protection.body:
In short: Reduce radiation by limiting time, increasing distance and using shielding.

As Low As Reasonably Achievable

Reduce radiation by limiting time, increasing distance and using shielding. Pregnant staff should discuss monitoring with the radiation safety officer.

Wear dosimeters under and over the lead apron if required.

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Report any lost or damaged protective equipment.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about alara and staff protection?

Report any lost or damaged protective equipment.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

echocardiography.title: Echocardiography
echocardiography.caption: An echocardiogram shows heart size, valve function and pumping.
echocardiography.body:
In short: An echocardiogram shows heart size, valve function and pumping.

Heart Ultrasound

An echocardiogram shows heart size, valve function and pumping. Transoesophageal echo (TOE) uses a probe in the oesophagus and gives clearer views in theatre.

TOE can injure the oesophagus and needs trained operators.

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Know when a TOE probe is in place.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about echocardiography?

Know when a TOE probe is in place.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

contrast-after-bowel-injury.title: Contrast after bowel injury
contrast-after-bowel-injury.caption: If bowel perforation is suspected, water-soluble contrast is used rather than barium.
contrast-after-bowel-injury.body:
In short: If bowel perforation is suspected, water-soluble contrast is used rather than barium.

Water-Soluble Contrast

If bowel perforation is suspected, water-soluble contrast is used rather than barium. Barium leaking into the abdomen can cause serious inflammation.

Water-soluble contrast is absorbed from the peritoneum.

Why it matters in theatre

Imaging helps diagnose and guide surgery, but some methods use radiation or strong magnets. Staff need to know the benefits and the protection rules.

Remember

Check which contrast has been ordered.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about contrast after bowel injury?

Check which contrast has been ordered.

the-who-analgesic-ladder.title: The WHO analgesic ladder
the-who-analgesic-ladder.caption: A quick list on the who analgesic ladder: Step 1: non-opioids such as paracetamol and NSAIDs; Step 2: weak opioids such as codeine.
the-who-analgesic-ladder.body:
In short: A quick list on the who analgesic ladder: Step 1: non-opioids such as paracetamol and NSAIDs; Step 2: weak opioids such as codeine.

The WHO analgesic ladder

  • Step 1: non-opioids such as paracetamol and NSAIDs
  • Step 2: weak opioids such as codeine
  • Step 3: strong opioids such as morphine
  • Add adjuvant drugs as needed

Why it matters in theatre

Controlling pain is part of good care and helps recovery. Understanding how pain works guides safe choices of treatment.

Remember

Reassess pain after every step.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "The WHO analgesic ladder".

Step 1: non-opioids such as paracetamol and NSAIDs; Step 2: weak opioids such as codeine; Step 3: strong opioids such as morphine; Add adjuvant drugs as needed.

paracetamol-safety.title: Paracetamol safety
paracetamol-safety.caption: The usual adult maximum is 4 g in 24 hours, with doses of 1 g at least 4 hours apart.
paracetamol-safety.body:
In short: The usual adult maximum is 4 g in 24 hours, with doses of 1 g at least 4 hours apart.

Do Not Exceed

The usual adult maximum is 4 g in 24 hours, with doses of 1 g at least 4 hours apart. Lower doses are used for low body weight, liver disease or long-term alcohol use.

Overdose can cause liver failure. Count all sources of paracetamol.

Why it matters in theatre

Controlling pain is part of good care and helps recovery. Understanding how pain works guides safe choices of treatment.

Remember

Check that other medicines do not contain paracetamol.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about paracetamol safety?

Check that other medicines do not contain paracetamol.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

nsaid-risks.title: NSAID risks
nsaid-risks.caption: NSAIDs can cause stomach bleeding, kidney injury, raised blood pressure and reduce platelet function.
nsaid-risks.body:
In short: NSAIDs can cause stomach bleeding, kidney injury, raised blood pressure and reduce platelet function.

Beware

NSAIDs can cause stomach bleeding, kidney injury, raised blood pressure and reduce platelet function. They can trigger bronchospasm in some asthma patients.

Use the lowest dose for the shortest time and check kidney function.

Why it matters in theatre

Controlling pain is part of good care and helps recovery. Understanding how pain works guides safe choices of treatment.

Remember

Avoid NSAIDs in kidney disease and active ulcers.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about nsaid risks?

Avoid NSAIDs in kidney disease and active ulcers.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

patient-controlled-analgesia.title: Patient-controlled analgesia
patient-controlled-analgesia.caption: A PCA pump lets the patient give themselves a small dose of opioid by pressing a button.
patient-controlled-analgesia.body:
In short: A PCA pump lets the patient give themselves a small dose of opioid by pressing a button.

Pca Pumps

A PCA pump lets the patient give themselves a small dose of opioid by pressing a button. A lockout time prevents too many doses.

Only the patient should press the button. Monitor sedation and breathing.

Why it matters in theatre

Controlling pain is part of good care and helps recovery. Understanding how pain works guides safe choices of treatment.

Remember

Never press the button for the patient.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about patient-controlled analgesia?

Never press the button for the patient.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

opioid-sedation-scoring.title: Opioid sedation scoring
opioid-sedation-scoring.caption: Increasing sleepiness often appears before breathing slows.
opioid-sedation-scoring.body:
In short: Increasing sleepiness often appears before breathing slows.

Sedation Comes First

Increasing sleepiness often appears before breathing slows. A sedation score (alert, drowsy, difficult to rouse) is a simple way to catch problems early.

Naloxone is used for dangerous respiratory depression.

virchow-s-triad.title: Virchow's triad
virchow-s-triad.caption: A quick list on virchow's triad: Stasis of blood flow; Endothelial injury (damage to the vessel wall).
virchow-s-triad.body:
In short: A quick list on virchow's triad: Stasis of blood flow; Endothelial injury (damage to the vessel wall).

Virchow's triad

  • Stasis of blood flow
  • Endothelial injury (damage to the vessel wall)
  • Hypercoagulability of the blood
  • Surgery can add all three

Why it matters in theatre

Mnemonics give a quick memory hook for lists that are easy to forget. They are most useful once you understand what each part means.

Remember

The three factors behind blood clots.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Virchow's triad".

Stasis of blood flow; Endothelial injury (damage to the vessel wall); Hypercoagulability of the blood; Surgery can add all three.

frailty-and-surgical-risk.title: Frailty and surgical risk
frailty-and-surgical-risk.caption: Frailty means reduced reserve.
frailty-and-surgical-risk.body:
In short: Frailty means reduced reserve.

Beyond Age

Frailty means reduced reserve. Two patients of the same age can have very different risk. Slow walking, weight loss, weakness and needing help at home point to frailty.

Frail patients have more complications, delirium and loss of independence after surgery.

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Ask about function, not just age.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about frailty and surgical risk?

Ask about function, not just age.

post-operative-delirium.title: Post-operative delirium
post-operative-delirium.caption: Delirium is a sudden change in attention and thinking, often fluctuating through the day.
post-operative-delirium.body:
In short: Delirium is a sudden change in attention and thinking, often fluctuating through the day.

Acute Confusion

Delirium is a sudden change in attention and thinking, often fluctuating through the day. It is common in older patients after surgery.

Look for pain, infection, urinary retention, low oxygen, drugs, dehydration and poor sleep. Glasses, hearing aids and familiar faces help.

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Treat the cause, not just the behaviour.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about post-operative delirium?

Treat the cause, not just the behaviour.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

drugs-in-older-patients.title: Drugs in older patients
drugs-in-older-patients.caption: Older patients often have less muscle, more fat, and slower kidney and liver clearance.
drugs-in-older-patients.body:
In short: Older patients often have less muscle, more fat, and slower kidney and liver clearance.

Start Low, Go Slow

Older patients often have less muscle, more fat, and slower kidney and liver clearance. Many drugs last longer and act more strongly.

Sedatives and opioids need smaller doses and more time between them. Check their regular medicines for interactions.

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Smaller doses, longer watch.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about drugs in older patients?

Smaller doses, longer watch.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

skin-and-positioning-in-the-elderly.title: Skin and positioning in the elderly
skin-and-positioning-in-the-elderly.caption: Older skin is thin and tears easily.
skin-and-positioning-in-the-elderly.body:
In short: Older skin is thin and tears easily.

Fragile Skin

Older skin is thin and tears easily. Pressure injuries form faster, and adhesive tape can strip skin.

Pad bony areas, lift rather than drag, and use gentle removal for dressings and tapes. Joints may be stiff, so do not force positions.

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Check the skin before and after.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about skin and positioning in the elderly?

Check the skin before and after.

keeping-older-patients-warm.title: Keeping older patients warm
keeping-older-patients-warm.caption: Older patients lose heat faster and recover from cold more slowly.
keeping-older-patients-warm.body:
In short: Older patients lose heat faster and recover from cold more slowly.

Heat Loss

Older patients lose heat faster and recover from cold more slowly. Cold raises the risk of bleeding, infection and heart strain.

Use warmed blankets, forced-air warming, warmed fluids and a warm room. Keep exposure short.

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Warm before, during and after.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about keeping older patients warm?

Warm before, during and after.

hip-fracture-and-pre-operative-care.title: Hip fracture and pre-operative care
hip-fracture-and-pre-operative-care.caption: Hip fracture patients are often frail and in pain.
hip-fracture-and-pre-operative-care.body:
In short: Hip fracture patients are often frail and in pain.

Before The Operation

Hip fracture patients are often frail and in pain. Give good pain relief early, keep them hydrated, and treat oxygen or fluid problems.

Handle the limb gently. Early surgery usually gives better outcomes, so avoid avoidable delays.

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Pain relief and fluids first.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about hip fracture and pre-operative care?

Pain relief and fluids first.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

dementia-and-consent.title: Dementia and consent
dementia-and-consent.caption: Dementia does not automatically mean a patient lacks capacity.
dementia-and-consent.body:
In short: Dementia does not automatically mean a patient lacks capacity.

Capacity

Dementia does not automatically mean a patient lacks capacity. Capacity is decision-specific and can change through the day.

Explain simply, use short sentences and give time. If capacity is lacking, follow local law and involve family or guardians as required.

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Assess capacity for each decision.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about dementia and consent?

Assess capacity for each decision.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

falls-after-surgery.title: Falls after surgery
falls-after-surgery.caption: Older patients are at risk after sedation, with low blood pressure, weakness and unfamiliar rooms.
falls-after-surgery.body:
In short: Older patients are at risk after sedation, with low blood pressure, weakness and unfamiliar rooms.

Prevent Falls

Older patients are at risk after sedation, with low blood pressure, weakness and unfamiliar rooms.

Keep the bed low, the call bell in reach and the floor clear. Help them mobilise early with support. Check for dizziness when sitting up.

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Sit up slowly, then stand.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about falls after surgery?

Sit up slowly, then stand.

hydration-and-fasting-in-older-people.title: Hydration and fasting in older people
hydration-and-fasting-in-older-people.caption: Older patients become dehydrated quickly.
hydration-and-fasting-in-older-people.body:
In short: Older patients become dehydrated quickly.

Avoid Long Fasts

Older patients become dehydrated quickly. Long fasts raise the risk of confusion, low blood pressure and kidney injury.

Follow the fasting guidance but do not extend it without reason. Encourage clear fluids until the allowed time.

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Fast only as long as needed.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about hydration and fasting in older people?

Fast only as long as needed.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

pressure-injuries-staging.title: Pressure injuries: staging
pressure-injuries-staging.caption: A quick list on pressure injuries: staging: Stage 1: red skin that does not blanch; Stage 2: partial-thickness skin loss or blister.
pressure-injuries-staging.body:
In short: A quick list on pressure injuries: staging: Stage 1: red skin that does not blanch; Stage 2: partial-thickness skin loss or blister.

Pressure injuries: staging

  • Stage 1: red skin that does not blanch
  • Stage 2: partial-thickness skin loss or blister
  • Stage 3: full skin loss, fat visible
  • Stage 4: muscle or bone exposed

Why it matters in theatre

Older patients have less physical reserve and respond differently to drugs and stress. Adjusting care for them reduces complications.

Remember

Prevention is far better than treatment.

Check yourself

Stage 1: red skin that does not blanch; Stage 2: partial-thickness skin loss or blister; Stage 3: full skin loss, fat visible; Stage 4: muscle or bone exposed.

oxygen-devices-compared.title: Oxygen devices compared
oxygen-devices-compared.caption: A quick list on oxygen devices compared: Nasal prongs give low flow, about 24 to 40 percent; Simple face mask gives moderate oxygen.
oxygen-devices-compared.body:
In short: A quick list on oxygen devices compared: Nasal prongs give low flow, about 24 to 40 percent; Simple face mask gives moderate oxygen.

Oxygen devices compared

  • Nasal prongs give low flow, about 24 to 40 percent
  • Simple face mask gives moderate oxygen
  • Non-rebreather mask with reservoir gives high oxygen
  • High-flow nasal oxygen gives warmed, humidified flow

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Match the device to the need and recheck.

sepsis-early-signs.title: Sepsis: early signs
sepsis-early-signs.caption: Sepsis is a dangerous response to infection.
sepsis-early-signs.body:
In short: Sepsis is a dangerous response to infection.

Spot It Early

Sepsis is a dangerous response to infection. Early signs include fast heart rate, fast breathing, fever or low temperature, confusion and low blood pressure.

Early antibiotics, fluids and source control improve survival. Follow local sepsis protocols.

Why it matters in theatre

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Think sepsis in any unwell patient with infection.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about sepsis: early signs?

Think sepsis in any unwell patient with infection.

septic-shock-basics.title: Septic shock basics
septic-shock-basics.caption: In septic shock, blood pressure stays low despite fluids and the patient may need vasopressors.
septic-shock-basics.body:
In short: In septic shock, blood pressure stays low despite fluids and the patient may need vasopressors.

When Fluids Are Not Enough

In septic shock, blood pressure stays low despite fluids and the patient may need vasopressors.

Treatment focuses on antibiotics, fluids, finding and removing the source, and organ support. Lactate is often used to judge severity.

Why it matters in theatre

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Treat early and reassess often.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about septic shock basics?

Treat early and reassess often.

mechanical-ventilation-basics.title: Mechanical ventilation basics
mechanical-ventilation-basics.caption: A ventilator delivers breaths using set pressure or volume, rate and oxygen concentration.
mechanical-ventilation-basics.body:
In short: A ventilator delivers breaths using set pressure or volume, rate and oxygen concentration.

Breathing For The Patient

A ventilator delivers breaths using set pressure or volume, rate and oxygen concentration. PEEP keeps airways open at the end of breathing out.

High pressures or volumes can injure lungs, so settings are tailored to the patient.

Why it matters in theatre

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Know the alarms and the patient's settings.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about mechanical ventilation basics?

Know the alarms and the patient's settings.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

ards-the-idea.title: ARDS: the idea
ards-the-idea.caption: ARDS is severe lung injury with inflammation, fluid in the air sacs and low oxygen.
ards-the-idea.body:
In short: ARDS is severe lung injury with inflammation, fluid in the air sacs and low oxygen.

Stiff, Leaky Lungs

ARDS is severe lung injury with inflammation, fluid in the air sacs and low oxygen. It can follow pneumonia, sepsis, trauma or aspiration.

Care often includes lung-protective ventilation, treating the cause and sometimes lying the patient prone.

Why it matters in theatre

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Small breaths protect injured lungs.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ards: the idea?

Small breaths protect injured lungs.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

acute-kidney-injury.title: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.caption: AKI is a sudden fall in kidney function.
acute-kidney-injury.body:
In short: AKI is a sudden fall in kidney function.

When Urine Drops

AKI is a sudden fall in kidney function. Causes include low blood pressure, dehydration, sepsis, obstruction and some drugs.

Watch urine output and creatinine, treat the cause and avoid nephrotoxic drugs where possible.

Why it matters in theatre

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Low urine output is an early clue.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about acute kidney injury?

Low urine output is an early clue.

vasopressors-in-simple-terms.title: Vasopressors in simple terms
vasopressors-in-simple-terms.caption: Vasopressors such as noradrenaline narrow blood vessels to raise blood pressure.
vasopressors-in-simple-terms.body:
In short: Vasopressors such as noradrenaline narrow blood vessels to raise blood pressure.

Squeezing The Vessels

Vasopressors such as noradrenaline narrow blood vessels to raise blood pressure. They are given by carefully controlled infusion.

Use a reliable line, as leaking into tissue can cause damage. Monitor blood pressure closely and change doses only as ordered.

Why it matters in theatre

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Check the line and the site.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about vasopressors in simple terms?

Check the line and the site.

delirium-in-intensive-care.title: Delirium in intensive care
delirium-in-intensive-care.caption: ICU patients are at high risk of delirium.
delirium-in-intensive-care.body:
In short: ICU patients are at high risk of delirium.

Common And Harmful

ICU patients are at high risk of delirium. Contributors include sedatives, pain, sleep loss, infection and being tied to lines and tubes.

Reduce sedation when safe, support sleep, orient the patient, and mobilise early.

Why it matters in theatre

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Light sedation and early mobility help.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about delirium in intensive care?

Light sedation and early mobility help.

preventing-ventilator-associated-pneumon.title: Preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia
preventing-ventilator-associated-pneumon.caption: Common measures include raising the head of the bed, mouth care, daily review of sedation, and checking if the tube is still needed.
preventing-ventilator-associated-pneumon.body:
In short: Common measures include raising the head of the bed, mouth care, daily review of sedation, and checking if the tube is still needed.

Care Bundle

Common measures include raising the head of the bed, mouth care, daily review of sedation, and checking if the tube is still needed.

Always use clean technique with suction and circuits.

Why it matters in theatre

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Small habits prevent pneumonia.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia?

Small habits prevent pneumonia.

handover-from-theatre-to-icu.title: Handover from theatre to ICU
handover-from-theatre-to-icu.caption: Include patient identity, procedure, anaesthetic details, airway, allergies, fluids and blood given, drugs, lines, drains and problems that occurred.
handover-from-theatre-to-icu.body:
In short: Include patient identity, procedure, anaesthetic details, airway, allergies, fluids and blood given, drugs, lines, drains and problems that occurred.

What To Say

Include patient identity, procedure, anaesthetic details, airway, allergies, fluids and blood given, drugs, lines, drains and problems that occurred.

State current concerns and the plan. Allow questions and confirm understanding.

Why it matters in theatre

Critically ill patients depend on organ support and close monitoring. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff hand over and work with intensive care teams.

Remember

Structured handover prevents loss of information.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about handover from theatre to icu?

Structured handover prevents loss of information.

why-nutrition-matters-in-surgery.title: Why nutrition matters in surgery
why-nutrition-matters-in-surgery.caption: Poor nutrition increases infection, delays wound healing and prolongs hospital stay.
why-nutrition-matters-in-surgery.body:
In short: Poor nutrition increases infection, delays wound healing and prolongs hospital stay.

Healing Needs Fuel

Poor nutrition increases infection, delays wound healing and prolongs hospital stay. Protein and energy are both needed.

Screen patients early, and treat deficits before major elective surgery where possible.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Remember

Ask about weight loss and appetite.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about why nutrition matters in surgery?

Ask about weight loss and appetite.

screening-for-malnutrition.title: Screening for malnutrition
screening-for-malnutrition.caption: Many hospitals use a short screening tool.
screening-for-malnutrition.body:
In short: Many hospitals use a short screening tool.

Simple Questions

Many hospitals use a short screening tool. Typical questions ask about recent weight loss, reduced eating and body mass index.

Patients at risk should be referred to a dietitian or nutrition team where available.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Remember

Screen on admission.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about screening for malnutrition?

Screen on admission.

early-feeding-after-surgery.title: Early feeding after surgery
early-feeding-after-surgery.caption: Many patients can eat and drink within hours of surgery.
early-feeding-after-surgery.body:
In short: Many patients can eat and drink within hours of surgery.

Eat Sooner

Many patients can eat and drink within hours of surgery. Early feeding supports recovery and is part of enhanced recovery programmes.

Some operations, such as certain bowel or upper gut surgery, need individual plans.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Remember

Follow the surgical team's instructions.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about early feeding after surgery?

Follow the surgical team's instructions.

enteral-vs-parenteral-feeding.title: Enteral vs parenteral feeding
enteral-vs-parenteral-feeding.caption: Enteral feeding goes through the gut, by mouth or a tube.
enteral-vs-parenteral-feeding.body:
In short: Enteral feeding goes through the gut, by mouth or a tube.

Use The Gut

Enteral feeding goes through the gut, by mouth or a tube. Parenteral nutrition goes directly into a vein.

Enteral feeding is usually preferred when the gut works. Parenteral feeding has more infection and metabolic risks and needs strict aseptic care.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Remember

If the gut works, use it.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about enteral vs parenteral feeding?

If the gut works, use it.

checking-a-nasogastric-tube.title: Checking a nasogastric tube
checking-a-nasogastric-tube.caption: A misplaced tube in the lung can cause serious harm.
checking-a-nasogastric-tube.body:
In short: A misplaced tube in the lung can cause serious harm.

Before Feeding

A misplaced tube in the lung can cause serious harm. Follow your local policy to confirm position, which often includes testing aspirate pH and sometimes an X-ray.

Do not rely on listening for air.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Remember

Never feed without confirming position.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about checking a nasogastric tube?

Never feed without confirming position.

protein-needs-for-healing.title: Protein needs for healing
protein-needs-for-healing.caption: Protein supports wound healing and muscle recovery.
protein-needs-for-healing.body:
In short: Protein supports wound healing and muscle recovery.

Building Blocks

Protein supports wound healing and muscle recovery. Needs rise after surgery, burns and infection.

Sources include eggs, fish, beans, lentils, meat and milk products. Dietitians can calculate the right amount.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Remember

Protein with every meal.

Check yourself

Protein with every meal.

vitamin-c-and-zinc-in-wound-healing.title: Vitamin C and zinc in wound healing
vitamin-c-and-zinc-in-wound-healing.caption: Vitamin C is needed for collagen formation and zinc supports tissue repair.
vitamin-c-and-zinc-in-wound-healing.body:
In short: Vitamin C is needed for collagen formation and zinc supports tissue repair.

Micronutrients

Vitamin C is needed for collagen formation and zinc supports tissue repair. Deficiency can slow healing.

Supplements help mainly when there is a deficiency, so routine high doses are not recommended without advice.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Remember

Treat deficiency, not guesses.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about vitamin c and zinc in wound healing?

Treat deficiency, not guesses.

diabetes-and-meals-before-surgery.title: Diabetes and meals before surgery
diabetes-and-meals-before-surgery.caption: Fasting changes insulin needs.
diabetes-and-meals-before-surgery.body:
In short: Fasting changes insulin needs.

Blood Sugar Plans

Fasting changes insulin needs. Patients with diabetes need an individual plan for tablets and insulin.

Check glucose before and after surgery and treat low blood sugar promptly. Avoid stopping basal insulin completely unless advised.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Ask what the diabetes plan is.

Ask what the diabetes plan is.

swallowing-problems.title: Swallowing problems
swallowing-problems.caption: Difficulty swallowing raises the risk of choking and aspiration.
swallowing-problems.body:
In short: Difficulty swallowing raises the risk of choking and aspiration.

Dysphagia

Difficulty swallowing raises the risk of choking and aspiration. Watch for coughing with meals, a wet voice and food pocketing.

Sit upright, supervise meals and refer to a speech and language therapist where available.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Remember

Upright for every meal.

Upright for every meal.

hydration-how-much-is-enough.title: Hydration: how much is enough?
hydration-how-much-is-enough.caption: Adults often need around 25 to 30 mL per kilogram of fluid per day, adjusted for fever, losses, heart and kidney disease.
hydration-how-much-is-enough.body:
In short: Adults often need around 25 to 30 mL per kilogram of fluid per day, adjusted for fever, losses, heart and kidney disease.

Fluid Needs

Adults often need around 25 to 30 mL per kilogram of fluid per day, adjusted for fever, losses, heart and kidney disease.

Check urine colour and volume, thirst, blood pressure and weight trends.

Why it matters in theatre

Good nutrition and hydration support healing and lower complications. Recognising poor intake early lets the team act before surgery.

Remember

Individualise, do not memorise one number.

Individualise, do not memorise one number.

what-makes-a-good-day-surgery-patient.title: What makes a good day-surgery patient
what-makes-a-good-day-surgery-patient.caption: Good candidates have low-risk operations, stable medical conditions, a responsible adult at home and reasonable travel time to the hospital.
what-makes-a-good-day-surgery-patient.body:
In short: Good candidates have low-risk operations, stable medical conditions, a responsible adult at home and reasonable travel time to the hospital.

Selection

Good candidates have low-risk operations, stable medical conditions, a responsible adult at home and reasonable travel time to the hospital.

Poorly controlled illness or no home support may need admission.

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Remember

Plan the home support first.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about what makes a good day-surgery patient?

Plan the home support first.

discharge-criteria.title: Discharge criteria
discharge-criteria.caption: Typical criteria include stable vital signs, pain controlled, minimal nausea, able to drink, passing urine if required, and no excess bleeding.
discharge-criteria.body:
In short: Typical criteria include stable vital signs, pain controlled, minimal nausea, able to drink, passing urine if required, and no excess bleeding.

Ready To Go

Typical criteria include stable vital signs, pain controlled, minimal nausea, able to drink, passing urine if required, and no excess bleeding.

A responsible adult should take the patient home.

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Use a clear checklist.

What is the main thing to remember about discharge criteria?

Use a clear checklist.

post-operative-instructions.title: Post-operative instructions
post-operative-instructions.caption: Give written advice on pain relief, wound care, diet, activity and warning signs.
post-operative-instructions.body:

Written And Simple

Give written advice on pain relief, wound care, diet, activity and warning signs. Include a contact number.

Explain it to both the patient and the escort, because patients may remember little after sedation.

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Remember

Teach back to confirm.

What is the main thing to remember about post-operative instructions?

Teach back to confirm.

driving-and-decisions-after-anaesthesia.title: Driving and decisions after anaesthesia
driving-and-decisions-after-anaesthesia.caption: Patients should not drive, operate machinery, drink alcohol or sign important documents for about 24 hours after a general anaesthetic or sedation, or as advised locally.
driving-and-decisions-after-anaesthesia.body:
In short: Patients should not drive, operate machinery, drink alcohol or sign important documents for about 24 hours after a general anaesthetic or sedation, or as advised locally.

Stay Safe

Patients should not drive, operate machinery, drink alcohol or sign important documents for about 24 hours after a general anaesthetic or sedation, or as advised locally.

They should have an adult with them overnight.

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Remember

Do not drive for 24 hours.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about driving and decisions after anaesthesia?

Do not drive for 24 hours.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

managing-pain-at-home.title: Managing pain at home
managing-pain-at-home.caption: Start simple pain relief before the block or anaesthetic wears off.
managing-pain-at-home.body:
In short: Start simple pain relief before the block or anaesthetic wears off.

Plan Ahead

Start simple pain relief before the block or anaesthetic wears off. Combining paracetamol with an anti-inflammatory is common if there is no contraindication.

Use stronger drugs only as prescribed, and warn about constipation and drowsiness.

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Remember

Regular doses beat waiting for pain.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about managing pain at home?

Regular doses beat waiting for pain.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

nausea-after-discharge.title: Nausea after discharge
nausea-after-discharge.caption: PONV can occur after going home.
nausea-after-discharge.body:
In short: PONV can occur after going home.

Prevent And Treat

PONV can occur after going home. Risk factors include female sex, non-smoking, previous PONV and opioids.

Give an anti-sickness plan, encourage small sips, and avoid heavy meals at first. Persistent vomiting needs review.

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Remember

Offer a plan before leaving.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about nausea after discharge?

Offer a plan before leaving.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

when-to-seek-help-after-discharge.title: When to seek help after discharge
when-to-seek-help-after-discharge.caption: A quick list on when to seek help after discharge: Heavy bleeding that soaks the dressing; Fever or spreading redness.
when-to-seek-help-after-discharge.body:
In short: A quick list on when to seek help after discharge: Heavy bleeding that soaks the dressing; Fever or spreading redness.

When to seek help after discharge

  • Heavy bleeding that soaks the dressing
  • Fever or spreading redness
  • Severe pain not helped by tablets
  • Cannot pass urine
  • Vomiting that does not stop

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Remember

Give these in writing.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "When to seek help after discharge".

Heavy bleeding that soaks the dressing; Fever or spreading redness; Severe pain not helped by tablets; Cannot pass urine; Vomiting that does not stop.

local-anaesthesia-and-sedation-checks.title: Local anaesthesia and sedation checks
local-anaesthesia-and-sedation-checks.caption: Even with local anaesthesia, monitor oxygen, pulse and blood pressure.
local-anaesthesia-and-sedation-checks.body:
In short: Even with local anaesthesia, monitor oxygen, pulse and blood pressure.

Stay Alert

Even with local anaesthesia, monitor oxygen, pulse and blood pressure. Sedation can depress breathing.

Have suction, oxygen and airway equipment ready, and know the maximum safe dose of local anaesthetic.

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Remember

Local does not mean low risk.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about local anaesthesia and sedation checks?

Local does not mean low risk.
