smoking-and-surgical-recovery.title: Smoking and surgical recovery
smoking-and-surgical-recovery.caption: Smoking increases lung complications, infection and poor wound healing.
smoking-and-surgical-recovery.body:
In short: Smoking increases lung complications, infection and poor wound healing.

Stop Early

Smoking increases lung complications, infection and poor wound healing. Stopping even a few weeks beforehand can help, and longer is better.

Offer support and advice at every opportunity.

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Remember

Every smoke-free day helps.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about smoking and surgical recovery?

Every smoke-free day helps.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cancellations-common-causes.title: Cancellations: common causes
cancellations-common-causes.caption: Common reasons include illness on the day, not following fasting advice, medicines not stopped, no escort and incomplete tests.
cancellations-common-causes.body:
In short: Common reasons include illness on the day, not following fasting advice, medicines not stopped, no escort and incomplete tests.

Avoidable Delays

Common reasons include illness on the day, not following fasting advice, medicines not stopped, no escort and incomplete tests.

Clear pre-operative calls and instructions reduce cancellations.

Why it matters in theatre

Day surgery sends patients home the same day. It needs careful selection, clear instructions and a safe plan for the hours after discharge.

Call the patient before the day.

Call the patient before the day.

parts-of-the-urinary-tract.title: Parts of the urinary tract
parts-of-the-urinary-tract.caption: A quick list on parts of the urinary tract: Kidneys make urine; Ureters carry urine to the bladder.
parts-of-the-urinary-tract.body:
In short: A quick list on parts of the urinary tract: Kidneys make urine; Ureters carry urine to the bladder.

Parts of the urinary tract

  • Kidneys make urine
  • Ureters carry urine to the bladder
  • Bladder stores urine
  • Urethra carries urine out

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

Drain or block, the path matters.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Parts of the urinary tract".

Kidneys make urine; Ureters carry urine to the bladder; Bladder stores urine; Urethra carries urine out.

renal-colic.title: Renal colic
renal-colic.caption: A stone in the ureter can cause severe loin pain that comes in waves, often radiating to the groin, with blood in the urine.
renal-colic.body:
In short: A stone in the ureter can cause severe loin pain that comes in waves, often radiating to the groin, with blood in the urine.

Stone Pain

A stone in the ureter can cause severe loin pain that comes in waves, often radiating to the groin, with blood in the urine.

Pain relief, fluids if allowed and imaging are usual first steps. Infection with obstruction needs urgent help.

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

Fever plus a stone is an emergency.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about renal colic?

Fever plus a stone is an emergency.

acute-urinary-retention.title: Acute urinary retention
acute-urinary-retention.caption: Painful inability to pass urine can be caused by prostate enlargement, constipation, drugs, infection or nerve problems.
acute-urinary-retention.body:
In short: Painful inability to pass urine can be caused by prostate enlargement, constipation, drugs, infection or nerve problems.

Cannot Pass Urine

Painful inability to pass urine can be caused by prostate enlargement, constipation, drugs, infection or nerve problems.

A catheter relieves the bladder. Watch for large urine output afterwards and for low blood pressure.

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

Record urine volume after catheterisation.

Record urine volume after catheterisation.

enlarged-prostate.title: Enlarged prostate
enlarged-prostate.caption: An enlarged prostate can narrow the urethra, causing weak flow, frequent night urination and incomplete emptying.
enlarged-prostate.body:
In short: An enlarged prostate can narrow the urethra, causing weak flow, frequent night urination and incomplete emptying.

Benign Prostatic Enlargement

An enlarged prostate can narrow the urethra, causing weak flow, frequent night urination and incomplete emptying.

Treatment ranges from drugs to surgery. Transurethral resection of the prostate is a common operation.

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

Know the risks of TUR syndrome.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about enlarged prostate?

Know the risks of TUR syndrome.

testicular-torsion.title: Testicular torsion
testicular-torsion.caption: Torsion is twisting of the spermatic cord that cuts off blood supply.
testicular-torsion.body:
In short: Torsion is twisting of the spermatic cord that cuts off blood supply.

A Time-Critical Emergency

Torsion is twisting of the spermatic cord that cuts off blood supply. It causes sudden severe testicular pain, often with nausea.

It needs urgent surgery, ideally within hours, so do not delay for imaging if suspicion is high.

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

Time is testicle.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about testicular torsion?

Time is testicle.

circumcision-safety.title: Circumcision safety
circumcision-safety.caption: Confirm consent and identity, use a safe anaesthetic technique, and keep the surgical area clean.
circumcision-safety.body:
In short: Confirm consent and identity, use a safe anaesthetic technique, and keep the surgical area clean.

Checks

Confirm consent and identity, use a safe anaesthetic technique, and keep the surgical area clean.

Use only the diathermy type your surgeon requests, with local safety rules. Check for bleeding before leaving theatre.

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

Count swabs and check haemostasis.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about circumcision safety?

Count swabs and check haemostasis.

catheter-associated-infection.title: Catheter-associated infection
catheter-associated-infection.caption: Use a catheter only if needed, insert with aseptic technique, keep the bag below the bladder and the system closed.
catheter-associated-infection.body:
In short: Use a catheter only if needed, insert with aseptic technique, keep the bag below the bladder and the system closed.

Preventing Uti

Use a catheter only if needed, insert with aseptic technique, keep the bag below the bladder and the system closed.

Review daily and remove as soon as possible.

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

The shortest time is the safest.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about catheter-associated infection?

The shortest time is the safest.

haematuria.title: Haematuria
haematuria.caption: Blood in the urine can come from infection, stones, injury, kidney disease or cancer.
haematuria.body:
In short: Blood in the urine can come from infection, stones, injury, kidney disease or cancer.

Blood In Urine

Blood in the urine can come from infection, stones, injury, kidney disease or cancer. Painless haematuria needs investigation.

Clots can block a catheter and may need bladder irrigation.

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

Never ignore blood in the urine.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about haematuria?

Never ignore blood in the urine.

lithotomy-and-urology-positions.title: Lithotomy and urology positions
lithotomy-and-urology-positions.caption: Many urological procedures use the lithotomy position.
lithotomy-and-urology-positions.body:
In short: Many urological procedures use the lithotomy position.

Position Care

Many urological procedures use the lithotomy position. Raise and lower the legs together and slowly, as blood pressure can change.

Pad pressure points and protect the peroneal nerve and calves.

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

Limit time in lithotomy.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about lithotomy and urology positions?

Limit time in lithotomy.

bladder-irrigation-fluids.title: Bladder irrigation fluids
bladder-irrigation-fluids.caption: Non-electrolyte fluids may be used with monopolar resection, but absorption can cause low sodium.
bladder-irrigation-fluids.body:
In short: Non-electrolyte fluids may be used with monopolar resection, but absorption can cause low sodium.

Why Glycine Or Saline

Non-electrolyte fluids may be used with monopolar resection, but absorption can cause low sodium. Saline is used with bipolar systems.

Watch for confusion, nausea and changes in blood pressure and sodium.

Why it matters in theatre

Urological problems affect the kidneys, bladder and genital organs. Knowing the common conditions helps staff recognise emergencies and prepare for procedures.

Remember

Absorbed fluid can be dangerous.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about bladder irrigation fluids?

Absorbed fluid can be dangerous.

choosing-a-peripheral-cannula.title: Choosing a peripheral cannula
choosing-a-peripheral-cannula.caption: Larger cannulas flow faster.
choosing-a-peripheral-cannula.body:
In short: Larger cannulas flow faster.

Size And Colour

Larger cannulas flow faster. The colour code is widely used: pink 20G, green 18G, grey 16G, blue 22G, yellow 24G. Always confirm the size on the packaging.

Use the smallest that meets the need.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

Remember

Large for blood, small for veins that are fragile.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about choosing a peripheral cannula?

Large for blood, small for veins that are fragile.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

inserting-a-cannula-safely.title: Inserting a cannula safely
inserting-a-cannula-safely.caption: Clean your hands, apply a tourniquet, clean the skin and let it dry, insert with the bevel up, and look for flashback.
inserting-a-cannula-safely.body:
In short: Clean your hands, apply a tourniquet, clean the skin and let it dry, insert with the bevel up, and look for flashback.

Steps

Clean your hands, apply a tourniquet, clean the skin and let it dry, insert with the bevel up, and look for flashback.

Advance the catheter, release the tourniquet, remove the needle into a sharps box and secure the cannula.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

Remember

Dispose of the needle immediately.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about inserting a cannula safely?

Dispose of the needle immediately.

signs-of-phlebitis.title: Signs of phlebitis
signs-of-phlebitis.caption: Pain, redness, warmth, swelling or a hard cord along the vein suggest phlebitis.
signs-of-phlebitis.body:
In short: Pain, redness, warmth, swelling or a hard cord along the vein suggest phlebitis.

Check The Site

Pain, redness, warmth, swelling or a hard cord along the vein suggest phlebitis. Remove the cannula and resite if needed.

Check the site at least daily, and record observations.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

Remember

Remove if it looks irritated.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about signs of phlebitis?

Remove if it looks irritated.

extravasation-vs-infiltration.title: Extravasation vs infiltration
extravasation-vs-infiltration.caption: Infiltration is leakage of a non-irritant fluid into surrounding tissue.
extravasation-vs-infiltration.body:
In short: Infiltration is leakage of a non-irritant fluid into surrounding tissue.

Fluid In The Tissue

Infiltration is leakage of a non-irritant fluid into surrounding tissue. Extravasation is leakage of a drug that can damage tissue.

Stop the infusion, aspirate if possible, elevate the limb and follow local guidance.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

Remember

Stop at the first sign.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about extravasation vs infiltration?

Stop at the first sign.

central-venous-catheter-basics.title: Central venous catheter basics
central-venous-catheter-basics.caption: Central lines end in a large central vein and can give irritant drugs, vasopressors and parenteral nutrition.
central-venous-catheter-basics.body:
In short: Central lines end in a large central vein and can give irritant drugs, vasopressors and parenteral nutrition.

Deep Lines

Central lines end in a large central vein and can give irritant drugs, vasopressors and parenteral nutrition.

Risks include infection, bleeding, pneumothorax and air embolism. Strict aseptic technique and dressings are essential.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

Remember

Review the need every day.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about central venous catheter basics?

Review the need every day.

preventing-line-infection.title: Preventing line infection
preventing-line-infection.caption: Clean hands, full barrier precautions for central lines, chlorhexidine skin preparation and a clean dressing reduce infection.
preventing-line-infection.body:
In short: Clean hands, full barrier precautions for central lines, chlorhexidine skin preparation and a clean dressing reduce infection.

Care Bundle

Clean hands, full barrier precautions for central lines, chlorhexidine skin preparation and a clean dressing reduce infection.

Scrub the hub before each access and remove unneeded lines.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

Remember

Scrub the hub.

Scrub the hub.

intraosseous-access.title: Intraosseous access
intraosseous-access.caption: Intraosseous access delivers fluids and drugs through bone marrow when veins cannot be found quickly in an emergency.
intraosseous-access.body:
In short: Intraosseous access delivers fluids and drugs through bone marrow when veins cannot be found quickly in an emergency.

When Veins Fail

Intraosseous access delivers fluids and drugs through bone marrow when veins cannot be found quickly in an emergency.

It is used in adults and children. Confirm placement and secure the device, and replace it with other access when practical.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

A fast route in a crisis.

flushing-and-locking.title: Flushing and locking
flushing-and-locking.caption: Flushing with saline helps keep catheters clear and separates incompatible drugs.
flushing-and-locking.body:
In short: Flushing with saline helps keep catheters clear and separates incompatible drugs.

Keep It Open

Flushing with saline helps keep catheters clear and separates incompatible drugs. Use a push-pause technique and a syringe size recommended locally.

Never force a blocked line.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

Resistance means stop and check.

air-in-the-line.title: Air in the line
air-in-the-line.caption: Small amounts of air in peripheral lines are usually harmless, but large amounts can cause serious air embolism, especially in central lines.
air-in-the-line.body:
In short: Small amounts of air in peripheral lines are usually harmless, but large amounts can cause serious air embolism, especially in central lines.

Avoid Air

Small amounts of air in peripheral lines are usually harmless, but large amounts can cause serious air embolism, especially in central lines.

Prime all lines, check for bubbles and clamp when disconnecting.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

Remember

Prime, check, clamp.

Prime, check, clamp.

difficult-veins.title: Difficult veins
difficult-veins.caption: Warmth, gravity, a tourniquet and gentle tapping can help.
difficult-veins.body:
In short: Warmth, gravity, a tourniquet and gentle tapping can help.

Helpful Tricks

Warmth, gravity, a tourniquet and gentle tapping can help. Ultrasound guidance helps when veins are not visible.

Avoid limbs with fistulas, lymphoedema or previous surgery as advised.

Why it matters in theatre

Cannulas and central lines deliver drugs and fluids, but they are also a route for infection and injury. Careful technique and checking keep them safe.

Ask for help early.

greeting-the-patient.title: Greeting the patient
greeting-the-patient.caption: Introduce yourself, confirm the patient's name, and explain what you are about to do.
greeting-the-patient.body:
In short: Introduce yourself, confirm the patient's name, and explain what you are about to do.

First Impression

Introduce yourself, confirm the patient's name, and explain what you are about to do. Many patients are anxious in theatre.

A calm voice and eye contact reduce fear. Protect privacy and dignity.

Why it matters in theatre

Clear communication with patients and colleagues prevents errors and builds trust. It is a clinical skill that can be practised.

Remember

Say your name and role.

Check yourself

Say your name and role.

explaining-in-plain-language.caption: Use everyday words instead of medical terms.
explaining-in-plain-language.body:

Avoid Jargon

Use everyday words instead of medical terms. Check understanding by asking patients to say it back in their own words.

Interpreters or family members may help if there is a language barrier, following local policy.

Clear communication with patients and colleagues prevents errors and builds trust. It is a clinical skill that can be practised.

breaking-bad-news-in-brief.body:
In short: Find a private place, sit down, give a warning that serious news is coming, and use clear, honest language.

Keep It Human

Find a private place, sit down, give a warning that serious news is coming, and use clear, honest language.

Allow silence, show empathy and offer support. Follow local rules about who should deliver news.

Clear communication with patients and colleagues prevents errors and builds trust. It is a clinical skill that can be practised.

closed-loop-communication-communication.caption: The sender gives a clear order, the receiver repeats it back, and the sender confirms.

The sender gives a clear order, the receiver repeats it back, and the sender confirms.

Concerns And Escalation

If unsafe, escalate to a senior or follow your safety policy.

Clear communication with patients and colleagues prevents errors and builds trust. It is a clinical skill that can be practised.

working-with-an-interpreter.body:

Short sentences and pauses help accuracy.

Clear communication with patients and colleagues prevents errors and builds trust. It is a clinical skill that can be practised.

dealing-with-anxious-patients.body:
In short: Anxious patients may benefit from clear information, a familiar person nearby, and kind reassurance.

Calm Before Anaesthesia

Anxious patients may benefit from clear information, a familiar person nearby, and kind reassurance.

Ask what worries them. Do not promise outcomes you cannot guarantee.

Listen first.

Listen first.

handling-a-complaint.body:

Stay Professional

Listen without interrupting, acknowledge feelings, avoid blame and explain what will happen next.

Record the facts and escalate according to your hospital's process.

Keep the bone flap safe and labelled.

What is the main thing to remember about burr holes and craniotomy?

Keep the bone flap safe and labelled.

extradural-haematoma.title: Extradural haematoma
extradural-haematoma.caption: Often follows a head injury with a skull fracture tearing a meningeal artery.
extradural-haematoma.body:
In short: Often follows a head injury with a skull fracture tearing a meningeal artery.

Bleed Outside The Dura

Often follows a head injury with a skull fracture tearing a meningeal artery. The patient may be lucid for a while, then deteriorate quickly.

It is a surgical emergency. Early evacuation can give a good recovery.

Why it matters

Brain and spine operations leave little room for error. Teams must protect intracranial pressure, position carefully and watch for neurological change.

Remember

Lucid interval, then rapid decline.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about extradural haematoma?

Lucid interval, then rapid decline.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

hydrocephalus-and-shunts.title: Hydrocephalus and shunts
hydrocephalus-and-shunts.caption: Hydrocephalus is a build-up of cerebrospinal fluid causing raised pressure.
hydrocephalus-and-shunts.body:
In short: Hydrocephalus is a build-up of cerebrospinal fluid causing raised pressure.

Too Much Csf

Hydrocephalus is a build-up of cerebrospinal fluid causing raised pressure. A shunt drains fluid, often from the brain to the abdomen.

Shunts are strict no-touch implants, as infection can cause serious harm. Keep exposure and theatre traffic low.

Why it matters

Brain and spine operations leave little room for error. Teams must protect intracranial pressure, position carefully and watch for neurological change.

Remember

Shunt surgery demands strict asepsis.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about hydrocephalus and shunts?

Shunt surgery demands strict asepsis.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

neurosurgical-instruments.title: Neurosurgical instruments
neurosurgical-instruments.caption: Delicate work uses fine forceps, dissectors, bipolar diathermy and self-retaining retainers.
neurosurgical-instruments.body:
In short: Delicate work uses fine forceps, dissectors, bipolar diathermy and self-retaining retainers.

Special Kit

Delicate work uses fine forceps, dissectors, bipolar diathermy and self-retaining retainers. Cottonoids protect brain tissue and must be counted carefully.

Bipolar diathermy limits spread of current and is preferred near nerves and vessels.

Why it matters

Brain and spine operations leave little room for error. Teams must protect intracranial pressure, position carefully and watch for neurological change.

Remember

Count cottonoids like swabs.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about neurosurgical instruments?

Count cottonoids like swabs.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

spinal-surgery-positioning.title: Spinal surgery positioning
spinal-surgery-positioning.caption: Many spine operations are done prone.
spinal-surgery-positioning.body:
In short: Many spine operations are done prone.

Prone Safety

Many spine operations are done prone. The abdomen should hang free to reduce venous bleeding, and eyes, face, chest and genitals need padding.

The airway tube must be well secured, and the team turns together on a command.

Why it matters

Brain and spine operations leave little room for error. Teams must protect intracranial pressure, position carefully and watch for neurological change.

Remember

Prone means pressure checks everywhere.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about spinal surgery positioning?

Prone means pressure checks everywhere.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

laminectomy.title: Laminectomy
laminectomy.caption: A laminectomy removes part of the vertebral arch to relieve pressure on the spinal cord or nerve roots.
laminectomy.body:
In short: A laminectomy removes part of the vertebral arch to relieve pressure on the spinal cord or nerve roots.

Decompressing The Cord

A laminectomy removes part of the vertebral arch to relieve pressure on the spinal cord or nerve roots. It may treat tumours or severe narrowing.

Correct level confirmation, often by imaging, avoids wrong-level surgery.

Why it matters

Brain and spine operations leave little room for error. Teams must protect intracranial pressure, position carefully and watch for neurological change.

Remember

Confirm the spinal level before cutting.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about laminectomy?

Confirm the spinal level before cutting.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cauda-equina-warning-signs.title: Cauda equina warning signs
cauda-equina-warning-signs.caption: A quick list on cauda equina warning signs: Back pain with new numbness between the legs; Loss of bladder or bowel control.
cauda-equina-warning-signs.body:
In short: A quick list on cauda equina warning signs: Back pain with new numbness between the legs; Loss of bladder or bowel control.

Cauda equina warning signs

  • Back pain with new numbness between the legs
  • Loss of bladder or bowel control
  • Leg weakness that is worsening
  • This is an emergency needing urgent imaging

Why it matters

Brain and spine operations leave little room for error. Teams must protect intracranial pressure, position carefully and watch for neurological change.

Remember

Saddle numbness plus bladder change: act now.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Cauda equina warning signs".

Back pain with new numbness between the legs; Loss of bladder or bowel control; Leg weakness that is worsening; This is an emergency needing urgent imaging.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

heart-lung-bypass.title: Heart-lung bypass
heart-lung-bypass.caption: Cardiopulmonary bypass diverts blood away from the heart and lungs, oxygenates it in a machine and returns it to the body.
heart-lung-bypass.body:
In short: Cardiopulmonary bypass diverts blood away from the heart and lungs, oxygenates it in a machine and returns it to the body.

Taking Over

Cardiopulmonary bypass diverts blood away from the heart and lungs, oxygenates it in a machine and returns it to the body.

This gives a still, empty heart to operate on. A perfusionist runs the machine and works closely with the team.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

The perfusionist is a core team member.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about heart-lung bypass?

The perfusionist is a core team member.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cardioplegia.title: Cardioplegia
cardioplegia.caption: Cardioplegia solution is given to stop the heart in a controlled way and protect the muscle during surgery.
cardioplegia.body:
In short: Cardioplegia solution is given to stop the heart in a controlled way and protect the muscle during surgery.

Stopping The Heart

Cardioplegia solution is given to stop the heart in a controlled way and protect the muscle during surgery.

Cold temperature slows the heart's energy use. Timing is carefully recorded.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

A protected heart is a still heart.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cardioplegia?

A protected heart is a still heart.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

heparin-and-bypass.title: Heparin and bypass
heparin-and-bypass.caption: Heparin prevents clotting as blood passes through the bypass circuit.
heparin-and-bypass.body:
In short: Heparin prevents clotting as blood passes through the bypass circuit.

Blood Thinning

Heparin prevents clotting as blood passes through the bypass circuit. Its effect is checked by clotting tests.

After bypass it is reversed with another drug. Bleeding is closely watched afterwards.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

No clotting control, no safe bypass.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about heparin and bypass?

No clotting control, no safe bypass.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

coronary-artery-bypass-grafting.title: Coronary artery bypass grafting
coronary-artery-bypass-grafting.caption: CABG uses vessels from elsewhere in the body, such as the internal thoracic artery or leg veins, to bypass narrowed coronary arteries.
coronary-artery-bypass-grafting.body:
In short: CABG uses vessels from elsewhere in the body, such as the internal thoracic artery or leg veins, to bypass narrowed coronary arteries.

New Routes

CABG uses vessels from elsewhere in the body, such as the internal thoracic artery or leg veins, to bypass narrowed coronary arteries.

This improves blood flow to the heart muscle in selected patients.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

Grafts reroute around blockages.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about coronary artery bypass grafting?

Grafts reroute around blockages.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

sternotomy-basics.title: Sternotomy basics
sternotomy-basics.caption: A median sternotomy splits the breastbone down the middle.
sternotomy-basics.body:
In short: A median sternotomy splits the breastbone down the middle.

Opening The Chest

A median sternotomy splits the breastbone down the middle. A saw cuts it and a retractor holds it open.

It is closed with strong wires. Pain control and chest support help later breathing and healing.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

Support the chest when coughing.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about sternotomy basics?

Support the chest when coughing.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

chest-drains.title: Chest drains
chest-drains.caption: Chest drains remove air, blood or fluid so the lungs can expand.
chest-drains.body:
In short: Chest drains remove air, blood or fluid so the lungs can expand.

Draining The Chest

Chest drains remove air, blood or fluid so the lungs can expand. They connect to an underwater seal or suction system.

The collection bottle stays below chest level. Do not clamp a drain unless instructed.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

Keep the bottle below the chest.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about chest drains?

Keep the bottle below the chest.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

pneumothorax.title: Pneumothorax
pneumothorax.caption: Air between lung and chest wall can collapse the lung.
pneumothorax.body:
In short: Air between lung and chest wall can collapse the lung.

Air In The Pleura

Air between lung and chest wall can collapse the lung. A tension pneumothorax pushes the heart and vessels aside, causing shock.

Signs include severe breathlessness and low blood pressure. It needs urgent decompression.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

Tension is a clinical, emergency diagnosis.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about pneumothorax?

Tension is a clinical, emergency diagnosis.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

valve-surgery.title: Valve surgery
valve-surgery.caption: Heart valves may narrow or leak.
valve-surgery.body:
In short: Heart valves may narrow or leak.

Repair Or Replace

Heart valves may narrow or leak. A damaged valve may be repaired or replaced with a mechanical or tissue valve.

Mechanical valves need lifelong blood thinners, while tissue valves often do not but may wear sooner.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

Valve choice depends on the patient.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about valve surgery?

Valve choice depends on the patient.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

rheumatic-heart-disease.title: Rheumatic heart disease
rheumatic-heart-disease.caption: Rheumatic fever can follow untreated throat infection and permanently scar heart valves.
rheumatic-heart-disease.body:
In short: Rheumatic fever can follow untreated throat infection and permanently scar heart valves.

A Local Concern

Rheumatic fever can follow untreated throat infection and permanently scar heart valves. It remains an important cause of valve surgery in many low-resource settings.

Treating sore throats and giving preventive antibiotics reduces risk.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

Prevention starts with a sore throat.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about rheumatic heart disease?

Prevention starts with a sore throat.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

thoracotomy.title: Thoracotomy
thoracotomy.caption: A thoracotomy is an incision between the ribs, used for lung, oesophageal and some heart operations.
thoracotomy.body:
In short: A thoracotomy is an incision between the ribs, used for lung, oesophageal and some heart operations.

Opening The Side

A thoracotomy is an incision between the ribs, used for lung, oesophageal and some heart operations. The patient lies on their side.

It is painful, so analgesia is important. Epidural or regional blocks are often used.

Why it matters

Heart and chest operations involve bypass machines, drains and high-risk patients. Understanding the basics helps theatre staff anticipate needs and respond quickly.

Remember

Good pain relief protects the lungs.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about thoracotomy?

Good pain relief protects the lungs.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

principles-of-plastic-surgery.title: Principles of plastic surgery
principles-of-plastic-surgery.caption: Plastic surgery rebuilds or reshapes tissue to restore form and function, after injury, burns, cancer or birth differences.
principles-of-plastic-surgery.body:
In short: Plastic surgery rebuilds or reshapes tissue to restore form and function, after injury, burns, cancer or birth differences.

Restoring Form

Plastic surgery rebuilds or reshapes tissue to restore form and function, after injury, burns, cancer or birth differences.

Gentle tissue handling, good blood supply and careful closure matter most.

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Gentle hands heal better.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about principles of plastic surgery?

Gentle hands heal better.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

skin-grafts.title: Skin grafts
skin-grafts.caption: A graft takes skin from a donor site and places it on a wound.
skin-grafts.body:
In short: A graft takes skin from a donor site and places it on a wound.

Moving Skin

A graft takes skin from a donor site and places it on a wound. It survives by gaining new blood supply from the wound bed.

It needs a clean bed, firm contact and rest. Split-thickness grafts take only part of the skin.

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Graft needs contact and stillness.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about skin grafts?

Graft needs contact and stillness.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

flaps-versus-grafts.title: Flaps versus grafts
flaps-versus-grafts.caption: A flap moves tissue with its own blood supply attached.
flaps-versus-grafts.body:
In short: A flap moves tissue with its own blood supply attached.

Bringing A Blood Supply

A flap moves tissue with its own blood supply attached. A graft has none and depends on the wound bed.

Flaps can cover deeper, poorer wounds. Their blood supply must be protected from pressure and kinking.

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Flaps bring their own blood supply.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about flaps versus grafts?

Flaps bring their own blood supply.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

burn-depth.title: Burn depth
burn-depth.caption: Superficial burns are red and painful.
burn-depth.body:
In short: Superficial burns are red and painful.

How Deep

Superficial burns are red and painful. Partial-thickness burns blister. Full-thickness burns may look white, leathery or charred and may feel numb.

Deeper burns often need surgery to heal well.

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Painless burns are often the deepest.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about burn depth?

Painless burns are often the deepest.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

burn-first-aid.title: Burn first aid
burn-first-aid.caption: A quick list on burn first aid: Stop the burning process; Cool with running clean water for about 20 minutes.
burn-first-aid.body:
In short: A quick list on burn first aid: Stop the burning process; Cool with running clean water for about 20 minutes.

Burn first aid

  • Stop the burning process
  • Cool with running clean water for about 20 minutes
  • Remove rings and tight items early
  • Cover loosely with clean non-stick material

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Cool first, cover, then seek care.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Burn first aid".

Stop the burning process; Cool with running clean water for about 20 minutes; Remove rings and tight items early; Cover loosely with clean non-stick material.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tangential-excision.title: Tangential excision
tangential-excision.caption: Dead burn tissue is shaved in thin layers until healthy bleeding tissue appears.
tangential-excision.body:
In short: Dead burn tissue is shaved in thin layers until healthy bleeding tissue appears.

Shaving The Burn

Dead burn tissue is shaved in thin layers until healthy bleeding tissue appears. It can then be covered with a graft.

Blood loss can be significant, so preparation for bleeding is important.

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Early excision cuts infection risk.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tangential excision?

Early excision cuts infection risk.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

burn-scars-and-contractures.title: Burn scars and contractures
burn-scars-and-contractures.caption: Burn scars can shorten as they mature, restricting movement.
burn-scars-and-contractures.body:
In short: Burn scars can shorten as they mature, restricting movement.

Tight Scars

Burn scars can shorten as they mature, restricting movement. Joints near burns are most affected.

Positioning, splints, exercises and pressure garments help. Surgery may release tight scars later.

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Movement prevents contracture.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about burn scars and contractures?

Movement prevents contracture.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cleft-lip-and-palate.title: Cleft lip and palate
cleft-lip-and-palate.caption: A cleft is a gap in the lip or palate from incomplete joining during development.
cleft-lip-and-palate.body:
In short: A cleft is a gap in the lip or palate from incomplete joining during development.

A Birth Difference

A cleft is a gap in the lip or palate from incomplete joining during development. Feeding and speech can be affected.

Repair is usually done in stages by a team, often with the lip first and palate later in infancy.

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Team care gives the best results.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cleft lip and palate?

Team care gives the best results.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

hand-injuries.title: Hand injuries
hand-injuries.caption: Hands are complex, with tendons, nerves and fine blood vessels.
hand-injuries.body:
In short: Hands are complex, with tendons, nerves and fine blood vessels.

Protect The Hand

Hands are complex, with tendons, nerves and fine blood vessels. A missed injury can limit function for life.

Elevate, cover with moist clean dressings and keep amputated parts cool and dry in a bag, not frozen directly.

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Cool amputated parts, never freeze them.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about hand injuries?

Cool amputated parts, never freeze them.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tourniquet-use-on-limbs.title: Tourniquet use on limbs
tourniquet-use-on-limbs.caption: A tourniquet gives a dry field in limb surgery.
tourniquet-use-on-limbs.body:
In short: A tourniquet gives a dry field in limb surgery.

Bloodless Field

A tourniquet gives a dry field in limb surgery. Time on is recorded and kept as short as possible.

Padding protects the skin. Release is announced to anaesthesia, as blood pressure and other changes may follow.

Why it matters

Burns, wounds, hand injuries and reconstruction are common in many settings. Good tissue handling and flap care protect both function and appearance.

Remember

Record tourniquet start time.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tourniquet use on limbs?

Record tourniquet start time.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tonsillectomy.title: Tonsillectomy
tonsillectomy.caption: Tonsillectomy is considered for repeated severe tonsillitis or breathing problems in sleep.
tonsillectomy.body:
In short: Tonsillectomy is considered for repeated severe tonsillitis or breathing problems in sleep.

Removing The Tonsils

Tonsillectomy is considered for repeated severe tonsillitis or breathing problems in sleep. The airway is shared between surgeon and anaesthetist.

Bleeding is the main risk, including in the days after surgery. Parents are told warning signs.

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Bleeding can occur after discharge.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tonsillectomy?

Bleeding can occur after discharge.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

shared-airway-surgery.title: Shared airway surgery
shared-airway-surgery.caption: In mouth, throat and nose operations, the surgeon and anaesthetist work around the same airway.
shared-airway-surgery.body:
In short: In mouth, throat and nose operations, the surgeon and anaesthetist work around the same airway.

Sharing The Airway

In mouth, throat and nose operations, the surgeon and anaesthetist work around the same airway. A secure tube and clear communication are key.

Suction, throat packs and swab counts need careful tracking.

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Count and remove throat packs.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about shared airway surgery?

Count and remove throat packs.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

throat-pack-safety.title: Throat pack safety
throat-pack-safety.caption: A throat pack stops blood and debris entering the airway.
throat-pack-safety.body:
In short: A throat pack stops blood and debris entering the airway.

Do Not Forget

A throat pack stops blood and debris entering the airway. A retained pack can block breathing.

It must be recorded when placed and removed, and confirmed before waking the patient.

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Pack in, pack out, written down.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about throat pack safety?

Pack in, pack out, written down.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tracheostomy.title: Tracheostomy
tracheostomy.caption: A tracheostomy is an opening in the neck leading to the trachea, giving a safe airway for breathing or long ventilation.
tracheostomy.body:
In short: A tracheostomy is an opening in the neck leading to the trachea, giving a safe airway for breathing or long ventilation.

A New Airway

A tracheostomy is an opening in the neck leading to the trachea, giving a safe airway for breathing or long ventilation.

The tube needs regular suction and humidification. A spare tube and suction stay at the bedside.

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Spare tube and suction at the bedside.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tracheostomy?

Spare tube and suction at the bedside.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tracheostomy-tube-blockage.title: Tracheostomy tube blockage
tracheostomy-tube-blockage.caption: A blocked tracheostomy tube can stop breathing quickly.
tracheostomy-tube-blockage.body:
In short: A blocked tracheostomy tube can stop breathing quickly.

Emergency

A blocked tracheostomy tube can stop breathing quickly. Signs are noisy breathing, distress and falling oxygen.

Suction, remove the inner tube if present, and replace the tube if needed. Call for help immediately.

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Cannot breathe through it? Change or remove.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tracheostomy tube blockage?

Cannot breathe through it? Change or remove.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

foreign-body-in-the-airway.title: Foreign body in the airway
foreign-body-in-the-airway.caption: Inhaled objects, especially in small children, can cause sudden coughing, wheeze or noisy breathing.
foreign-body-in-the-airway.body:
In short: Inhaled objects, especially in small children, can cause sudden coughing, wheeze or noisy breathing.

Choking

Inhaled objects, especially in small children, can cause sudden coughing, wheeze or noisy breathing. Beans, nuts and small toys are common.

Removal by bronchoscopy may be needed. Never blindly sweep a child's mouth.

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Do not blind sweep a child's mouth.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about foreign body in the airway?

Do not blind sweep a child's mouth.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

grommets.title: Grommets
grommets.caption: A grommet is a tiny tube placed in the eardrum to drain fluid from the middle ear.
grommets.body:
In short: A grommet is a tiny tube placed in the eardrum to drain fluid from the middle ear.

Ventilating The Ear

A grommet is a tiny tube placed in the eardrum to drain fluid from the middle ear. It is often used for repeated infections or glue ear.

It usually falls out on its own. Ears should be kept as advised.

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Keep ears dry as instructed.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about grommets?

Keep ears dry as instructed.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

glue-ear.title: Glue ear
glue-ear.caption: Fluid behind the eardrum can dull hearing, especially in children.
glue-ear.body:
In short: Fluid behind the eardrum can dull hearing, especially in children.

Fluid Behind The Drum

Fluid behind the eardrum can dull hearing, especially in children. It often settles by itself.

Persistent cases may need hearing tests and grommets, as poor hearing can affect speech and school.

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Check hearing in a quiet child.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about glue ear?

Check hearing in a quiet child.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

nose-bleeds.title: Nose bleeds
nose-bleeds.caption: A quick list on nose bleeds: Sit up and lean forward; Pinch the soft part of the nose for about 10 minutes.
nose-bleeds.body:
In short: A quick list on nose bleeds: Sit up and lean forward; Pinch the soft part of the nose for about 10 minutes.

Nose bleeds

  • Sit up and lean forward
  • Pinch the soft part of the nose for about 10 minutes
  • Breathe through the mouth
  • Seek help if bleeding continues or is heavy

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Pinch soft part, lean forward.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Nose bleeds".

Sit up and lean forward; Pinch the soft part of the nose for about 10 minutes; Breathe through the mouth; Seek help if bleeding continues or is heavy.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

nasal-packing.title: Nasal packing
nasal-packing.caption: Nasal packs or balloons compress bleeding vessels.
nasal-packing.body:
In short: Nasal packs or balloons compress bleeding vessels.

Controlling Bleeding

Nasal packs or balloons compress bleeding vessels. They can block the nose, so the patient breathes through the mouth.

Watch for airway trouble and slipping of the pack. Packs are removed according to medical orders.

Why it matters

Ear, nose and throat surgery shares the airway with the anaesthetist. Airway safety, bleeding and counts are everyday concerns.

Remember

Count and record all nasal packing.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about nasal packing?

Count and record all nasal packing.

cataract-surgery.title: Cataract surgery
cataract-surgery.caption: A cataract is a cloudy lens that dulls vision.
cataract-surgery.body:
In short: A cataract is a cloudy lens that dulls vision.

Cloudy Lens

A cataract is a cloudy lens that dulls vision. Surgery removes it and usually places a clear artificial lens.

It is among the most common operations worldwide and often restores sight well.

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Cataract is treatable blindness.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cataract surgery?

Cataract is treatable blindness.

eye-operation-asepsis.title: Eye operation asepsis
eye-operation-asepsis.caption: Infection inside the eye can destroy sight.
eye-operation-asepsis.body:
In short: Infection inside the eye can destroy sight.

Protecting The Eye

Infection inside the eye can destroy sight. The eye and lids are cleaned with an approved antiseptic and draped with the lashes covered.

Instruments are used for one patient and sterilised carefully between cases.

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Intra-ocular infection is devastating.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about eye operation asepsis?

Intra-ocular infection is devastating.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

glaucoma.title: Glaucoma
glaucoma.caption: Glaucoma damages the optic nerve, often with raised eye pressure.
glaucoma.body:
In short: Glaucoma damages the optic nerve, often with raised eye pressure.

Pressure In The Eye

Glaucoma damages the optic nerve, often with raised eye pressure. Early disease causes no symptoms and slowly narrows peripheral vision.

Treatment aims to lower pressure with drops, laser or surgery.

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Lost vision cannot be regained.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about glaucoma?

Lost vision cannot be regained.

local-anaesthesia-for-eyes.title: Local anaesthesia for eyes
local-anaesthesia-for-eyes.caption: Many eye operations use topical drops or a local anaesthetic block, with the patient awake.
local-anaesthesia-for-eyes.body:
In short: Many eye operations use topical drops or a local anaesthetic block, with the patient awake.

Blocks And Drops

Many eye operations use topical drops or a local anaesthetic block, with the patient awake. The patient must stay still and lie flat.

Reassure them, and explain that they may see light and movement.

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Talk to awake eye patients throughout.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about local anaesthesia for eyes?

Talk to awake eye patients throughout.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

operating-microscope.title: Operating microscope
operating-microscope.caption: Fine eye surgery is done under a microscope.
operating-microscope.body:
In short: Fine eye surgery is done under a microscope.

Magnified View

Fine eye surgery is done under a microscope. Focus, light and position are set before draping.

The microscope is expensive and delicate, and lenses are cleaned only with approved materials.

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Set up and test before starting.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about operating microscope?

Set up and test before starting.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

oculocardiac-reflex.title: Oculocardiac reflex
oculocardiac-reflex.caption: Pulling on eye muscles or pressing on the eye can slow the heart.
oculocardiac-reflex.body:
In short: Pulling on eye muscles or pressing on the eye can slow the heart.

Pulling On The Eye

Pulling on eye muscles or pressing on the eye can slow the heart. It is especially common in squint surgery in children.

The surgeon stops the traction, and the heart rate usually recovers.

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Slow pulse in squint surgery: stop pulling.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about oculocardiac reflex?

Slow pulse in squint surgery: stop pulling.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

retinal-detachment.title: Retinal detachment
retinal-detachment.caption: The retina can peel away from the back of the eye.
retinal-detachment.body:
In short: The retina can peel away from the back of the eye.

Curtain Over Vision

The retina can peel away from the back of the eye. Warning signs are new flashes, many floaters and a curtain-like shadow.

Urgent repair offers the best chance of saving vision.

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Curtain across vision is urgent.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about retinal detachment?

Curtain across vision is urgent.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

trauma-to-the-eye.title: Trauma to the eye
trauma-to-the-eye.caption: If an eye injury may have punctured the globe, do not press on it.
trauma-to-the-eye.body:
In short: If an eye injury may have punctured the globe, do not press on it.

Open Globe

If an eye injury may have punctured the globe, do not press on it. Protect it with a rigid shield and avoid ointments or drops unless advised.

The patient should be kept calm and nil by mouth for surgery.

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Shield, don't press.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about trauma to the eye?

Shield, don't press.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

chemical-eye-injury.title: Chemical eye injury
chemical-eye-injury.caption: A quick list on chemical eye injury: Start washing the eye straight away; Use plenty of clean water or saline.
chemical-eye-injury.body:
In short: A quick list on chemical eye injury: Start washing the eye straight away; Use plenty of clean water or saline.

Chemical eye injury

  • Start washing the eye straight away
  • Use plenty of clean water or saline
  • Keep eyelids open during irrigation
  • Continue until the surface is neutral, then get help

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Irrigate first, ask questions later.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Chemical eye injury".

Start washing the eye straight away; Use plenty of clean water or saline; Keep eyelids open during irrigation; Continue until the surface is neutral, then get help.

corneal-transplant.title: Corneal transplant
corneal-transplant.caption: A damaged cornea can be replaced with donor tissue.
corneal-transplant.body:
In short: A damaged cornea can be replaced with donor tissue.

Donor Tissue

A damaged cornea can be replaced with donor tissue. Donor tissue is stored and handled under strict conditions.

Corneal donation is a gift that restores sight, and families are approached with great sensitivity.

Why it matters

Eye surgery is delicate and sight is precious. Clean technique, careful instrument care and knowing urgent eye signs protect vision.

Remember

Handle donor tissue as precious.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about corneal transplant?

Handle donor tissue as precious.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

dental-extraction-basics.title: Dental extraction basics
dental-extraction-basics.caption: Extractions use local anaesthetic, an elevator and forceps.
dental-extraction-basics.body:
In short: Extractions use local anaesthetic, an elevator and forceps.

Removing A Tooth

Extractions use local anaesthetic, an elevator and forceps. The aim is a clean removal without damaging nearby teeth, bone or nerves.

Gauze pressure after the extraction helps clotting. Patients are warned not to rinse hard that day.

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

Bite on gauze, avoid vigorous rinsing.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about dental extraction basics?

Bite on gauze, avoid vigorous rinsing.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

dry-socket.title: Dry socket
dry-socket.caption: If the clot in an extraction socket is lost, the bone is exposed and causes severe, throbbing pain a few days later.
dry-socket.body:
In short: If the clot in an extraction socket is lost, the bone is exposed and causes severe, throbbing pain a few days later.

Lost Clot

If the clot in an extraction socket is lost, the bone is exposed and causes severe, throbbing pain a few days later.

Smoking, vigorous rinsing and poor hygiene raise risk. The dentist cleans and dresses the socket.

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

Protect the clot to prevent pain.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about dry socket?

Protect the clot to prevent pain.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

facial-fractures.title: Facial fractures
facial-fractures.caption: Facial injuries may involve the jaw, cheekbone or the bones around the eye and nose.
facial-fractures.body:
In short: Facial injuries may involve the jaw, cheekbone or the bones around the eye and nose.

Bones Of The Face

Facial injuries may involve the jaw, cheekbone or the bones around the eye and nose. Bleeding, swelling and a changed bite are clues.

Check the airway and neck before anything else.

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

Airway and neck first, face second.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about facial fractures?

Airway and neck first, face second.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

mandible-fracture.title: Mandible fracture
mandible-fracture.caption: Signs include pain, an uneven bite, numb lower lip and difficulty opening the mouth.
mandible-fracture.body:
In short: Signs include pain, an uneven bite, numb lower lip and difficulty opening the mouth.

Broken Jaw

Signs include pain, an uneven bite, numb lower lip and difficulty opening the mouth. Fractures are often in more than one place.

Treatment may use plates and screws or wiring the jaws together for a time.

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

A changed bite suggests a jaw fracture.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about mandible fracture?

A changed bite suggests a jaw fracture.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

wired-jaws-and-airway.title: Wired jaws and airway
wired-jaws-and-airway.caption: When the jaws are wired shut, vomiting can be dangerous.
wired-jaws-and-airway.body:
In short: When the jaws are wired shut, vomiting can be dangerous.

If The Jaws Are Fixed

When the jaws are wired shut, vomiting can be dangerous. The patient must be able to clear the airway.

Wire cutters or scissors are kept with the patient in case of emergency, and staff know how to use them.

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

Cutters must stay with the patient.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about wired jaws and airway?

Cutters must stay with the patient.

difficult-airway-in-jaw-surgery.title: Difficult airway in jaw surgery
difficult-airway-in-jaw-surgery.caption: Facial trauma and swelling can make intubation hard.
difficult-airway-in-jaw-surgery.body:
In short: Facial trauma and swelling can make intubation hard.

Securing Breathing

Facial trauma and swelling can make intubation hard. A nasal route is often used to leave the mouth free for the surgeon.

Backup airway equipment must be ready before induction.

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

Plan the airway before induction.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about difficult airway in jaw surgery?

Plan the airway before induction.

dental-abscess.title: Dental abscess
dental-abscess.caption: A tooth infection can spread into the face and neck spaces.
dental-abscess.body:
In short: A tooth infection can spread into the face and neck spaces.

Infection At The Root

A tooth infection can spread into the face and neck spaces. Swelling, fever and difficulty swallowing or opening the mouth are danger signs.

Drainage, antibiotics and removing the cause are needed.

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

Spreading swelling threatens the airway.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about dental abscess?

Spreading swelling threatens the airway.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

ludwig-s-angina.title: Ludwig's angina
ludwig-s-angina.caption: A rapidly spreading infection under the tongue and jaw can push the tongue up and block the airway.
ludwig-s-angina.body:
In short: A rapidly spreading infection under the tongue and jaw can push the tongue up and block the airway.

Floor Of Mouth Infection

A rapidly spreading infection under the tongue and jaw can push the tongue up and block the airway.

Signs are swelling under the chin, drooling and trouble speaking. It needs urgent specialist care.

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

Swollen floor of mouth means airway risk.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ludwig's angina?

Swollen floor of mouth means airway risk.

impacted-wisdom-teeth.title: Impacted wisdom teeth
impacted-wisdom-teeth.caption: Third molars may lack room and stay partly under the gum.
impacted-wisdom-teeth.body:
In short: Third molars may lack room and stay partly under the gum.

Stuck Teeth

Third molars may lack room and stay partly under the gum. This can cause pain, infection and decay in neighbouring teeth.

Surgical removal uses local or general anaesthesia and care to avoid nerve injury.

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

Lower lip numbness needs reporting.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about impacted wisdom teeth?

Lower lip numbness needs reporting.

dental-instruments-in-theatre.title: Dental instruments in theatre
dental-instruments-in-theatre.caption: A quick list on dental instruments in theatre: Elevators loosen teeth from the socket; Forceps grip and remove the tooth.
dental-instruments-in-theatre.body:
In short: A quick list on dental instruments in theatre: Elevators loosen teeth from the socket; Forceps grip and remove the tooth.

Dental instruments in theatre

  • Elevators loosen teeth from the socket
  • Forceps grip and remove the tooth
  • Curettes clean the socket
  • Mouth props and retractors hold the field

Why it matters

Mouth, jaw and face problems often threaten the airway and may be linked to infection, trauma or tumours. Early recognition helps patients.

Remember

Right instrument, correct count.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Dental instruments in theatre".

Elevators loosen teeth from the socket; Forceps grip and remove the tooth; Curettes clean the socket; Mouth props and retractors hold the field.

children-are-not-small-adults.title: Children are not small adults
children-are-not-small-adults.caption: Children have faster heart and breathing rates, smaller airways and less energy reserve.
children-are-not-small-adults.body:
In short: Children have faster heart and breathing rates, smaller airways and less energy reserve.

Different Physiology

Children have faster heart and breathing rates, smaller airways and less energy reserve. They lose heat quickly and may deteriorate fast.

Drug and fluid amounts are weight-based, and equipment must be the right size.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

Right size, right dose, right temperature.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about children are not small adults?

Right size, right dose, right temperature.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

preoperative-fasting-in-children.title: Preoperative fasting in children
preoperative-fasting-in-children.caption: Children need clear fasting guidance but should not fast longer than necessary.
preoperative-fasting-in-children.body:
In short: Children need clear fasting guidance but should not fast longer than necessary.

Empty But Not Starved

Children need clear fasting guidance but should not fast longer than necessary. Long fasts cause crying, low sugar and dehydration.

Follow local guidance on milk, solids and clear fluids.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

Do not fast longer than needed.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about preoperative fasting in children?

Do not fast longer than needed.

paediatric-fluid-care.title: Paediatric fluid care
paediatric-fluid-care.caption: Small errors in fluid volume matter a lot in infants.
paediatric-fluid-care.body:
In short: Small errors in fluid volume matter a lot in infants.

Careful Volumes

Small errors in fluid volume matter a lot in infants. Fluids are measured carefully and use set types for maintenance and resuscitation.

Blood glucose may need checking in small babies.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

Count every millilitre.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about paediatric fluid care?

Count every millilitre.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

paediatric-airway.title: Paediatric airway
paediatric-airway.caption: Children have larger tongues, a higher larynx and a floppy epiglottis.
paediatric-airway.body:
In short: Children have larger tongues, a higher larynx and a floppy epiglottis.

Small And Delicate

Children have larger tongues, a higher larynx and a floppy epiglottis. The narrowest point is often below the vocal cords, so swelling matters.

Use correct tube sizes and avoid pressure injuries.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

A little swelling can obstruct a child.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about paediatric airway?

A little swelling can obstruct a child.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

inguinal-hernia-in-infants.title: Inguinal hernia in infants
inguinal-hernia-in-infants.caption: Hernias in children usually result from a duct that failed to close.
inguinal-hernia-in-infants.body:
In short: Hernias in children usually result from a duct that failed to close.

Common Child Operation

Hernias in children usually result from a duct that failed to close. A groin bulge that appears with crying is typical.

A hard, painful, non-reducible lump may be strangulated and needs urgent surgery.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

Painful irreducible lump: emergency.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about inguinal hernia in infants?

Painful irreducible lump: emergency.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

undescended-testis.title: Undescended testis
undescended-testis.caption: If a testis has not come down to the scrotum, surgery is usually done in infancy to bring it down.
undescended-testis.body:
In short: If a testis has not come down to the scrotum, surgery is usually done in infancy to bring it down.

Orchidopexy

If a testis has not come down to the scrotum, surgery is usually done in infancy to bring it down. A testis left too long risks reduced fertility and later problems.

Diagnosis follows careful examination.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

Check and refer early.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about undescended testis?

Check and refer early.

intussusception.title: Intussusception
intussusception.caption: One part of bowel slides into another.
intussusception.body:
In short: One part of bowel slides into another.

Telescoping Bowel

One part of bowel slides into another. A baby may draw up their legs, cry in waves, vomit and pass blood-stained mucus.

It needs prompt treatment, either by air or fluid enema or by surgery.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

Colicky cries and blood: suspect it.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about intussusception?

Colicky cries and blood: suspect it.

gastroschisis-and-exomphalos.title: Gastroschisis and exomphalos
gastroschisis-and-exomphalos.caption: Both are birth defects where bowel and organs lie outside the abdomen.
gastroschisis-and-exomphalos.body:
In short: Both are birth defects where bowel and organs lie outside the abdomen.

Abdominal Wall Defects

Both are birth defects where bowel and organs lie outside the abdomen. In exomphalos they are covered by a sac, in gastroschisis they are not.

Cover with warm, clean, moist material and keep the baby warm.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

Cover, warm and refer.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about gastroschisis and exomphalos?

Cover, warm and refer.
