oesophageal-atresia.title: Oesophageal atresia
oesophageal-atresia.caption: The oesophagus ends blindly in some newborns.
oesophageal-atresia.body:
In short: The oesophagus ends blindly in some newborns.

Blocked Food Pipe

The oesophagus ends blindly in some newborns. Signs include drooling, choking and coughing with first feeds.

Do not feed. Keep upright, suction the mouth and arrange urgent surgery.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

Excess drooling in a newborn: stop feeds.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about oesophageal atresia?

Excess drooling in a newborn: stop feeds.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

hirschsprung-disease.title: Hirschsprung disease
hirschsprung-disease.caption: Some newborns lack nerve cells in part of the bowel.
hirschsprung-disease.body:
In short: Some newborns lack nerve cells in part of the bowel.

No Nerve Cells

Some newborns lack nerve cells in part of the bowel. They fail to pass meconium within the first couple of days and have a swollen abdomen.

Treatment is surgical removal of the affected bowel.

Why it matters

Children differ from adults in size, physiology and fears. Warmth, accurate dosing and recognising congenital conditions are essential.

Remember

Late first stool needs investigation.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about hirschsprung disease?

Late first stool needs investigation.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

arteries-versus-veins.title: Arteries versus veins
arteries-versus-veins.caption: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under higher pressure and have thick, muscular walls.
arteries-versus-veins.body:
In short: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under higher pressure and have thick, muscular walls.

Basic Differences

Arteries carry blood away from the heart under higher pressure and have thick, muscular walls. Veins return blood and have thinner walls and valves.

Arterial bleeding is often bright and pulsatile.

Why it matters

Blood vessel emergencies threaten limb and life. Quick recognition of ischaemia, bleeding and clots makes a big difference.

Remember

Pulsatile bright bleeding means artery.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about arteries versus veins?

Pulsatile bright bleeding means artery.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

the-six-ps-of-acute-limb-ischaemia.title: The six Ps of acute limb ischaemia
the-six-ps-of-acute-limb-ischaemia.caption: A quick list on the six ps of acute limb ischaemia: Pain, pallor, pulselessness; Paraesthesia, paralysis.
the-six-ps-of-acute-limb-ischaemia.body:
In short: A quick list on the six ps of acute limb ischaemia: Pain, pallor, pulselessness; Paraesthesia, paralysis.

The six Ps of acute limb ischaemia

  • Pain, pallor, pulselessness
  • Paraesthesia, paralysis
  • Perishing cold
  • Any of these needs urgent assessment

Why it matters

Blood vessel emergencies threaten limb and life. Quick recognition of ischaemia, bleeding and clots makes a big difference.

Remember

Time is limb: act quickly.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "The six Ps of acute limb ischaemia".

Pain, pallor, pulselessness; Paraesthesia, paralysis; Perishing cold; Any of these needs urgent assessment.

embolectomy.title: Embolectomy
embolectomy.caption: A balloon catheter can be passed beyond a clot in an artery, inflated, and pulled back to remove the clot.
embolectomy.body:
In short: A balloon catheter can be passed beyond a clot in an artery, inflated, and pulled back to remove the clot.

Clot Removal

A balloon catheter can be passed beyond a clot in an artery, inflated, and pulled back to remove the clot.

It restores flow in acute limb ischaemia. Heparin is usually given to prevent more clot.

Why it matters

Blood vessel emergencies threaten limb and life. Quick recognition of ischaemia, bleeding and clots makes a big difference.

Remember

Quick restoration of blood flow saves limbs.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about embolectomy?

Quick restoration of blood flow saves limbs.

abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.caption: An aneurysm is a widened section of the aorta.
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.body:
In short: An aneurysm is a widened section of the aorta.

Ballooned Aorta

An aneurysm is a widened section of the aorta. Many cause no symptoms until they leak or rupture.

Sudden severe abdominal or back pain with collapse is an emergency. Large ones are repaired electively.

Why it matters

Blood vessel emergencies threaten limb and life. Quick recognition of ischaemia, bleeding and clots makes a big difference.

Remember

Collapse with back pain: think rupture.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about abdominal aortic aneurysm?

Collapse with back pain: think rupture.

permissive-hypotension.title: Permissive hypotension
permissive-hypotension.caption: In a bleeding patient, pushing blood pressure too high may dislodge clots and increase bleeding.
permissive-hypotension.body:
In short: In a bleeding patient, pushing blood pressure too high may dislodge clots and increase bleeding.

Careful Resuscitation

In a bleeding patient, pushing blood pressure too high may dislodge clots and increase bleeding.

Teams often aim for a lower-than-normal pressure until bleeding is controlled. Protocols differ.

Why it matters

Blood vessel emergencies threaten limb and life. Quick recognition of ischaemia, bleeding and clots makes a big difference.

Remember

Resuscitate to a target, not a number.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about permissive hypotension?

Resuscitate to a target, not a number.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

varicose-veins.title: Varicose veins
varicose-veins.caption: Varicose veins form when valves fail and blood pools in superficial leg veins.
varicose-veins.body:
In short: Varicose veins form when valves fail and blood pools in superficial leg veins.

Faulty Valves

Varicose veins form when valves fail and blood pools in superficial leg veins. They can cause aching, swelling and skin changes.

recognising-a-blocked-airway.caption: A quick list on recognising a blocked airway: Snoring means a partial blockage; Gurgling means fluid in the airway.
recognising-a-blocked-airway.body:
In short: A quick list on recognising a blocked airway: Snoring means a partial blockage; Gurgling means fluid in the airway.

Recognising a blocked airway

  • Snoring means a partial blockage
  • Gurgling means fluid in the airway
  • Stridor means narrowing at or below the larynx
  • See-saw chest and abdomen movement
  • Silence with effort can mean complete blockage

Why it matters

A clear airway is the first priority of any anaesthetic. Theatre staff must know the basic manoeuvres, devices and checks to assist safely.

Remember

Noisy breathing is obstructed breathing.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Recognising a blocked airway".

Snoring means a partial blockage; Gurgling means fluid in the airway; Stridor means narrowing at or below the larynx; See-saw chest and abdomen movement; Silence with effort can mean complete blockage.

pulse-oximetry-limits.title: Pulse oximetry limits
pulse-oximetry-limits.caption: Pulse oximetry shows oxygen saturation of haemoglobin, not ventilation.
pulse-oximetry-limits.body:
In short: Pulse oximetry shows oxygen saturation of haemoglobin, not ventilation.

What Spo2 Tells You

Pulse oximetry shows oxygen saturation of haemoglobin, not ventilation. A patient may keep a normal reading for a time while carbon dioxide rises.

Cold hands, poor perfusion, nail polish, movement and carbon monoxide can give false readings.

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

A good SpO2 does not mean good breathing.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about pulse oximetry limits?

A good SpO2 does not mean good breathing.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

capnograph-waveform-shapes.title: Capnograph waveform shapes
capnograph-waveform-shapes.caption: The capnograph shows carbon dioxide in each breath.
capnograph-waveform-shapes.body:
In short: The capnograph shows carbon dioxide in each breath.

End-Tidal Co2

The capnograph shows carbon dioxide in each breath. A normal trace has a flat baseline, a sharp rise and a plateau.

A sudden fall to zero suggests disconnection, blocked or dislodged tube, or circulatory arrest. A slow rise may suggest hypoventilation.

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

Look at the shape, not just the number.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about capnograph waveform shapes?

Look at the shape, not just the number.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

ecg-leads-in-theatre.title: ECG leads in theatre
ecg-leads-in-theatre.caption: Theatre ECG shows heart rate and rhythm.
ecg-leads-in-theatre.body:
In short: Theatre ECG shows heart rate and rhythm.

Heart Rhythm

Theatre ECG shows heart rate and rhythm. Lead II is often used because the P wave is clear and it helps detect rhythm problems. A V5 lead can help show ischaemia.

Diathermy and movement can cause artefact, so always confirm with the pulse.

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

Check the patient, not just the screen.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ecg leads in theatre?

Check the patient, not just the screen.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cuff-size-and-blood-pressure.title: Cuff size and blood pressure
cuff-size-and-blood-pressure.caption: The blood pressure cuff bladder should cover about two thirds of the upper arm length and wrap around most of its circumference.
cuff-size-and-blood-pressure.body:
In short: The blood pressure cuff bladder should cover about two thirds of the upper arm length and wrap around most of its circumference.

Get The Cuff Right

The blood pressure cuff bladder should cover about two thirds of the upper arm length and wrap around most of its circumference.

A cuff too small reads falsely high. A cuff too large reads falsely low. Avoid an arm with a drip or fistula.

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

Wrong cuff, wrong pressure.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cuff size and blood pressure?

Wrong cuff, wrong pressure.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

why-measure-temperature.title: Why measure temperature
why-measure-temperature.caption: Anaesthesia impairs temperature control, so patients often become cold.
why-measure-temperature.body:
In short: Anaesthesia impairs temperature control, so patients often become cold.

Thermal Monitoring

Anaesthesia impairs temperature control, so patients often become cold. Rarely, they become dangerously hot, as in malignant hyperthermia.

Measure temperature in cases over a short time, using oesophageal, nasopharyngeal, tympanic or skin probes as available.

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

Anaesthesia switches off the thermostat.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about why measure temperature?

Anaesthesia switches off the thermostat.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

urine-output-as-a-monitor.title: Urine output as a monitor
urine-output-as-a-monitor.caption: Urine output reflects blood flow to the kidneys and gives a clue to fluid status.
urine-output-as-a-monitor.body:
In short: Urine output reflects blood flow to the kidneys and gives a clue to fluid status.

Kidney As A Gauge

Urine output reflects blood flow to the kidneys and gives a clue to fluid status. A catheter and hourly measurement help in major or long surgery.

Low output may mean too little fluid, low pressure or kidney injury. Interpret it with the whole picture.

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

Urine output is a window on perfusion.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about urine output as a monitor?

Urine output is a window on perfusion.

minimum-monitoring-standard.title: Minimum monitoring standard
minimum-monitoring-standard.caption: A quick list on minimum monitoring standard: Oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry; Blood pressure at regular intervals.
minimum-monitoring-standard.body:
In short: A quick list on minimum monitoring standard: Oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry; Blood pressure at regular intervals.

Minimum monitoring standard

  • Oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry
  • Blood pressure at regular intervals
  • ECG for heart rate and rhythm
  • Capnography when the airway is secured
  • Anaesthetic agent and inspired oxygen

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

Monitor from induction to recovery.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Minimum monitoring standard".

Oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry; Blood pressure at regular intervals; ECG for heart rate and rhythm; Capnography when the airway is secured; Anaesthetic agent and inspired oxygen.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

depth-of-anaesthesia-monitors.title: Depth of anaesthesia monitors
depth-of-anaesthesia-monitors.caption: Processed EEG monitors such as BIS give a number linked to how deeply the brain is anaesthetised.
depth-of-anaesthesia-monitors.body:
In short: Processed EEG monitors such as BIS give a number linked to how deeply the brain is anaesthetised.

Bis And Similar

Processed EEG monitors such as BIS give a number linked to how deeply the brain is anaesthetised. They can help reduce awareness, especially with total intravenous anaesthesia and muscle relaxants.

They guide clinical judgement but do not replace it.

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

A monitor guides; the clinician decides.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about depth of anaesthesia monitors?

A monitor guides; the clinician decides.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

neuromuscular-monitoring.title: Neuromuscular monitoring
neuromuscular-monitoring.caption: A nerve stimulator on a peripheral nerve checks how much a muscle relaxant is working.
neuromuscular-monitoring.body:
In short: A nerve stimulator on a peripheral nerve checks how much a muscle relaxant is working.

Train Of Four

A nerve stimulator on a peripheral nerve checks how much a muscle relaxant is working. Four twitches are delivered and the fade between them is assessed.

The train-of-four ratio helps judge when it is safe to reverse the block and extubate.

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

Count twitches before you reverse.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about neuromuscular monitoring?

Count twitches before you reverse.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

alarms-set-and-respect.title: Alarms: set and respect
alarms-set-and-respect.caption: A quick list on alarms: set and respect: Set limits suitable for this patient; Never switch alarms off for convenience.
alarms-set-and-respect.body:
In short: A quick list on alarms: set and respect: Set limits suitable for this patient; Never switch alarms off for convenience.

Alarms: set and respect

  • Set limits suitable for this patient
  • Never switch alarms off for convenience
  • Check the patient first, then the machine
  • Respond to artefact too, do not ignore it
  • Handover includes alarm settings

Why it matters

Monitors give early warning of problems that the eye alone may miss. Knowing what each monitor shows, and its limits, supports safe care.

Remember

An alarm ignored is a warning wasted.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Alarms: set and respect".

Set limits suitable for this patient; Never switch alarms off for convenience; Check the patient first, then the machine; Respond to artefact too, do not ignore it; Handover includes alarm settings.

spontaneous-vs-controlled.title: Spontaneous vs controlled
spontaneous-vs-controlled.caption: In spontaneous ventilation the patient draws air by negative chest pressure.
spontaneous-vs-controlled.body:
In short: In spontaneous ventilation the patient draws air by negative chest pressure.

Two Ways To Breathe

In spontaneous ventilation the patient draws air by negative chest pressure. In controlled ventilation the machine or bag pushes air in with positive pressure.

Positive pressure can lower venous return and blood pressure, particularly in dehydrated or bleeding patients.

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

Positive pressure can lower blood pressure.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about spontaneous vs controlled?

Positive pressure can lower blood pressure.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tidal-volume-and-rate.title: Tidal volume and rate
tidal-volume-and-rate.caption: Tidal volume is usually set by ideal body weight, not actual weight.
tidal-volume-and-rate.body:
In short: Tidal volume is usually set by ideal body weight, not actual weight.

Setting The Ventilator

Tidal volume is usually set by ideal body weight, not actual weight. Rate is adjusted to keep end-tidal carbon dioxide in a normal range.

Lung-protective ventilation uses smaller breaths to reduce lung injury. Follow local guidance and the anaesthetist's plan.

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

Use ideal body weight for tidal volume.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tidal volume and rate?

Use ideal body weight for tidal volume.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

peep-explained.title: PEEP explained
peep-explained.caption: PEEP keeps some pressure in the airways at the end of each breath.
peep-explained.body:
In short: PEEP keeps some pressure in the airways at the end of each breath.

Positive End-Expiratory

PEEP keeps some pressure in the airways at the end of each breath. It stops small airways and alveoli from collapsing and often improves oxygenation.

High PEEP can reduce venous return and blood pressure, and may over-distend healthy lung.

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

PEEP props the lung open.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about peep explained?

PEEP props the lung open.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

bag-mask-ventilation-technique.title: Bag-mask ventilation technique
bag-mask-ventilation-technique.caption: Use a C-grip on the mask with thumb and index finger, and lift the jaw with the remaining fingers.
bag-mask-ventilation-technique.body:
In short: Use a C-grip on the mask with thumb and index finger, and lift the jaw with the remaining fingers.

Mask Seal

Use a C-grip on the mask with thumb and index finger, and lift the jaw with the remaining fingers. A good seal matters more than squeezing hard.

Two-person technique often helps in bearded, edentulous or obese patients. Squeeze gently to avoid inflating the stomach.

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

Seal first, squeeze second.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about bag-mask ventilation technique?

Seal first, squeeze second.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

reading-airway-pressures.title: Reading airway pressures
reading-airway-pressures.caption: A rising peak airway pressure suggests a problem such as a kinked tube, bronchospasm, secretions, a tube in one lung, or the patient coughing or straining.
reading-airway-pressures.body:
In short: A rising peak airway pressure suggests a problem such as a kinked tube, bronchospasm, secretions, a tube in one lung, or the patient coughing or straining.

Peak Pressure

A rising peak airway pressure suggests a problem such as a kinked tube, bronchospasm, secretions, a tube in one lung, or the patient coughing or straining.

A sudden fall may mean a leak or disconnection. Always check the patient and circuit.

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

High pressure means find the cause.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about reading airway pressures?

High pressure means find the cause.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

causes-of-hypoxia-under-ga.title: Causes of hypoxia under GA
causes-of-hypoxia-under-ga.caption: A quick list on causes of hypoxia under ga: Equipment: no oxygen, disconnection, blocked tube; Airway: obstruction, laryngospasm, oesophageal tube.
causes-of-hypoxia-under-ga.body:
In short: A quick list on causes of hypoxia under ga: Equipment: no oxygen, disconnection, blocked tube; Airway: obstruction, laryngospasm, oesophageal tube.

Causes of hypoxia under GA

  • Equipment: no oxygen, disconnection, blocked tube
  • Airway: obstruction, laryngospasm, oesophageal tube
  • Breathing: bronchospasm, pneumothorax, aspiration
  • Circulation: low cardiac output
  • Patient: shunt, anaemia, pre-existing disease

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

Disconnect, then use a bag and 100% oxygen.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Causes of hypoxia under GA".

Equipment: no oxygen, disconnection, blocked tube; Airway: obstruction, laryngospasm, oesophageal tube; Breathing: bronchospasm, pneumothorax, aspiration; Circulation: low cardiac output; Patient: shunt, anaemia, pre-existing disease.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

atelectasis-after-anaesthesia.title: Atelectasis after anaesthesia
atelectasis-after-anaesthesia.caption: Atelectasis is collapse of small areas of lung.
atelectasis-after-anaesthesia.body:
In short: Atelectasis is collapse of small areas of lung.

Collapsed Lung

Atelectasis is collapse of small areas of lung. It is common after general anaesthesia, and is made worse by very high oxygen concentrations, obesity and abdominal surgery.

PEEP, recruitment breaths, sitting up and early deep breathing can help.

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

Sit up and breathe deeply after surgery.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about atelectasis after anaesthesia?

Sit up and breathe deeply after surgery.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

one-lung-ventilation-basics.title: One-lung ventilation basics
one-lung-ventilation-basics.caption: In some chest operations one lung is deflated so the surgeon can work.
one-lung-ventilation-basics.body:
In short: In some chest operations one lung is deflated so the surgeon can work.

Thoracic Surgery

In some chest operations one lung is deflated so the surgeon can work. A double-lumen tube or a bronchial blocker is used.

The ventilated lung receives all the breaths, so oxygenation needs close watching. Tube position is checked and rechecked after turning the patient.

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

Check tube position after every move.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about one-lung ventilation basics?

Check tube position after every move.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

weaning-from-the-ventilator.title: Weaning from the ventilator
weaning-from-the-ventilator.caption: A quick list on weaning from the ventilator: Patient warm and reasonably pain controlled; Muscle relaxant worn off or reversed.
weaning-from-the-ventilator.body:
In short: A quick list on weaning from the ventilator: Patient warm and reasonably pain controlled; Muscle relaxant worn off or reversed.

Weaning from the ventilator

  • Patient warm and reasonably pain controlled
  • Muscle relaxant worn off or reversed
  • Spontaneous breaths with good volume
  • Oxygen and carbon dioxide levels acceptable
  • Awake, cooperative and protecting the airway

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

Breathe on their own before you extubate.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Weaning from the ventilator".

Patient warm and reasonably pain controlled; Muscle relaxant worn off or reversed; Spontaneous breaths with good volume; Oxygen and carbon dioxide levels acceptable; Awake, cooperative and protecting the airway.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

hypo-and-hyperventilation.title: Hypo- and hyperventilation
hypo-and-hyperventilation.caption: Hypoventilation raises carbon dioxide, causing drowsiness, a fast pulse and, when severe, acidosis.
hypo-and-hyperventilation.body:
In short: Hypoventilation raises carbon dioxide, causing drowsiness, a fast pulse and, when severe, acidosis.

Carbon Dioxide Clues

Hypoventilation raises carbon dioxide, causing drowsiness, a fast pulse and, when severe, acidosis. Hyperventilation lowers it and can reduce blood flow to the brain.

The capnograph helps adjust ventilation. Other causes of changes include fever, pain and rebreathing.

Why it matters

Anaesthesia often reduces or removes the patient's own breathing. Understanding ventilation helps theatre staff support oxygenation and spot trouble.

Remember

CO2 is controlled by ventilation.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about hypo- and hyperventilation?

CO2 is controlled by ventilation.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

nausea-and-vomiting-risks.title: Nausea and vomiting risks
nausea-and-vomiting-risks.caption: Post-operative nausea and vomiting is more likely in women, non-smokers, those with a past history or motion sickness, and after long surgery or opioids.
nausea-and-vomiting-risks.body:
In short: Post-operative nausea and vomiting is more likely in women, non-smokers, those with a past history or motion sickness, and after long surgery or opioids.

Ponv

Post-operative nausea and vomiting is more likely in women, non-smokers, those with a past history or motion sickness, and after long surgery or opioids.

Prevention may use anti-emetic drugs, good hydration and avoiding triggers. Follow the anaesthetist's plan.

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Spot risk factors before surgery.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about nausea and vomiting risks?

Spot risk factors before surgery.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

laryngospasm.title: Laryngospasm
laryngospasm.caption: Laryngospasm is a forceful closure of the vocal cords, often at light anaesthesia from secretions, blood or stimulation.
laryngospasm.body:
In short: Laryngospasm is a forceful closure of the vocal cords, often at light anaesthesia from secretions, blood or stimulation.

Vocal Cords Close

Laryngospasm is a forceful closure of the vocal cords, often at light anaesthesia from secretions, blood or stimulation. There is stridor or silence and no air movement.

Give 100% oxygen, apply gentle pressure with a jaw thrust, and call for help. Drugs may be needed if it does not resolve.

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Oxygen, jaw thrust, call for help.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about laryngospasm?

Oxygen, jaw thrust, call for help.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

bronchospasm.title: Bronchospasm
bronchospasm.caption: Bronchospasm is narrowing of the small airways.
bronchospasm.body:
In short: Bronchospasm is narrowing of the small airways.

Wheeze After Induction

Bronchospasm is narrowing of the small airways. Signs include wheeze, rising airway pressure, a slanted capnograph and falling oxygen.

Causes include asthma, light anaesthesia, aspiration and allergy. Increase oxygen, deepen anaesthesia and treat per protocol.

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Check tube first, then treat the spasm.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about bronchospasm?

Check tube first, then treat the spasm.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

aspiration-of-stomach-contents.title: Aspiration of stomach contents
aspiration-of-stomach-contents.caption: Aspiration happens when stomach contents enter the lungs, usually when airway reflexes are lost.
aspiration-of-stomach-contents.body:
In short: Aspiration happens when stomach contents enter the lungs, usually when airway reflexes are lost.

A Feared Complication

Aspiration happens when stomach contents enter the lungs, usually when airway reflexes are lost. It can cause pneumonitis and serious breathing problems.

Risks include a full stomach, pregnancy, obesity, reflux and emergency surgery. Fasting and rapid sequence induction reduce risk.

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Fasting and RSI protect the lungs.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about aspiration of stomach contents?

Fasting and RSI protect the lungs.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

anaphylaxis-in-theatre.title: Anaphylaxis in theatre
anaphylaxis-in-theatre.caption: A quick list on anaphylaxis in theatre: Sudden fall in blood pressure or collapse; Bronchospasm, rash or swelling of the face.
anaphylaxis-in-theatre.body:
In short: A quick list on anaphylaxis in theatre: Sudden fall in blood pressure or collapse; Bronchospasm, rash or swelling of the face.

Anaphylaxis in theatre

  • Sudden fall in blood pressure or collapse
  • Bronchospasm, rash or swelling of the face
  • Likely triggers: relaxants, antibiotics, latex
  • Stop the trigger, call for help, give oxygen
  • Adrenaline is the key drug, per local protocol

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Think anaphylaxis with unexplained collapse.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Anaphylaxis in theatre".

Sudden fall in blood pressure or collapse; Bronchospasm, rash or swelling of the face; Likely triggers: relaxants, antibiotics, latex; Stop the trigger, call for help, give oxygen; Adrenaline is the key drug, per local protocol.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

accidental-awareness-prevention.title: Accidental awareness: prevention
accidental-awareness-prevention.caption: Awareness means the patient recalls events during surgery.
accidental-awareness-prevention.body:
In short: Awareness means the patient recalls events during surgery.

Aware But Paralysed

Awareness means the patient recalls events during surgery. It is rare but distressing, and is more likely with muscle relaxants and light anaesthesia.

Check vaporiser levels and IV lines, watch for fast pulse, sweating and tears, and use depth monitors if available.

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Paralysed does not mean unaware.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about accidental awareness: prevention?

Paralysed does not mean unaware.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

post-operative-sore-throat.title: Post-operative sore throat
post-operative-sore-throat.caption: Sore throat is common after intubation or a laryngeal mask.
post-operative-sore-throat.body:
In short: Sore throat is common after intubation or a laryngeal mask.

Common And Minor

Sore throat is common after intubation or a laryngeal mask. Causes include airway irritation, high cuff pressure, dry gases and rough handling.

Using the smallest suitable tube, lubrication, gentle technique and cuff pressure checks may reduce it. Usually it settles in a few days.

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Gentle hands, fewer sore throats.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about post-operative sore throat?

Gentle hands, fewer sore throats.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

dental-and-eye-injuries.title: Dental and eye injuries
dental-and-eye-injuries.caption: Teeth can be damaged by laryngoscopy, especially if loose or capped.
dental-and-eye-injuries.body:
In short: Teeth can be damaged by laryngoscopy, especially if loose or capped.

Preventable Harm

Teeth can be damaged by laryngoscopy, especially if loose or capped. Check and document dental state before induction.

Corneal abrasion is also common in anaesthetised patients. Tape the eyes closed, avoid pressure from masks and drapes, and protect them during positioning.

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Check the teeth, tape the eyes.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about dental and eye injuries?

Check the teeth, tape the eyes.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

peripheral-nerve-injury.title: Peripheral nerve injury
peripheral-nerve-injury.caption: Nerves can be stretched or compressed when patients are anaesthetised.
peripheral-nerve-injury.body:
In short: Nerves can be stretched or compressed when patients are anaesthetised.

Positioning Matters

Nerves can be stretched or compressed when patients are anaesthetised. Common sites include the ulnar nerve at the elbow, the brachial plexus, and the peroneal nerve at the knee.

Pad, avoid overextending arms past about 90 degrees, and recheck positions during long cases.

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Pad and position every pressure point.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about peripheral nerve injury?

Pad and position every pressure point.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

hypotension-under-anaesthesia.title: Hypotension under anaesthesia
hypotension-under-anaesthesia.caption: A quick list on hypotension under anaesthesia: Common causes: anaesthetic drugs, low volume; Bleeding, regional block, or sepsis.
hypotension-under-anaesthesia.body:
In short: A quick list on hypotension under anaesthesia: Common causes: anaesthetic drugs, low volume; Bleeding, regional block, or sepsis.

Hypotension under anaesthesia

  • Common causes: anaesthetic drugs, low volume
  • Bleeding, regional block, or sepsis
  • Check the cuff, trace and the patient first
  • Treat the cause: fluids, vasopressors, stop bleeding
  • Ask about drugs given and surgical stage

Why it matters

Complications can arise even with careful care. Early recognition and a calm, practised response reduce harm.

Remember

Treat the cause, not only the number.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Hypotension under anaesthesia".

Common causes: anaesthetic drugs, low volume; Bleeding, regional block, or sepsis; Check the cuff, trace and the patient first; Treat the cause: fluids, vasopressors, stop bleeding; Ask about drugs given and surgical stage.

physiology-of-pregnancy.title: Physiology of pregnancy
physiology-of-pregnancy.caption: In pregnancy the airway is swollen, oxygen consumption rises, and the lungs have less reserve.
physiology-of-pregnancy.body:
In short: In pregnancy the airway is swollen, oxygen consumption rises, and the lungs have less reserve.

Why It Changes Things

In pregnancy the airway is swollen, oxygen consumption rises, and the lungs have less reserve. Stomach emptying is affected and the sphincter at the stomach is more lax.

The growing uterus can also press on the great veins when the woman lies flat.

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Pregnant women desaturate fast.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about physiology of pregnancy?

Pregnant women desaturate fast.

tilting-the-pregnant-woman.title: Tilting the pregnant woman
tilting-the-pregnant-woman.caption: Lying flat late in pregnancy, the uterus can press on the vena cava and reduce blood return to the heart.
tilting-the-pregnant-woman.body:
In short: Lying flat late in pregnancy, the uterus can press on the vena cava and reduce blood return to the heart.

Aortocaval Compression

Lying flat late in pregnancy, the uterus can press on the vena cava and reduce blood return to the heart. This can cause low blood pressure and affect the baby.

Tilt the operating table to the left, or place a wedge under the right hip, from mid pregnancy.

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Never leave a pregnant woman flat.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tilting the pregnant woman?

Never leave a pregnant woman flat.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

spinal-for-caesarean.title: Spinal for caesarean
spinal-for-caesarean.caption: Spinal anaesthesia is often preferred for caesarean section.
spinal-for-caesarean.body:
In short: Spinal anaesthesia is often preferred for caesarean section.

Common Choice

Spinal anaesthesia is often preferred for caesarean section. The mother stays awake, the airway is not instrumented, and the baby gets little drug exposure.

The main early risk is low blood pressure, so fluids or vasopressors are prepared. Check for contraindications first.

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Awake mother, safer airway.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about spinal for caesarean?

Awake mother, safer airway.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

difficult-airway-in-pregnancy.title: Difficult airway in pregnancy
difficult-airway-in-pregnancy.caption: Airway swelling, large breasts and weight gain can make intubation harder in pregnancy.
difficult-airway-in-pregnancy.body:
In short: Airway swelling, large breasts and weight gain can make intubation harder in pregnancy.

Extra Caution

Airway swelling, large breasts and weight gain can make intubation harder in pregnancy. Failed intubation is a known cause of maternal harm.

Have smaller tubes, a bougie, a laryngeal mask and a failed intubation plan ready before every general anaesthetic.

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Always have a failed intubation plan.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about difficult airway in pregnancy?

Always have a failed intubation plan.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

aspiration-prophylaxis.title: Aspiration prophylaxis
aspiration-prophylaxis.caption: Pregnant women are treated as having a full stomach from mid pregnancy onward, especially in labour.
aspiration-prophylaxis.body:
In short: Pregnant women are treated as having a full stomach from mid pregnancy onward, especially in labour.

Protect The Stomach

Pregnant women are treated as having a full stomach from mid pregnancy onward, especially in labour. Acid-reducing drugs are often given before caesarean section.

If general anaesthesia is needed, a rapid sequence induction with cricoid pressure per local practice is the norm.

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Treat every labouring woman as full stomach.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about aspiration prophylaxis?

Treat every labouring woman as full stomach.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

labour-epidural-basics.title: Labour epidural basics
labour-epidural-basics.caption: An epidural places a thin catheter near the spinal nerves so local anaesthetic can be given gradually.
labour-epidural-basics.body:
In short: An epidural places a thin catheter near the spinal nerves so local anaesthetic can be given gradually.

Pain Relief In Labour

An epidural places a thin catheter near the spinal nerves so local anaesthetic can be given gradually. It provides good pain relief for many labouring women.

The mother's blood pressure, pain level and leg movement are monitored. Usual contraindications include infection at the site and clotting problems.

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Catheter in, pain down, watch the pressure.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about labour epidural basics?

Catheter in, pain down, watch the pressure.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

post-partum-haemorrhage.title: Post-partum haemorrhage
post-partum-haemorrhage.caption: A quick list on post-partum haemorrhage: Think the four Ts: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin; Call for help early and start two large drips.
post-partum-haemorrhage.body:
In short: A quick list on post-partum haemorrhage: Think the four Ts: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin; Call for help early and start two large drips.

Post-partum haemorrhage

  • Think the four Ts: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin
  • Call for help early and start two large drips
  • Uterine massage and uterotonic drugs
  • Send bloods, give fluids and blood products
  • Monitor closely and keep the woman warm

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Bleeding mothers need teamwork fast.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Post-partum haemorrhage".

Think the four Ts: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin; Call for help early and start two large drips; Uterine massage and uterotonic drugs; Send bloods, give fluids and blood products; Monitor closely and keep the woman warm.

pre-eclampsia-and-theatre.title: Pre-eclampsia and theatre
pre-eclampsia-and-theatre.caption: Pre-eclampsia involves raised blood pressure, protein in the urine and possible organ involvement.
pre-eclampsia-and-theatre.body:
In short: Pre-eclampsia involves raised blood pressure, protein in the urine and possible organ involvement.

High Pressure In Pregnancy

Pre-eclampsia involves raised blood pressure, protein in the urine and possible organ involvement. The risk is seizures and bleeding in the brain.

Magnesium is commonly used to prevent seizures. Blood pressure control and a plan for the airway and clotting tests are key.

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Control pressure, protect the brain.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about pre-eclampsia and theatre?

Control pressure, protect the brain.

keeping-the-newborn-in-mind.title: Keeping the newborn in mind
keeping-the-newborn-in-mind.caption: Drugs given to the mother can cross the placenta and affect the baby.
keeping-the-newborn-in-mind.body:
In short: Drugs given to the mother can cross the placenta and affect the baby.

Two Patients

Drugs given to the mother can cross the placenta and affect the baby. Opioids and sedatives may slow the newborn's breathing.

Have a warm area, suction, oxygen and a neonatal resuscitation trained person ready at every caesarean delivery.

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Prepare for the baby as well as the mother.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about keeping the newborn in mind?

Prepare for the baby as well as the mother.

oxytocin-and-the-anaesthetist.title: Oxytocin and the anaesthetist
oxytocin-and-the-anaesthetist.caption: After delivery, oxytocin helps the uterus contract and reduces bleeding.
oxytocin-and-the-anaesthetist.body:
In short: After delivery, oxytocin helps the uterus contract and reduces bleeding.

Uterotonic Drugs

After delivery, oxytocin helps the uterus contract and reduces bleeding. Given too fast as a bolus it can cause low blood pressure and a fast heart rate.

It is usually given slowly. Other uterotonics may be added if bleeding continues, according to local protocol.

Why it matters

Pregnancy changes the body and adds a second patient. Caesarean section and labour care carry particular airway and bleeding risks.

Remember

Give oxytocin slowly.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about oxytocin and the anaesthetist?

Give oxytocin slowly.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

the-anaesthetic-history.title: The anaesthetic history
the-anaesthetic-history.caption: A quick list on the anaesthetic history: Past anaesthetics and any problems; Family history of anaesthetic reactions.
the-anaesthetic-history.body:
In short: A quick list on the anaesthetic history: Past anaesthetics and any problems; Family history of anaesthetic reactions.

The anaesthetic history

  • Past anaesthetics and any problems
  • Family history of anaesthetic reactions
  • Current medicines and allergies
  • Smoking, alcohol and drug use
  • Chest, heart, kidney or other conditions

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

History finds most hidden risks.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "The anaesthetic history".

Past anaesthetics and any problems; Family history of anaesthetic reactions; Current medicines and allergies; Smoking, alcohol and drug use; Chest, heart, kidney or other conditions.

asa-grade-explained.title: ASA grade explained
asa-grade-explained.caption: The ASA score groups patients from healthy (class 1) to brain dead (class 6).
asa-grade-explained.body:
In short: The ASA score groups patients from healthy (class 1) to brain dead (class 6).

Risk Classification

The ASA score groups patients from healthy (class 1) to brain dead (class 6). Higher numbers mean more systemic disease and more risk.

An E is added for emergency surgery. It is a quick communication tool, not an exact risk calculator.

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

ASA grades fitness, not the operation.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about asa grade explained?

ASA grades fitness, not the operation.

mallampati-classification.title: Mallampati classification
mallampati-classification.caption: The patient sits, opens wide and sticks out the tongue without saying a sound.
mallampati-classification.body:
In short: The patient sits, opens wide and sticks out the tongue without saying a sound.

Looking Into The Mouth

The patient sits, opens wide and sticks out the tongue without saying a sound. The visible structures are graded I to IV. Class I shows more of the throat, class IV shows only the hard palate.

It predicts difficulty only when combined with other tests.

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

One test never predicts airway difficulty.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about mallampati classification?

One test never predicts airway difficulty.

other-airway-tests.title: Other airway tests
other-airway-tests.caption: A quick list on other airway tests: Mouth opening: can three fingers fit?; Thyromental distance: space under the chin.
other-airway-tests.body:
In short: A quick list on other airway tests: Mouth opening: can three fingers fit?; Thyromental distance: space under the chin.

Other airway tests

  • Mouth opening: can three fingers fit?
  • Thyromental distance: space under the chin
  • Neck movement: flexion and extension
  • Jaw protrusion: can lower teeth pass upper?
  • Beard, teeth, short neck and obesity

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

Combine tests before judging the airway.

Mouth opening: can three fingers fit?; Thyromental distance: space under the chin; Neck movement: flexion and extension; Jaw protrusion: can lower teeth pass upper?; Beard, teeth, short neck and obesity.

fasting-guidelines.title: Fasting guidelines
fasting-guidelines.caption: Fasting reduces the risk of aspiration.
fasting-guidelines.body:
In short: Fasting reduces the risk of aspiration.

Nil By Mouth

Fasting reduces the risk of aspiration. Common guidance allows clear fluids up to about two hours before surgery, and a light meal up to about six hours. Fatty meals may need longer.

Follow local protocol. Emergency and pregnant patients are treated as full stomach.

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

Check fasting at every handover.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about fasting guidelines?

Check fasting at every handover.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

functional-capacity.title: Functional capacity
functional-capacity.caption: Asking about daily activity helps predict risk.
functional-capacity.body:
In short: Asking about daily activity helps predict risk.

Can They Climb Stairs?

Asking about daily activity helps predict risk. A patient who can climb two flights of stairs without stopping generally tolerates surgery better.

Poor exercise tolerance may signal heart or lung disease and may prompt further tests before major surgery.

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

Stairs tell you a lot.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about functional capacity?

Stairs tell you a lot.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

medicines-before-surgery.title: Medicines before surgery
medicines-before-surgery.caption: Some drugs are usually continued, such as many heart and asthma medicines.
medicines-before-surgery.body:
In short: Some drugs are usually continued, such as many heart and asthma medicines.

What To Continue

Some drugs are usually continued, such as many heart and asthma medicines. Others are held, such as certain blood thinners and diabetes drugs.

Plans depend on the drug and the surgery, so always check against the anaesthetic and surgical team's instructions.

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

Never guess about a medicine.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about medicines before surgery?

Never guess about a medicine.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

consent-and-the-anaesthetic.title: Consent and the anaesthetic
consent-and-the-anaesthetic.caption: The patient should understand the anaesthetic plan, main risks, alternatives and what to expect after.
consent-and-the-anaesthetic.body:
In short: The patient should understand the anaesthetic plan, main risks, alternatives and what to expect after.

Informed Choice

The patient should understand the anaesthetic plan, main risks, alternatives and what to expect after. Use plain language and an interpreter if needed.

Consent is given freely by a capable patient. Document the discussion and who was present.

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

Explain simply and document it.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about consent and the anaesthetic?

Explain simply and document it.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

anaemia-before-surgery.title: Anaemia before surgery
anaemia-before-surgery.caption: Anaemia reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood and increases the need for transfusion.
anaemia-before-surgery.body:
In short: Anaemia reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood and increases the need for transfusion.

Low Haemoglobin

Anaemia reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood and increases the need for transfusion. It is common and often treatable, for example with iron.

Check haemoglobin before major or bleeding-prone surgery and, where possible, correct it in advance.

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

Fix anaemia before the knife.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about anaemia before surgery?

Fix anaemia before the knife.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

pre-operative-checklist.title: Pre-operative checklist
pre-operative-checklist.caption: A quick list on pre-operative checklist: Right patient, procedure and site; Consent signed and fasting confirmed.
pre-operative-checklist.body:
In short: A quick list on pre-operative checklist: Right patient, procedure and site; Consent signed and fasting confirmed.

Pre-operative checklist

  • Right patient, procedure and site
  • Consent signed and fasting confirmed
  • Allergies and medicines noted
  • Investigations and blood available
  • Jewellery, dentures and make-up removed

Why it matters

Good assessment finds risks before the patient reaches theatre. It guides the choice of anaesthetic and avoids many preventable problems.

Remember

Check, then check again.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Pre-operative checklist".

Right patient, procedure and site; Consent signed and fasting confirmed; Allergies and medicines noted; Investigations and blood available; Jewellery, dentures and make-up removed.

sedation-levels.title: Sedation levels
sedation-levels.caption: A quick list on sedation levels: Minimal: calm, responds normally to voice; Moderate: responds purposefully to touch or voice.
sedation-levels.body:
In short: A quick list on sedation levels: Minimal: calm, responds normally to voice; Moderate: responds purposefully to touch or voice.

Sedation levels

  • Minimal: calm, responds normally to voice
  • Moderate: responds purposefully to touch or voice
  • Deep: responds only to repeated or painful stimulus
  • General anaesthesia: not rousable
  • Levels shift, so be ready to rescue

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Sedation is a spectrum, not a switch.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Sedation levels".

Minimal: calm, responds normally to voice; Moderate: responds purposefully to touch or voice; Deep: responds only to repeated or painful stimulus; General anaesthesia: not rousable; Levels shift, so be ready to rescue.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

midazolam-in-practice.title: Midazolam in practice
midazolam-in-practice.caption: Midazolam gives anxiety relief, sedation and memory loss and is short acting.
midazolam-in-practice.body:
In short: Midazolam gives anxiety relief, sedation and memory loss and is short acting.

A Common Benzodiazepine

Midazolam gives anxiety relief, sedation and memory loss and is short acting. It can cause breathing depression, especially with opioids, older patients or fast injection.

Give it slowly in small steps and watch the response. Flumazenil can reverse it, per protocol.

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Titrate slowly, watch the breathing.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about midazolam in practice?

Titrate slowly, watch the breathing.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

propofol-for-sedation.title: Propofol for sedation
propofol-for-sedation.caption: Propofol acts quickly and wears off quickly, but the line between sedation and general anaesthesia is thin.
propofol-for-sedation.body:
In short: Propofol acts quickly and wears off quickly, but the line between sedation and general anaesthesia is thin.

Light To Deep Fast

Propofol acts quickly and wears off quickly, but the line between sedation and general anaesthesia is thin. It can lower blood pressure and stop breathing.

Only staff trained in airway rescue should use it for sedation, with full monitoring and equipment.

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Propofol sedation needs airway skills.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about propofol for sedation?

Propofol sedation needs airway skills.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

ketamine-sedation.title: Ketamine sedation
ketamine-sedation.caption: Ketamine produces a trance-like state with strong pain relief, while airway reflexes and breathing are often better preserved.
ketamine-sedation.body:
In short: Ketamine produces a trance-like state with strong pain relief, while airway reflexes and breathing are often better preserved.

Dissociative

Ketamine produces a trance-like state with strong pain relief, while airway reflexes and breathing are often better preserved. It can raise blood pressure and heart rate.

It may cause vivid dreams or emergence reactions and increases secretions. It is useful in some settings but still needs monitoring.

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Ketamine preserves breathing, not safety.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ketamine sedation?

Ketamine preserves breathing, not safety.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

fasting-for-sedation.title: Fasting for sedation
fasting-for-sedation.caption: Sedation can lower airway protection even if the patient seems awake.
fasting-for-sedation.body:
In short: Sedation can lower airway protection even if the patient seems awake.

Still A Risk

Sedation can lower airway protection even if the patient seems awake. Many centres apply similar fasting rules as for general anaesthesia for deep sedation.

Emergencies need a risk and benefit decision by the clinician. Do not assume sedation is risk-free.

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Sedated patients can still aspirate.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about fasting for sedation?

Sedated patients can still aspirate.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

monitoring-sedated-patients.title: Monitoring sedated patients
monitoring-sedated-patients.caption: A quick list on monitoring sedated patients: Continuous pulse oximetry; Capnography where available.
monitoring-sedated-patients.body:
In short: A quick list on monitoring sedated patients: Continuous pulse oximetry; Capnography where available.

Monitoring sedated patients

  • Continuous pulse oximetry
  • Capnography where available
  • Blood pressure at regular intervals
  • A trained person watching only the patient
  • Oxygen, suction and bag-mask at the bedside

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Someone must watch the patient the whole time.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Monitoring sedated patients".

Continuous pulse oximetry; Capnography where available; Blood pressure at regular intervals; A trained person watching only the patient; Oxygen, suction and bag-mask at the bedside.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

sedation-in-children.title: Sedation in children
sedation-in-children.caption: Children have less oxygen reserve, smaller airways and fast metabolism.
sedation-in-children.body:
In short: Children have less oxygen reserve, smaller airways and fast metabolism.

Extra Care

Children have less oxygen reserve, smaller airways and fast metabolism. Sedation may make them obstruct their airway or stop breathing quickly.

Use weight-based plans, child-sized equipment and trained staff, and monitor until fully awake.

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Small airway, small margin.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about sedation in children?

Small airway, small margin.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

opioids-and-sedatives-together.title: Opioids and sedatives together
opioids-and-sedatives-together.caption: Opioids and sedatives each depress breathing and together the effect is more than doubled.
opioids-and-sedatives-together.body:
In short: Opioids and sedatives each depress breathing and together the effect is more than doubled.

Combined Effect

Opioids and sedatives each depress breathing and together the effect is more than doubled. This is a common cause of harm in sedation and in recovery.

Reduce doses when both are used, give them one at a time, and watch respiratory rate and depth.

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Together they are stronger than apart.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about opioids and sedatives together?

Together they are stronger than apart.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

reversal-agents.title: Reversal agents
reversal-agents.caption: Naloxone reverses opioid effect and flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines.
reversal-agents.body:
In short: Naloxone reverses opioid effect and flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines.

Naloxone And Flumazenil

Naloxone reverses opioid effect and flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines. Both may wear off sooner than the original drug, so sedation or breathing problems can return.

Naloxone can also cause sudden pain and agitation. Use small doses and continue observation.

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Reversal wears off before the drug does.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about reversal agents?

Reversal wears off before the drug does.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

discharge-after-sedation.title: Discharge after sedation
discharge-after-sedation.caption: A patient is ready to go home when awake, oriented, breathing and moving normally, and with stable observations.
discharge-after-sedation.body:
In short: A patient is ready to go home when awake, oriented, breathing and moving normally, and with stable observations.

When Is It Safe?

A patient is ready to go home when awake, oriented, breathing and moving normally, and with stable observations. Pain and nausea should be controlled.

Give written advice. A responsible adult should accompany them, and they should avoid driving or major decisions for the rest of the day.

Why it matters

Sedation is used outside as well as inside theatre and can easily progress to deeper levels. Safe practice relies on monitoring and rescue skills.

Remember

Do not discharge a half-awake patient.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about discharge after sedation?

Do not discharge a half-awake patient.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

oxygen-and-nitrous-oxide.title: Oxygen and nitrous oxide
oxygen-and-nitrous-oxide.caption: Oxygen supports life and nitrous oxide gives analgesia and mild anaesthesia.
oxygen-and-nitrous-oxide.body:
In short: Oxygen supports life and nitrous oxide gives analgesia and mild anaesthesia.

Carrier Gases

Oxygen supports life and nitrous oxide gives analgesia and mild anaesthesia. Nitrous oxide is a weak anaesthetic and is often combined with a volatile agent.

It should always be given with enough oxygen, and the oxygen is turned on first and off last.

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

Oxygen on first, off last.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about oxygen and nitrous oxide?

Oxygen on first, off last.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

gas-cylinder-colours.title: Gas cylinder colours
gas-cylinder-colours.caption: A quick list on gas cylinder colours: Oxygen: white shoulders, black body (common); Nitrous oxide: blue.
gas-cylinder-colours.body:
In short: A quick list on gas cylinder colours: Oxygen: white shoulders, black body (common); Nitrous oxide: blue.

Gas cylinder colours

  • Oxygen: white shoulders, black body (common)
  • Nitrous oxide: blue
  • Air: black body, white and black shoulders
  • Entonox: blue and white shoulders
  • Colours vary by country, so check labels

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

Always read the label.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Gas cylinder colours".

Oxygen: white shoulders, black body (common); Nitrous oxide: blue; Air: black body, white and black shoulders; Entonox: blue and white shoulders; Colours vary by country, so check labels.

pin-index-safety-system.title: Pin index safety system
pin-index-safety-system.caption: Cylinder yokes have pins in set positions, and each cylinder has matching holes.
pin-index-safety-system.body:
In short: Cylinder yokes have pins in set positions, and each cylinder has matching holes.

Stops Wrong Connection

Cylinder yokes have pins in set positions, and each cylinder has matching holes. Only the correct gas fits the correct yoke.

Never force a cylinder onto a yoke, and never use more than one washer. Damaged pins or holes should be reported.

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

Do not force a cylinder on.

Check yourself

Do not force a cylinder on.

volatile-agents-overview.title: Volatile agents overview
volatile-agents-overview.caption: Sevoflurane, isoflurane, desflurane and halothane are examples of volatile agents.
volatile-agents-overview.body:
In short: Sevoflurane, isoflurane, desflurane and halothane are examples of volatile agents.

Inhaled Anaesthetics

Sevoflurane, isoflurane, desflurane and halothane are examples of volatile agents. They are liquids turned into vapour in a vaporiser.

Sevoflurane is pleasant to breathe and often used for children. Each agent has its own vaporiser and should be used only in a matching one.

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

One agent, one vaporiser.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about volatile agents overview?

One agent, one vaporiser.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

mac-explained.title: MAC explained
mac-explained.caption: MAC is the minimum alveolar concentration of an agent that prevents movement in half of patients in response to a surgical stimulus.
mac-explained.body:
In short: MAC is the minimum alveolar concentration of an agent that prevents movement in half of patients in response to a surgical stimulus.

Potency

MAC is the minimum alveolar concentration of an agent that prevents movement in half of patients in response to a surgical stimulus. It is a measure of potency.

A lower MAC means a more potent agent. Age, temperature and other drugs change the requirement.

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

Lower MAC means a stronger agent.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about mac explained?

Lower MAC means a stronger agent.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

vaporiser-safety.title: Vaporiser safety
vaporiser-safety.caption: A quick list on vaporiser safety: Fill only with the agent named on the vaporiser; Use the correct, keyed filling system.
vaporiser-safety.body:
In short: A quick list on vaporiser safety: Fill only with the agent named on the vaporiser; Use the correct, keyed filling system.

Vaporiser safety

  • Fill only with the agent named on the vaporiser
  • Use the correct, keyed filling system
  • Keep it upright and never tip it
  • Turn it off when not in use
  • Check the level before each case

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

One wrong fill can overdose a patient.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Vaporiser safety".

Fill only with the agent named on the vaporiser; Use the correct, keyed filling system; Keep it upright and never tip it; Turn it off when not in use; Check the level before each case.

soda-lime-and-co2-absorption.title: Soda lime and CO2 absorption
soda-lime-and-co2-absorption.caption: In circle systems, soda lime absorbs the carbon dioxide patients breathe out so gases can be reused.
soda-lime-and-co2-absorption.body:
In short: In circle systems, soda lime absorbs the carbon dioxide patients breathe out so gases can be reused.

Rebreathing Circuits

In circle systems, soda lime absorbs the carbon dioxide patients breathe out so gases can be reused. It gives off heat and changes colour as it is used up.

A colour change may revert after rest, so watch the capnograph for rising inspired carbon dioxide.

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

Spent soda lime means CO2 rebreathing.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about soda lime and co2 absorption?

Spent soda lime means CO2 rebreathing.
