diffusion-hypoxia.title: Diffusion hypoxia
diffusion-hypoxia.caption: When nitrous oxide is switched off, it moves rapidly from blood into the lungs and can dilute the oxygen there.
diffusion-hypoxia.body:
In short: When nitrous oxide is switched off, it moves rapidly from blood into the lungs and can dilute the oxygen there.

At The End Of N2O

When nitrous oxide is switched off, it moves rapidly from blood into the lungs and can dilute the oxygen there. This may cause a short drop in oxygen levels.

Give 100% oxygen for several minutes after turning it off, and watch saturations.

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

Give oxygen after switching off N2O.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about diffusion hypoxia?

Give oxygen after switching off N2O.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

waste-gas-scavenging.title: Waste gas scavenging
waste-gas-scavenging.caption: Anaesthetic gases leaking into theatre can be breathed by staff.
waste-gas-scavenging.body:
In short: Anaesthetic gases leaking into theatre can be breathed by staff.

Protecting Staff

Anaesthetic gases leaking into theatre can be breathed by staff. Scavenging systems carry waste gases away from the breathing circuit to the outside.

Check connections for leaks, avoid spills during filling and ventilate rooms well, following local safety rules.

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

Scavenge it away from the team.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about waste gas scavenging?

Scavenge it away from the team.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

environment-and-gases.title: Environment and gases
environment-and-gases.caption: Some anaesthetic gases are strong greenhouse gases, and desflurane and nitrous oxide have a larger impact than most others.
environment-and-gases.body:
In short: Some anaesthetic gases are strong greenhouse gases, and desflurane and nitrous oxide have a larger impact than most others.

Climate Impact

Some anaesthetic gases are strong greenhouse gases, and desflurane and nitrous oxide have a larger impact than most others. Using lower flows, avoiding high impact agents when safe, and fixing leaks reduces waste.

Patient safety always comes first.

Why it matters

Medical gases and vapours are central to anaesthesia and carry safety and environmental issues. Staff need to handle them correctly.

Remember

Low flow is kinder to the planet.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about environment and gases?

Low flow is kinder to the planet.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

why-give-oxygen.title: Why give oxygen
why-give-oxygen.caption: Oxygen is given to prevent or treat low blood oxygen.
why-give-oxygen.body:
In short: Oxygen is given to prevent or treat low blood oxygen.

Treating Hypoxia

Oxygen is given to prevent or treat low blood oxygen. It helps in shock, breathing problems, heart attack, sepsis and recovery from anaesthesia.

It is a drug: give it with a clear aim, check the response and avoid giving more than needed.

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Oxygen is a drug, so prescribe it.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about why give oxygen?

Oxygen is a drug, so prescribe it.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

nasal-cannula.title: Nasal cannula
nasal-cannula.caption: Nasal cannulae are comfortable and allow eating and talking.
nasal-cannula.body:
In short: Nasal cannulae are comfortable and allow eating and talking.

Low-Flow Device

Nasal cannulae are comfortable and allow eating and talking. They deliver a lower, variable oxygen concentration that depends on flow and the patient's breathing.

They are suitable for mild hypoxia and long-term use. Dry gas at high flow can dry the nose.

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Comfortable, but not for severe hypoxia.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about nasal cannula?

Comfortable, but not for severe hypoxia.

simple-face-mask.title: Simple face mask
simple-face-mask.caption: A simple face mask delivers a moderate oxygen concentration and needs a minimum flow to wash out exhaled carbon dioxide.
simple-face-mask.body:
In short: A simple face mask delivers a moderate oxygen concentration and needs a minimum flow to wash out exhaled carbon dioxide.

Medium Concentration

A simple face mask delivers a moderate oxygen concentration and needs a minimum flow to wash out exhaled carbon dioxide. Check the flow recommended on the device.

The concentration varies with how the patient breathes. It can feel hot and hinder eating or speaking.

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Never run a mask at very low flow.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about simple face mask?

Never run a mask at very low flow.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

non-rebreather-mask.title: Non-rebreather mask
non-rebreather-mask.caption: A mask with a reservoir bag and one-way valves delivers high oxygen concentrations.
non-rebreather-mask.body:
In short: A mask with a reservoir bag and one-way valves delivers high oxygen concentrations.

High Concentration

A mask with a reservoir bag and one-way valves delivers high oxygen concentrations. The bag should stay inflated, so use a flow high enough to keep it filling.

It suits severe hypoxia, major trauma and resuscitation, as a bridge to definitive care.

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Keep the reservoir bag inflated.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about non-rebreather mask?

Keep the reservoir bag inflated.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

venturi-masks.title: Venturi masks
venturi-masks.caption: A Venturi mask delivers a fixed oxygen percentage using colour-coded valves and a set flow.
venturi-masks.body:
In short: A Venturi mask delivers a fixed oxygen percentage using colour-coded valves and a set flow.

Controlled Oxygen

A Venturi mask delivers a fixed oxygen percentage using colour-coded valves and a set flow. It is accurate and independent of breathing pattern.

It is useful for patients with COPD or those at risk of carbon dioxide retention, where oxygen levels must be controlled.

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Venturi gives a known concentration.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about venturi masks?

Venturi gives a known concentration.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

copd-and-oxygen-targets.title: COPD and oxygen targets
copd-and-oxygen-targets.caption: In some people with chronic lung disease, too much oxygen can cause carbon dioxide retention and drowsiness.
copd-and-oxygen-targets.body:
In short: In some people with chronic lung disease, too much oxygen can cause carbon dioxide retention and drowsiness.

Avoid Too Much

In some people with chronic lung disease, too much oxygen can cause carbon dioxide retention and drowsiness. They often need a lower saturation target than others.

Use controlled oxygen, monitor closely and follow the target set by the clinician. Never withhold oxygen from a hypoxic patient.

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Aim for the target, not the highest number.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about copd and oxygen targets?

Aim for the target, not the highest number.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

oxygen-concentrators.title: Oxygen concentrators
oxygen-concentrators.caption: An oxygen concentrator takes in room air, removes most nitrogen and delivers oxygen-enriched air.
oxygen-concentrators.body:
In short: An oxygen concentrator takes in room air, removes most nitrogen and delivers oxygen-enriched air.

Where Cylinders Are Scarce

An oxygen concentrator takes in room air, removes most nitrogen and delivers oxygen-enriched air. It needs only electricity and maintenance, not refills.

It is valuable in low-resource facilities. Keep a backup cylinder for power cuts and keep filters clean.

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Plan for power cuts.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about oxygen concentrators?

Plan for power cuts.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

oxygen-cylinder-safety.title: Oxygen cylinder safety
oxygen-cylinder-safety.caption: A quick list on oxygen cylinder safety: Keep cylinders upright and secured; No oil, grease or open flames nearby.
oxygen-cylinder-safety.body:
In short: A quick list on oxygen cylinder safety: Keep cylinders upright and secured; No oil, grease or open flames nearby.

Oxygen cylinder safety

  • Keep cylinders upright and secured
  • No oil, grease or open flames nearby
  • Open the valve slowly and fully
  • Check the contents gauge before moving a patient
  • Store in a cool, ventilated place

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Oxygen supports fire, so respect it.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Oxygen cylinder safety".

Keep cylinders upright and secured; No oil, grease or open flames nearby; Open the valve slowly and fully; Check the contents gauge before moving a patient; Store in a cool, ventilated place.

humidification.title: Humidification
humidification.caption: Dry oxygen can dry and irritate airways, thicken secretions and make patients uncomfortable.
humidification.body:
In short: Dry oxygen can dry and irritate airways, thicken secretions and make patients uncomfortable.

Warm And Moist

Dry oxygen can dry and irritate airways, thicken secretions and make patients uncomfortable. Humidification is useful in long treatment or at higher flows.

Humidifiers must be kept clean and refilled with sterile water to avoid infection.

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Dry gas dries the airway.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about humidification?

Dry gas dries the airway.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

signs-oxygen-is-not-enough.title: Signs oxygen is not enough
signs-oxygen-is-not-enough.caption: A quick list on signs oxygen is not enough: Rising breathing rate and effort; Confusion, restlessness or drowsiness.
signs-oxygen-is-not-enough.body:
In short: A quick list on signs oxygen is not enough: Rising breathing rate and effort; Confusion, restlessness or drowsiness.

Signs oxygen is not enough

  • Rising breathing rate and effort
  • Confusion, restlessness or drowsiness
  • Blue lips or fingertips
  • Falling saturation despite oxygen
  • Time to escalate and call for senior help

Why it matters

Oxygen is the most used drug in theatre and recovery. Choosing the right device and target keeps patients safe.

Remember

Oxygen is a bridge, not a cure.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Signs oxygen is not enough".

Rising breathing rate and effort; Confusion, restlessness or drowsiness; Blue lips or fingertips; Falling saturation despite oxygen; Time to escalate and call for senior help.

malignant-hyperthermia.title: Malignant hyperthermia
malignant-hyperthermia.caption: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited reaction to some volatile agents and suxamethonium.
malignant-hyperthermia.body:
In short: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited reaction to some volatile agents and suxamethonium.

Rare But Life-Threatening

Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited reaction to some volatile agents and suxamethonium. Signs include rising carbon dioxide, fast heart rate, muscle rigidity and rising temperature.

Stop triggers, call for help, give dantrolene and cool the patient, per protocol.

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Rising CO2 can be the first sign.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about malignant hyperthermia?

Rising CO2 can be the first sign.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

local-anaesthetic-toxicity.title: Local anaesthetic toxicity
local-anaesthetic-toxicity.caption: Too much local anaesthetic in the blood, or an accidental injection into a vein, can cause tingling around the mouth, seizures, collapse and cardiac arrest.
local-anaesthetic-toxicity.body:
In short: Too much local anaesthetic in the blood, or an accidental injection into a vein, can cause tingling around the mouth, seizures, collapse and cardiac arrest.

Last

Too much local anaesthetic in the blood, or an accidental injection into a vein, can cause tingling around the mouth, seizures, collapse and cardiac arrest.

Stop the injection, call for help and give oxygen. Lipid emulsion is the specific treatment, as in local protocol.

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Aspirate before injecting, inject slowly.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about local anaesthetic toxicity?

Aspirate before injecting, inject slowly.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

total-spinal.title: Total spinal
total-spinal.caption: A total spinal happens when local anaesthetic spreads too high in the spinal fluid.
total-spinal.body:
In short: A total spinal happens when local anaesthetic spreads too high in the spinal fluid.

Block Too High

A total spinal happens when local anaesthetic spreads too high in the spinal fluid. The patient has low blood pressure, difficulty breathing, and may lose consciousness.

Support the airway and breathing, give fluids and vasopressors, and call for help. It is rare but treatable with prompt care.

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Support airway, breathing and circulation.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about total spinal?

Support airway, breathing and circulation.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

suxamethonium-apnoea.title: Suxamethonium apnoea
suxamethonium-apnoea.caption: Some people break down suxamethonium slowly because of a genetic enzyme variation.
suxamethonium-apnoea.body:
In short: Some people break down suxamethonium slowly because of a genetic enzyme variation.

Prolonged Paralysis

Some people break down suxamethonium slowly because of a genetic enzyme variation. Paralysis may last far longer than expected.

The patient is kept anaesthetised and ventilated until recovery. Family testing and a warning card can then be advised.

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Keep ventilating until they recover.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about suxamethonium apnoea?

Keep ventilating until they recover.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tension-pneumothorax-in-theatre.title: Tension pneumothorax in theatre
tension-pneumothorax-in-theatre.caption: Air trapped in the chest can push the lung and heart to one side.
tension-pneumothorax-in-theatre.body:
In short: Air trapped in the chest can push the lung and heart to one side.

Air Under Pressure

Air trapped in the chest can push the lung and heart to one side. Signs are sudden low oxygen, falling blood pressure, high airway pressures and absent breath sounds on one side.

It is a clinical diagnosis needing urgent decompression, followed by a chest drain.

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Do not wait for an X-ray if unstable.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tension pneumothorax in theatre?

Do not wait for an X-ray if unstable.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

air-embolism.title: Air embolism
air-embolism.caption: Air can enter veins during neurosurgery, laparoscopy or central line work.
air-embolism.body:
In short: Air can enter veins during neurosurgery, laparoscopy or central line work.

Bubbles In The Blood

Air can enter veins during neurosurgery, laparoscopy or central line work. A large amount may cause sudden low blood pressure, falling end-tidal carbon dioxide and a mill-wheel murmur.

Flood the field, lower the head, give 100% oxygen and call for help.

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Falling CO2 plus collapse: think embolism.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about air embolism?

Falling CO2 plus collapse: think embolism.

cement-reaction-in-hip-surgery.title: Cement reaction in hip surgery
cement-reaction-in-hip-surgery.caption: When cement is placed in the bone during some orthopaedic operations, some patients develop low oxygen, low blood pressure or cardiac arrest.
cement-reaction-in-hip-surgery.body:
In short: When cement is placed in the bone during some orthopaedic operations, some patients develop low oxygen, low blood pressure or cardiac arrest.

During Hip Surgery

When cement is placed in the bone during some orthopaedic operations, some patients develop low oxygen, low blood pressure or cardiac arrest.

The anaesthetist may increase oxygen, ensure good hydration and warn the team before cementing.

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Warn the team before cementing.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cement reaction in hip surgery?

Warn the team before cementing.

cannot-intubate-cannot-oxygenate.title: Cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate
cannot-intubate-cannot-oxygenate.caption: If tracheal intubation fails and the patient cannot be oxygenated by mask or supraglottic device, a front-of-neck access procedure may be needed.
cannot-intubate-cannot-oxygenate.body:
In short: If tracheal intubation fails and the patient cannot be oxygenated by mask or supraglottic device, a front-of-neck access procedure may be needed.

Emergency Plan

If tracheal intubation fails and the patient cannot be oxygenated by mask or supraglottic device, a front-of-neck access procedure may be needed. A scalpel technique is widely taught.

Call for help early and know the local equipment and plan.

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Declare the emergency early.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate?

Declare the emergency early.

intraoperative-cardiac-arrest.title: Intraoperative cardiac arrest
intraoperative-cardiac-arrest.caption: A quick list on intraoperative cardiac arrest: Call for help and start chest compressions; Check rhythm and treat per protocol.
intraoperative-cardiac-arrest.body:
In short: A quick list on intraoperative cardiac arrest: Call for help and start chest compressions; Check rhythm and treat per protocol.

Intraoperative cardiac arrest

  • Call for help and start chest compressions
  • Check rhythm and treat per protocol
  • Stop anaesthetic drugs, use 100% oxygen
  • Think 4 Hs and 4 Ts for causes
  • One person leads, and everyone is briefed

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Causes in theatre are often reversible.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Intraoperative cardiac arrest".

Call for help and start chest compressions; Check rhythm and treat per protocol; Stop anaesthetic drugs, use 100% oxygen; Think 4 Hs and 4 Ts for causes; One person leads, and everyone is briefed.

transfusion-reaction.title: Transfusion reaction
transfusion-reaction.caption: A transfusion reaction may show as fever, rash, breathlessness, back pain or low blood pressure.
transfusion-reaction.body:
In short: A transfusion reaction may show as fever, rash, breathlessness, back pain or low blood pressure.

Blood Gone Wrong

A transfusion reaction may show as fever, rash, breathlessness, back pain or low blood pressure. Under anaesthesia, clues may be unexplained hypotension or bleeding.

Stop the transfusion, keep the line open with saline, check patient details and inform the blood bank.

Why it matters

These events are uncommon but serious. Recognising them quickly and knowing the team's role can save lives.

Remember

Stop, check, tell the blood bank.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about transfusion reaction?

Stop, check, tell the blood bank.

basic-laparotomy-set-contents.title: Basic laparotomy set contents
basic-laparotomy-set-contents.caption: A general abdominal set usually holds scalpel handles, scissors, tissue and dissecting forceps, many artery forceps, needle holders, retractors and towel clips.
basic-laparotomy-set-contents.body:
In short: A general abdominal set usually holds scalpel handles, scissors, tissue and dissecting forceps, many artery forceps, needle holders, retractors and towel clips.

What Is In The Tray

A general abdominal set usually holds scalpel handles, scissors, tissue and dissecting forceps, many artery forceps, needle holders, retractors and towel clips.

Exact contents vary by hospital, so learn your own set list and check it against the tray card.

Why it matters

Knowing what is in each set, what each instrument does and how to count and set up is the daily work of the scrub team and underpins safe surgery.

Remember

Know the set list before you count.

Check yourself

Know the set list before you count.

counting-instruments-in-a-set.body:
In short: A quick list on counting instruments in a set: Count at set-up, before closure and at the end; Two people count aloud and both agree.

Counting instruments in a set

  • Count at set-up, before closure and at the end
  • Two people count aloud and both agree
  • Sharps, swabs and instruments are all counted
  • A discrepancy means stop and recount
  • Record the final count as per local policy

Knowing what is in each set, what each instrument does and how to count and set up is the daily work of the scrub team and underpins safe surgery.

Remember

Count together, count aloud.

instrument-classes-by-function.caption: A quick list on instrument classes by function: Cutting: scalpels, scissors, osteotomes; Grasping: tissue and dissecting forceps.
instrument-classes-by-function.body:
In short: A quick list on instrument classes by function: Cutting: scalpels, scissors, osteotomes; Grasping: tissue and dissecting forceps.

Instrument classes by function

  • Cutting: scalpels, scissors, osteotomes
  • Grasping: tissue and dissecting forceps

artery-forceps-and-clamps.title: Artery forceps and clamps
artery-forceps-and-clamps.caption: Artery forceps have serrated jaws and a ratchet that locks the handles shut.
artery-forceps-and-clamps.body:
In short: Artery forceps have serrated jaws and a ratchet that locks the handles shut.

Clamping Vessels

Artery forceps have serrated jaws and a ratchet that locks the handles shut. They hold bleeding vessels while they are tied or cauterised.

Shapes vary: straight, curved, small mosquito types and larger types. Check the ratchet closes firmly and the tips meet.

Why it matters

Knowing what is in each set, what each instrument does and how to count and set up is the daily work of the scrub team and underpins safe surgery.

Remember

Tips must meet and the ratchet must hold.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about artery forceps and clamps?

Tips must meet and the ratchet must hold.

hand-held-and-self-retaining-types.title: Hand-held and self-retaining types
hand-held-and-self-retaining-types.caption: Hand-held retractors, such as Langenbeck or Deaver types, are held by an assistant.
hand-held-and-self-retaining-types.body:
In short: Hand-held retractors, such as Langenbeck or Deaver types, are held by an assistant.

Keeping The Field Open

Hand-held retractors, such as Langenbeck or Deaver types, are held by an assistant. Self-retaining retractors, such as Balfour or Weitlaner types, hold themselves open with a ratchet or screw.

Use them gently, since prolonged pressure can injure tissue and nerves.

Why it matters

Knowing what is in each set, what each instrument does and how to count and set up is the daily work of the scrub team and underpins safe surgery.

Remember

Retractors expose, they must not crush.

needle-holders-and-suture-scissors.title: Needle holders and suture scissors
needle-holders-and-suture-scissors.caption: A needle holder grips the curved needle near its back third.
needle-holders-and-suture-scissors.body:
In short: A needle holder grips the curved needle near its back third.

Suturing Tools

A needle holder grips the curved needle near its back third. The jaws are short and often have a fine cross-hatched grip.

Suture scissors cut only thread. Keep them separate from tissue scissors, which are for dissecting, so each stays sharp.

Why it matters

Knowing what is in each set, what each instrument does and how to count and set up is the daily work of the scrub team and underpins safe surgery.

Remember

Right scissors for the right job.

toothed-and-plain-forceps.title: Toothed and plain forceps
toothed-and-plain-forceps.caption: Toothed forceps grip tough tissue such as skin and fascia with little pressure.
toothed-and-plain-forceps.body:
In short: Toothed forceps grip tough tissue such as skin and fascia with little pressure.

Choosing Forceps

Toothed forceps grip tough tissue such as skin and fascia with little pressure. Plain (non-toothed) forceps are gentler and used on bowel, vessels and delicate tissue.

Passing the wrong type can crush tissue, so listen for the surgeon's request.

Why it matters

Knowing what is in each set, what each instrument does and how to count and set up is the daily work of the scrub team and underpins safe surgery.

Remember

Toothed for tough, plain for delicate.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about toothed and plain forceps?

Toothed for tough, plain for delicate.

caesarean-section-set-basics.title: Caesarean section set basics
caesarean-section-set-basics.caption: A caesarean set usually includes scalpel handles, scissors, forceps, artery forceps, retractors such as a bladder blade, needle holders and cord clamps.
caesarean-section-set-basics.body:
In short: A caesarean set usually includes scalpel handles, scissors, forceps, artery forceps, retractors such as a bladder blade, needle holders and cord clamps.

Obstetric Tray

A caesarean set usually includes scalpel handles, scissors, forceps, artery forceps, retractors such as a bladder blade, needle holders and cord clamps.

Have extra swabs, suture and suction ready, because speed and bleeding control matter in obstetrics.

Why it matters

Knowing what is in each set, what each instrument does and how to count and set up is the daily work of the scrub team and underpins safe surgery.

Prepare for speed and bleeding.

orthopaedic-set-handling.title: Orthopaedic set handling
orthopaedic-set-handling.caption: Orthopaedic sets contain heavy items such as mallets, osteotomes, drills, reamers and bone levers.
orthopaedic-set-handling.body:
In short: Orthopaedic sets contain heavy items such as mallets, osteotomes, drills, reamers and bone levers.

Heavy And Sharp

Orthopaedic sets contain heavy items such as mallets, osteotomes, drills, reamers and bone levers. Power tools may need batteries, cables or air hoses.

Check that each drill bit, saw blade and guide wire is complete and in good condition before and after use.

Why it matters

Knowing what is in each set, what each instrument does and how to count and set up is the daily work of the scrub team and underpins safe surgery.

Remember

Count the small metal pieces.

setting-up-the-mayo-stand.title: Setting up the Mayo stand
setting-up-the-mayo-stand.caption: A quick list on setting up the mayo stand: Place sharps and most-used items within reach; Arrange instruments in the order of use.
setting-up-the-mayo-stand.body:
In short: A quick list on setting up the mayo stand: Place sharps and most-used items within reach; Arrange instruments in the order of use.

Setting up the Mayo stand

  • Place sharps and most-used items within reach
  • Arrange instruments in the order of use
  • Keep the stand in the sterile field only
  • Do not pass instruments over the patient's face
  • Reset between steps to keep it tidy

Knowing what is in each set, what each instrument does and how to count and set up is the daily work of the scrub team and underpins safe surgery.

Remember

A tidy stand saves seconds.

rigid-and-flexible-endoscopes.title: Rigid and flexible endoscopes
rigid-and-flexible-endoscopes.caption: Rigid endoscopes, such as laparoscopes and cystoscopes, are metal tubes with lens systems.
rigid-and-flexible-endoscopes.body:
In short: Rigid endoscopes, such as laparoscopes and cystoscopes, are metal tubes with lens systems.

Two Families

Rigid endoscopes, such as laparoscopes and cystoscopes, are metal tubes with lens systems. They give a sharp image but cannot bend.

Flexible endoscopes, such as gastroscopes and colonoscopes, bend and have narrow channels. They are heat-sensitive and need careful cleaning.

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

Rigid: sharp. Flexible: gentle.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about rigid and flexible endoscopes?

Rigid: sharp. Flexible: gentle.

light-source-and-fibre-optic-cable.title: Light source and fibre-optic cable
light-source-and-fibre-optic-cable.caption: The light source sends bright light along a fibre-optic cable to the scope.
light-source-and-fibre-optic-cable.body:
In short: The light source sends bright light along a fibre-optic cable to the scope.

Bringing Light In

The light source sends bright light along a fibre-optic cable to the scope. Broken fibres show as dark spots when the cable is held to light.

Never place a lit cable end on drapes or skin because it can get hot enough to burn or ignite. Switch the light to standby when not in use.

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

Lit cable ends can burn drapes.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about light source and fibre-optic cable?

Lit cable ends can burn drapes.

camera-head-and-white-balance.title: Camera head and white balance
camera-head-and-white-balance.caption: The camera head attaches to the eyepiece and sends the picture to the monitor.
camera-head-and-white-balance.body:
In short: The camera head attaches to the eyepiece and sends the picture to the monitor.

Clear Picture

The camera head attaches to the eyepiece and sends the picture to the monitor. It is covered with a sterile sleeve or is itself sterilised.

White balance is set by pointing the scope at a white swab so colours look natural. Repeat it if the picture looks tinted.

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

White swab, white balance.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about camera head and white balance?

White swab, white balance.

laparoscopic-insufflator.title: Laparoscopic insufflator
laparoscopic-insufflator.caption: The insufflator delivers carbon dioxide into the abdomen to lift the wall and create working space.
laparoscopic-insufflator.body:
In short: The insufflator delivers carbon dioxide into the abdomen to lift the wall and create working space.

Creating Space

The insufflator delivers carbon dioxide into the abdomen to lift the wall and create working space. It displays pressure and gas flow.

Check the gas cylinder level before starting. The surgeon and anaesthetist should be told of pressure changes, which can affect the patient's breathing and circulation.

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

Check the gas before the incision.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about laparoscopic insufflator?

Check the gas before the incision.

trocars-and-ports.title: Trocars and ports
trocars-and-ports.caption: A trocar with a sleeve (cannula) is used to make an access port for instruments.
trocars-and-ports.body:
In short: A trocar with a sleeve (cannula) is used to make an access port for instruments.

Entry Points

A trocar with a sleeve (cannula) is used to make an access port for instruments. After entry the sharp inner part is removed and the sleeve stays in place.

Valves and seals stop gas leaking. Check seals before use, and handle trocar tips carefully as they are sharp.

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

Sharp tips need safe handling.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about trocars and ports?

Sharp tips need safe handling.

basic-video-tower-layout.title: Basic video tower layout
basic-video-tower-layout.caption: A quick list on basic video tower layout: Monitor placed in the surgeon's line of sight; Light source, camera unit and insufflator on tower.
basic-video-tower-layout.body:
In short: A quick list on basic video tower layout: Monitor placed in the surgeon's line of sight; Light source, camera unit and insufflator on tower.

Basic video tower layout

  • Monitor placed in the surgeon's line of sight
  • Light source, camera unit and insufflator on tower
  • Cables run clear of walking paths
  • Diathermy and suction cables secured
  • Spare telescope and cables within reach

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

Plan the tower before the patient arrives.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Basic video tower layout".

Monitor placed in the surgeon's line of sight; Light source, camera unit and insufflator on tower; Cables run clear of walking paths; Diathermy and suction cables secured; Spare telescope and cables within reach.

handling-rigid-telescopes.title: Handling rigid telescopes
handling-rigid-telescopes.caption: The lens system inside a rigid telescope is delicate.
handling-rigid-telescopes.body:
In short: The lens system inside a rigid telescope is delicate.

Fragile Optics

The lens system inside a rigid telescope is delicate. A drop, a bend or a knock can damage it, leading to a poor image.

Carry it by the body, never by the light post or eyepiece, and keep it in a protective case or tray. Do not stack heavy instruments on it.

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

Treat the telescope like glass.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about handling rigid telescopes?

Treat the telescope like glass.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

leak-testing-flexible-scopes.title: Leak testing flexible scopes
leak-testing-flexible-scopes.caption: A leak test pressurises the scope to check that the outer covering is intact.
leak-testing-flexible-scopes.body:
In short: A leak test pressurises the scope to check that the outer covering is intact.

Check The Skin

A leak test pressurises the scope to check that the outer covering is intact. It is done before manual cleaning, according to the manufacturer's instructions.

A leak lets fluid enter and damage the inside. Do not use a scope that fails; send it for repair.

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

Leaking scope: stop and report.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about leak testing flexible scopes?

Leaking scope: stop and report.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cleaning-a-flexible-scope.title: Cleaning a flexible scope
cleaning-a-flexible-scope.caption: A quick list on cleaning a flexible scope: Wipe and flush channels straight after use; Leak test before immersion.
cleaning-a-flexible-scope.body:
In short: A quick list on cleaning a flexible scope: Wipe and flush channels straight after use; Leak test before immersion.

Cleaning a flexible scope

  • Wipe and flush channels straight after use
  • Leak test before immersion
  • Brush and flush all channels as directed
  • High-level disinfect or sterilise as per policy
  • Rinse, dry and store hanging if possible

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

Clean straight away, never let it dry.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Cleaning a flexible scope".

Wipe and flush channels straight after use; Leak test before immersion; Brush and flush all channels as directed; High-level disinfect or sterilise as per policy; Rinse, dry and store hanging if possible.

irrigation-fluid-in-endoscopy.title: Irrigation fluid in endoscopy
irrigation-fluid-in-endoscopy.caption: Procedures such as cystoscopy or hysteroscopy use fluid to expand the space and clear the view.
irrigation-fluid-in-endoscopy.body:
In short: Procedures such as cystoscopy or hysteroscopy use fluid to expand the space and clear the view.

Fluid Choice

Procedures such as cystoscopy or hysteroscopy use fluid to expand the space and clear the view. The type depends on the procedure and on whether diathermy is used.

Fluid absorbed through the tissues can upset body salts, so the team tracks the volume in against the volume out.

Why it matters

Endoscopic surgery depends on delicate, costly optical equipment that must be handled, cleaned and set up correctly to give a clear picture and avoid harm.

Remember

Measure fluid in and fluid out.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about irrigation fluid in endoscopy?

Measure fluid in and fluid out.

zoning-of-the-theatre-suite.title: Zoning of the theatre suite
zoning-of-the-theatre-suite.caption: A quick list on zoning of the theatre suite: Outer zone: reception, changing, store; Clean zone: pre-op area and clean corridors.
zoning-of-the-theatre-suite.body:
In short: A quick list on zoning of the theatre suite: Outer zone: reception, changing, store; Clean zone: pre-op area and clean corridors.

Zoning of the theatre suite

  • Outer zone: reception, changing, store
  • Clean zone: pre-op area and clean corridors
  • Aseptic zone: scrub area and operating room
  • Disposal zone: dirty utility and waste exit
  • Movement should flow from clean to dirty

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Design keeps clean and dirty apart.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Zoning of the theatre suite".

Outer zone: reception, changing, store; Clean zone: pre-op area and clean corridors; Aseptic zone: scrub area and operating room; Disposal zone: dirty utility and waste exit; Movement should flow from clean to dirty.

positive-pressure-ventilation.title: Positive pressure ventilation
positive-pressure-ventilation.caption: In many theatres, air pressure inside is slightly higher than in the corridor.
positive-pressure-ventilation.body:
In short: In many theatres, air pressure inside is slightly higher than in the corridor.

Air Flows Outwards

In many theatres, air pressure inside is slightly higher than in the corridor. Air then flows out when doors open instead of dirty air flowing in.

This only works if doors stay closed, so keep door opening to a minimum during surgery.

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Closed doors keep the pressure.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about positive pressure ventilation?

Closed doors keep the pressure.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

air-filtration-and-air-changes.title: Air filtration and air changes
air-filtration-and-air-changes.caption: Theatres need many air changes per hour to dilute airborne microbes.
air-filtration-and-air-changes.body:
In short: Theatres need many air changes per hour to dilute airborne microbes.

Clean Air

Theatres need many air changes per hour to dilute airborne microbes. Air is usually filtered, often with HEPA filters in modern units, before it enters the room.

Filters need scheduled replacement. In facilities without full systems, keep windows and doors managed according to local practice.

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Filters only work if they are changed.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about air filtration and air changes?

Filters only work if they are changed.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

limiting-traffic-in-theatre.title: Limiting traffic in theatre
limiting-traffic-in-theatre.caption: Each opening of the door and each person in the room raises the number of microbes in the air.
limiting-traffic-in-theatre.body:
In short: Each opening of the door and each person in the room raises the number of microbes in the air.

Fewer Movements

Each opening of the door and each person in the room raises the number of microbes in the air. Staff movement is a major source of contamination.

Limit people to those needed, plan equipment before starting, and avoid unnecessary entering and leaving during the operation.

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Less movement, fewer microbes.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about limiting traffic in theatre?

Less movement, fewer microbes.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

theatre-floors-and-walls.title: Theatre floors and walls
theatre-floors-and-walls.caption: Floors, walls and ceilings in theatre should be smooth, seamless, non-porous and able to withstand frequent cleaning and disinfectants.
theatre-floors-and-walls.body:
In short: Floors, walls and ceilings in theatre should be smooth, seamless, non-porous and able to withstand frequent cleaning and disinfectants.

Easy To Clean

Floors, walls and ceilings in theatre should be smooth, seamless, non-porous and able to withstand frequent cleaning and disinfectants.

Coved (curved) corners where the floor meets the wall help stop dirt collecting. Cracks and peeling paint can harbour microbes and should be reported.

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Smooth surfaces clean best.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about theatre floors and walls?

Smooth surfaces clean best.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

scrub-area-design.title: Scrub area design
scrub-area-design.caption: The scrub area has deep sinks with elbow, knee, foot or sensor taps so hands are not used to turn water on or off.
scrub-area-design.body:
In short: The scrub area has deep sinks with elbow, knee, foot or sensor taps so hands are not used to turn water on or off.

Hand Wash Space

The scrub area has deep sinks with elbow, knee, foot or sensor taps so hands are not used to turn water on or off.

It is positioned near the operating room with clear sight of the patient. Enough space avoids splashing and crowding.

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Hands-free taps protect clean hands.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about scrub area design?

Hands-free taps protect clean hands.

temperature-and-humidity-control.title: Temperature and humidity control
temperature-and-humidity-control.caption: Theatre temperature is set to balance staff comfort with patient warmth, and it often differs for babies and burns patients, who need warmer rooms.
temperature-and-humidity-control.body:
In short: Theatre temperature is set to balance staff comfort with patient warmth, and it often differs for babies and burns patients, who need warmer rooms.

Comfort And Safety

Theatre temperature is set to balance staff comfort with patient warmth, and it often differs for babies and burns patients, who need warmer rooms.

Humidity is usually kept in a controlled range, as very dry or damp air can affect static and microbial growth. Follow local policy.

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Warm for the patient, cool for the team.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about temperature and humidity control?

Warm for the patient, cool for the team.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

medical-gas-pipelines.title: Medical gas pipelines
medical-gas-pipelines.caption: Many theatres have wall or pendant outlets for oxygen, medical air, suction and sometimes nitrous oxide.
medical-gas-pipelines.body:
In short: Many theatres have wall or pendant outlets for oxygen, medical air, suction and sometimes nitrous oxide.

Piped Supply

Many theatres have wall or pendant outlets for oxygen, medical air, suction and sometimes nitrous oxide. Outlets are colour-coded and use special connectors to avoid wrong connections.

A cylinder backup should always be available in case the pipeline fails.

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Always have a backup cylinder.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about medical gas pipelines?

Always have a backup cylinder.

emergency-power-supply.title: Emergency power supply
emergency-power-supply.caption: Theatre needs electricity for lights, anaesthesia machines, suction and monitors.
emergency-power-supply.body:
In short: Theatre needs electricity for lights, anaesthesia machines, suction and monitors.

When The Power Fails

Theatre needs electricity for lights, anaesthesia machines, suction and monitors. Generators and uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) provide backup, though they may take seconds to start.

Know where torches, manual suction and hand-ventilation equipment are kept.

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Plan for power cuts before they happen.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about emergency power supply?

Plan for power cuts before they happen.

clean-and-dirty-flow.title: Clean and dirty flow
clean-and-dirty-flow.caption: A quick list on clean and dirty flow: Sterile supplies enter through the clean route; Patient enters through the reception route.
clean-and-dirty-flow.body:
In short: A quick list on clean and dirty flow: Sterile supplies enter through the clean route; Patient enters through the reception route.

Clean and dirty flow

  • Sterile supplies enter through the clean route
  • Patient enters through the reception route
  • Waste and used instruments leave separately
  • Dirty items should not cross clean areas
  • If you cannot separate by route, separate by time

Why it matters

The layout, air flow and surfaces of a theatre suite are designed to limit infection, so staff must understand and respect how the space is meant to work.

Remember

Keep clean routes clean.

Check yourself

Sterile supplies enter through the clean route; Patient enters through the reception route; Waste and used instruments leave separately; Dirty items should not cross clean areas; If you cannot separate by route, separate by time.

cssd-one-way-workflow.title: CSSD one-way workflow
cssd-one-way-workflow.caption: A quick list on cssd one-way workflow: Receive used items in the dirty area; Clean and decontaminate.
cssd-one-way-workflow.body:
In short: A quick list on cssd one-way workflow: Receive used items in the dirty area; Clean and decontaminate.

CSSD one-way workflow

  • Receive used items in the dirty area
  • Clean and decontaminate
  • Inspect, assemble and pack in the clean area
  • Sterilise in the autoclave
  • Store and issue sterile items

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

One-way flow prevents cross-contamination.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "CSSD one-way workflow".

Receive used items in the dirty area; Clean and decontaminate; Inspect, assemble and pack in the clean area; Sterilise in the autoclave; Store and issue sterile items.

why-clean-before-sterilising.title: Why clean before sterilising
why-clean-before-sterilising.caption: Blood and tissue left on instruments protect microbes from steam and chemicals.
why-clean-before-sterilising.body:
In short: Blood and tissue left on instruments protect microbes from steam and chemicals.

Dirt Blocks Sterilisation

Blood and tissue left on instruments protect microbes from steam and chemicals. Sterilising an unclean item can fail.

Cleaning removes most of the soil first, whether by hand or machine. Clean first, then disinfect or sterilise as appropriate.

Why it matters

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

No cleaning, no sterility.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about why clean before sterilising?

No cleaning, no sterility.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

manual-cleaning-safely.title: Manual cleaning safely
manual-cleaning-safely.caption: Staff handle sharps, so wear gloves, a plastic apron and eye protection.
manual-cleaning-safely.body:
In short: Staff handle sharps, so wear gloves, a plastic apron and eye protection.

Hand Washing Instruments

Staff handle sharps, so wear gloves, a plastic apron and eye protection. Open hinged instruments and dismantle parts.

Use brushes under the water surface to avoid splashing, and use the detergent as directed. Never overload sinks with heavy items on top of delicate ones.

Why it matters

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

Brush under water, not above.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about manual cleaning safely?

Brush under water, not above.

ultrasonic-cleaning.title: Ultrasonic cleaning
ultrasonic-cleaning.caption: An ultrasonic cleaner uses high-frequency sound in liquid to loosen dirt from joints, serrations and hollow parts.
ultrasonic-cleaning.body:
In short: An ultrasonic cleaner uses high-frequency sound in liquid to loosen dirt from joints, serrations and hollow parts.

Sound-Wave Cleaning

An ultrasonic cleaner uses high-frequency sound in liquid to loosen dirt from joints, serrations and hollow parts. It works best after a first rinse and with the right detergent.

Instruments should be open and not overloaded. Change the solution when it is visibly dirty.

Why it matters

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

Open the box joints before the bath.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ultrasonic cleaning?

Open the box joints before the bath.

wrapping-and-packing-sets.title: Wrapping and packing sets
wrapping-and-packing-sets.caption: Sets are packed so that steam can reach all surfaces.
wrapping-and-packing-sets.body:
In short: Sets are packed so that steam can reach all surfaces.

Packing Rules

Sets are packed so that steam can reach all surfaces. Instruments are placed open and in an orderly way, with an indicator inside the pack.

Wrappers or pouches must be intact and the pack not too heavy. Label with the contents, date and operator as per local policy.

Why it matters

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

Steam must reach every surface.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about wrapping and packing sets?

Steam must reach every surface.

steam-sterilisation-cycle.title: Steam sterilisation cycle
steam-sterilisation-cycle.caption: A quick list on steam sterilisation cycle: Air is removed from the chamber; Steam enters and heats the load.
steam-sterilisation-cycle.body:
In short: A quick list on steam sterilisation cycle: Air is removed from the chamber; Steam enters and heats the load.

Steam sterilisation cycle

  • Air is removed from the chamber
  • Steam enters and heats the load
  • Temperature and pressure held for set time
  • Steam is removed and the load is dried
  • Check the printout and indicators before release

Why it matters

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

Time, temperature and pressure together.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Steam sterilisation cycle".

Air is removed from the chamber; Steam enters and heats the load; Temperature and pressure held for set time; Steam is removed and the load is dried; Check the printout and indicators before release.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

chemical-and-biological-indicators.title: Chemical and biological indicators
chemical-and-biological-indicators.caption: Chemical indicators change colour when conditions are met, such as on tape or strips inside packs.
chemical-and-biological-indicators.body:
In short: Chemical indicators change colour when conditions are met, such as on tape or strips inside packs.

Proving Sterility

Chemical indicators change colour when conditions are met, such as on tape or strips inside packs. They show exposure, not complete sterility.

Biological indicators contain bacterial spores and are checked at intervals as per policy. Failed indicators mean the load must not be used.

Why it matters

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

Colour change is not the final proof.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about chemical and biological indicators?

Colour change is not the final proof.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

loading-the-autoclave.title: Loading the autoclave
loading-the-autoclave.caption: Leave space between packs so steam can circulate.
loading-the-autoclave.body:
In short: Leave space between packs so steam can circulate.

Good Loading

Leave space between packs so steam can circulate. Do not stack tightly or press packs against the chamber walls.

Place heavy metal items in lower positions where they will not cause wet packs. Follow the machine and loading instructions.

Why it matters

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

Space between packs lets steam in.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about loading the autoclave?

Space between packs lets steam in.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

storage-and-shelf-life.title: Storage and shelf life
storage-and-shelf-life.caption: Sterile items are stored in clean, dry, closed shelves or cupboards away from sinks, dust and direct sunlight.
storage-and-shelf-life.body:
In short: Sterile items are stored in clean, dry, closed shelves or cupboards away from sinks, dust and direct sunlight.

Keeping Sterile

Sterile items are stored in clean, dry, closed shelves or cupboards away from sinks, dust and direct sunlight.

Check packs for damage, dampness or opened seals before use. Many facilities use event-related storage, meaning a pack stays sterile until its packaging is damaged. Follow local policy.

Why it matters

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

Damaged or damp pack: not sterile.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about storage and shelf life?

Damaged or damp pack: not sterile.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

traceability-of-sterile-sets.title: Traceability of sterile sets
traceability-of-sterile-sets.caption: Each autoclave load gets a record of the machine, cycle, date and contents.
traceability-of-sterile-sets.body:
In short: Each autoclave load gets a record of the machine, cycle, date and contents.

Track Every Load

Each autoclave load gets a record of the machine, cycle, date and contents. Sets may carry labels linking them to the patient record.

If a failure is found later, traceability lets staff recall the items. Keep records for the period required by local policy.

Why it matters

The central sterile services department makes instruments safe to reuse. Every step, from cleaning to storage, affects whether the patient receives a sterile item.

Remember

If it is not recorded, you cannot trace it.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about traceability of sterile sets?

If it is not recorded, you cannot trace it.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

reusable-and-disposable-drapes.title: Reusable and disposable drapes
reusable-and-disposable-drapes.caption: Reusable cloth drapes are washed, checked and sterilised after each use.
reusable-and-disposable-drapes.body:
In short: Reusable cloth drapes are washed, checked and sterilised after each use.

Two Options

Reusable cloth drapes are washed, checked and sterilised after each use. Disposable drapes are single use and often have a built-in fluid barrier.

Both must prevent fluid soaking through. Cloth wears out over repeated washing, so inspect for holes and thin patches.

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

Check for holes before using drapes.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about reusable and disposable drapes?

Check for holes before using drapes.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

types-of-surgical-gown.title: Types of surgical gown
types-of-surgical-gown.caption: Standard gowns protect the surgical team from moderate splashes.
types-of-surgical-gown.body:
In short: Standard gowns protect the surgical team from moderate splashes.

Gown Choice

Standard gowns protect the surgical team from moderate splashes. Reinforced gowns have a stronger, fluid-resistant panel at the front and sleeves.

Reinforced gowns suit long cases or those with much fluid, such as orthopaedic and caesarean surgery. Choose according to risk.

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

More fluid, more protection.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about types of surgical gown?

More fluid, more protection.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

sterile-and-non-sterile-gown-areas.title: Sterile and non-sterile gown areas
sterile-and-non-sterile-gown-areas.caption: On a sterile gown, the front from chest to waist level and the sleeves up to the elbows are regarded as sterile.
sterile-and-non-sterile-gown-areas.body:
In short: On a sterile gown, the front from chest to waist level and the sleeves up to the elbows are regarded as sterile.

Where Is Sterile

On a sterile gown, the front from chest to waist level and the sleeves up to the elbows are regarded as sterile. The neckline, shoulders, underarms and back are not.

Keep hands in view, above waist level and away from the unsterile areas.

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

Front sterile, back not.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about sterile and non-sterile gown areas?

Front sterile, back not.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

steps-for-gowning.title: Steps for gowning
steps-for-gowning.caption: A quick list on steps for gowning: Open the pack without touching the gown; Lift it by the inside neckline.
steps-for-gowning.body:
In short: A quick list on steps for gowning: Open the pack without touching the gown; Lift it by the inside neckline.

Steps for gowning

  • Open the pack without touching the gown
  • Lift it by the inside neckline
  • Slide arms in and keep hands inside sleeves
  • Have a helper tie the neck and back
  • Glove closed, then fasten the waist tie

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

Gown first, then glove.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Steps for gowning".

Open the pack without touching the gown; Lift it by the inside neckline; Slide arms in and keep hands inside sleeves; Have a helper tie the neck and back; Glove closed, then fasten the waist tie.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

closed-gloving-technique.title: Closed gloving technique
closed-gloving-technique.caption: In closed gloving, hands remain inside the gown cuffs while pulling the glove on.
closed-gloving-technique.body:
In short: In closed gloving, hands remain inside the gown cuffs while pulling the glove on.

Hands Stay Covered

In closed gloving, hands remain inside the gown cuffs while pulling the glove on. The glove is pushed over the cuff and fingers are worked through from outside the cuff.

This keeps skin from touching the outer glove and is preferred when gowning yourself.

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

Cuffs stay over the hands.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about closed gloving technique?

Cuffs stay over the hands.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

draping-the-surgical-site.title: Draping the surgical site
draping-the-surgical-site.caption: A quick list on draping the surgical site: Drape only after skin preparation has dried; Place drapes from the clean area outwards.
draping-the-surgical-site.body:
In short: A quick list on draping the surgical site: Drape only after skin preparation has dried; Place drapes from the clean area outwards.

Draping the surgical site

  • Drape only after skin preparation has dried
  • Place drapes from the clean area outwards
  • Once placed, do not slide a drape across skin
  • Cover the whole patient with a large drape
  • Avoid contaminating the drape edges

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

Place once and do not move it.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Draping the surgical site".

Drape only after skin preparation has dried; Place drapes from the clean area outwards; Once placed, do not slide a drape across skin; Cover the whole patient with a large drape; Avoid contaminating the drape edges.
