fenestrated-and-split-drapes.title: Fenestrated and split drapes
fenestrated-and-split-drapes.caption: A fenestrated drape has an opening (a fenestration) to expose only the operating site.
fenestrated-and-split-drapes.body:
In short: A fenestrated drape has an opening (a fenestration) to expose only the operating site.

Windows And Splits

A fenestrated drape has an opening (a fenestration) to expose only the operating site. Split drapes have a slit to allow wrapping around limbs, or are used for the head and neck.

Use the right drape for the body area so that no unsterile skin is exposed.

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

Open only the area to be cut.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about fenestrated and split drapes?

Open only the area to be cut.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

adhesive-incise-drapes.title: Adhesive incise drapes
adhesive-incise-drapes.caption: Some operations use a clear adhesive film over the prepared skin so the incision goes through it.
adhesive-incise-drapes.body:
In short: Some operations use a clear adhesive film over the prepared skin so the incision goes through it.

Film Over The Skin

Some operations use a clear adhesive film over the prepared skin so the incision goes through it. This helps hold the edge of drapes and may limit skin microbes.

Apply it smoothly, avoiding wrinkles. Skin must be fully dry, or it will not stick.

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

Dry skin, smooth film.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about adhesive incise drapes?

Dry skin, smooth film.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

wet-drapes-and-strike-through.title: Wet drapes and strike-through
wet-drapes-and-strike-through.caption: When fluid soaks through a drape or gown, microbes can travel from the unsterile layer to the sterile surface.
wet-drapes-and-strike-through.body:
In short: When fluid soaks through a drape or gown, microbes can travel from the unsterile layer to the sterile surface.

When Fluid Soaks

When fluid soaks through a drape or gown, microbes can travel from the unsterile layer to the sterile surface. This is called strike-through.

If a drape or gown becomes wet, reinforce it with a waterproof layer or replace it, as per local policy. Wet means contaminated.

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

Wet cloth is a bridge for microbes.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about wet drapes and strike-through?

Wet cloth is a bridge for microbes.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

drape-and-gown-packaging-checks.title: Drape and gown packaging checks
drape-and-gown-packaging-checks.caption: A quick list on drape and gown packaging checks: Check pack is intact and not damp; Check indicator has changed colour.
drape-and-gown-packaging-checks.body:
In short: A quick list on drape and gown packaging checks: Check pack is intact and not damp; Check indicator has changed colour.

Drape and gown packaging checks

  • Check pack is intact and not damp
  • Check indicator has changed colour
  • Check the expiry or packing date
  • Open away from yourself
  • Discard any pack that is torn or wet

Why it matters

Drapes and gowns form the barrier between the sterile field and everything else, so correct choice, wearing and handling protect both patients and staff.

Remember

Check the pack before opening.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Drape and gown packaging checks".

Check pack is intact and not damp; Check indicator has changed colour; Check the expiry or packing date; Open away from yourself; Discard any pack that is torn or wet.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

suture-needle-shapes.title: Suture needle shapes
suture-needle-shapes.caption: Most surgical needles are curved so they can turn through tissue.
suture-needle-shapes.body:
In short: Most surgical needles are curved so they can turn through tissue.

Curved And Straight

Most surgical needles are curved so they can turn through tissue. Straight needles are used for skin and some tough tissue.

Cutting needles have sharp edges for skin and tough tissue. Round-bodied needles part the tissue fibres and are used for softer tissue such as bowel.

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

Cutting for tough, round for soft.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about suture needle shapes?

Cutting for tough, round for soft.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

absorbable-and-permanent-sutures.title: Absorbable and permanent sutures
absorbable-and-permanent-sutures.caption: Absorbable sutures are broken down by the body over time and are used for internal tissue.
absorbable-and-permanent-sutures.body:
In short: Absorbable sutures are broken down by the body over time and are used for internal tissue.

Will It Dissolve

Absorbable sutures are broken down by the body over time and are used for internal tissue. Non-absorbable sutures remain, and are used for skin, tendon, vessels and implants, sometimes removed later.

The choice depends on the tissue and how long support is needed.

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

Match the thread to the healing time.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about absorbable and permanent sutures?

Match the thread to the healing time.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

reading-suture-packets.title: Reading suture packets
reading-suture-packets.caption: A quick list on reading suture packets: Material, such as silk, nylon or polyglactin; Size number, with more zeros meaning finer.
reading-suture-packets.body:
In short: A quick list on reading suture packets: Material, such as silk, nylon or polyglactin; Size number, with more zeros meaning finer.

Reading suture packets

  • Material, such as silk, nylon or polyglactin
  • Size number, with more zeros meaning finer
  • Thread length
  • Needle type and shape
  • Expiry date and sterility seal

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

Read the packet before opening.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Reading suture packets".

Material, such as silk, nylon or polyglactin; Size number, with more zeros meaning finer; Thread length; Needle type and shape; Expiry date and sterility seal.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

x-ray-detectable-swabs.title: X-ray detectable swabs
x-ray-detectable-swabs.caption: Swabs used inside body cavities should have an X-ray detectable marker so a retained item can be found by imaging.
x-ray-detectable-swabs.body:
In short: Swabs used inside body cavities should have an X-ray detectable marker so a retained item can be found by imaging.

Detectable Swabs

Swabs used inside body cavities should have an X-ray detectable marker so a retained item can be found by imaging. Counting remains the main safety check.

Never cut swabs, and never use small gauze pieces in a cavity without a tag or holder as required by local policy.

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

Count first, imaging second.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about x-ray detectable swabs?

Count first, imaging second.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

skin-staplers-and-clips.title: Skin staplers and clips
skin-staplers-and-clips.caption: Skin staplers place metal staples quickly and are common in long wounds.
skin-staplers-and-clips.body:
In short: Skin staplers place metal staples quickly and are common in long wounds.

Fast Skin Closure

Skin staplers place metal staples quickly and are common in long wounds. Staples need a special remover later.

Clips and staplers for internal use, such as for vessels or bowel, are different devices, so check you have the correct one. Count staples used if your policy requires.

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

Use the stapler made for the job.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about skin staplers and clips?

Use the stapler made for the job.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

surgical-drains.title: Surgical drains
surgical-drains.caption: A drain removes blood or fluid that could collect after surgery.
surgical-drains.body:
In short: A drain removes blood or fluid that could collect after surgery.

Removing Fluid

A drain removes blood or fluid that could collect after surgery. Passive drains allow fluid to flow out. Closed suction drains collect it into a bottle or bulb.

The team records the drain type, site and amount drained. Secure the drain to prevent dislodging when moving the patient.

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

Secure and label every drain.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about surgical drains?

Secure and label every drain.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

dressings-for-wounds.title: Dressings for wounds
dressings-for-wounds.caption: A wound dressing protects the wound, absorbs fluid and keeps it clean.
dressings-for-wounds.body:
In short: A wound dressing protects the wound, absorbs fluid and keeps it clean.

Protecting The Wound

A wound dressing protects the wound, absorbs fluid and keeps it clean. A non-stick layer touches the wound and a pad absorbs ooze.

Some wounds need special dressings, but the basic rules are the same: apply to a clean, dry wound and secure without too much pressure.

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

Cover clean wounds with clean dressings.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about dressings for wounds?

Cover clean wounds with clean dressings.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

haemostatic-agents.title: Haemostatic agents
haemostatic-agents.caption: Haemostatic products, such as absorbable gelatin sponges or cellulose-based materials, help control oozing from raw surfaces.
haemostatic-agents.body:
In short: Haemostatic products, such as absorbable gelatin sponges or cellulose-based materials, help control oozing from raw surfaces.

Helping Clot

Haemostatic products, such as absorbable gelatin sponges or cellulose-based materials, help control oozing from raw surfaces.

They are used with pressure and good surgical technique, not instead of them. Record the use and quantity if local policy requires it.

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

They help clotting but do not replace control.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about haemostatic agents?

They help clotting but do not replace control.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

urinary-catheters-in-theatre.title: Urinary catheters in theatre
urinary-catheters-in-theatre.caption: A urinary catheter drains the bladder and measures urine output in long or major surgery.
urinary-catheters-in-theatre.body:
In short: A urinary catheter drains the bladder and measures urine output in long or major surgery.

Bladder Drainage

A urinary catheter drains the bladder and measures urine output in long or major surgery. It is passed with sterile technique, and the balloon is inflated only when the tip is well inside.

Attach to a closed drainage bag and secure the tubing so it is not pulled.

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

Sterile insertion, closed drainage.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about urinary catheters in theatre?

Sterile insertion, closed drainage.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

stock-rotation-and-expiry.title: Stock rotation and expiry
stock-rotation-and-expiry.caption: A quick list on stock rotation and expiry: Place new stock behind older stock; Use items with the earliest expiry first.
stock-rotation-and-expiry.body:
In short: A quick list on stock rotation and expiry: Place new stock behind older stock; Use items with the earliest expiry first.

Stock rotation and expiry

  • Place new stock behind older stock
  • Use items with the earliest expiry first
  • Check expiry dates when stock is delivered
  • Remove expired or damaged items
  • Store supplies off the floor and dry

Why it matters

Theatre staff must know and manage the sutures, swabs, drains and other supplies used in every operation, since the wrong item or an expired one can cause harm.

Remember

First to expire, first out.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Stock rotation and expiry".

Place new stock behind older stock; Use items with the earliest expiry first; Check expiry dates when stock is delivered; Remove expired or damaged items; Store supplies off the floor and dry.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

preventive-or-corrective-repairs.title: Preventive or corrective repairs
preventive-or-corrective-repairs.caption: Preventive maintenance is planned servicing done on a schedule to stop breakdowns.
preventive-or-corrective-repairs.body:
In short: Preventive maintenance is planned servicing done on a schedule to stop breakdowns.

Two Kinds Of Care

Preventive maintenance is planned servicing done on a schedule to stop breakdowns. Corrective maintenance is repair after a fault.

Good planning reduces emergencies, cancelled lists and unsafe equipment. Staff help by reporting small problems early.

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

Service before it fails.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about preventive or corrective repairs?

Service before it fails.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

daily-equipment-checks.title: Daily equipment checks
daily-equipment-checks.caption: A quick list on daily equipment checks: Check power cables and plugs for damage; Switch on and test alarms.
daily-equipment-checks.body:
In short: A quick list on daily equipment checks: Check power cables and plugs for damage; Switch on and test alarms.

Daily equipment checks

  • Check power cables and plugs for damage
  • Switch on and test alarms
  • Check suction, gas and batteries
  • Confirm accessories are present
  • Record the check and report any fault

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

Check it before the first case.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Daily equipment checks".

Check power cables and plugs for damage; Switch on and test alarms; Check suction, gas and batteries; Confirm accessories are present; Record the check and report any fault.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

equipment-logbooks.title: Equipment logbooks
equipment-logbooks.caption: Each major item should have a record of its serial number, service dates, repairs and faults.
equipment-logbooks.body:
In short: Each major item should have a record of its serial number, service dates, repairs and faults.

Keep A Record

Each major item should have a record of its serial number, service dates, repairs and faults. This shows when it is due for servicing and helps predict failures.

Write clear, dated entries with your name. Missing records make it hard to prove equipment is safe.

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

If it is not written, it did not happen.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about equipment logbooks?

If it is not written, it did not happen.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cleaning-equipment-between-cases.title: Cleaning equipment between cases
cleaning-equipment-between-cases.caption: Surfaces that staff and patients touch, such as tables, light handles, monitors, trolleys and pendants, are wiped down with a suitable disinfectant between cases.
cleaning-equipment-between-cases.body:
In short: Surfaces that staff and patients touch, such as tables, light handles, monitors, trolleys and pendants, are wiped down with a suitable disinfectant between cases.

Wipe Down

Surfaces that staff and patients touch, such as tables, light handles, monitors, trolleys and pendants, are wiped down with a suitable disinfectant between cases.

Use the right product and the right contact time, and unplug electrical equipment before cleaning unless the maker says otherwise.

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

Wipe, wait, then dry.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cleaning equipment between cases?

Wipe, wait, then dry.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

reporting-faulty-equipment.title: Reporting faulty equipment
reporting-faulty-equipment.caption: If equipment behaves oddly, stop using it if safe to do so, tell the team and report it as per local policy.
reporting-faulty-equipment.body:
In short: If equipment behaves oddly, stop using it if safe to do so, tell the team and report it as per local policy.

Speak Up

If equipment behaves oddly, stop using it if safe to do so, tell the team and report it as per local policy. Do not try repairs unless you are trained and authorised.

Note what happened, when, and what settings were in use. This helps the engineer.

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

Stop, label, report.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about reporting faulty equipment?

Stop, label, report.

out-of-service-tagging.title: Out-of-service tagging
out-of-service-tagging.caption: A faulty item should be clearly tagged "out of service" and moved away from working equipment.
out-of-service-tagging.body:
In short: A faulty item should be clearly tagged "out of service" and moved away from working equipment.

Do Not Use

A faulty item should be clearly tagged "out of service" and moved away from working equipment. The tag should state the fault, date and who reported it.

This stops the item being picked up by someone else in a rush. Remove the tag only once an engineer clears the item.

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

A clear tag prevents accidents.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about out-of-service tagging?

A clear tag prevents accidents.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

battery-care.title: Battery care
battery-care.caption: Many theatre devices rely on batteries as backup, such as monitors, laryngoscopes and suction units.
battery-care.body:
In short: Many theatre devices rely on batteries as backup, such as monitors, laryngoscopes and suction units.

Keep It Charged

Many theatre devices rely on batteries as backup, such as monitors, laryngoscopes and suction units. Weak batteries fail when most needed.

Keep devices on charge when not in use, check battery indicators in the daily checks, and replace batteries according to the maker's advice.

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

Charge before you need it.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about battery care?

Charge before you need it.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

inspecting-cables-and-plugs.title: Inspecting cables and plugs
inspecting-cables-and-plugs.caption: A quick list on inspecting cables and plugs: Look for cuts, kinks or exposed wire; Check plug pins for bending or burn marks.
inspecting-cables-and-plugs.body:
In short: A quick list on inspecting cables and plugs: Look for cuts, kinks or exposed wire; Check plug pins for bending or burn marks.

Inspecting cables and plugs

  • Look for cuts, kinks or exposed wire
  • Check plug pins for bending or burn marks
  • Check the connector is tight at the machine
  • Never pull a plug out by the cable
  • Report damaged leads for repair

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

Damaged cable, damaged patient.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Inspecting cables and plugs".

Look for cuts, kinks or exposed wire; Check plug pins for bending or burn marks; Check the connector is tight at the machine; Never pull a plug out by the cable; Report damaged leads for repair.

calibration-of-devices.title: Calibration of devices
calibration-of-devices.caption: Calibration compares a device with a known standard and adjusts it so readings are accurate.
calibration-of-devices.body:
In short: Calibration compares a device with a known standard and adjusts it so readings are accurate.

Accurate Readings

Calibration compares a device with a known standard and adjusts it so readings are accurate. Examples include vaporisers, monitors and weighing scales.

It is usually done by trained engineers on a schedule. A device that is out of date for calibration may give unreliable values.

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

A device can be working but wrong.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about calibration of devices?

A device can be working but wrong.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

autoclave-routine-maintenance.title: Autoclave routine maintenance
autoclave-routine-maintenance.caption: Autoclaves need regular checks such as cleaning the chamber and drain, checking door seals and gauges, and servicing by qualified staff.
autoclave-routine-maintenance.body:
In short: Autoclaves need regular checks such as cleaning the chamber and drain, checking door seals and gauges, and servicing by qualified staff.

Keeping Sterilisers Safe

Autoclaves need regular checks such as cleaning the chamber and drain, checking door seals and gauges, and servicing by qualified staff.

Daily tests and records show whether the machine is working. A leaking seal or poor steam supply can cause failed cycles.

Why it matters

Theatre equipment fails at the worst moment if it is not checked and serviced. Routine care, good records and early reporting keep patients and staff safe.

Remember

Check seals and gauges daily.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about autoclave routine maintenance?

Check seals and gauges daily.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

parts-of-the-operating-table.title: Parts of the operating table
parts-of-the-operating-table.caption: An operating table usually has a top that is divided into head, back, seat and leg sections.
parts-of-the-operating-table.body:
In short: An operating table usually has a top that is divided into head, back, seat and leg sections.

Know The Table

An operating table usually has a top that is divided into head, back, seat and leg sections. These can be tilted, raised or lowered, and the whole table can tilt head-down or head-up.

Controls may be electric, hydraulic or manual. Learn which one your table uses.

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Know the controls before the patient.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about parts of the operating table?

Know the controls before the patient.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

locking-the-table-safely.title: Locking the table safely
locking-the-table-safely.caption: Before moving a patient onto the table, make sure the brakes or locking mechanism are on and the table is at a safe height.
locking-the-table-safely.body:
In short: Before moving a patient onto the table, make sure the brakes or locking mechanism are on and the table is at a safe height.

Brakes And Locks

Before moving a patient onto the table, make sure the brakes or locking mechanism are on and the table is at a safe height. Trolleys should be locked next to the table when transferring.

Check locks again after any change of position, since an unstable table can cause falls.

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Lock, then transfer.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about locking the table safely?

Lock, then transfer.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

safe-patient-transfer.title: Safe patient transfer
safe-patient-transfer.caption: A quick list on safe patient transfer: Check table and trolley brakes are on; Use enough staff and a slide sheet or board.
safe-patient-transfer.body:
In short: A quick list on safe patient transfer: Check table and trolley brakes are on; Use enough staff and a slide sheet or board.

Safe patient transfer

  • Check table and trolley brakes are on
  • Use enough staff and a slide sheet or board
  • Explain to the patient if they are awake
  • Protect the airway, drips and catheters
  • Anaesthetist leads on the head and neck

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Move together on one command.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Safe patient transfer".

Check table and trolley brakes are on; Use enough staff and a slide sheet or board; Explain to the patient if they are awake; Protect the airway, drips and catheters; Anaesthetist leads on the head and neck.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

positioning-supports.title: Positioning supports
positioning-supports.caption: Positioning aids include arm boards, gel pads, head rings, side supports, leg holders and foot boards.
positioning-supports.body:
In short: Positioning aids include arm boards, gel pads, head rings, side supports, leg holders and foot boards.

Pads And Arm Boards

Positioning aids include arm boards, gel pads, head rings, side supports, leg holders and foot boards. They support the body and protect pressure points.

Check they are secure, clean and the right size. Arms placed on boards must not be pushed past a comfortable position.

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Support, pad and check.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about positioning supports?

Support, pad and check.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

lithotomy-position-care.title: Lithotomy position care
lithotomy-position-care.caption: In lithotomy, the legs are raised in supports for gynaecological, urological and some rectal surgery.
lithotomy-position-care.body:
In short: In lithotomy, the legs are raised in supports for gynaecological, urological and some rectal surgery.

Legs In Supports

In lithotomy, the legs are raised in supports for gynaecological, urological and some rectal surgery. Both legs are lifted and lowered together and slowly.

Pad the supports, avoid pressure on the calves and nerves, and watch for pinched fingers when the table sections move.

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Raise and lower both legs together.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about lithotomy position care?

Raise and lower both legs together.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

prone-position-safety.title: Prone position safety
prone-position-safety.caption: The prone position places the patient on the stomach, usually after anaesthesia.
prone-position-safety.body:
In short: The prone position places the patient on the stomach, usually after anaesthesia.

Face Down

The prone position places the patient on the stomach, usually after anaesthesia. Many staff are needed to turn the patient, with one person protecting the airway and tubes.

Pad the chest, hips and knees, keep the eyes free of pressure and watch the neck position. Breathing and circulation can be affected.

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Protect the face, eyes and chest.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about prone position safety?

Protect the face, eyes and chest.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

lateral-position-care.title: Lateral position care
lateral-position-care.caption: In the lateral position, the patient lies on one side, often for kidney or chest operations.
lateral-position-care.body:
In short: In the lateral position, the patient lies on one side, often for kidney or chest operations.

Lying On The Side

In the lateral position, the patient lies on one side, often for kidney or chest operations. Supports hold the back and hips, and a pillow lies between the knees.

Check the dependent shoulder, arm and ear for pressure and keep the neck in line with the spine.

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Keep the neck in line.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about lateral position care?

Keep the neck in line.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

head-down-and-head-up-tilts.title: Head-down and head-up tilts
head-down-and-head-up-tilts.caption: Trendelenburg tilts the patient head-down.
head-down-and-head-up-tilts.body:
In short: Trendelenburg tilts the patient head-down.

Tilting The Table

Trendelenburg tilts the patient head-down. Reverse Trendelenburg tilts head-up. Both help surgeons see by shifting organs, but they alter blood flow and breathing.

Tilt slowly and tell the anaesthetist before moving. Check the patient is not sliding on the table.

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Warn the anaesthetist before tilting.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about head-down and head-up tilts?

Warn the anaesthetist before tilting.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

features-of-theatre-lights.title: Features of theatre lights
features-of-theatre-lights.caption: Theatre lights give bright, white, shadow-free light on the surgical site.
features-of-theatre-lights.body:
In short: Theatre lights give bright, white, shadow-free light on the surgical site.

Good Light

Theatre lights give bright, white, shadow-free light on the surgical site. They have adjustable brightness and focus, and double heads reduce shadows when one is blocked.

Lights should keep colours looking natural so that tissue and blood can be identified correctly.

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Light should show true colours.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about features of theatre lights?

Light should show true colours.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

handling-and-positioning-lights.title: Handling and positioning lights
handling-and-positioning-lights.caption: A quick list on handling and positioning lights: Use the sterile handle or cover as directed; Move slowly to avoid bumping heads.
handling-and-positioning-lights.body:
In short: A quick list on handling and positioning lights: Use the sterile handle or cover as directed; Move slowly to avoid bumping heads.

Handling and positioning lights

  • Use the sterile handle or cover as directed
  • Move slowly to avoid bumping heads
  • Focus the beam at the incision site
  • Keep the light away from drapes when hot
  • Report flickering or failed bulbs at once

Why it matters

The table and light are in every operation. Safe positioning and handling prevent nerve injury, pressure damage and falls, and good lighting helps the surgeon.

Remember

Good lighting saves time and errors.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Handling and positioning lights".

Use the sterile handle or cover as directed; Move slowly to avoid bumping heads; Focus the beam at the incision site; Keep the light away from drapes when hot; Report flickering or failed bulbs at once.

implant-and-prosthesis.title: Implant and prosthesis
implant-and-prosthesis.caption: An implant is a device placed inside the body, often for a long time, such as a screw or mesh.
implant-and-prosthesis.body:
In short: An implant is a device placed inside the body, often for a long time, such as a screw or mesh.

What The Words Mean

An implant is a device placed inside the body, often for a long time, such as a screw or mesh. A prosthesis replaces a body part, such as a hip joint or an artificial limb.

Both are medical devices. They must be sterile, correct and recorded.

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Implants stay, so be certain.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about implant and prosthesis?

Implants stay, so be certain.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

common-implant-materials.title: Common implant materials
common-implant-materials.caption: Implants are often made from stainless steel, titanium, special plastics or ceramics.
common-implant-materials.body:
In short: Implants are often made from stainless steel, titanium, special plastics or ceramics.

What They Are Made Of

Implants are often made from stainless steel, titanium, special plastics or ceramics. Materials are chosen for strength, weight and how well the body tolerates them.

Some patients are allergic to metals such as nickel, so tell the team about any known allergy.

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Know the patient's allergy status.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about common implant materials?

Know the patient's allergy status.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

plates-and-screws.title: Plates and screws
plates-and-screws.caption: Plates and screws hold fractured bone in position while it heals.
plates-and-screws.body:
In short: Plates and screws hold fractured bone in position while it heals.

Holding Bone

Plates and screws hold fractured bone in position while it heals. Different plates suit different bones, and screw length and thread type matter.

The sets often include measuring devices, drill guides and screwdrivers. Keep the screws organised by size so the surgeon gets the right one.

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Right size, right screw.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about plates and screws?

Right size, right screw.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

intramedullary-nails.title: Intramedullary nails
intramedullary-nails.caption: An intramedullary nail is a rod passed down the hollow centre of a long bone, such as the femur or tibia, to hold a fracture.
intramedullary-nails.body:
In short: An intramedullary nail is a rod passed down the hollow centre of a long bone, such as the femur or tibia, to hold a fracture.

Inside The Bone

An intramedullary nail is a rod passed down the hollow centre of a long bone, such as the femur or tibia, to hold a fracture. Locking screws pass through the bone and nail to hold it.

Sets are large with many parts, so check that every item and size is present.

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Check every piece of the nail set.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about intramedullary nails?

Check every piece of the nail set.

joint-replacement-components.title: Joint replacement components
joint-replacement-components.caption: Hip and knee replacements use several parts that must fit together, such as a stem, a head and a socket for the hip.
joint-replacement-components.body:
In short: Hip and knee replacements use several parts that must fit together, such as a stem, a head and a socket for the hip.

Hip And Knee Parts

Hip and knee replacements use several parts that must fit together, such as a stem, a head and a socket for the hip. Trial components help the surgeon pick the correct size.

Sizes and sides, left or right, are checked carefully. Bone cement may be used.

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Check size and side twice.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about joint replacement components?

Check size and side twice.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

handling-sterile-implants.title: Handling sterile implants
handling-sterile-implants.caption: A quick list on handling sterile implants: Open only when the surgeon asks for it; Check name, size, side and expiry.
handling-sterile-implants.body:
In short: A quick list on handling sterile implants: Open only when the surgeon asks for it; Check name, size, side and expiry.

Handling sterile implants

  • Open only when the surgeon asks for it
  • Check name, size, side and expiry
  • Pass without touching the implant surface
  • If dropped on the floor, treat it as contaminated
  • Do not reuse single-use implants

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Never open the wrong implant.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Handling sterile implants".

Open only when the surgeon asks for it; Check name, size, side and expiry; Pass without touching the implant surface; If dropped on the floor, treat it as contaminated; Do not reuse single-use implants.

implant-records-and-traceability.title: Implant records and traceability
implant-records-and-traceability.caption: A quick list on implant records and traceability: Record the type, size and batch number; Store the sticker or label in the notes.
implant-records-and-traceability.body:
In short: A quick list on implant records and traceability: Record the type, size and batch number; Store the sticker or label in the notes.

Implant records and traceability

  • Record the type, size and batch number
  • Store the sticker or label in the notes
  • Note the manufacturer and expiry
  • Log the implant in the register as required
  • Records help if a recall occurs

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Record every implant.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Implant records and traceability".

Record the type, size and batch number; Store the sticker or label in the notes; Note the manufacturer and expiry; Log the implant in the register as required; Records help if a recall occurs.

surgical-mesh-in-hernia-repair.title: Surgical mesh in hernia repair
surgical-mesh-in-hernia-repair.caption: A surgical mesh is a net-like implant placed to strengthen a weak area, such as in hernia repair.
surgical-mesh-in-hernia-repair.body:
In short: A surgical mesh is a net-like implant placed to strengthen a weak area, such as in hernia repair.

Support For Weak Walls

A surgical mesh is a net-like implant placed to strengthen a weak area, such as in hernia repair. Meshes differ in material, size and shape.

The mesh must be sterile and must be handled with gloves that are clean of powder or talc. Keep it away from skin contact.

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Handle mesh only with clean gloves.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about surgical mesh in hernia repair?

Handle mesh only with clean gloves.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

bone-cement-basics.title: Bone cement basics
bone-cement-basics.caption: Bone cement is mixed from a powder and a liquid in theatre.
bone-cement-basics.body:
In short: Bone cement is mixed from a powder and a liquid in theatre.

Fixing Prostheses

Bone cement is mixed from a powder and a liquid in theatre. It sets by a chemical reaction, giving off heat, and must be used within its working time.

Fumes are irritating and the liquid can affect blood pressure in some patients. Mix as per the maker's instruction with good ventilation.

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Watch the clock when mixing cement.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about bone cement basics?

Watch the clock when mixing cement.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

implants-and-diathermy.title: Implants and diathermy
implants-and-diathermy.caption: Patients may have implanted devices such as pacemakers, which can be affected by diathermy current.
implants-and-diathermy.body:
In short: Patients may have implanted devices such as pacemakers, which can be affected by diathermy current.

Metal And Current

Patients may have implanted devices such as pacemakers, which can be affected by diathermy current. Metal implants can also conduct heat.

Tell the surgeon and anaesthetist early, and follow local advice on the placement of diathermy pads and use of bipolar settings.

Why it matters

Implants stay in the patient, so correct selection, sterile handling and clear records matter long after the operation has finished.

Remember

Tell the team about any implant.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about implants and diathermy?

Tell the team about any implant.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

what-a-biomedical-engineer-does.title: What a biomedical engineer does
what-a-biomedical-engineer-does.caption: Biomedical engineers install, test, maintain and repair medical equipment.
what-a-biomedical-engineer-does.body:
In short: Biomedical engineers install, test, maintain and repair medical equipment.

Behind The Machines

Biomedical engineers install, test, maintain and repair medical equipment. They also advise on purchases and train staff in safe use.

They rely on theatre staff to report faults accurately, so work as a team and give clear details.

Why it matters

Understanding the basic science behind theatre machines helps staff use them safely, spot problems early and communicate well with biomedical engineers.

Remember

Engineers and clinicians work together.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about what a biomedical engineer does?

Engineers and clinicians work together.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

electrical-earthing.title: Electrical earthing
electrical-earthing.caption: Earthing gives stray electrical current a safe path to the ground, so it does not pass through a person.
electrical-earthing.body:
In short: Earthing gives stray electrical current a safe path to the ground, so it does not pass through a person.

A Safe Path For Faults

Earthing gives stray electrical current a safe path to the ground, so it does not pass through a person. Metal cases on many devices are connected to earth through the plug.

Never cut off or bypass the earth pin, and report loose or damaged sockets.

Why it matters

Understanding the basic science behind theatre machines helps staff use them safely, spot problems early and communicate well with biomedical engineers.

Remember

The earth pin protects people.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about electrical earthing?

The earth pin protects people.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

leakage-current.title: Leakage current
leakage-current.caption: All electrical equipment has a tiny leakage current.
leakage-current.body:
In short: All electrical equipment has a tiny leakage current.

Small Currents

All electrical equipment has a tiny leakage current. In theatre this matters because patients may be unconscious, and devices touch the heart or skin directly.

Engineers test equipment to ensure leakage remains within safe limits. Damaged or wet equipment can raise leakage.

Why it matters

Understanding the basic science behind theatre machines helps staff use them safely, spot problems early and communicate well with biomedical engineers.

Remember

Wet or damaged kit raises risk.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about leakage current?

Wet or damaged kit raises risk.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

pulse-oximeter-principle.title: Pulse oximeter principle
pulse-oximeter-principle.caption: A pulse oximeter shines two types of light through tissue, usually a finger or ear.
pulse-oximeter-principle.body:
In short: A pulse oximeter shines two types of light through tissue, usually a finger or ear.

Light Through The Finger

A pulse oximeter shines two types of light through tissue, usually a finger or ear. Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood absorb the lights differently, so the device estimates oxygen saturation.

Cold hands, nail polish, movement and poor circulation can give unreliable readings.

Why it matters

Understanding the basic science behind theatre machines helps staff use them safely, spot problems early and communicate well with biomedical engineers.

Remember

Poor signal can mean a poor reading.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about pulse oximeter principle?

Poor signal can mean a poor reading.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

diathermy-principle.title: Diathermy principle
diathermy-principle.caption: Diathermy passes high-frequency current through tissue to cut or coagulate.
diathermy-principle.body:
In short: Diathermy passes high-frequency current through tissue to cut or coagulate.

Heat From Current

Diathermy passes high-frequency current through tissue to cut or coagulate. In monopolar mode, current passes through the patient to a return pad. Bipolar mode passes between two tips and does not use a pad.

A poorly attached pad can cause burns.

Why it matters

Understanding the basic science behind theatre machines helps staff use them safely, spot problems early and communicate well with biomedical engineers.

Remember

Good pad contact prevents burns.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about diathermy principle?

Good pad contact prevents burns.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

suction-unit-basics.title: Suction unit basics
suction-unit-basics.caption: A quick list on suction unit basics: Collection jar to hold fluid; Tubing linking patient to jar.
suction-unit-basics.body:
In short: A quick list on suction unit basics: Collection jar to hold fluid; Tubing linking patient to jar.

Suction unit basics

  • Collection jar to hold fluid
  • Tubing linking patient to jar
  • Vacuum pump or pipeline source
  • Filter or overflow protection
  • Pressure control and gauge

Why it matters

Understanding the basic science behind theatre machines helps staff use them safely, spot problems early and communicate well with biomedical engineers.

Remember

Test suction before every list.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Suction unit basics".

Collection jar to hold fluid; Tubing linking patient to jar; Vacuum pump or pipeline source; Filter or overflow protection; Pressure control and gauge.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

defibrillator-basics.title: Defibrillator basics
defibrillator-basics.caption: A defibrillator delivers a controlled electric shock to treat certain life-threatening heart rhythms.
defibrillator-basics.body:
In short: A defibrillator delivers a controlled electric shock to treat certain life-threatening heart rhythms.

Restarting The Heart

A defibrillator delivers a controlled electric shock to treat certain life-threatening heart rhythms. Modern units analyse the rhythm and guide the user.

Staff in theatre should know where it is kept, how to switch it on and how to attach the pads. Check it daily according to policy.

Why it matters

Understanding the basic science behind theatre machines helps staff use them safely, spot problems early and communicate well with biomedical engineers.

Remember

Know where the defibrillator is.

There are usually four small parathyroid glands behind the thyroid. They control blood calcium.

After thyroid surgery, damaged glands can cause low calcium: tingling around the mouth, cramps and spasms. Report these signs early.

This membrane lies between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages, just below the vocal cords, and is thin and near the skin.

The triangle of safety lies on the side of the chest. Its borders are the front edge of latissimus dorsi, the side edge of pectoralis major and a line at about nipple level.

Drains are usually placed here, in the fifth intercostal space area.

The pleura covers the lung and lines the chest wall. At the base, the costodiaphragmatic recess is a gap the lung does not fill in quiet breathing.

Fluid collects here first, and drains are placed to reach it when the patient sits or lies as needed.

The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical than the left.

Inhaled objects tend to enter the right lung, and a tracheal tube pushed in too far often ends up in the right main bronchus, leaving the left lung under-ventilated.

The coronary arteries arise from the aortic root just above the aortic valve. The left main divides into the anterior descending and circumflex branches; the right supplies the right heart.

The left ventricle fills most during diastole, so low diastolic pressure risks ischaemia.

The inguinal canal is an oblique passage about 4 cm long above the inguinal ligament. It carries the spermatic cord in men and the round ligament in women.

The ilioinguinal nerve runs along it, and the canal is a common place for hernias.

  • Common bile duct runs to the duodenum
  • It meets the pancreatic duct at the ampulla

Why it matters

Most general surgery happens in the abdomen. Knowing wall layers, blood supply and organ relations helps you anticipate steps, instruments and complications.

Remember

Bile flows down to duodenum.

appendix-and-its-position.title: Appendix and its position
appendix-and-its-position.caption: The appendix base lies at the point where the three taenia coli of the caecum meet.
appendix-and-its-position.body:
In short: The appendix base lies at the point where the three taenia coli of the caecum meet.

Variable Tip

The appendix base lies at the point where the three taenia coli of the caecum meet. The tip may lie behind the caecum, in the pelvis or elsewhere.

Because its position varies, pain may be felt in different places, not only the right lower abdomen.

Why it matters

Most general surgery happens in the abdomen. Knowing wall layers, blood supply and organ relations helps you anticipate steps, instruments and complications.

Remember

Base is fixed, tip wanders.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about appendix and its position?

Base is fixed, tip wanders.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

spleen-and-injury.title: Spleen and injury
spleen-and-injury.caption: The spleen sits under the left ribs, roughly ribs 9 to 11, and is soft and rich in blood.
spleen-and-injury.body:
In short: The spleen sits under the left ribs, roughly ribs 9 to 11, and is soft and rich in blood.

Fragile Organ

The spleen sits under the left ribs, roughly ribs 9 to 11, and is soft and rich in blood.

It is often injured in trauma and may cause major bleeding. People without a spleen are more prone to serious infection and usually need vaccines.

Why it matters

Most general surgery happens in the abdomen. Knowing wall layers, blood supply and organ relations helps you anticipate steps, instruments and complications.

Remember

Left rib injury, think spleen.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about spleen and injury?

Left rib injury, think spleen.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

bones-and-joints-of-the-pelvis.title: Bones and joints of the pelvis
bones-and-joints-of-the-pelvis.caption: The pelvis is formed by two hip bones, the sacrum and the coccyx.
bones-and-joints-of-the-pelvis.body:
In short: The pelvis is formed by two hip bones, the sacrum and the coccyx.

The Bony Ring

The pelvis is formed by two hip bones, the sacrum and the coccyx. They join at the sacroiliac joints and the pubic symphysis.

The female pelvis is usually wider and shallower to allow childbirth. Pelvic fractures can bleed heavily.

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

Ring breaks in more than one place.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about bones and joints of the pelvis?

Ring breaks in more than one place.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

pelvic-floor-muscles.title: Pelvic floor muscles
pelvic-floor-muscles.caption: Levator ani and related muscles form a sling that supports the bladder, uterus or prostate, and rectum.
pelvic-floor-muscles.body:
In short: Levator ani and related muscles form a sling that supports the bladder, uterus or prostate, and rectum.

Support Base

Levator ani and related muscles form a sling that supports the bladder, uterus or prostate, and rectum.

Childbirth, chronic straining and ageing can weaken it, causing leaks or prolapse. Pelvic floor exercises help many people.

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

A hammock for pelvic organs.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about pelvic floor muscles?

A hammock for pelvic organs.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

female-pelvic-organs.title: Female pelvic organs
female-pelvic-organs.caption: A quick list on female pelvic organs: Bladder lies in front; Uterus sits in the middle, with the cervix below.
female-pelvic-organs.body:
In short: A quick list on female pelvic organs: Bladder lies in front; Uterus sits in the middle, with the cervix below.

Female pelvic organs

  • Bladder lies in front
  • Uterus sits in the middle, with the cervix below
  • Fallopian tubes and ovaries at each side
  • Vagina leads down to the outside
  • Rectum lies behind the uterus

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

Bladder, uterus, rectum - front to back.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Female pelvic organs".

Bladder lies in front; Uterus sits in the middle, with the cervix below; Fallopian tubes and ovaries at each side; Vagina leads down to the outside; Rectum lies behind the uterus.

ureter-near-the-uterine-artery.title: Ureter near the uterine artery
ureter-near-the-uterine-artery.caption: In the pelvis, the ureter passes close to and beneath the uterine artery, like water under a bridge.
ureter-near-the-uterine-artery.body:
In short: In the pelvis, the ureter passes close to and beneath the uterine artery, like water under a bridge.

Water Under The Bridge

In the pelvis, the ureter passes close to and beneath the uterine artery, like water under a bridge.

This is a classic risk during hysterectomy: clamping the artery can injure the ureter. Surgeons trace it and avoid blind clamping.

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

Ureter goes under the artery.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ureter near the uterine artery?

Ureter goes under the artery.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

blood-supply-of-the-uterus.title: Blood supply of the uterus
blood-supply-of-the-uterus.caption: The uterine artery comes from the internal iliac artery and joins branches from the ovarian artery.
blood-supply-of-the-uterus.body:
In short: The uterine artery comes from the internal iliac artery and joins branches from the ovarian artery.

Rich But Risky

The uterine artery comes from the internal iliac artery and joins branches from the ovarian artery.

Because the supply is rich, bleeding can be heavy at caesarean section or after childbirth. Surgeons may ligate vessels to control it.

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

Rich supply means rapid blood loss.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about blood supply of the uterus?

Rich supply means rapid blood loss.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

prostate-gland.title: Prostate gland
prostate-gland.caption: The prostate surrounds the first part of the urethra just below the bladder.
prostate-gland.body:
In short: The prostate surrounds the first part of the urethra just below the bladder.

Around The Urethra

The prostate surrounds the first part of the urethra just below the bladder.

With age it often enlarges, narrowing the urethra and causing slow urine flow. Nerves needed for erection run beside it, so surgery is carefully planned.

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

Enlarged prostate blocks the flow.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about prostate gland?

Enlarged prostate blocks the flow.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

urinary-bladder.title: Urinary bladder
urinary-bladder.caption: An empty bladder sits behind the pubic bones; when full it rises into the abdomen.
urinary-bladder.body:
In short: An empty bladder sits behind the pubic bones; when full it rises into the abdomen.

Stretchy Store

An empty bladder sits behind the pubic bones; when full it rises into the abdomen.

This lets a suprapubic catheter be placed above the pubis without entering the peritoneum. Empty the bladder before pelvic surgery to protect it.

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

Full bladder rises, empty bladder hides.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about urinary bladder?

Full bladder rises, empty bladder hides.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

pudendal-nerve-block.title: Pudendal nerve block
pudendal-nerve-block.caption: The pudendal nerve comes from sacral roots S2 to S4 and supplies the perineum and part of the pelvic floor.
pudendal-nerve-block.body:
In short: The pudendal nerve comes from sacral roots S2 to S4 and supplies the perineum and part of the pelvic floor.

Birth Analgesia

The pudendal nerve comes from sacral roots S2 to S4 and supplies the perineum and part of the pelvic floor.

An obstetrician may block it near the ischial spine to numb the area for assisted vaginal delivery or repair.

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

Ischial spine is the landmark.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about pudendal nerve block?

Ischial spine is the landmark.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

rectum-and-anal-canal.title: Rectum and anal canal
rectum-and-anal-canal.caption: A quick list on rectum and anal canal: Rectum follows the curve of the sacrum; Anal canal is the last part, about 4 cm.
rectum-and-anal-canal.body:
In short: A quick list on rectum and anal canal: Rectum follows the curve of the sacrum; Anal canal is the last part, about 4 cm.

Rectum and anal canal

  • Rectum follows the curve of the sacrum
  • Anal canal is the last part, about 4 cm
  • Internal sphincter is involuntary muscle
  • External sphincter is voluntary muscle
  • Dentate line marks a change in nerve supply

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

Two sphincters keep control.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Rectum and anal canal".

Rectum follows the curve of the sacrum; Anal canal is the last part, about 4 cm; Internal sphincter is involuntary muscle; External sphincter is voluntary muscle; Dentate line marks a change in nerve supply.

pelvic-inlet-and-outlet.title: Pelvic inlet and outlet
pelvic-inlet-and-outlet.caption: A quick list on pelvic inlet and outlet: Inlet (brim) - top opening of the true pelvis; Cavity - the canal between inlet and outlet.
pelvic-inlet-and-outlet.body:
In short: A quick list on pelvic inlet and outlet: Inlet (brim) - top opening of the true pelvis; Cavity - the canal between inlet and outlet.

Pelvic inlet and outlet

  • Inlet (brim) - top opening of the true pelvis
  • Cavity - the canal between inlet and outlet
  • Outlet - bottom opening, bordered by the coccyx
  • Baby's head enters at the inlet and turns inside

Why it matters

Pelvic anatomy is central to obstetric, gynaecological, urological and colorectal surgery, where vessels, ureters and nerves lie close together.

Remember

Inlet, cavity, outlet.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Pelvic inlet and outlet".

Inlet (brim) - top opening of the true pelvis; Cavity - the canal between inlet and outlet; Outlet - bottom opening, bordered by the coccyx; Baby's head enters at the inlet and turns inside.

brachial-plexus-layout.title: Brachial plexus layout
brachial-plexus-layout.caption: A quick list on brachial plexus layout: Roots - C5 to T1; Trunks - upper, middle, lower.
brachial-plexus-layout.body:
In short: A quick list on brachial plexus layout: Roots - C5 to T1; Trunks - upper, middle, lower.

Brachial plexus layout

  • Roots - C5 to T1
  • Trunks - upper, middle, lower
  • Divisions - anterior and posterior
  • Cords - lateral, posterior, medial
  • Branches - the main arm nerves

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

Roots, trunks, divisions, cords, branches.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Brachial plexus layout".

Roots - C5 to T1; Trunks - upper, middle, lower; Divisions - anterior and posterior; Cords - lateral, posterior, medial; Branches - the main arm nerves.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

plexus-in-the-neck.title: Plexus in the neck
plexus-in-the-neck.caption: The brachial plexus leaves the neck between the anterior and middle scalene muscles and passes above the first rib and under the collarbone.
plexus-in-the-neck.body:
In short: The brachial plexus leaves the neck between the anterior and middle scalene muscles and passes above the first rib and under the collarbone.

Block Target

The brachial plexus leaves the neck between the anterior and middle scalene muscles and passes above the first rib and under the collarbone.

Nerve blocks at these levels numb the arm for shoulder and arm surgery, often guided by ultrasound.

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

Plexus passes between scalenes.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about plexus in the neck?

Plexus passes between scalenes.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

axillary-nerve.title: Axillary nerve
axillary-nerve.caption: The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck of the humerus and supplies the deltoid and a patch of skin over the shoulder.
axillary-nerve.body:
In short: The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck of the humerus and supplies the deltoid and a patch of skin over the shoulder.

Deltoid Nerve

The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck of the humerus and supplies the deltoid and a patch of skin over the shoulder.

Shoulder dislocation or neck-of-humerus fracture can injure it, causing weak shoulder lift and numbness there.

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

Check the badge-patch sensation.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about axillary nerve?

Check the badge-patch sensation.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

radial-nerve.title: Radial nerve
radial-nerve.caption: The radial nerve spirals around the humerus in the spiral groove and supplies the muscles that extend the wrist and fingers.
radial-nerve.body:
In short: The radial nerve spirals around the humerus in the spiral groove and supplies the muscles that extend the wrist and fingers.

Wrist Drop

The radial nerve spirals around the humerus in the spiral groove and supplies the muscles that extend the wrist and fingers.

Fracture of the shaft of the humerus can injure it, causing wrist drop. Check wrist extension before and after treatment.

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

Humerus fracture, test the wrist.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about radial nerve?

Humerus fracture, test the wrist.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

median-nerve.title: Median nerve
median-nerve.caption: The median nerve passes through the carpal tunnel at the wrist and supplies the thumb side of the hand and the muscles of the thumb base.
median-nerve.body:
In short: The median nerve passes through the carpal tunnel at the wrist and supplies the thumb side of the hand and the muscles of the thumb base.

Carpal Tunnel

The median nerve passes through the carpal tunnel at the wrist and supplies the thumb side of the hand and the muscles of the thumb base.

Compression there causes tingling in the thumb and first fingers, often worse at night.

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

Thumb tingling, think carpal tunnel.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about median nerve?

Thumb tingling, think carpal tunnel.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

ulnar-nerve-and-the-funny-bone.title: Ulnar nerve and the funny bone
ulnar-nerve-and-the-funny-bone.caption: The ulnar nerve passes behind the medial epicondyle, close to the skin, where a bump causes a sharp tingle.
ulnar-nerve-and-the-funny-bone.body:
In short: The ulnar nerve passes behind the medial epicondyle, close to the skin, where a bump causes a sharp tingle.

Funny Bone

The ulnar nerve passes behind the medial epicondyle, close to the skin, where a bump causes a sharp tingle.

Pressure on the elbow during long surgery can injure it. Pad the elbow and avoid resting it on hard edges.

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

Pad the elbow.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ulnar nerve and the funny bone?

Pad the elbow.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cubital-fossa-contents.title: Cubital fossa contents
cubital-fossa-contents.caption: A quick list on cubital fossa contents: Triangle in front of the elbow; Medial to lateral: median nerve, brachial artery.
cubital-fossa-contents.body:
In short: A quick list on cubital fossa contents: Triangle in front of the elbow; Medial to lateral: median nerve, brachial artery.

Cubital fossa contents

  • Triangle in front of the elbow
  • Medial to lateral: median nerve, brachial artery
  • Then biceps tendon, then radial nerve
  • Median cubital vein lies on top

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

Nerve, artery, tendon, nerve.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Cubital fossa contents".

Triangle in front of the elbow; Medial to lateral: median nerve, brachial artery; Then biceps tendon, then radial nerve; Median cubital vein lies on top.

radial-and-ulnar-arteries.title: Radial and ulnar arteries
radial-and-ulnar-arteries.caption: Both arteries supply the hand through arches in the palm.
radial-and-ulnar-arteries.body:
In short: Both arteries supply the hand through arches in the palm.

Hand Supply

Both arteries supply the hand through arches in the palm. If one is blocked, the other often compensates.

The Allen test checks this collateral flow before radial artery puncture, though it is not perfectly reliable.

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

Check the hand has a backup supply.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about radial and ulnar arteries?

Check the hand has a backup supply.

rotator-cuff-muscles.title: Rotator cuff muscles
rotator-cuff-muscles.caption: A quick list on rotator cuff muscles: Supraspinatus - starts arm abduction; Infraspinatus - rotates arm outward.
rotator-cuff-muscles.body:
In short: A quick list on rotator cuff muscles: Supraspinatus - starts arm abduction; Infraspinatus - rotates arm outward.

Rotator cuff muscles

  • Supraspinatus - starts arm abduction
  • Infraspinatus - rotates arm outward
  • Teres minor - rotates arm outward
  • Subscapularis - rotates arm inward

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

SITS holds the shoulder.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Rotator cuff muscles".

Supraspinatus - starts arm abduction; Infraspinatus - rotates arm outward; Teres minor - rotates arm outward; Subscapularis - rotates arm inward.

veins-for-cannulation.title: Veins for cannulation
veins-for-cannulation.caption: The cephalic vein runs on the thumb side and the basilic vein on the little finger side.
veins-for-cannulation.body:
In short: The cephalic vein runs on the thumb side and the basilic vein on the little finger side.

Arm Veins

The cephalic vein runs on the thumb side and the basilic vein on the little finger side. They join at the elbow through the median cubital vein.

In the elbow, the brachial artery lies close, so cannulate with care and avoid inadvertent arterial puncture.

Why it matters

Arm anatomy guides nerve blocks, cannulation, positioning and orthopaedic surgery. Nerve injury from poor positioning is preventable with good knowledge.

Remember

Pulsing blood means artery.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about veins for cannulation?

Pulsing blood means artery.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

femoral-triangle-contents.title: Femoral triangle contents
femoral-triangle-contents.caption: A quick list on femoral triangle contents: Edges: inguinal ligament, sartorius, adductor; Contents from lateral to medial:.
femoral-triangle-contents.body:
In short: A quick list on femoral triangle contents: Edges: inguinal ligament, sartorius, adductor; Contents from lateral to medial:.

Femoral triangle contents

  • Edges: inguinal ligament, sartorius, adductor
  • Contents from lateral to medial:
  • Nerve (femoral)
  • Artery, then Vein (NAVY)
  • Empty space, lymph nodes and femoral canal

Why it matters

Leg anatomy matters for orthopaedic and vascular surgery, regional blocks, injections and tourniquet use. Several nerves are easily damaged by pressure.

Remember

NAVY from the outside in.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Femoral triangle contents".

Edges: inguinal ligament, sartorius, adductor; Contents from lateral to medial:; Nerve (femoral); Artery, then Vein (NAVY); Empty space, lymph nodes and femoral canal.
