liver-failure-and-clotting.title: Liver failure and clotting
liver-failure-and-clotting.caption: Liver failure lowers albumin and clotting factors.
liver-failure-and-clotting.body:
In short: Liver failure lowers albumin and clotting factors.

Synthetic Function

Liver failure lowers albumin and clotting factors. Patients may swell with fluid and bleed more easily.

Low albumin also means more free drug in the blood, so some drugs have stronger effects.

Why it matters

The gut and liver affect drug effects, fasting, bleeding and recovery. This knowledge helps you understand why some patients need special precautions.

Remember

Liver failure can mean bleeding.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about liver failure and clotting?

Liver failure can mean bleeding.

portal-hypertension-features.title: Portal hypertension features
portal-hypertension-features.caption: A quick list on portal hypertension features: Raised pressure in the portal venous system; Oesophageal varices that may bleed.
portal-hypertension-features.body:
In short: A quick list on portal hypertension features: Raised pressure in the portal venous system; Oesophageal varices that may bleed.

Portal hypertension features

  • Raised pressure in the portal venous system
  • Oesophageal varices that may bleed
  • Ascites, fluid in the abdomen
  • Splenomegaly
  • Common in cirrhosis

Why it matters

The gut and liver affect drug effects, fasting, bleeding and recovery. This knowledge helps you understand why some patients need special precautions.

Remember

Varices bleed heavily.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Portal hypertension features".

Raised pressure in the portal venous system; Oesophageal varices that may bleed; Ascites, fluid in the abdomen; Splenomegaly; Common in cirrhosis.

glucose-handling-by-the-liver.title: Glucose handling by the liver
glucose-handling-by-the-liver.caption: After meals the liver stores glucose as glycogen.
glucose-handling-by-the-liver.body:
In short: After meals the liver stores glucose as glycogen.

Sugar Bank

After meals the liver stores glucose as glycogen. During fasting it releases glucose from glycogen and can also make new glucose.

Liver disease or prolonged fasting can lead to low blood sugar, so monitor glucose in at-risk patients.

Why it matters

The gut and liver affect drug effects, fasting, bleeding and recovery. This knowledge helps you understand why some patients need special precautions.

Remember

The liver keeps blood sugar steady.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about glucose handling by the liver?

The liver keeps blood sugar steady.

the-action-potential.title: The action potential
the-action-potential.caption: A nerve impulse is a wave of sodium entering the cell, followed by potassium leaving.
the-action-potential.body:
In short: A nerve impulse is a wave of sodium entering the cell, followed by potassium leaving.

Nerve Signals

A nerve impulse is a wave of sodium entering the cell, followed by potassium leaving. This briefly reverses the membrane charge.

Local anaesthetics block sodium channels, which is why they stop the impulse and cause numbness.

Why it matters

Nerves, pain pathways and the brain are the targets of anaesthesia and analgesia, so understanding them explains how and why our drugs work.

Remember

Block sodium and the signal stops.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about the action potential?

Block sodium and the signal stops.

synapse-and-neurotransmitters.title: Synapse and neurotransmitters
synapse-and-neurotransmitters.caption: At a synapse, a nerve releases a chemical messenger that binds to receptors on the next cell.
synapse-and-neurotransmitters.body:
In short: At a synapse, a nerve releases a chemical messenger that binds to receptors on the next cell.

Chemical Messages

At a synapse, a nerve releases a chemical messenger that binds to receptors on the next cell. The signal is then ended by reuptake or breakdown.

Many anaesthetic and sedative drugs act by altering these messengers or their receptors.

Why it matters

Nerves, pain pathways and the brain are the targets of anaesthesia and analgesia, so understanding them explains how and why our drugs work.

Remember

Drugs often act at synapses.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about synapse and neurotransmitters?

Drugs often act at synapses.

sympathetic-versus-parasympathetic.title: Sympathetic versus parasympathetic
sympathetic-versus-parasympathetic.caption: A quick list on sympathetic versus parasympathetic: Sympathetic: fight or flight; Raises heart rate and widens airways.
sympathetic-versus-parasympathetic.body:
In short: A quick list on sympathetic versus parasympathetic: Sympathetic: fight or flight; Raises heart rate and widens airways.

Sympathetic versus parasympathetic

  • Sympathetic: fight or flight
  • Raises heart rate and widens airways
  • Parasympathetic: rest and digest
  • Slows heart rate and boosts gut activity
  • Both operate together constantly

Why it matters

Nerves, pain pathways and the brain are the targets of anaesthesia and analgesia, so understanding them explains how and why our drugs work.

Remember

Think accelerator and brake.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Sympathetic versus parasympathetic".

Sympathetic: fight or flight; Raises heart rate and widens airways; Parasympathetic: rest and digest; Slows heart rate and boosts gut activity; Both operate together constantly.

pain-pathway-steps.title: Pain pathway steps
pain-pathway-steps.caption: A quick list on pain pathway steps: Transduction: the stimulus is detected; Transmission: impulse travels to the spinal cord.
pain-pathway-steps.body:
In short: A quick list on pain pathway steps: Transduction: the stimulus is detected; Transmission: impulse travels to the spinal cord.

Pain pathway steps

  • Transduction: the stimulus is detected
  • Transmission: impulse travels to the spinal cord
  • Modulation: signals are boosted or dampened
  • Perception: the brain interprets the pain
  • Different drugs target different steps

Why it matters

Nerves, pain pathways and the brain are the targets of anaesthesia and analgesia, so understanding them explains how and why our drugs work.

Remember

Pain treatment can act at four levels.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Pain pathway steps".

Transduction: the stimulus is detected; Transmission: impulse travels to the spinal cord; Modulation: signals are boosted or dampened; Perception: the brain interprets the pain; Different drugs target different steps.

cerebral-blood-flow-control.title: Cerebral blood flow control
cerebral-blood-flow-control.caption: Brain blood flow is tightly controlled and is strongly affected by carbon dioxide.
cerebral-blood-flow-control.body:
In short: Brain blood flow is tightly controlled and is strongly affected by carbon dioxide.

Protecting The Brain

Brain blood flow is tightly controlled and is strongly affected by carbon dioxide. Raised CO2 widens brain vessels, and lowered CO2 narrows them.

In head injury, avoiding high CO2 and low blood pressure helps protect the brain.

Why it matters

Nerves, pain pathways and the brain are the targets of anaesthesia and analgesia, so understanding them explains how and why our drugs work.

Remember

CO2 changes brain blood flow.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cerebral blood flow control?

CO2 changes brain blood flow.

intracranial-pressure-basics.title: Intracranial pressure basics
intracranial-pressure-basics.caption: The skull has a fixed volume containing brain, blood and cerebrospinal fluid.
intracranial-pressure-basics.body:
In short: The skull has a fixed volume containing brain, blood and cerebrospinal fluid.

A Fixed Box

The skull has a fixed volume containing brain, blood and cerebrospinal fluid. A swelling or bleed increases pressure.

Warning signs include headache, vomiting, drowsiness, slow pulse and high blood pressure. Escalate urgently.

Why it matters

Nerves, pain pathways and the brain are the targets of anaesthesia and analgesia, so understanding them explains how and why our drugs work.

Remember

Rising pressure needs urgent action.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about intracranial pressure basics?

Rising pressure needs urgent action.

spinal-cord-levels-and-block-height.title: Spinal cord levels and block height
spinal-cord-levels-and-block-height.caption: Nerves leave the spinal cord at set levels.
spinal-cord-levels-and-block-height.body:
In short: Nerves leave the spinal cord at set levels.

What Spinal Blocks Hit

Nerves leave the spinal cord at set levels. Anaesthetic spread blocks sensory, motor and sympathetic fibres, in varying degrees.

A high block can cause low blood pressure, slow heart rate and breathing difficulty. Monitor level and vital signs.

Why it matters

Nerves, pain pathways and the brain are the targets of anaesthesia and analgesia, so understanding them explains how and why our drugs work.

Remember

Block height matters.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about spinal cord levels and block height?

Block height matters.

neuromuscular-junction.title: Neuromuscular junction
neuromuscular-junction.caption: A motor nerve releases acetylcholine, which binds receptors on muscle and triggers contraction.
neuromuscular-junction.body:
In short: A motor nerve releases acetylcholine, which binds receptors on muscle and triggers contraction.

Where Nerve Meets Muscle

A motor nerve releases acetylcholine, which binds receptors on muscle and triggers contraction.

Muscle relaxants interfere at this point. Reversal agents help restore normal transmission before waking the patient.

Why it matters

Nerves, pain pathways and the brain are the targets of anaesthesia and analgesia, so understanding them explains how and why our drugs work.

Remember

Check recovery before extubation.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about neuromuscular junction?

Check recovery before extubation.

stages-of-sleep-and-anaesthesia.title: Stages of sleep and anaesthesia
stages-of-sleep-and-anaesthesia.caption: General anaesthesia is a drug-induced state with loss of awareness, and is different from natural sleep.
stages-of-sleep-and-anaesthesia.body:
In short: General anaesthesia is a drug-induced state with loss of awareness, and is different from natural sleep.

Not The Same

General anaesthesia is a drug-induced state with loss of awareness, and is different from natural sleep. Patients do not respond to pain unless the depth is low.

Monitoring depth helps lower the risk of awareness.

Why it matters

Nerves, pain pathways and the brain are the targets of anaesthesia and analgesia, so understanding them explains how and why our drugs work.

Remember

Anaesthesia is not just deep sleep.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about stages of sleep and anaesthesia?

Anaesthesia is not just deep sleep.

components-of-blood.title: Components of blood
components-of-blood.caption: A quick list on components of blood: Red cells carry oxygen; White cells fight infection.
components-of-blood.body:
In short: A quick list on components of blood: Red cells carry oxygen; White cells fight infection.

Components of blood

  • Red cells carry oxygen
  • White cells fight infection
  • Platelets plug damaged vessels
  • Plasma carries proteins and clotting factors
  • Each has a role in surgical recovery

Why it matters

Blood carries oxygen, clots and is sometimes transfused. Knowing the basics helps you handle anaemia, bleeding disorders and transfusion safely.

Remember

Four parts, four jobs.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Components of blood".

Red cells carry oxygen; White cells fight infection; Platelets plug damaged vessels; Plasma carries proteins and clotting factors; Each has a role in surgical recovery.

haemoglobin-and-oxygen-carriage.title: Haemoglobin and oxygen carriage
haemoglobin-and-oxygen-carriage.caption: Haemoglobin inside red cells carries most of the oxygen in blood.
haemoglobin-and-oxygen-carriage.body:
In short: Haemoglobin inside red cells carries most of the oxygen in blood.

Oxygen Taxi

Haemoglobin inside red cells carries most of the oxygen in blood. Each molecule can bind oxygen at four sites.

Low haemoglobin means less oxygen delivery, even when the oxygen saturation reads normal.

Why it matters

Blood carries oxygen, clots and is sometimes transfused. Knowing the basics helps you handle anaemia, bleeding disorders and transfusion safely.

Remember

Normal saturation can hide anaemia.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about haemoglobin and oxygen carriage?

Normal saturation can hide anaemia.

causes-of-anaemia.title: Causes of anaemia
causes-of-anaemia.caption: A quick list on causes of anaemia: Iron deficiency: low iron, small pale cells; B12 or folate deficiency: large cells.
causes-of-anaemia.body:
In short: A quick list on causes of anaemia: Iron deficiency: low iron, small pale cells; B12 or folate deficiency: large cells.

Causes of anaemia

  • Iron deficiency: low iron, small pale cells
  • B12 or folate deficiency: large cells
  • Haemolytic: red cells destroyed early
  • Blood loss: acute or chronic
  • Treatment depends on the cause

Why it matters

Blood carries oxygen, clots and is sometimes transfused. Knowing the basics helps you handle anaemia, bleeding disorders and transfusion safely.

Remember

Find the cause before treating.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Causes of anaemia".

Iron deficiency: low iron, small pale cells; B12 or folate deficiency: large cells; Haemolytic: red cells destroyed early; Blood loss: acute or chronic; Treatment depends on the cause.

sickle-cell-disease-and-surgery.title: Sickle cell disease and surgery
sickle-cell-disease-and-surgery.caption: Sickle haemoglobin can distort red cells, blocking small vessels.
sickle-cell-disease-and-surgery.body:
In short: Sickle haemoglobin can distort red cells, blocking small vessels.

Careful Planning

Sickle haemoglobin can distort red cells, blocking small vessels. Low oxygen, cold, dehydration, acidosis and infection can trigger crises.

Teams usually aim to keep patients warm, well hydrated and well oxygenated, and to treat pain promptly.

Why it matters

Blood carries oxygen, clots and is sometimes transfused. Knowing the basics helps you handle anaemia, bleeding disorders and transfusion safely.

Remember

Warm, wet and well oxygenated.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about sickle cell disease and surgery?

Warm, wet and well oxygenated.

primary-haemostasis.title: Primary haemostasis
primary-haemostasis.caption: When a vessel is injured, it narrows and platelets stick to the exposed wall, then clump together to form a plug.
primary-haemostasis.body:
In short: When a vessel is injured, it narrows and platelets stick to the exposed wall, then clump together to form a plug.

Platelet Plug

When a vessel is injured, it narrows and platelets stick to the exposed wall, then clump together to form a plug.

Low platelet numbers or antiplatelet drugs such as aspirin can lead to prolonged bleeding.

Why it matters

Blood carries oxygen, clots and is sometimes transfused. Knowing the basics helps you handle anaemia, bleeding disorders and transfusion safely.

Remember

Platelets form the first plug.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about primary haemostasis?

Platelets form the first plug.

the-coagulation-cascade.title: The coagulation cascade
the-coagulation-cascade.caption: Clotting factors activate each other in sequence, finally turning fibrinogen into fibrin, which strengthens the platelet plug.
the-coagulation-cascade.body:
In short: Clotting factors activate each other in sequence, finally turning fibrinogen into fibrin, which strengthens the platelet plug.

Fibrin Mesh

Clotting factors activate each other in sequence, finally turning fibrinogen into fibrin, which strengthens the platelet plug.

Vitamin K is needed for several factors. Liver disease and anticoagulants can weaken the process.

Why it matters

Blood carries oxygen, clots and is sometimes transfused. Knowing the basics helps you handle anaemia, bleeding disorders and transfusion safely.

Remember

Fibrin makes the plug strong.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about the coagulation cascade?

Fibrin makes the plug strong.

blood-group-basics.title: Blood group basics
blood-group-basics.caption: ABO groups depend on antigens on red cells.
blood-group-basics.body:
In short: ABO groups depend on antigens on red cells.

Abo And Rhesus

ABO groups depend on antigens on red cells. Plasma holds antibodies against the antigens a person lacks. Rhesus D is a separate system.

Crossmatching checks compatibility before transfusion, and correct identification at the bedside prevents serious errors.

Why it matters

Blood carries oxygen, clots and is sometimes transfused. Knowing the basics helps you handle anaemia, bleeding disorders and transfusion safely.

Remember

Check, check and check again.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about blood group basics?

Check, check and check again.

transfusion-reaction-signs.title: Transfusion reaction signs
transfusion-reaction-signs.caption: A quick list on transfusion reaction signs: Fever or chills; Chest or back pain.
transfusion-reaction-signs.body:
In short: A quick list on transfusion reaction signs: Fever or chills; Chest or back pain.

Transfusion reaction signs

Fibrinolysis is the natural breakdown of clots. Antifibrinolytic drugs such as tranexamic acid slow this process.

They are often used when bleeding is expected or active. Follow local protocol for timing and dose.

Why it matters

Blood carries oxygen, clots and is sometimes transfused. Knowing the basics helps you handle anaemia, bleeding disorders and transfusion safely.

Anti-fibrinolytics preserve clots.

Low Platelets

A low platelet count raises the risk of bleeding, especially with surgery or injections near the spine. Causes include marrow disease, some drugs, infection and heavy use.

The safe level depends on the procedure, so follow local protocol and ask the surgeon.

Why it matters

Blood carries oxygen, clots and is sometimes transfused. Knowing the basics helps you handle anaemia, bleeding disorders and transfusion safely.

innate-versus-adaptive-immunity.caption: Innate immunity is quick and general, and includes skin, mucus, phagocytes and inflammation.
innate-versus-adaptive-immunity.body:
In short: Innate immunity is quick and general, and includes skin, mucus, phagocytes and inflammation.

Two Lines Of Defence

Innate immunity is quick and general, and includes skin, mucus, phagocytes and inflammation. Adaptive immunity is slower, specific and has memory.

Vaccines train the adaptive system without causing the disease.

Why it matters

The immune system governs infection risk, allergy and healing. Recognising reactions such as anaphylaxis can save a life in theatre.

Remember

Fast general, slow specific.

First Defence

Intact skin blocks most microbes. Surgery breaks this barrier, which is why skin preparation and aseptic technique matter so much.

Warmth, moisture and tape irritation can also weaken skin protection.

The immune system governs infection risk, allergy and healing. Recognising reactions such as anaphylaxis can save a life in theatre.

Remember

Break the barrier, raise the risk.

A Time-Critical Event

Anaphylaxis can cause low blood pressure, wheeze, swelling of the face or airway, rash and fast heart rate, often within minutes of exposure.

Common triggers in theatre include antibiotics, muscle relaxants, latex and some dyes. Call for help and follow the emergency protocol.

Why it matters

The immune system governs infection risk, allergy and healing. Recognising reactions such as anaphylaxis can save a life in theatre.

Remember

Think anaphylaxis with sudden collapse.

latex-allergy-in-theatre.caption: Latex allergy may be immediate or delayed.
latex-allergy-in-theatre.body:

Know The Risk

Latex allergy may be immediate or delayed. People who have had many surgeries, or work in healthcare, may be at higher risk.

Patients with latex allergy usually need a latex-free environment and gloves. Check the allergy list before every case.

Why it matters

The immune system governs infection risk, allergy and healing. Recognising reactions such as anaphylaxis can save a life in theatre.

Latex-free means checking everything.

Extra Care

Steroids, chemotherapy, HIV and transplant drugs can weaken immune defences. Infections may be more severe and signs may be less obvious.

Strict hand hygiene and aseptic technique are especially important for these patients.

The immune system governs infection risk, allergy and healing. Recognising reactions such as anaphylaxis can save a life in theatre.

active-versus-passive-immunity.caption: Active immunity develops when the body makes its own response, through infection or vaccination.
active-versus-passive-immunity.body:
In short: Active immunity develops when the body makes its own response, through infection or vaccination.

Make Or Borrow

Active immunity develops when the body makes its own response, through infection or vaccination. Passive immunity comes from ready-made antibodies, such as from the mother or immunoglobulin injections.

Passive protection is faster but temporary.

Why it matters

The immune system governs infection risk, allergy and healing. Recognising reactions such as anaphylaxis can save a life in theatre.

Remember

Passive is quick but short.

complement-system.caption: Complement proteins circulate in the blood and activate in sequence.
complement-system.body:
In short: Complement proteins circulate in the blood and activate in sequence.

A Cascade Of Proteins

Complement proteins circulate in the blood and activate in sequence. They mark microbes for destruction, attract white cells and can directly burst some bacteria.

Over-activation can add to inflammation and tissue damage.

Why it matters

The immune system governs infection risk, allergy and healing. Recognising reactions such as anaphylaxis can save a life in theatre.

Remember

Complement helps clear invaders.

types-of-cell-injury.caption: Cells may adapt, suffer reversible injury or die.
types-of-cell-injury.body:
In short: Cells may adapt, suffer reversible injury or die.

Reversible Or Not

Cells may adapt, suffer reversible injury or die. Causes include low oxygen, toxins, infection, heat, cold and immune attack.

If the injury is removed in time, cells may recover. Severe or prolonged injury leads to death of cells.

Why it matters

Understanding how injury, healing, clotting and tumours behave helps you handle specimens, anticipate complications and care for surgical patients.

Remember

Early removal of the cause helps recovery.

necrosis-versus-apoptosis.title: Necrosis versus apoptosis
necrosis-versus-apoptosis.caption: Necrosis is uncontrolled death from injury, often causing inflammation.
necrosis-versus-apoptosis.body:
In short: Necrosis is uncontrolled death from injury, often causing inflammation.

Two Ways Cells Die

Necrosis is uncontrolled death from injury, often causing inflammation. Apoptosis is programmed, tidy cell death that is part of normal development and tissue renewal.

Both are seen in disease and in healing.

Why it matters

Understanding how injury, healing, clotting and tumours behave helps you handle specimens, anticipate complications and care for surgical patients.

Remember

Necrosis is messy, apoptosis is orderly.

Virchow'S Triad

Clots are more likely with slow blood flow, damaged vessel walls or blood that clots too easily.

embolism-types.body:

When Something Travels

An embolus is a mass that travels in the blood and blocks a vessel. It may be a clot, fat, air, amniotic fluid or tumour tissue.

Sudden breathlessness, chest pain or collapse can signal a pulmonary embolus, and needs urgent help.

Why it matters

Understanding how injury, healing, clotting and tumours behave helps you handle specimens, anticipate complications and care for surgical patients.

Extra Fluid In Tissues

Oedema can come from raised vessel pressure, low albumin, leaky vessels or blocked lymph drainage.

Heart failure, liver and kidney disease, infection and burns are common causes. Identifying the cause guides treatment.

gram-positive-and-gram-negative.body:

A Stain With Meaning

Gram staining separates bacteria by cell wall structure. Gram-positive bacteria stain purple and Gram-negative bacteria stain pink.

The difference helps guide antibiotic choice, as Gram-negative bacteria have an outer membrane that blocks some drugs.

Why it matters

Surgical infection prevention depends on knowing the germs involved, how they spread and how sterilisation and hygiene stop them.

Purple positive, pink negative.

Some bacteria, such as Clostridium and Bacillus, form spores that resist heat, drying and many disinfectants.

Sterilisation must be thorough enough to destroy spores. Boiling alone is not enough for surgical instruments.

Surgical infection prevention depends on knowing the germs involved, how they spread and how sterilisation and hygiene stop them.

Spores survive simple cleaning.

Clostridium Tetani

Tetanus bacteria live in soil and dung, and spores enter dirty wounds. The toxin causes painful muscle spasm and stiffness, including lockjaw.

Good wound cleaning and vaccination are key to prevention. Ask about tetanus immunisation in injured patients.

Why it matters

Surgical infection prevention depends on knowing the germs involved, how they spread and how sterilisation and hygiene stop them.

Clean wounds and check immunisation.

After a sharps injury, wash the wound with soap and running water, do not squeeze or scrub hard, and report it right away.

Surgical infection prevention depends on knowing the germs involved, how they spread and how sterilisation and hygiene stop them.

tuberculosis-and-airborne-spread.body:

A Serious Airborne Risk

Tuberculosis spreads through tiny droplets that stay in the air. Cough lasting weeks, night sweats, weight loss and fever raise suspicion.

Suspected patients need isolation, good ventilation and appropriate respirator masks for staff, as per local policy.

Why it matters

Surgical infection prevention depends on knowing the germs involved, how they spread and how sterilisation and hygiene stop them.

Ventilation and the right mask protect staff.

A Growing Problem

Bacteria can become resistant when antibiotics are overused or taken incompletely. Resistant infections are harder and more costly to treat.

Give prophylaxis at the right time and for the right duration, and follow antibiotic guidelines carefully.

Why it matters

Surgical infection prevention depends on knowing the germs involved, how they spread and how sterilisation and hygiene stop them.

Use antibiotics only when needed.

mrsa-awareness.caption: MRSA is a Staphylococcus aureus resistant to many common antibiotics.
mrsa-awareness.body:

A Resistant Staphylococcus

MRSA is a Staphylococcus aureus resistant to many common antibiotics. Spread is mostly through contact, especially on hands and equipment.

Hand hygiene, cleaning, contact precautions and appropriate patient isolation help limit its spread in theatre.

Why it matters

Surgical infection prevention depends on knowing the germs involved, how they spread and how sterilisation and hygiene stop them.

Remember

Hands and surfaces spread MRSA.

Hands and surfaces spread MRSA.

sepsis-recognition.body:

Body'S Extreme Response

Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by infection. Look for fever or low temperature, fast heart rate, fast breathing, confusion and low blood pressure.

Early antibiotics, fluids and source control improve outcomes. Escalate quickly.

Why it matters

Surgical infection prevention depends on knowing the germs involved, how they spread and how sterilisation and hygiene stop them.

Early recognition saves lives.

malaria-life-cycle-in-brief.body:
In short: Plasmodium parasites enter through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito, multiply in the liver, then infect red cells and cause fever.

Mosquito And Liver

Plasmodium parasites enter through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito, multiply in the liver, then infect red cells and cause fever.

Plasmodium falciparum can be severe and quickly dangerous, so it needs urgent diagnosis.

Why it matters

Parasitic diseases remain common in East Africa and affect anaemia, surgical risk and emergencies, so theatre staff should recognise them.

Remember

Fever in a malaria area needs a test.

Severe malaria warning signs

  • Dark urine or jaundice

malaria-before-surgery.caption: Patients with active malaria may have anaemia, low platelets, low blood sugar and organ involvement.

Plan With Care

Patients with active malaria may have anaemia, low platelets, low blood sugar and organ involvement. Elective surgery is usually delayed until treated.

In emergencies, check blood sugar, haemoglobin and hydration, and monitor closely.

Why it matters

Parasitic diseases remain common in East Africa and affect anaemia, surgical risk and emergencies, so theatre staff should recognise them.

Remember

Treat malaria before elective surgery.

Treat malaria before elective surgery.

schistosomiasis.body:
In short: Schistosomiasis is caught from freshwater containing larvae released by certain snails.

Freshwater Flukes

Schistosomiasis is caught from freshwater containing larvae released by certain snails. Chronic infection can damage the bladder, liver or bowel depending on the species.

Blood in the urine in endemic areas is a classic sign of urinary disease.

Why it matters

Parasitic diseases remain common in East Africa and affect anaemia, surgical risk and emergencies, so theatre staff should recognise them.

Remember

Freshwater contact is the risk.

Freshwater contact is the risk.

hydatid-disease.caption: People can swallow eggs of Echinococcus tapeworms from dogs or contaminated food.
hydatid-disease.body:
In short: People can swallow eggs of Echinococcus tapeworms from dogs or contaminated food.

Echinococcus Cysts

People can swallow eggs of Echinococcus tapeworms from dogs or contaminated food. Cysts form slowly, most often in the liver or lungs.

Spillage of cyst fluid during surgery can cause spread or severe allergic reactions, so handling needs care.

Why it matters

Parasitic diseases remain common in East Africa and affect anaemia, surgical risk and emergencies, so theatre staff should recognise them.

Remember

Do not spill hydatid cyst fluid.

Do not spill hydatid cyst fluid.

soil-transmitted-helminths.caption: A quick list on soil-transmitted helminths: Roundworm (Ascaris); Hookworm.
soil-transmitted-helminths.body:
In short: A quick list on soil-transmitted helminths: Roundworm (Ascaris); Hookworm.

Soil-transmitted helminths

  • Hookworm

Worms can cause anaemia and poor growth.

ascaris-and-bowel-obstruction.title: Ascaris and bowel obstruction
ascaris-and-bowel-obstruction.caption: Heavy roundworm infection, especially in children, can form a mass that blocks the bowel or bile ducts.
ascaris-and-bowel-obstruction.body:
In short: Heavy roundworm infection, especially in children, can form a mass that blocks the bowel or bile ducts.

A Ball Of Worms

Heavy roundworm infection, especially in children, can form a mass that blocks the bowel or bile ducts.

Patients may have colicky abdominal pain and vomiting. Surgery is sometimes needed for obstruction.

Parasitic diseases remain common in East Africa and affect anaemia, surgical risk and emergencies, so theatre staff should recognise them.

Worms can cause surgical emergencies.

amoebiasis.title: Amoebiasis
amoebiasis.caption: This parasite spreads through contaminated food and water.
amoebiasis.body:
In short: This parasite spreads through contaminated food and water.

Entamoeba Histolytica

This parasite spreads through contaminated food and water. It may cause bloody diarrhoea and can reach the liver to form an abscess.

Fever, right upper abdominal pain and tenderness may suggest a liver abscess.

Why it matters

Parasitic diseases remain common in East Africa and affect anaemia, surgical risk and emergencies, so theatre staff should recognise them.

Clean water prevents amoebiasis.

lymphatic-filariasis.caption: Filarial worms live in lymph vessels and can cause chronic swelling of limbs or genitals.
lymphatic-filariasis.body:
In short: Filarial worms live in lymph vessels and can cause chronic swelling of limbs or genitals.

Mosquito-Borne Worms

Filarial worms live in lymph vessels and can cause chronic swelling of limbs or genitals. Spread is by mosquito bites.

Affected skin is fragile and prone to infection, so careful handling, positioning and hygiene are important.

Why it matters

Parasitic diseases remain common in East Africa and affect anaemia, surgical risk and emergencies, so theatre staff should recognise them.

Remember

Protect swollen limbs from injury.

Protect swollen limbs from injury.

preventing-parasitic-infection.title: Preventing parasitic infection
preventing-parasitic-infection.caption: A quick list on preventing parasitic infection: Safe drinking water; Handwashing and good sanitation.
preventing-parasitic-infection.body:
In short: A quick list on preventing parasitic infection: Safe drinking water; Handwashing and good sanitation.

Preventing parasitic infection

  • Safe drinking water
  • Handwashing and good sanitation
  • Cooking meat and fish fully
  • Mosquito nets and repellents
  • Wearing shoes in high-risk areas

Why it matters

Parasitic diseases remain common in East Africa and affect anaemia, surgical risk and emergencies, so theatre staff should recognise them.

Remember

Prevention is cheaper than treatment.

three-levels-of-prevention.title: Three levels of prevention
three-levels-of-prevention.caption: Primary prevention stops disease before it starts, such as vaccination.
three-levels-of-prevention.body:
In short: Primary prevention stops disease before it starts, such as vaccination.

Prevention

Primary prevention stops disease before it starts, such as vaccination. Secondary prevention finds disease early, such as screening. Tertiary prevention limits harm and disability in people already ill, such as rehabilitation.

Why it matters

Theatre staff work within wider health systems. Prevention, surveillance and outbreak control shape the patients who reach surgery and the safety of those who care for them.

Remember

Prevent, detect early, limit harm.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about three levels of prevention?

Prevent, detect early, limit harm.

incidence-versus-prevalence.title: Incidence versus prevalence
incidence-versus-prevalence.caption: Incidence is the number of new cases in a set period.
incidence-versus-prevalence.body:
In short: Incidence is the number of new cases in a set period.

Counting Disease

Incidence is the number of new cases in a set period. Prevalence is all existing cases at a point in time.

A long-lasting disease can have high prevalence even when few new cases appear.

Why it matters

Theatre staff work within wider health systems. Prevention, surveillance and outbreak control shape the patients who reach surgery and the safety of those who care for them.

Remember

Incidence is new, prevalence is all.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about incidence versus prevalence?

Incidence is new, prevalence is all.

herd-immunity.title: Herd immunity
herd-immunity.caption: When enough people are immune, the germ struggles to spread and some unprotected people are shielded.
herd-immunity.body:
In short: When enough people are immune, the germ struggles to spread and some unprotected people are shielded.

Community Shield

When enough people are immune, the germ struggles to spread and some unprotected people are shielded. The level needed differs by disease.

It works best when vaccine coverage is high and even across areas.

Why it matters

Theatre staff work within wider health systems. Prevention, surveillance and outbreak control shape the patients who reach surgery and the safety of those who care for them.

Remember

Your vaccine protects others too.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about herd immunity?

Your vaccine protects others too.

steps-of-an-outbreak-response.title: Steps of an outbreak response
steps-of-an-outbreak-response.caption: A quick list on steps of an outbreak response: Confirm the cases and the diagnosis; Define a case and count cases by time, place, person.
steps-of-an-outbreak-response.body:
In short: A quick list on steps of an outbreak response: Confirm the cases and the diagnosis; Define a case and count cases by time, place, person.

Steps of an outbreak response

  • Confirm the cases and the diagnosis
  • Define a case and count cases by time, place, person
  • Find the likely source and how it spreads
  • Start control measures and inform the community
  • Keep watching until cases stop

Why it matters

Theatre staff work within wider health systems. Prevention, surveillance and outbreak control shape the patients who reach surgery and the safety of those who care for them.

Remember

Act early, do not wait for perfect data.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Steps of an outbreak response".

Confirm the cases and the diagnosis; Define a case and count cases by time, place, person; Find the likely source and how it spreads; Start control measures and inform the community; Keep watching until cases stop.

disease-surveillance.caption: Surveillance is the steady collection and review of health data so action can follow.
disease-surveillance.body:
In short: Surveillance is the steady collection and review of health data so action can follow.

Watching For Trouble

Surveillance is the steady collection and review of health data so action can follow. Clinics report certain illnesses to district teams, who look for unusual rises.

Accurate, timely reporting is how outbreaks are caught early.

Why it matters

Theatre staff work within wider health systems. Prevention, surveillance and outbreak control shape the patients who reach surgery and the safety of those who care for them.

Remember

Good records protect whole communities.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about disease surveillance?

Good records protect whole communities.

the-vaccine-cold-chain.title: The vaccine cold chain
the-vaccine-cold-chain.caption: Most vaccines lose potency if too warm, and some are damaged by freezing.
the-vaccine-cold-chain.body:
In short: Most vaccines lose potency if too warm, and some are damaged by freezing.

Keep It Cold

Most vaccines lose potency if too warm, and some are damaged by freezing. The cold chain is the system of fridges, cold boxes and monitoring that keeps them in range from store to clinic.

Check temperature records and vial monitors, and follow local policy.

Why it matters

Theatre staff work within wider health systems. Prevention, surveillance and outbreak control shape the patients who reach surgery and the safety of those who care for them.

Remember

A warm vaccine may be a useless vaccine.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about the vaccine cold chain?

A warm vaccine may be a useless vaccine.

epidemiological-triad.caption: Disease results from an agent (germ), a host (person) and an environment that brings them together.
epidemiological-triad.body:
In short: Disease results from an agent (germ), a host (person) and an environment that brings them together.

Agent, Host, Environment

Disease results from an agent (germ), a host (person) and an environment that brings them together.

Control works by attacking any side: kill or block the agent, raise host immunity, or improve water, housing and sanitation.

Why it matters

Theatre staff work within wider health systems. Prevention, surveillance and outbreak control shape the patients who reach surgery and the safety of those who care for them.

Remember

Break any side of the triangle.

Check yourself

Break any side of the triangle.

notifiable-diseases.caption: Some diseases must be reported to health authorities as soon as they are suspected, for example cholera and measles.
notifiable-diseases.body:

Must Be Reported

Some diseases must be reported to health authorities as soon as they are suspected, for example cholera and measles. The list is set by national policy.

Report on suspicion, not only after lab confirmation, so control can start quickly.

Suspect it, report it.

how-malaria-spreads.title: How malaria spreads
how-malaria-spreads.caption: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites passed on by bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes, mostly at night.
how-malaria-spreads.body:
In short: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites passed on by bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes, mostly at night.

Mosquito And Parasite

Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites passed on by bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes, mostly at night. It can also pass through infected blood or from mother to baby.

Nets, room spraying and draining standing water cut spread.

Why it matters

Malaria, typhoid, schistosomiasis and other tropical illnesses are commonly seen in East Africa, and they affect fitness for anaesthesia and surgery and complicate emergencies.

Remember

Sleep under a treated net every night.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about how malaria spreads?

Sleep under a treated net every night.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

malaria-rapid-tests.title: Malaria rapid tests
malaria-rapid-tests.caption: A rapid diagnostic test detects malaria parasite proteins in a drop of blood and gives a result in minutes.
malaria-rapid-tests.body:
In short: A rapid diagnostic test detects malaria parasite proteins in a drop of blood and gives a result in minutes.

Quick Diagnosis

A rapid diagnostic test detects malaria parasite proteins in a drop of blood and gives a result in minutes. Microscopy can also show the parasite type and density.

Test before treating wherever possible, as fever has many other causes.

Why it matters

Malaria, typhoid, schistosomiasis and other tropical illnesses are commonly seen in East Africa, and they affect fitness for anaesthesia and surgery and complicate emergencies.

Remember

Test first, then treat.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about malaria rapid tests?

Test first, then treat.

typhoid-fever.title: Typhoid fever
typhoid-fever.caption: Typhoid spreads through food and water contaminated by faeces of an infected person.
typhoid-fever.body:
In short: Typhoid spreads through food and water contaminated by faeces of an infected person.

Enteric Fever

Typhoid spreads through food and water contaminated by faeces of an infected person. It causes prolonged fever, headache, abdominal pain and sometimes constipation or diarrhoea.

Complications can include bowel bleeding or perforation, an emergency.

Why it matters

Malaria, typhoid, schistosomiasis and other tropical illnesses are commonly seen in East Africa, and they affect fitness for anaesthesia and surgery and complicate emergencies.

Remember

Clean water and hands stop typhoid.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about typhoid fever?

Clean water and hands stop typhoid.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cholera-and-fluid-loss.title: Cholera and fluid loss
cholera-and-fluid-loss.caption: Cholera causes sudden, profuse watery diarrhoea that can lead to dangerous dehydration within hours.
cholera-and-fluid-loss.body:
In short: Cholera causes sudden, profuse watery diarrhoea that can lead to dangerous dehydration within hours.

Rice-Water Stools

Cholera causes sudden, profuse watery diarrhoea that can lead to dangerous dehydration within hours. Rapid fluid replacement, orally if possible or by drip if severe, is the main treatment.

Isolate patients, disinfect waste and notify authorities.

Why it matters

Malaria, typhoid, schistosomiasis and other tropical illnesses are commonly seen in East Africa, and they affect fitness for anaesthesia and surgery and complicate emergencies.

Remember

Replace fluids fast, then find the source.

Check yourself

Replace fluids fast, then find the source.

visceral-leishmaniasis.title: Visceral leishmaniasis
visceral-leishmaniasis.caption: Spread by sandfly bites, kala-azar causes long fever, weight loss, a big spleen and anaemia.
visceral-leishmaniasis.body:
In short: Spread by sandfly bites, kala-azar causes long fever, weight loss, a big spleen and anaemia.

Kala-Azar

Spread by sandfly bites, kala-azar causes long fever, weight loss, a big spleen and anaemia. It occurs in some dry regions of East Africa.

Diagnosis needs special tests, and treatment is given under specialist supervision.

Why it matters

Malaria, typhoid, schistosomiasis and other tropical illnesses are commonly seen in East Africa, and they affect fitness for anaesthesia and surgery and complicate emergencies.

Prolonged fever and big spleen need testing.

intestinal-worm-infections.title: Intestinal worm infections
intestinal-worm-infections.caption: Roundworm, whipworm and hookworm spread through soil contaminated by faeces.
intestinal-worm-infections.body:
In short: Roundworm, whipworm and hookworm spread through soil contaminated by faeces.

Soil-Transmitted Worms

Roundworm, whipworm and hookworm spread through soil contaminated by faeces. Hookworm enters through bare feet and can cause anaemia.

Regular deworming, latrine use, handwashing and wearing shoes lower the burden, especially in children.

Why it matters

Malaria, typhoid, schistosomiasis and other tropical illnesses are commonly seen in East Africa, and they affect fitness for anaesthesia and surgery and complicate emergencies.

Remember

Shoes, latrines and handwashing beat worms.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about intestinal worm infections?

Shoes, latrines and handwashing beat worms.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

rabies-and-animal-bites.title: Rabies and animal bites
rabies-and-animal-bites.caption: Rabies spreads in the saliva of an infected animal, often a dog.
rabies-and-animal-bites.body:
In short: Rabies spreads in the saliva of an infected animal, often a dog.

Urgent Wound Care

Rabies spreads in the saliva of an infected animal, often a dog. Once signs appear it is almost always fatal, but prompt care after a bite works.

Wash the wound with soap and running water for several minutes, then seek urgent vaccination assessment.

Why it matters

Malaria, typhoid, schistosomiasis and other tropical illnesses are commonly seen in East Africa, and they affect fitness for anaesthesia and surgery and complicate emergencies.

Remember

Wash the bite, then go for vaccine.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about rabies and animal bites?

Wash the bite, then go for vaccine.

antenatal-care-contacts.title: Antenatal care contacts
antenatal-care-contacts.caption: Current WHO advice is for pregnant women to have several antenatal contacts, starting early.
antenatal-care-contacts.body:
In short: Current WHO advice is for pregnant women to have several antenatal contacts, starting early.

Regular Checks

Current WHO advice is for pregnant women to have several antenatal contacts, starting early. Visits check blood pressure, anaemia, growth of the baby, infections and give advice and supplements.

Early booking lets problems be found and managed in time.

Why it matters

Obstetric emergencies and caesarean sections make up a big part of theatre work, so understanding pregnancy danger signs and bleeding saves mothers' lives.

Remember

Start antenatal care early.

Check yourself

Start antenatal care early.

  • Fits or convulsions

pre-eclampsia.caption: Pre-eclampsia is high blood pressure with signs of organ strain, such as protein in urine, usually after 20 weeks.
pre-eclampsia.body:
In short: Pre-eclampsia is high blood pressure with signs of organ strain, such as protein in urine, usually after 20 weeks.

High Blood Pressure

Pre-eclampsia is high blood pressure with signs of organ strain, such as protein in urine, usually after 20 weeks. It can progress to eclampsia, with fits.

Blood pressure checks at every visit matter. Magnesium sulphate is the usual drug to prevent and treat fits.

Why it matters

Obstetric emergencies and caesarean sections make up a big part of theatre work, so understanding pregnancy danger signs and bleeding saves mothers' lives.

Remember

Check BP and urine every visit.

Check yourself

Check BP and urine every visit.

third-stage-of-labour-care.caption: The third stage runs from birth of the baby to delivery of the placenta.
third-stage-of-labour-care.body:
In short: The third stage runs from birth of the baby to delivery of the placenta.

After The Baby

The third stage runs from birth of the baby to delivery of the placenta. Active management usually includes a uterotonic drug soon after birth, careful cord traction and uterine massage.

It lowers the risk of postpartum bleeding. Check the placenta is complete.

Why it matters

Obstetric emergencies and caesarean sections make up a big part of theatre work, so understanding pregnancy danger signs and bleeding saves mothers' lives.

Remember

Active management cuts bleeding risk.

What is the main thing to remember about third stage of labour care?

Active management cuts bleeding risk.

the-partograph.title: The partograph
the-partograph.caption: A partograph charts cervical opening, baby's heart rate, contractions, and maternal observations over time.
the-partograph.body:
In short: A partograph charts cervical opening, baby's heart rate, contractions, and maternal observations over time.

Labour On One Page

A partograph charts cervical opening, baby's heart rate, contractions, and maternal observations over time. Lines on the chart show when labour is slow and action is needed.

It helps catch obstructed labour early, so referral or surgery is timely.

Why it matters

Obstetric emergencies and caesarean sections make up a big part of theatre work, so understanding pregnancy danger signs and bleeding saves mothers' lives.

Remember

The chart warns before the crisis.

postnatal-checks.caption: Mothers and babies need checks soon after birth and again within the first days and weeks.
postnatal-checks.body:
In short: Mothers and babies need checks soon after birth and again within the first days and weeks.

The First Weeks

Mothers and babies need checks soon after birth and again within the first days and weeks. Look for bleeding, fever, wound problems, breast issues, low mood and baby feeding and jaundice.

Advise on danger signs and family planning.

Why it matters

Obstetric emergencies and caesarean sections make up a big part of theatre work, so understanding pregnancy danger signs and bleeding saves mothers' lives.

Care does not end at delivery.

anaemia-in-pregnancy.title: Anaemia in pregnancy
anaemia-in-pregnancy.caption: Anaemia is common in pregnancy and raises risks of bleeding, infection and early birth.
anaemia-in-pregnancy.body:
In short: Anaemia is common in pregnancy and raises risks of bleeding, infection and early birth.

Low Haemoglobin

Anaemia is common in pregnancy and raises risks of bleeding, infection and early birth. Causes include iron lack, malaria, hookworm and poor diet.

Prevention uses iron and folic acid supplements, malaria control and deworming per national policy.

Why it matters

Obstetric emergencies and caesarean sections make up a big part of theatre work, so understanding pregnancy danger signs and bleeding saves mothers' lives.

Remember

Iron plus malaria control protects mothers.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about anaemia in pregnancy?

Iron plus malaria control protects mothers.

  • Arrange transport in advance

Plan early, as delays cost lives.

family-planning-counselling.title: Family planning counselling
family-planning-counselling.caption: Counselling should give clear, unbiased information about methods, how well they work, side effects and who they suit.
family-planning-counselling.body:

Informed Choice

Counselling should give clear, unbiased information about methods, how well they work, side effects and who they suit. The client chooses.

Check medical eligibility, explain what to do if problems arise, and respect privacy.

Why it matters

Obstetric emergencies and caesarean sections make up a big part of theatre work, so understanding pregnancy danger signs and bleeding saves mothers' lives.

Remember

The client makes the choice.

routine-childhood-immunisation.title: Routine childhood immunisation
routine-childhood-immunisation.caption: Children receive scheduled vaccines from birth, with doses at set ages, against diseases such as tuberculosis, polio, measles, diphtheria, tetanus and whooping cough.
routine-childhood-immunisation.body:
In short: Children receive scheduled vaccines from birth, with doses at set ages, against diseases such as tuberculosis, polio, measles, diphtheria, tetanus and whooping cough.

Protection Early

Children receive scheduled vaccines from birth, with doses at set ages, against diseases such as tuberculosis, polio, measles, diphtheria, tetanus and whooping cough. The schedule is set nationally.

Record doses on the child health card and follow up missed doses.

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

Keep the card, complete the schedule.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about routine childhood immunisation?

Keep the card, complete the schedule.

imci-general-danger-signs.body:
In short: A quick list on imci general danger signs: Unable to drink or breastfeed; Vomits everything.

IMCI general danger signs

  • Unable to drink or breastfeed
  • Vomits everything
  • Has had convulsions
  • Lethargic or unconscious

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

A child with any of these is urgent.

growth-monitoring.title: Growth monitoring
growth-monitoring.caption: Plotting weight against age on a growth chart over time matters more than one reading.
growth-monitoring.body:
In short: Plotting weight against age on a growth chart over time matters more than one reading.

The Growth Chart

Plotting weight against age on a growth chart over time matters more than one reading. A flat or falling line suggests trouble before the child looks thin.

Early signs lead to feeding advice and a search for illness.

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

Follow the curve, not one point.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about growth monitoring?

Follow the curve, not one point.

kangaroo-mother-care.title: Kangaroo mother care
kangaroo-mother-care.caption: Small babies are held upright against the mother's bare chest, wrapped, with frequent breastfeeding.
kangaroo-mother-care.body:
In short: Small babies are held upright against the mother's bare chest, wrapped, with frequent breastfeeding.

Skin To Skin

Small babies are held upright against the mother's bare chest, wrapped, with frequent breastfeeding. It helps keep them warm, supports feeding and reduces infection and deaths.

Fathers and relatives can also give skin contact.

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

Skin to skin keeps small babies warm.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about kangaroo mother care?

Skin to skin keeps small babies warm.

exclusive-breastfeeding.title: Exclusive breastfeeding
exclusive-breastfeeding.caption: WHO advises breast milk alone, with no water or other foods, for about the first six months, then continued breastfeeding with other foods.
exclusive-breastfeeding.body:
In short: WHO advises breast milk alone, with no water or other foods, for about the first six months, then continued breastfeeding with other foods.

First Six Months

WHO advises breast milk alone, with no water or other foods, for about the first six months, then continued breastfeeding with other foods.

It protects against infections, supports growth and bonding. HIV-positive mothers on treatment are usually advised to breastfeed too.

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

Breast milk alone for six months.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about exclusive breastfeeding?

Breast milk alone for six months.

ors-and-zinc-for-diarrhoea.title: ORS and zinc for diarrhoea
ors-and-zinc-for-diarrhoea.caption: Oral rehydration solution replaces water and salts lost in diarrhoea.
ors-and-zinc-for-diarrhoea.body:
In short: Oral rehydration solution replaces water and salts lost in diarrhoea.

Treat The Loss

Oral rehydration solution replaces water and salts lost in diarrhoea. Zinc given for around ten days shortens illness and lowers repeat episodes.

Keep feeding and breastfeeding. Refer if blood in stool, repeated vomiting or very sleepy.

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

ORS plus zinc, and keep feeding.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ors and zinc for diarrhoea?

ORS plus zinc, and keep feeding.

spotting-childhood-pneumonia.title: Spotting childhood pneumonia
spotting-childhood-pneumonia.caption: In children with cough, fast breathing for their age is a key sign of pneumonia.
spotting-childhood-pneumonia.body:
In short: In children with cough, fast breathing for their age is a key sign of pneumonia.

Fast Breathing

In children with cough, fast breathing for their age is a key sign of pneumonia. Chest indrawing or inability to drink suggests severe disease needing referral.

Count breaths for a full minute while the child is calm.

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

Count breaths for a full minute.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about spotting childhood pneumonia?

Count breaths for a full minute.

newborn-danger-signs.title: Newborn danger signs
newborn-danger-signs.caption: A quick list on newborn danger signs: Not feeding well or feeding poorly; Fits, floppy or very sleepy.
newborn-danger-signs.body:
In short: A quick list on newborn danger signs: Not feeding well or feeding poorly; Fits, floppy or very sleepy.

Newborn danger signs

  • Not feeding well or feeding poorly
  • Fits, floppy or very sleepy
  • Fever or feeling cold
  • Fast or difficult breathing
  • Yellow skin in the first day

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

Newborns worsen quickly, so refer early.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Newborn danger signs".

Not feeding well or feeding poorly; Fits, floppy or very sleepy; Fever or feeling cold; Fast or difficult breathing; Yellow skin in the first day.

febrile-convulsions.title: Febrile convulsions
febrile-convulsions.caption: Some young children have a seizure with a high temperature.
febrile-convulsions.body:
In short: Some young children have a seizure with a high temperature.

Fever Fits

Some young children have a seizure with a high temperature. Most stop within minutes. Place the child on their side, protect from injury, and do not put anything in the mouth.

Seek care, as the fever cause must be found, and seizures that last long are an emergency.

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

Side position, nothing in the mouth.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about febrile convulsions?

Side position, nothing in the mouth.

developmental-milestones.title: Developmental milestones
developmental-milestones.caption: Children usually learn to smile, sit, walk and talk in a broad but predictable order.
developmental-milestones.body:
In short: Children usually learn to smile, sit, walk and talk in a broad but predictable order.

Watching Development

Children usually learn to smile, sit, walk and talk in a broad but predictable order. Wide delays in several areas deserve assessment.

Hearing, vision and early stimulation matter. Talking, play and responsive care help brain development.

Why it matters

Children are not small adults. Knowing danger signs, feeding and common childhood illnesses helps teams recognise sick children early and prepare for paediatric surgery.

Remember

Ask caregivers what the child can do.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about developmental milestones?

Ask caregivers what the child can do.

the-hiv-window-period.title: The HIV window period
the-hiv-window-period.caption: After infection, tests may not yet detect HIV.
the-hiv-window-period.body:
In short: After infection, tests may not yet detect HIV.

Testing Timing

After infection, tests may not yet detect HIV. This is the window period, and its length depends on the test type. A negative result soon after a risk may need repeating.

A positive screening test is confirmed by following the national testing algorithm.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

A recent risk may need a retest.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about the hiv window period?

A recent risk may need a retest.

confidential-hiv-testing.title: Confidential HIV testing
confidential-hiv-testing.caption: HIV testing is voluntary, with pre-test information, informed consent and confidentiality.
confidential-hiv-testing.body:
In short: HIV testing is voluntary, with pre-test information, informed consent and confidentiality.

Consent And Privacy

HIV testing is voluntary, with pre-test information, informed consent and confidentiality. Results are shared only with those who need to know for care.

Good counselling supports linking positive clients to treatment and negative clients to prevention.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

Consent and confidentiality always.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about confidential hiv testing?

Consent and confidentiality always.

undetectable-equals-untransmittable.title: Undetectable equals untransmittable
undetectable-equals-untransmittable.caption: People on effective antiretroviral therapy with a sustained undetectable viral load do not pass HIV on through sex.
undetectable-equals-untransmittable.body:
In short: People on effective antiretroviral therapy with a sustained undetectable viral load do not pass HIV on through sex.

U Equals U

People on effective antiretroviral therapy with a sustained undetectable viral load do not pass HIV on through sex. Treatment is also prevention.

This needs regular adherence and viral load checks. Other infections still need condoms.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

Treatment protects the person and partners.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about undetectable equals untransmittable?

Treatment protects the person and partners.

preventing-hiv-passing-to-babies.title: Preventing HIV passing to babies
preventing-hiv-passing-to-babies.caption: Without intervention, HIV can pass during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding.
preventing-hiv-passing-to-babies.body:
In short: Without intervention, HIV can pass during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding.

Pmtct

Without intervention, HIV can pass during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding. Mothers on lifelong antiretroviral therapy, with infant prophylaxis and safe feeding advice, greatly reduce this risk.

Babies exposed to HIV are tested at set ages.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

Treat the mother, protect the baby.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about preventing hiv passing to babies?

Treat the mother, protect the baby.

post-exposure-prophylaxis.title: Post-exposure prophylaxis
post-exposure-prophylaxis.caption: After a needlestick or other high-risk exposure, antiretroviral drugs can lower infection risk if started quickly, ideally within hours and no later than around 72 hours.
post-exposure-prophylaxis.body:
In short: After a needlestick or other high-risk exposure, antiretroviral drugs can lower infection risk if started quickly, ideally within hours and no later than around 72 hours.

After Exposure

After a needlestick or other high-risk exposure, antiretroviral drugs can lower infection risk if started quickly, ideally within hours and no later than around 72 hours.

Wash the area, report it and get assessed urgently. Follow-up testing is done.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

Start PEP fast, within hours.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about post-exposure prophylaxis?

Start PEP fast, within hours.

cd4-cells-and-infections.title: CD4 cells and infections
cd4-cells-and-infections.caption: HIV damages CD4 cells, so the body fails to resist infections such as TB, thrush and pneumonia.
cd4-cells-and-infections.body:
In short: HIV damages CD4 cells, so the body fails to resist infections such as TB, thrush and pneumonia.

Weakened Defences

HIV damages CD4 cells, so the body fails to resist infections such as TB, thrush and pneumonia. Advanced disease raises these risks.

Starting antiretroviral therapy early restores immunity. Preventive medicines are used in some patients.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

Early treatment rebuilds immunity.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cd4 cells and infections?

Early treatment rebuilds immunity.

supporting-adherence.title: Supporting adherence
supporting-adherence.caption: A quick list on supporting adherence: Link pills to a daily routine; Use reminders, such as alarms or a buddy.
supporting-adherence.body:
In short: A quick list on supporting adherence: Link pills to a daily routine; Use reminders, such as alarms or a buddy.

Supporting adherence

  • Link pills to a daily routine
  • Use reminders, such as alarms or a buddy
  • Plan for travel and for running out
  • Talk openly about side effects
  • Never stop without advice

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

Missed doses can lead to drug resistance.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Supporting adherence".

Link pills to a daily routine; Use reminders, such as alarms or a buddy; Plan for travel and for running out; Talk openly about side effects; Never stop without advice.

viral-load-monitoring.title: Viral load monitoring
viral-load-monitoring.caption: Viral load measures how much HIV is in the blood.
viral-load-monitoring.body:
In short: Viral load measures how much HIV is in the blood.

Tracking Treatment

Viral load measures how much HIV is in the blood. It is the best sign that treatment works. A raised viral load prompts adherence support and then review of the regimen.

Tests are usually done at set intervals set by national guidelines.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

Viral load shows how well treatment works.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about viral load monitoring?

Viral load shows how well treatment works.

fighting-hiv-stigma.title: Fighting HIV stigma
fighting-hiv-stigma.caption: Fear of judgement keeps people from testing and treatment.
fighting-hiv-stigma.body:
In short: Fear of judgement keeps people from testing and treatment.

Respect

Fear of judgement keeps people from testing and treatment. Health workers must not gossip, refuse care or treat patients differently.

Use respectful language and keep records safe. Stigma harms health outcomes, so care should always be kind.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

Respect makes people come back.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about fighting hiv stigma?

Respect makes people come back.

after-a-sharps-injury.title: After a sharps injury
after-a-sharps-injury.caption: A quick list on after a sharps injury: Let the wound bleed gently, do not squeeze hard; Wash with soap and running water.
after-a-sharps-injury.body:
In short: A quick list on after a sharps injury: Let the wound bleed gently, do not squeeze hard; Wash with soap and running water.

After a sharps injury

  • Let the wound bleed gently, do not squeeze hard
  • Wash with soap and running water
  • Rinse splashed eyes or mouth with water
  • Report to the supervisor at once
  • Get assessed for PEP and follow-up

Why it matters

Many surgical patients live with HIV. Respectful care, confidentiality and knowing treatment basics and exposure response protect patients and staff.

Remember

Do not delay reporting a needlestick.

List the points covered under "After a sharps injury".

Let the wound bleed gently, do not squeeze hard; Wash with soap and running water; Rinse splashed eyes or mouth with water; Report to the supervisor at once; Get assessed for PEP and follow-up.

how-tb-spreads.title: How TB spreads
how-tb-spreads.caption: Pulmonary TB spreads when a person with active disease coughs, sneezes or speaks, releasing tiny droplets carrying Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
how-tb-spreads.body:
In short: Pulmonary TB spreads when a person with active disease coughs, sneezes or speaks, releasing tiny droplets carrying Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

Airborne Germs

Pulmonary TB spreads when a person with active disease coughs, sneezes or speaks, releasing tiny droplets carrying Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Others breathe them in.

TB does not spread from shaking hands or sharing plates. Latent TB is not infectious.

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

TB travels through the air.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about how tb spreads?

TB travels through the air.

tb-symptom-screening.title: TB symptom screening
tb-symptom-screening.caption: A quick list on tb symptom screening: Cough, especially lasting two weeks or more; Fever or night sweats.
tb-symptom-screening.body:
In short: A quick list on tb symptom screening: Cough, especially lasting two weeks or more; Fever or night sweats.

TB symptom screening

  • Cough, especially lasting two weeks or more
  • Fever or night sweats
  • Weight loss
  • Extreme tiredness
  • Sometimes blood in the sputum

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

Cough for two weeks needs a test.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "TB symptom screening".

Cough, especially lasting two weeks or more; Fever or night sweats; Weight loss; Extreme tiredness; Sometimes blood in the sputum.

genexpert-testing.title: GeneXpert testing
genexpert-testing.caption: GeneXpert is a molecular test that detects TB germs in sputum within hours and also shows if rifampicin resistance is likely.
genexpert-testing.body:
In short: GeneXpert is a molecular test that detects TB germs in sputum within hours and also shows if rifampicin resistance is likely.

Fast Tb Test

GeneXpert is a molecular test that detects TB germs in sputum within hours and also shows if rifampicin resistance is likely. It is now often the first test.

Smear microscopy, culture and chest X-ray still have roles.

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

Rapid tests speed up the right treatment.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about genexpert testing?

Rapid tests speed up the right treatment.

directly-observed-therapy.title: Directly observed therapy
directly-observed-therapy.caption: TB treatment takes months, with several medicines.
directly-observed-therapy.body:
In short: TB treatment takes months, with several medicines.

Supported Treatment

TB treatment takes months, with several medicines. Treatment supporters or digital reminders help patients finish. Stopping early causes relapse and drug resistance.

A relative, health worker or volunteer may be trained to support.

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

Finish the course, even when feeling well.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about directly observed therapy?

Finish the course, even when feeling well.

drug-resistant-tb.title: Drug-resistant TB
drug-resistant-tb.caption: TB resistant to rifampicin or other first-line drugs needs special regimens, longer follow-up and expert care.
drug-resistant-tb.body:
In short: TB resistant to rifampicin or other first-line drugs needs special regimens, longer follow-up and expert care.

When Drugs Fail

TB resistant to rifampicin or other first-line drugs needs special regimens, longer follow-up and expert care. It arises from incomplete treatment or from catching a resistant strain.

Good adherence and early testing prevent it.

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

Incomplete treatment breeds resistance.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about drug-resistant tb?

Incomplete treatment breeds resistance.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tb-and-hiv-together.title: TB and HIV together
tb-and-hiv-together.caption: TB is a leading cause of illness in people with HIV.
tb-and-hiv-together.body:
In short: TB is a leading cause of illness in people with HIV.

Double Burden

TB is a leading cause of illness in people with HIV. Everyone with TB should be offered an HIV test, and people with HIV should be screened for TB regularly.

Treatment for both is usually coordinated and monitored for drug interactions.

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

Test TB patients for HIV.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tb and hiv together?

Test TB patients for HIV.

tb-infection-control.title: TB infection control
tb-infection-control.caption: A quick list on tb infection control: Open windows for good air flow; Cover coughs and teach cough etiquette.
tb-infection-control.body:
In short: A quick list on tb infection control: Open windows for good air flow; Cover coughs and teach cough etiquette.

TB infection control

  • Open windows for good air flow
  • Cover coughs and teach cough etiquette
  • Separate coughing patients when possible
  • Staff use N95 or similar respirators
  • Start treatment promptly

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

Air and speed are the best protection.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "TB infection control".

Open windows for good air flow; Cover coughs and teach cough etiquette; Separate coughing patients when possible; Staff use N95 or similar respirators; Start treatment promptly.

tb-outside-the-lungs.title: TB outside the lungs
tb-outside-the-lungs.caption: TB can affect lymph nodes, bones and spine, the brain's lining, the abdomen and other organs.
tb-outside-the-lungs.body:
In short: TB can affect lymph nodes, bones and spine, the brain's lining, the abdomen and other organs.

Extrapulmonary Tb

TB can affect lymph nodes, bones and spine, the brain's lining, the abdomen and other organs. Signs depend on the site, such as neck swellings or back pain with deformity.

Biopsy or fluid tests may be needed. Many forms are not infectious.

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

TB can appear almost anywhere.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tb outside the lungs?

TB can appear almost anywhere.
