contact-tracing.title: Contact tracing
contact-tracing.caption: People living closely with a TB patient, especially children and those with HIV, are at risk.
contact-tracing.body:
In short: People living closely with a TB patient, especially children and those with HIV, are at risk.

Finding Others

People living closely with a TB patient, especially children and those with HIV, are at risk. Contacts are screened for symptoms and tested where needed.

Young children and people with HIV may receive preventive treatment as per national guidelines.

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

Screen the household.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about contact tracing?

Screen the household.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tb-medicine-side-effects.title: TB medicine side effects
tb-medicine-side-effects.caption: Common side effects include nausea, rash, joint pain and orange urine.
tb-medicine-side-effects.body:
In short: Common side effects include nausea, rash, joint pain and orange urine.

Watch The Patient

Common side effects include nausea, rash, joint pain and orange urine. Jaundice, persistent vomiting, vision change or hearing loss need prompt review, as some drugs affect the liver, eyes or nerves.

Explain these early to avoid stopping treatment.

Why it matters

TB remains common and affects the lungs, bones and other organs. Theatre and ward staff need to understand its signs, treatment and infection control.

Remember

Report jaundice or vision change quickly.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tb medicine side effects?

Report jaundice or vision change quickly.

drabc-approach.title: DRABC approach
drabc-approach.caption: A quick list on drabc approach: D: check for Danger to you and others; R: check Response, shout and tap.
drabc-approach.body:
In short: A quick list on drabc approach: D: check for Danger to you and others; R: check Response, shout and tap.

DRABC approach

  • D: check for Danger to you and others
  • R: check Response, shout and tap
  • A: open the Airway
  • B: look for Breathing
  • C: check Circulation, control bleeding

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

Safety first, then airway.

D: check for Danger to you and others; R: check Response, shout and tap; A: open the Airway; B: look for Breathing; C: check Circulation, control bleeding.

placing-a-casualty-on-their-side.title: Placing a casualty on their side
placing-a-casualty-on-their-side.caption: A quick list on placing a casualty on their side: Use for unresponsive but breathing casualties; Kneel beside them, place near arm out.
placing-a-casualty-on-their-side.body:
In short: A quick list on placing a casualty on their side: Use for unresponsive but breathing casualties; Kneel beside them, place near arm out.

Placing a casualty on their side

  • Use for unresponsive but breathing casualties
  • Kneel beside them, place near arm out
  • Bring far knee up, roll gently onto the side
  • Tilt head back to keep airway open
  • Recheck breathing often

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

On the side keeps the airway clear.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Placing a casualty on their side".

Use for unresponsive but breathing casualties; Kneel beside them, place near arm out; Bring far knee up, roll gently onto the side; Tilt head back to keep airway open; Recheck breathing often.

stopping-heavy-bleeding.title: Stopping heavy bleeding
stopping-heavy-bleeding.caption: A quick list on stopping heavy bleeding: Apply firm direct pressure with a pad; Keep pressing, do not lift to peek.
stopping-heavy-bleeding.body:
In short: A quick list on stopping heavy bleeding: Apply firm direct pressure with a pad; Keep pressing, do not lift to peek.

Stopping heavy bleeding

  • Apply firm direct pressure with a pad
  • Keep pressing, do not lift to peek
  • Add more pads on top if soaked
  • Bandage firmly, raise limb if no fracture
  • Call for help, treat for shock

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

Press hard and keep pressing.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Stopping heavy bleeding".

Apply firm direct pressure with a pad; Keep pressing, do not lift to peek; Add more pads on top if soaked; Bandage firmly, raise limb if no fracture; Call for help, treat for shock.

cooling-a-burn.title: Cooling a burn
cooling-a-burn.caption: A quick list on cooling a burn: Stop the burning and remove from danger; Cool with running water for about 20 minutes.
cooling-a-burn.body:
In short: A quick list on cooling a burn: Stop the burning and remove from danger; Cool with running water for about 20 minutes.

Cooling a burn

  • Stop the burning and remove from danger
  • Cool with running water for about 20 minutes
  • Remove rings and tight items before swelling
  • Cover loosely with clean non-fluffy material
  • Seek help for large or deep burns

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

Cool the burn, do not use butter.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Cooling a burn".

Stop the burning and remove from danger; Cool with running water for about 20 minutes; Remove rings and tight items before swelling; Cover loosely with clean non-fluffy material; Seek help for large or deep burns.

choking-in-adults.title: Choking in adults
choking-in-adults.caption: A quick list on choking in adults: Ask if they can cough or speak; Encourage coughing if airway partly blocked.
choking-in-adults.body:
In short: A quick list on choking in adults: Ask if they can cough or speak; Encourage coughing if airway partly blocked.

Choking in adults

  • Ask if they can cough or speak
  • Encourage coughing if airway partly blocked
  • Give up to five back blows if it worsens
  • Then up to five abdominal thrusts
  • Call for help if it does not clear

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

Back blows first, then thrusts.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Choking in adults".

Ask if they can cough or speak; Encourage coughing if airway partly blocked; Give up to five back blows if it worsens; Then up to five abdominal thrusts; Call for help if it does not clear.

suspected-fractures.title: Suspected fractures
suspected-fractures.caption: Signs include pain, swelling, deformity and inability to use the limb.
suspected-fractures.body:
In short: Signs include pain, swelling, deformity and inability to use the limb.

Support And Immobilise

Signs include pain, swelling, deformity and inability to use the limb. Keep the limb still, support it as found, and immobilise the joints above and below with a splint.

Cover open wounds and check circulation beyond the splint. Do not try to straighten it.

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

Splint it as found.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about suspected fractures?

Splint it as found.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

recognising-shock.title: Recognising shock
recognising-shock.caption: Shock means poor blood flow to organs.
recognising-shock.body:
In short: Shock means poor blood flow to organs.

Circulation Failing

Shock means poor blood flow to organs. Signs include pale cool clammy skin, fast weak pulse, fast breathing and confusion.

Control bleeding, lay the person flat, keep them warm, give nothing by mouth, and get urgent help.

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

Lie flat, keep warm, call help.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about recognising shock?

Lie flat, keep warm, call help.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

snakebite-first-aid.title: Snakebite first aid
snakebite-first-aid.caption: Keep the person calm and still, with the bitten limb immobilised at about heart level.
snakebite-first-aid.body:
In short: Keep the person calm and still, with the bitten limb immobilised at about heart level.

Stay Calm, Stay Still

Keep the person calm and still, with the bitten limb immobilised at about heart level. Remove rings and tight items. Get to a hospital with antivenom quickly.

Avoid cutting, sucking, tourniquets or herbal treatments. Note the time and the snake's look if safe.

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

Immobilise and get to hospital fast.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about snakebite first aid?

Immobilise and get to hospital fast.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

helping-someone-having-a-seizure.title: Helping someone having a seizure
helping-someone-having-a-seizure.caption: Clear hard objects, cushion the head and loosen tight clothing.
helping-someone-having-a-seizure.body:
In short: Clear hard objects, cushion the head and loosen tight clothing.

Protect, Do Not Restrain

Clear hard objects, cushion the head and loosen tight clothing. Do not hold the person down or put anything in their mouth. Time the seizure.

Afterwards place them in the recovery position. Call help if it lasts over five minutes or repeats.

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

Protect the head, time the seizure.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about helping someone having a seizure?

Protect the head, time the seizure.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

suspected-poisoning.title: Suspected poisoning
suspected-poisoning.caption: Check the scene is safe and the airway and breathing are ok.
suspected-poisoning.body:
In short: Check the scene is safe and the airway and breathing are ok.

Act Quickly

Check the scene is safe and the airway and breathing are ok. Find out what, how much and when. Keep containers to show the doctor.

Do not induce vomiting unless told by a poison centre or clinician. Get medical help urgently.

Why it matters

Many patients arrive after injury, and early first aid decides outcomes. These steps are the foundation of emergency care before and during hospital arrival.

Remember

Keep the container, do not induce vomiting.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about suspected poisoning?

Keep the container, do not induce vomiting.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

five-moments-for-hand-hygiene.title: Five moments for hand hygiene
five-moments-for-hand-hygiene.caption: A quick list on five moments for hand hygiene: Before touching a patient; Before a clean or aseptic procedure.
five-moments-for-hand-hygiene.body:
In short: A quick list on five moments for hand hygiene: Before touching a patient; Before a clean or aseptic procedure.

Five moments for hand hygiene

  • Before touching a patient
  • Before a clean or aseptic procedure
  • After body fluid exposure risk
  • After touching a patient
  • After touching patient surroundings

Why it matters

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Remember

Clean hands at every moment.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Five moments for hand hygiene".

Before touching a patient; Before a clean or aseptic procedure; After body fluid exposure risk; After touching a patient; After touching patient surroundings.

taking-vital-signs.title: Taking vital signs
taking-vital-signs.caption: Pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature and oxygen saturation, often with consciousness level and pain score, show how a patient is doing.
taking-vital-signs.body:
In short: Pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature and oxygen saturation, often with consciousness level and pain score, show how a patient is doing.

The Basics

Pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature and oxygen saturation, often with consciousness level and pain score, show how a patient is doing. Trends matter more than a single reading.

Use the right equipment and size, and report abnormal values promptly.

Why it matters

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Remember

Trends tell the story.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about taking vital signs?

Trends tell the story.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

correct-patient-identification.title: Correct patient identification
correct-patient-identification.caption: Confirm identity using at least two identifiers, such as name and date of birth, and ask the patient to state them where possible.
correct-patient-identification.body:
In short: Confirm identity using at least two identifiers, such as name and date of birth, and ask the patient to state them where possible.

Right Patient

Confirm identity using at least two identifiers, such as name and date of birth, and ask the patient to state them where possible. Check against the wristband and records.

Do this before medicines, blood, tests and procedures.

Why it matters

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Remember

Two identifiers, every time.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about correct patient identification?

Two identifiers, every time.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

good-nursing-documentation.title: Good nursing documentation
good-nursing-documentation.caption: Records should be accurate, timely, legible, signed and dated, and describe what was seen and done.
good-nursing-documentation.body:
In short: Records should be accurate, timely, legible, signed and dated, and describe what was seen and done.

If Not Written

Records should be accurate, timely, legible, signed and dated, and describe what was seen and done. Write facts, not opinions, and never alter entries; correct with a single line and your signature.

Good notes support safe handover and continuity.

Why it matters

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Remember

Write facts, sign and date.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about good nursing documentation?

Write facts, sign and date.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

preventing-pressure-injuries.title: Preventing pressure injuries
preventing-pressure-injuries.caption: Pressure injuries arise when bony areas are squeezed for too long.
preventing-pressure-injuries.body:
In short: Pressure injuries arise when bony areas are squeezed for too long.

Skin Care

Pressure injuries arise when bony areas are squeezed for too long. Risk rises with immobility, moisture and poor nutrition.

Repeat position changes, keep skin clean and dry, use pressure-relieving surfaces and check heels, sacrum and hips.

Why it matters

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Remember

Move, check, and keep skin dry.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about preventing pressure injuries?

Move, check, and keep skin dry.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

fluid-balance-charting.title: Fluid balance charting
fluid-balance-charting.caption: Record all fluids in, orally and by drip, and fluids out, such as urine, drains, vomit and stool.
fluid-balance-charting.body:
In short: Record all fluids in, orally and by drip, and fluids out, such as urine, drains, vomit and stool.

Intake And Output

Record all fluids in, orally and by drip, and fluids out, such as urine, drains, vomit and stool. Total regularly to see the balance.

Low urine output or large imbalance may signal dehydration, bleeding or kidney problems, so report it.

Why it matters

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Remember

Record every drop in and out.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about fluid balance charting?

Record every drop in and out.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

rights-of-medication-safety.caption: A quick list on rights of medication safety: Right patient; Right drug.
rights-of-medication-safety.body:

Rights of medication safety

  • Right drug
  • Right dose and right route
  • Right time

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Check, then check again.

safe-moving-and-handling.title: Safe moving and handling
safe-moving-and-handling.caption: Assess the patient and the task before moving.
safe-moving-and-handling.body:
In short: Assess the patient and the task before moving.

Protect Back And Patient

Assess the patient and the task before moving. Use slide sheets, hoists and enough helpers. Keep your back straight, feet apart and the load close.

Explain the move to the patient and coordinate the lift with a clear count.

Why it matters

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Remember

Plan the move, then use help.

Check yourself

Plan the move, then use help.

communicating-with-anxious-patients.title: Communicating with anxious patients
communicating-with-anxious-patients.caption: Introduce yourself, use simple words and a calm tone, and let the patient ask questions.
communicating-with-anxious-patients.body:
In short: Introduce yourself, use simple words and a calm tone, and let the patient ask questions.

Calm And Clear

Introduce yourself, use simple words and a calm tone, and let the patient ask questions. Listen first. Use interpreters when languages differ.

Tell patients what will happen, protect privacy and acknowledge fear. Clear communication reduces anxiety.

Why it matters

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Remember

Listen first, explain simply.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about communicating with anxious patients?

Listen first, explain simply.

handover-with-sbar.title: Handover with SBAR
handover-with-sbar.caption: A quick list on handover with sbar: Situation: who and what is happening now; Background: history and what led here.
handover-with-sbar.body:

Handover with SBAR

  • Background: history and what led here

Core nursing skills such as hygiene, observations, identification and handover underpin safe perioperative care for every patient.

Short, clear, structured handover.

Situation: who and what is happening now; Background: history and what led here; Assessment: your findings and concerns; Recommendation: what you need done.

health-education-versus-promotion.title: Health education versus promotion
health-education-versus-promotion.caption: Health education gives information and skills.
health-education-versus-promotion.body:
In short: Health education gives information and skills.

Broader Than Teaching

Health education gives information and skills. Health promotion goes further, working on policies, supportive environments and community action so healthy choices are easier.

Teaching hand washing is education; building handwashing stations is promotion.

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Make healthy choices the easy choices.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about health education versus promotion?

Make healthy choices the easy choices.

stages-of-behaviour-change.title: Stages of behaviour change
stages-of-behaviour-change.caption: A quick list on stages of behaviour change: Pre-contemplation: not yet thinking of change; Contemplation: weighing it up.
stages-of-behaviour-change.body:
In short: A quick list on stages of behaviour change: Pre-contemplation: not yet thinking of change; Contemplation: weighing it up.

Stages of behaviour change

  • Pre-contemplation: not yet thinking of change
  • Contemplation: weighing it up
  • Preparation: planning to act
  • Action: making the change
  • Maintenance: keeping it going

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Meet people at their stage.

Check yourself

Pre-contemplation: not yet thinking of change; Contemplation: weighing it up; Preparation: planning to act; Action: making the change; Maintenance: keeping it going.

teach-back-method.title: Teach-back method
teach-back-method.caption: After explaining, ask the patient to say in their own words what they will do.
teach-back-method.body:
In short: After explaining, ask the patient to say in their own words what they will do.

Check Understanding

After explaining, ask the patient to say in their own words what they will do. It checks that your teaching worked, not that the patient is slow.

If they get it wrong, explain again differently. It improves safety and medicine use.

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Ask them to explain it back.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about teach-back method?

Ask them to explain it back.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

community-health-volunteers.title: Community health volunteers
community-health-volunteers.caption: Community health volunteers live among the people they serve.
community-health-volunteers.body:
In short: Community health volunteers live among the people they serve.

First Link

Community health volunteers live among the people they serve. They visit homes, give health messages, refer sick people and support follow-up of treatments and immunisation.

Supervision, training and trust from the community keep their work effective.

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Trusted neighbours extend health care.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about community health volunteers?

Trusted neighbours extend health care.

brief-advice-to-stop-tobacco.title: Brief advice to stop tobacco
brief-advice-to-stop-tobacco.caption: Ask about tobacco at each contact, advise clearly to quit, and offer support such as counselling, medicines where available and follow-up.
brief-advice-to-stop-tobacco.body:
In short: Ask about tobacco at each contact, advise clearly to quit, and offer support such as counselling, medicines where available and follow-up.

Ask, Advise, Assist

Ask about tobacco at each contact, advise clearly to quit, and offer support such as counselling, medicines where available and follow-up.

Quitting before surgery helps wound healing and lung function, and any time is a good time to stop.

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Every contact is a chance to ask.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about brief advice to stop tobacco?

Every contact is a chance to ask.

physical-activity-for-health.title: Physical activity for health
physical-activity-for-health.caption: Regular activity lowers risk of heart disease, diabetes, some cancers and depression.
physical-activity-for-health.body:
In short: Regular activity lowers risk of heart disease, diabetes, some cancers and depression.

Move More

Regular activity lowers risk of heart disease, diabetes, some cancers and depression. Adults are advised to do moderate activity such as brisk walking on most days.

Any increase helps. Choose enjoyable activities and begin gradually if unfit.

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Some movement beats none.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about physical activity for health?

Some movement beats none.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

harmful-use-of-alcohol.title: Harmful use of alcohol
harmful-use-of-alcohol.caption: Heavy alcohol use harms the liver, heart and brain, and raises risks of injury, violence and road crashes.
harmful-use-of-alcohol.body:
In short: Heavy alcohol use harms the liver, heart and brain, and raises risks of injury, violence and road crashes.

Know The Risks

Heavy alcohol use harms the liver, heart and brain, and raises risks of injury, violence and road crashes. It also complicates surgery and anaesthesia.

Ask about alcohol without judgement, give brief advice and refer those who need help.

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Ask without judging.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about harmful use of alcohol?

Ask without judging.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

road-traffic-injury-prevention.title: Road traffic injury prevention
road-traffic-injury-prevention.caption: Road crashes injure many, especially young people and riders of motorcycles.
road-traffic-injury-prevention.body:
In short: Road crashes injure many, especially young people and riders of motorcycles.

A Major Cause Of Injury

Road crashes injure many, especially young people and riders of motorcycles. Helmets, seat belts, child restraints, sober driving and sensible speed all reduce harm.

Theatre teams see the results, so community messages matter.

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Helmets and seat belts save lives.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about road traffic injury prevention?

Helmets and seat belts save lives.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

social-determinants-of-health.title: Social determinants of health
social-determinants-of-health.caption: Income, education, housing, clean water, work and social support strongly shape health.
social-determinants-of-health.body:
In short: Income, education, housing, clean water, work and social support strongly shape health.

Beyond The Clinic

Income, education, housing, clean water, work and social support strongly shape health. People in poorer conditions often fall ill more and reach care late.

Health workers can advocate and refer to social support.

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Health is shaped by living conditions.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about social determinants of health?

Health is shaped by living conditions.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

health-literacy.title: Health literacy
health-literacy.caption: Health literacy is the ability to find, understand and use health information.
health-literacy.body:
In short: Health literacy is the ability to find, understand and use health information.

Understanding Information

Health literacy is the ability to find, understand and use health information. Low literacy affects many people, including educated ones, when jargon is used.

Use plain language, pictures, local languages and short messages.

Why it matters

Health workers teach and advocate as well as treat. Promoting healthy behaviour reduces the illness and injury that bring people to hospital.

Remember

Plain words improve care.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about health literacy?

Plain words improve care.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

forms-of-malnutrition.title: Forms of malnutrition
forms-of-malnutrition.caption: Malnutrition includes undernutrition (wasting, stunting, underweight), micronutrient deficiencies, and overweight or obesity.
forms-of-malnutrition.body:
In short: Malnutrition includes undernutrition (wasting, stunting, underweight), micronutrient deficiencies, and overweight or obesity.

More Than Hunger

Malnutrition includes undernutrition (wasting, stunting, underweight), micronutrient deficiencies, and overweight or obesity. All can occur in the same community or even household.

Stunting reflects long-term shortage, wasting a recent severe loss.

Why it matters

Nutritional state strongly affects surgical risk, wound healing and recovery, and community nutrition work addresses the causes upstream.

Remember

Malnutrition has many faces.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about forms of malnutrition?

Malnutrition has many faces.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

muac-screening.title: MUAC screening
muac-screening.caption: Mid-upper arm circumference is measured with a coloured tape, often in children aged six to fifty-nine months.
muac-screening.body:
In short: Mid-upper arm circumference is measured with a coloured tape, often in children aged six to fifty-nine months.

Arm Band Check

Mid-upper arm circumference is measured with a coloured tape, often in children aged six to fifty-nine months. The colour bands show normal, moderate or severe acute malnutrition.

It is quick and suits community screening. Check for swelling of both feet too.

Why it matters

Nutritional state strongly affects surgical risk, wound healing and recovery, and community nutrition work addresses the causes upstream.

Remember

Red on the tape means refer.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about muac screening?

Red on the tape means refer.

a-balanced-diet.title: A balanced diet
a-balanced-diet.caption: A balanced diet includes staples for energy, beans or animal foods for protein, fruits and vegetables for vitamins, and some healthy fats, with limited sugar and salt.
a-balanced-diet.body:
In short: A balanced diet includes staples for energy, beans or animal foods for protein, fruits and vegetables for vitamins, and some healthy fats, with limited sugar and salt.

Food Groups

A balanced diet includes staples for energy, beans or animal foods for protein, fruits and vegetables for vitamins, and some healthy fats, with limited sugar and salt.

Eating a variety of local foods each day gives the needed nutrients.

Why it matters

Nutritional state strongly affects surgical risk, wound healing and recovery, and community nutrition work addresses the causes upstream.

Remember

Eat a variety of colours daily.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about a balanced diet?

Eat a variety of colours daily.

complementary-feeding.title: Complementary feeding
complementary-feeding.caption: From about six months, breast milk alone is no longer enough.
complementary-feeding.body:
In short: From about six months, breast milk alone is no longer enough.

Starting Solids

From about six months, breast milk alone is no longer enough. Add safe, thick, energy and nutrient-rich foods, including animal foods, pulses and vegetables, while continuing breastfeeding.

Increase amount and variety with age, and feed responsively.

Why it matters

Nutritional state strongly affects surgical risk, wound healing and recovery, and community nutrition work addresses the causes upstream.

Remember

Add foods at six months, keep breastfeeding.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about complementary feeding?

Add foods at six months, keep breastfeeding.

iron-deficiency.title: Iron deficiency
iron-deficiency.caption: Iron deficiency causes anaemia, tiredness, poor learning and pale skin.
iron-deficiency.body:
In short: Iron deficiency causes anaemia, tiredness, poor learning and pale skin.

Common And Fixable

Iron deficiency causes anaemia, tiredness, poor learning and pale skin. Good sources include meat, liver, beans and dark leafy vegetables.

Vitamin C foods help absorption, and tea with meals can reduce it. Supplements are given to some groups.

Why it matters

Nutritional state strongly affects surgical risk, wound healing and recovery, and community nutrition work addresses the causes upstream.

Remember

Pair iron foods with vitamin C.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about iron deficiency?

Pair iron foods with vitamin C.

vitamin-a.title: Vitamin A
vitamin-a.caption: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, serious eye damage and higher infection risk in children.
vitamin-a.body:
In short: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, serious eye damage and higher infection risk in children.

Eyes And Immunity

Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, serious eye damage and higher infection risk in children. Sources include liver, eggs, milk, orange fruits and dark leafy greens.

Routine supplementation for young children is part of many national programmes.

Why it matters

Nutritional state strongly affects surgical risk, wound healing and recovery, and community nutrition work addresses the causes upstream.

Remember

Vitamin A protects sight and immunity.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about vitamin a?

Vitamin A protects sight and immunity.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

food-hygiene-at-home.title: Food hygiene at home
food-hygiene-at-home.caption: A quick list on food hygiene at home: Wash hands before preparing and eating food; Keep raw and cooked foods separate.
food-hygiene-at-home.body:
In short: A quick list on food hygiene at home: Wash hands before preparing and eating food; Keep raw and cooked foods separate.

Food hygiene at home

  • Wash hands before preparing and eating food
  • Keep raw and cooked foods separate
  • Cook food thoroughly, reheat well
  • Store food covered and at safe temperatures
  • Use safe water and clean utensils

Why it matters

Nutritional state strongly affects surgical risk, wound healing and recovery, and community nutrition work addresses the causes upstream.

Remember

Clean food prevents diarrhoea.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Food hygiene at home".

Wash hands before preparing and eating food; Keep raw and cooked foods separate; Cook food thoroughly, reheat well; Store food covered and at safe temperatures; Use safe water and clean utensils.

nutrition-and-wound-healing.title: Nutrition and wound healing
nutrition-and-wound-healing.caption: Healing needs enough energy, protein, vitamins and minerals.
nutrition-and-wound-healing.body:
In short: Healing needs enough energy, protein, vitamins and minerals.

Fuel For Repair

Healing needs enough energy, protein, vitamins and minerals. Poor nutrition delays healing, raises infection risk and lengthens hospital stay.

Before planned surgery, patients with poor intake or weight loss may need nutrition assessment and support.

Why it matters

Nutritional state strongly affects surgical risk, wound healing and recovery, and community nutrition work addresses the causes upstream.

Remember

Well-fed patients heal better.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about nutrition and wound healing?

Well-fed patients heal better.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

kwashiorkor-versus-marasmus.title: Kwashiorkor versus marasmus
kwashiorkor-versus-marasmus.caption: A quick list on kwashiorkor versus marasmus: Kwashiorkor: swelling of both feet, face, belly; Kwashiorkor: skin and hair changes, irritable.
kwashiorkor-versus-marasmus.body:
In short: A quick list on kwashiorkor versus marasmus: Kwashiorkor: swelling of both feet, face, belly; Kwashiorkor: skin and hair changes, irritable.

Kwashiorkor versus marasmus

  • Kwashiorkor: swelling of both feet, face, belly
  • Kwashiorkor: skin and hair changes, irritable
  • Marasmus: severe wasting, very thin, old look
  • Both are severe malnutrition needing careful care

Why it matters

Nutritional state strongly affects surgical risk, wound healing and recovery, and community nutrition work addresses the causes upstream.

Remember

Swollen feet signal severe malnutrition.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Kwashiorkor versus marasmus".

Kwashiorkor: swelling of both feet, face, belly; Kwashiorkor: skin and hair changes, irritable; Marasmus: severe wasting, very thin, old look; Both are severe malnutrition needing careful care.

timing-of-prophylactic-antibiotics.title: Timing of prophylactic antibiotics
timing-of-prophylactic-antibiotics.caption: Prophylactic antibiotics work best when tissue levels are high at the moment of incision.
timing-of-prophylactic-antibiotics.body:
In short: Prophylactic antibiotics work best when tissue levels are high at the moment of incision.

Before The Incision

Prophylactic antibiotics work best when tissue levels are high at the moment of incision. They are usually given within an hour before the cut, by the IV route.

Giving them late, after the wound is open, reduces the benefit.

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Right drug, right time, before incision.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about timing of prophylactic antibiotics?

Right drug, right time, before incision.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

redosing-during-long-operations.title: Redosing during long operations
redosing-during-long-operations.caption: Some antibiotics wear off during long cases or heavy blood loss.
redosing-during-long-operations.body:
In short: Some antibiotics wear off during long cases or heavy blood loss.

Keeping Levels Up

Some antibiotics wear off during long cases or heavy blood loss. Protocols often call for a repeat dose after a set number of hours or major bleeding.

Note the time of the first dose on the chart so the team can judge when to redose.

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Record the time of every dose.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about redosing during long operations?

Record the time of every dose.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

checking-penicillin-allergy.title: Checking penicillin allergy
checking-penicillin-allergy.caption: Many people say they are penicillin allergic but only had a mild rash or stomach upset.
checking-penicillin-allergy.body:
In short: Many people say they are penicillin allergic but only had a mild rash or stomach upset.

Ask Properly

Many people say they are penicillin allergic but only had a mild rash or stomach upset. Ask what happened, when, and how severe it was.

Hives, swelling or breathing trouble suggest true allergy. Document it and tell the surgeon and anaesthetist before drugs are drawn up.

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Details matter more than the label.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about checking penicillin allergy?

Details matter more than the label.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

cephalosporins-and-allergy.title: Cephalosporins and allergy
cephalosporins-and-allergy.caption: Cephalosporins share a chemical structure with penicillins, so a few allergic patients react to both.
cephalosporins-and-allergy.body:
In short: Cephalosporins share a chemical structure with penicillins, so a few allergic patients react to both.

Cross-Reaction

Cephalosporins share a chemical structure with penicillins, so a few allergic patients react to both. The risk is usually low with later-generation drugs.

After a severe penicillin reaction, follow local protocol and let the prescriber choose.

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Severe reaction history needs a prescriber.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about cephalosporins and allergy?

Severe reaction history needs a prescriber.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

gentamicin-and-the-kidneys.title: Gentamicin and the kidneys
gentamicin-and-the-kidneys.caption: Gentamicin can harm the kidneys and the ears, especially in dehydrated or older patients or with long courses.
gentamicin-and-the-kidneys.body:
In short: Gentamicin can harm the kidneys and the ears, especially in dehydrated or older patients or with long courses.

Watch The Kidney

Gentamicin can harm the kidneys and the ears, especially in dehydrated or older patients or with long courses.

Check urine output and kidney results, and avoid combining it with other kidney-toxic drugs where possible. Dosing is often weight-based.

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Hydrate and monitor the kidneys.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about gentamicin and the kidneys?

Hydrate and monitor the kidneys.

metronidazole-for-gut-surgery.title: Metronidazole for gut surgery
metronidazole-for-gut-surgery.caption: Bowel contents contain many anaerobic bacteria.
metronidazole-for-gut-surgery.body:
In short: Bowel contents contain many anaerobic bacteria.

Anaerobic Cover

Bowel contents contain many anaerobic bacteria. Metronidazole is commonly added to cover them in abdominal and pelvic surgery.

It is often given by slow IV infusion. Patients may report a metallic taste.

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Gut surgery needs anaerobic cover.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about metronidazole for gut surgery?

Gut surgery needs anaerobic cover.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

vancomycin-infusion-reaction.title: Vancomycin infusion reaction
vancomycin-infusion-reaction.caption: Vancomycin given too fast can cause flushing, itching and low blood pressure, sometimes called red man syndrome.
vancomycin-infusion-reaction.body:
In short: Vancomycin given too fast can cause flushing, itching and low blood pressure, sometimes called red man syndrome.

Slow It Down

Vancomycin given too fast can cause flushing, itching and low blood pressure, sometimes called red man syndrome. It is a rate-related reaction, not true allergy.

Infuse slowly as directed, and slow or pause the drip if flushing starts.

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Slow infusion prevents flushing.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about vancomycin infusion reaction?

Slow infusion prevents flushing.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

culture-before-antibiotics.title: Culture before antibiotics
culture-before-antibiotics.caption: When infection is suspected, take wound swabs, pus or blood cultures before starting antibiotics if this does not delay urgent care.
culture-before-antibiotics.body:
In short: When infection is suspected, take wound swabs, pus or blood cultures before starting antibiotics if this does not delay urgent care.

Sample First

When infection is suspected, take wound swabs, pus or blood cultures before starting antibiotics if this does not delay urgent care.

A good sample lets the lab identify the germ and show which drugs work.

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Swab first, treat second.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about culture before antibiotics?

Swab first, treat second.

why-resistance-matters.title: Why resistance matters
why-resistance-matters.caption: A quick list on why resistance matters: Resistance grows when antibiotics are misused; Unneeded or incomplete courses help it spread.
why-resistance-matters.body:
In short: A quick list on why resistance matters: Resistance grows when antibiotics are misused; Unneeded or incomplete courses help it spread.

Why resistance matters

  • Resistance grows when antibiotics are misused
  • Unneeded or incomplete courses help it spread
  • Resistant wound infections are harder to treat
  • Hand hygiene and asepsis reduce drug use
  • Give antibiotics only as prescribed

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Fewer infections mean fewer antibiotics.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Why resistance matters".

Resistance grows when antibiotics are misused; Unneeded or incomplete courses help it spread; Resistant wound infections are harder to treat; Hand hygiene and asepsis reduce drug use; Give antibiotics only as prescribed.

prophylaxis-versus-treatment.title: Prophylaxis versus treatment
prophylaxis-versus-treatment.caption: A quick list on prophylaxis versus treatment: Prophylaxis: prevent infection, usually one dose; Treatment: clear an infection already present.
prophylaxis-versus-treatment.body:
In short: A quick list on prophylaxis versus treatment: Prophylaxis: prevent infection, usually one dose; Treatment: clear an infection already present.

Prophylaxis versus treatment

  • Prophylaxis: prevent infection, usually one dose
  • Treatment: clear an infection already present
  • Prophylaxis rarely continues past 24 hours
  • Treatment length depends on the infection
  • Prolonged prophylaxis does not add much

Why it matters

Antibiotics prevent and treat surgical infection, but misuse harms patients and fuels resistance. Theatre staff must know timing, allergy checks and safe administration.

Remember

Prevention is short; treatment is tailored.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Prophylaxis versus treatment".

Prophylaxis: prevent infection, usually one dose; Treatment: clear an infection already present; Prophylaxis rarely continues past 24 hours; Treatment length depends on the infection; Prolonged prophylaxis does not add much.

nsaids-and-bleeding-risk.title: NSAIDs and bleeding risk
nsaids-and-bleeding-risk.caption: NSAIDs such as diclofenac and ibuprofen reduce platelet function and can irritate the stomach lining.
nsaids-and-bleeding-risk.body:
In short: NSAIDs such as diclofenac and ibuprofen reduce platelet function and can irritate the stomach lining.

Caution

NSAIDs such as diclofenac and ibuprofen reduce platelet function and can irritate the stomach lining. They may also harm the kidneys in dehydrated patients.

Surgeons may prefer to avoid them where bleeding or kidney problems are a worry.

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Check kidneys and bleeding first.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about nsaids and bleeding risk?

Check kidneys and bleeding first.

morphine-side-effects.title: Morphine side effects
morphine-side-effects.caption: A quick list on morphine side effects: Slow breathing and drowsiness; Nausea and vomiting.
morphine-side-effects.body:
In short: A quick list on morphine side effects: Slow breathing and drowsiness; Nausea and vomiting.

Morphine side effects

  • Slow breathing and drowsiness
  • Nausea and vomiting
  • Itching
  • Constipation and urinary retention
  • Low blood pressure in some patients

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Watch breathing, not just pain scores.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Morphine side effects".

Slow breathing and drowsiness; Nausea and vomiting; Itching; Constipation and urinary retention; Low blood pressure in some patients.

multimodal-analgesia.title: Multimodal analgesia
multimodal-analgesia.caption: Combining different pain medicines works better than one alone and reduces opioid need.
multimodal-analgesia.body:
In short: Combining different pain medicines works better than one alone and reduces opioid need.

Mix And Match

Combining different pain medicines works better than one alone and reduces opioid need. A plan may include paracetamol, an NSAID, local anaesthetic infiltration or a nerve block, and an opioid for breakthrough pain.

Fewer opioids means fewer side effects.

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Several drugs, smaller opioid doses.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about multimodal analgesia?

Several drugs, smaller opioid doses.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

tramadol-cautions.title: Tramadol cautions
tramadol-cautions.caption: Tramadol is a weaker opioid but still causes nausea, dizziness and drowsiness.
tramadol-cautions.body:
In short: Tramadol is a weaker opioid but still causes nausea, dizziness and drowsiness.

Not Risk-Free

Tramadol is a weaker opioid but still causes nausea, dizziness and drowsiness. It can lower the seizure threshold and interact with some antidepressants.

Caution is needed in older patients and those with kidney problems.

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Weaker opioid does not mean harmless.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tramadol cautions?

Weaker opioid does not mean harmless.

spotting-opioid-over-sedation.title: Spotting opioid over-sedation
spotting-opioid-over-sedation.caption: Before breathing stops, patients become very sleepy, hard to rouse, and breathe slowly or shallowly.
spotting-opioid-over-sedation.body:
In short: Before breathing stops, patients become very sleepy, hard to rouse, and breathe slowly or shallowly.

Early Signs

Before breathing stops, patients become very sleepy, hard to rouse, and breathe slowly or shallowly. Pinpoint pupils are often seen.

Check sedation level and respiratory rate with each pain assessment, and call for help early. Naloxone may be needed.

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Sleepy and slow means act now.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about spotting opioid over-sedation?

Sleepy and slow means act now.

local-anaesthetic-toxicity-signs.title: Local anaesthetic toxicity signs
local-anaesthetic-toxicity-signs.caption: A quick list on local anaesthetic toxicity signs: Tingling around the mouth or metallic taste; Ringing in the ears, dizziness.
local-anaesthetic-toxicity-signs.body:
In short: A quick list on local anaesthetic toxicity signs: Tingling around the mouth or metallic taste; Ringing in the ears, dizziness.

Local anaesthetic toxicity signs

  • Tingling around the mouth or metallic taste
  • Ringing in the ears, dizziness
  • Twitching, confusion, seizures
  • Slow heart rate, collapse, cardiac arrest
  • Stop injecting and call for help

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Early warning is mouth tingling.

Check yourself

Tingling around the mouth or metallic taste; Ringing in the ears, dizziness; Twitching, confusion, seizures; Slow heart rate, collapse, cardiac arrest; Stop injecting and call for help.

ketamine-for-analgesia.title: Ketamine for analgesia
ketamine-for-analgesia.caption: Ketamine in small doses gives strong pain relief with less effect on breathing than opioids.
ketamine-for-analgesia.body:
In short: Ketamine in small doses gives strong pain relief with less effect on breathing than opioids.

A Different Drug

Ketamine in small doses gives strong pain relief with less effect on breathing than opioids. It can cause hallucinations, vivid dreams and raised heart rate and blood pressure.

A calm, quiet recovery setting helps reduce distress.

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Calm surroundings ease emergence.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ketamine for analgesia?

Calm surroundings ease emergence.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

using-pain-scores-well.title: Using pain scores well
using-pain-scores-well.caption: Ask patients to rate pain at rest and on movement, using a numbers or faces scale.
using-pain-scores-well.body:
In short: Ask patients to rate pain at rest and on movement, using a numbers or faces scale.

Measure It

Ask patients to rate pain at rest and on movement, using a numbers or faces scale. Repeat after every intervention.

In children and those who cannot speak, use behaviour-based scales. Treat the pattern, not a single number.

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Reassess after every dose.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about using pain scores well?

Reassess after every dose.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

opioid-and-sedative-combinations.title: Opioid and sedative combinations
opioid-and-sedative-combinations.caption: Opioids given with benzodiazepines, alcohol or other sedatives add to each other and can depress breathing more than either alone.
opioid-and-sedative-combinations.body:
In short: Opioids given with benzodiazepines, alcohol or other sedatives add to each other and can depress breathing more than either alone.

Added Effect

Opioids given with benzodiazepines, alcohol or other sedatives add to each other and can depress breathing more than either alone.

Use lower doses, watch sedation and breathing closely, and follow local protocol.

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Combined sedatives need closer watching.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about opioid and sedative combinations?

Combined sedatives need closer watching.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

simple-analgesics-first.title: Simple analgesics first
simple-analgesics-first.caption: A quick list on simple analgesics first: Paracetamol suits most mild to moderate pain; NSAIDs help if kidneys and bleeding risk allow.
simple-analgesics-first.body:
In short: A quick list on simple analgesics first: Paracetamol suits most mild to moderate pain; NSAIDs help if kidneys and bleeding risk allow.

Simple analgesics first

  • Paracetamol suits most mild to moderate pain
  • NSAIDs help if kidneys and bleeding risk allow
  • Give regularly rather than only when asked
  • Add stronger drugs only if still needed

Why it matters

Pain relief drives recovery, comfort and mobility. Each analgesic carries risks, so staff need to know effects, side effects and warning signs.

Remember

Start with the basics, then step up.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Simple analgesics first".

Paracetamol suits most mild to moderate pain; NSAIDs help if kidneys and bleeding risk allow; Give regularly rather than only when asked; Add stronger drugs only if still needed.

how-heparin-works.title: How heparin works
how-heparin-works.caption: Heparin enhances the body's natural clotting inhibitor, antithrombin, so clots form less easily.
how-heparin-works.body:
In short: Heparin enhances the body's natural clotting inhibitor, antithrombin, so clots form less easily.

Quick Acting

Heparin enhances the body's natural clotting inhibitor, antithrombin, so clots form less easily. It acts fast when given IV.

It is monitored with clotting tests such as aPTT. Always check the dose, rate and concentration with a second person.

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

Heparin acts fast and needs monitoring.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about how heparin works?

Heparin acts fast and needs monitoring.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

warfarin-and-the-inr.title: Warfarin and the INR
warfarin-and-the-inr.caption: Warfarin blocks vitamin K dependent clotting factors.
warfarin-and-the-inr.body:
In short: Warfarin blocks vitamin K dependent clotting factors.

Measuring Effect

Warfarin blocks vitamin K dependent clotting factors. Its effect is monitored with the INR blood test.

Many drugs and foods change its action. Before surgery, check the latest INR and the target range.

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

Check the INR before the knife.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about warfarin and the inr?

Check the INR before the knife.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

warfarin-before-surgery.title: Warfarin before surgery
warfarin-before-surgery.caption: Warfarin is often stopped several days before planned surgery so the INR falls.
warfarin-before-surgery.body:
In short: Warfarin is often stopped several days before planned surgery so the INR falls.

Planning Ahead

Warfarin is often stopped several days before planned surgery so the INR falls. Some patients with high clot risk are bridged with heparin.

The surgical and medical teams decide this. Confirm the INR on the day.

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

Follow the team's stop plan.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about warfarin before surgery?

Follow the team's stop plan.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

protamine-reverses-heparin.title: Protamine reverses heparin
protamine-reverses-heparin.caption: Protamine binds heparin and neutralises it.
protamine-reverses-heparin.body:
In short: Protamine binds heparin and neutralises it.

The Antidote

Protamine binds heparin and neutralises it. It is given slowly, because fast injection can cause low blood pressure and allergic-type reactions.

Patients who have had certain insulins or fish allergy may be at higher risk.

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

Give protamine slowly.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about protamine reverses heparin?

Give protamine slowly.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

lmwh-and-spinal-blocks.title: LMWH and spinal blocks
lmwh-and-spinal-blocks.caption: Low molecular weight heparin, such as enoxaparin, is used to prevent clots.
lmwh-and-spinal-blocks.body:
In short: Low molecular weight heparin, such as enoxaparin, is used to prevent clots.

Timing Matters

Low molecular weight heparin, such as enoxaparin, is used to prevent clots. Giving it too close to a spinal or epidural needle raises the risk of a spinal haematoma.

Guidelines set time gaps before and after the block.

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

vitamin-k-for-warfarin-reversal.title: Vitamin K for warfarin reversal
vitamin-k-for-warfarin-reversal.caption: Vitamin K helps the liver make clotting factors again, so it reverses warfarin over hours, not minutes.
vitamin-k-for-warfarin-reversal.body:
In short: Vitamin K helps the liver make clotting factors again, so it reverses warfarin over hours, not minutes.

Slow But Steady

Vitamin K helps the liver make clotting factors again, so it reverses warfarin over hours, not minutes.

In urgent bleeding, clotting factor concentrates or plasma may be used alongside it, according to local protocol.

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

Vitamin K works over hours.

What is the main thing to remember about vitamin k for warfarin reversal?

heparin-induced-thrombocytopenia.title: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
heparin-induced-thrombocytopenia.caption: Rarely, heparin triggers an immune reaction that drops platelets and can paradoxically cause clots.
heparin-induced-thrombocytopenia.body:
In short: Rarely, heparin triggers an immune reaction that drops platelets and can paradoxically cause clots.

Falling Platelets

Rarely, heparin triggers an immune reaction that drops platelets and can paradoxically cause clots. Suspect it if platelets fall several days after starting heparin.

Stop heparin and seek senior advice.

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

Falling platelets on heparin: alert.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about heparin-induced thrombocytopenia?

Falling platelets on heparin: alert.

newer-oral-anticoagulants.title: Newer oral anticoagulants
newer-oral-anticoagulants.caption: Direct oral anticoagulants, such as rivaroxaban, do not need regular INR checks and have fewer food interactions.
newer-oral-anticoagulants.body:
In short: Direct oral anticoagulants, such as rivaroxaban, do not need regular INR checks and have fewer food interactions.

Doacs

Direct oral anticoagulants, such as rivaroxaban, do not need regular INR checks and have fewer food interactions. Their effect is hard to measure with routine tests.

Kidney function affects how long they last. Ask when the last dose was taken.

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

Always ask when the last dose was.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about newer oral anticoagulants?

Always ask when the last dose was.

signs-of-bleeding-on-anticoagulants.title: Signs of bleeding on anticoagulants
signs-of-bleeding-on-anticoagulants.caption: A quick list on signs of bleeding on anticoagulants: Oozing from wounds or cannula sites; Bruising without clear injury.
signs-of-bleeding-on-anticoagulants.body:
In short: A quick list on signs of bleeding on anticoagulants: Oozing from wounds or cannula sites; Bruising without clear injury.

Signs of bleeding on anticoagulants

  • Oozing from wounds or cannula sites
  • Bruising without clear injury
  • Blood in urine, stool or vomit
  • Rising pulse with falling blood pressure
  • Report early to the surgeon

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

Quiet bleeding is still bleeding.

pre-op-anticoagulant-questions.title: Pre-op anticoagulant questions
pre-op-anticoagulant-questions.caption: A quick list on pre-op anticoagulant questions: Which drug, what dose, and when last taken?; Why is the patient on it?.
pre-op-anticoagulant-questions.body:
In short: A quick list on pre-op anticoagulant questions: Which drug, what dose, and when last taken?; Why is the patient on it?.

Pre-op anticoagulant questions

  • Which drug, what dose, and when last taken?
  • Why is the patient on it?
  • Was the drug stopped as planned?
  • Latest INR or clotting results?
  • Any bleeding history?

Why it matters

Patients on blood thinners can bleed heavily or clot dangerously. Knowing the drugs, timing and reversal helps keep surgery safe.

Remember

Ask before the patient is asleep.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Pre-op anticoagulant questions".

beta-blockers-around-surgery.title: Beta blockers around surgery
beta-blockers-around-surgery.caption: Patients who already take beta blockers, such as atenolol, are usually advised to continue them through surgery.
beta-blockers-around-surgery.body:
In short: Patients who already take beta blockers, such as atenolol, are usually advised to continue them through surgery.

Keep Them Going

Patients who already take beta blockers, such as atenolol, are usually advised to continue them through surgery. Stopping suddenly can cause fast heart rate and blood pressure rebound.

They can mask signs of shock or low blood sugar.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Do not stop beta blockers suddenly.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about beta blockers around surgery?

Do not stop beta blockers suddenly.

ace-inhibitors-and-anaesthesia.title: ACE inhibitors and anaesthesia
ace-inhibitors-and-anaesthesia.caption: ACE inhibitors and similar drugs can cause low blood pressure after anaesthesia induction.
ace-inhibitors-and-anaesthesia.body:
In short: ACE inhibitors and similar drugs can cause low blood pressure after anaesthesia induction.

Low Bp Risk

ACE inhibitors and similar drugs can cause low blood pressure after anaesthesia induction. Some teams hold the morning dose before surgery.

Follow the anaesthetist's instruction and note the last dose time.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Ask when the last dose was taken.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ace inhibitors and anaesthesia?

Ask when the last dose was taken.

digoxin-toxicity.title: Digoxin toxicity
digoxin-toxicity.caption: Digoxin controls heart rate but has a narrow safety range.
digoxin-toxicity.body:
In short: Digoxin controls heart rate but has a narrow safety range.

Narrow Margin

Digoxin controls heart rate but has a narrow safety range. Toxicity may cause nausea, visual changes and abnormal rhythms.

Low potassium raises the risk. Check electrolytes and kidney function.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Low potassium makes digoxin riskier.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about digoxin toxicity?

Low potassium makes digoxin riskier.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

amiodarone-basics.title: Amiodarone basics
amiodarone-basics.caption: Amiodarone treats and prevents many abnormal rhythms, including in cardiac arrest.
amiodarone-basics.body:
In short: Amiodarone treats and prevents many abnormal rhythms, including in cardiac arrest.

Rhythm Control

Amiodarone treats and prevents many abnormal rhythms, including in cardiac arrest. It can drop blood pressure and slow the heart when given quickly.

It is best given into a large vein, since it can irritate small ones.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Monitor the ECG and blood pressure.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about amiodarone basics?

Monitor the ECG and blood pressure.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

atropine-for-slow-heart-rate.title: Atropine for slow heart rate
atropine-for-slow-heart-rate.caption: Atropine blocks the vagus nerve and speeds the heart.
atropine-for-slow-heart-rate.body:
In short: Atropine blocks the vagus nerve and speeds the heart.

Speeding Up

Atropine blocks the vagus nerve and speeds the heart. It is used for symptomatic slow heart rate and to dry secretions.

It can cause dry mouth, blurred vision and fast pulse. Use with caution in some heart conditions.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Atropine raises the rate.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about atropine for slow heart rate?

Atropine raises the rate.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

glyceryl-trinitrate.title: Glyceryl trinitrate
glyceryl-trinitrate.caption: GTN relaxes blood vessels, easing chest pain and lowering blood pressure.
glyceryl-trinitrate.body:
In short: GTN relaxes blood vessels, easing chest pain and lowering blood pressure.

Opening Vessels

GTN relaxes blood vessels, easing chest pain and lowering blood pressure. It can cause headache and sudden drops in pressure.

It is unsuitable for patients with very low blood pressure. Protect tablets and sprays from light and heat.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Check blood pressure before GTN.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about glyceryl trinitrate?

Check blood pressure before GTN.

calcium-channel-blockers.title: Calcium channel blockers
calcium-channel-blockers.caption: Some, like amlodipine, mainly relax blood vessels.
calcium-channel-blockers.body:
In short: Some, like amlodipine, mainly relax blood vessels.

Two Families

Some, like amlodipine, mainly relax blood vessels. Others, like verapamil and diltiazem, also slow the heart.

Giving verapamil with a beta blocker can slow the heart too much. Check what the patient takes and when.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Know which type the patient takes.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about calcium channel blockers?

Know which type the patient takes.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

furosemide-and-electrolytes.title: Furosemide and electrolytes
furosemide-and-electrolytes.caption: Furosemide makes the kidneys pass more urine, which treats fluid overload.
furosemide-and-electrolytes.body:
In short: Furosemide makes the kidneys pass more urine, which treats fluid overload.

Water Pill

Furosemide makes the kidneys pass more urine, which treats fluid overload. It can lower potassium, sodium and blood volume.

Monitor urine output, electrolytes and blood pressure, especially in patients on digoxin.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Watch potassium after diuretics.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about furosemide and electrolytes?

Watch potassium after diuretics.

vasopressors-and-inotropes.title: Vasopressors and inotropes
vasopressors-and-inotropes.caption: A quick list on vasopressors and inotropes: Vasopressors tighten vessels, raising pressure; Inotropes strengthen the heart's contraction.
vasopressors-and-inotropes.body:
In short: A quick list on vasopressors and inotropes: Vasopressors tighten vessels, raising pressure; Inotropes strengthen the heart's contraction.

Vasopressors and inotropes

  • Vasopressors tighten vessels, raising pressure
  • Inotropes strengthen the heart's contraction
  • Some drugs, like adrenaline, do both
  • Give via a reliable line, with close monitoring
  • Extravasation can damage tissue

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Pressure versus pump strength.

Check yourself

antiplatelets-before-surgery.title: Antiplatelets before surgery
antiplatelets-before-surgery.caption: Antiplatelet drugs prevent clots in stents and heart disease, but increase bleeding.
antiplatelets-before-surgery.body:
In short: Antiplatelet drugs prevent clots in stents and heart disease, but increase bleeding.

Aspirin And Clopidogrel

Antiplatelet drugs prevent clots in stents and heart disease, but increase bleeding. Stopping them too early after a stent can be dangerous.

Never stop without a clear plan from the cardiologist and surgeon.

Why it matters

Many surgical patients take heart medicines that interact with anaesthesia. Knowing what to continue, hold and watch for protects the heart under stress.

Remember

Stents need a plan before stopping.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about antiplatelets before surgery?

Stents need a plan before stopping.

adrenaline-in-anaphylaxis.title: Adrenaline in anaphylaxis
adrenaline-in-anaphylaxis.caption: Adrenaline is the first-line drug for severe allergic reactions.
adrenaline-in-anaphylaxis.body:
In short: Adrenaline is the first-line drug for severe allergic reactions.

First Line

Adrenaline is the first-line drug for severe allergic reactions. It is usually given into the thigh muscle, and repeated if there is no response, as per protocol.

Give it early, call for help, lie the patient flat and give oxygen.

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

Adrenaline first, without delay.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about adrenaline in anaphylaxis?

Adrenaline first, without delay.

adrenaline-in-cardiac-arrest.title: Adrenaline in cardiac arrest
adrenaline-in-cardiac-arrest.caption: In cardiac arrest, adrenaline is given IV or IO at regular intervals according to resuscitation guidelines.
adrenaline-in-cardiac-arrest.body:
In short: In cardiac arrest, adrenaline is given IV or IO at regular intervals according to resuscitation guidelines.

Circulation

In cardiac arrest, adrenaline is given IV or IO at regular intervals according to resuscitation guidelines. Good chest compressions come first.

Always confirm the concentration: arrest and anaphylaxis preparations differ.

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

Check the adrenaline strength.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about adrenaline in cardiac arrest?

Check the adrenaline strength.

naloxone-reverses-opioids.title: Naloxone reverses opioids
naloxone-reverses-opioids.caption: Naloxone blocks opioid receptors and reverses sedation and slow breathing.
naloxone-reverses-opioids.body:
In short: Naloxone blocks opioid receptors and reverses sedation and slow breathing.

The Antidote

Naloxone blocks opioid receptors and reverses sedation and slow breathing. Its effect may wear off sooner than the opioid, so drowsiness can return.

It also reverses pain relief. Repeat doses or an infusion may be needed.

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

Watch for the opioid returning.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about naloxone reverses opioids?

Watch for the opioid returning.
