flumazenil-for-benzodiazepines.title: Flumazenil for benzodiazepines
flumazenil-for-benzodiazepines.caption: Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines such as diazepam and midazolam.
flumazenil-for-benzodiazepines.body:
In short: Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines such as diazepam and midazolam.

Use With Care

Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines such as diazepam and midazolam. It can trigger seizures in long-term benzodiazepine users or in mixed overdoses.

Its effect is short, so sedation may return. It is not routine.

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

Reversal can unmask seizures.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about flumazenil for benzodiazepines?

Reversal can unmask seizures.

treating-hypoglycaemia.title: Treating hypoglycaemia
treating-hypoglycaemia.caption: Low blood glucose can cause sweating, confusion, seizures or coma, and may be hidden under anaesthesia.
treating-hypoglycaemia.body:
In short: Low blood glucose can cause sweating, confusion, seizures or coma, and may be hidden under anaesthesia.

Low Sugar

Low blood glucose can cause sweating, confusion, seizures or coma, and may be hidden under anaesthesia. Check blood glucose in any unexplained drop in consciousness.

Treatment is usually IV glucose, or glucagon where available, per protocol.

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

Check glucose in any collapse.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about treating hypoglycaemia?

Check glucose in any collapse.

dantrolene-for-mh.title: Dantrolene for MH
dantrolene-for-mh.caption: Dantrolene is the key drug for malignant hyperthermia, a rare reaction to some anaesthetic agents.
dantrolene-for-mh.body:
In short: Dantrolene is the key drug for malignant hyperthermia, a rare reaction to some anaesthetic agents.

Specific Treatment

Dantrolene is the key drug for malignant hyperthermia, a rare reaction to some anaesthetic agents. It needs to be mixed with sterile water, which takes time.

Know where it is kept and have enough vials accessible.

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

Know where dantrolene is stored.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about dantrolene for mh?

Know where dantrolene is stored.

lipid-emulsion-rescue.title: Lipid emulsion rescue
lipid-emulsion-rescue.caption: In severe local anaesthetic toxicity, a lipid emulsion can be given as rescue alongside resuscitation.
lipid-emulsion-rescue.body:
In short: In severe local anaesthetic toxicity, a lipid emulsion can be given as rescue alongside resuscitation.

Intralipid

In severe local anaesthetic toxicity, a lipid emulsion can be given as rescue alongside resuscitation. It is thought to draw drug out of tissues.

Know where it is kept, and follow the local toxicity protocol.

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

Lipid rescue belongs in the theatre kit.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about lipid emulsion rescue?

Lipid rescue belongs in the theatre kit.

hydrocortisone-in-emergencies.title: Hydrocortisone in emergencies
hydrocortisone-in-emergencies.caption: Hydrocortisone is used as an adjunct in severe allergic reactions and for patients with adrenal insufficiency under stress.
hydrocortisone-in-emergencies.body:
In short: Hydrocortisone is used as an adjunct in severe allergic reactions and for patients with adrenal insufficiency under stress.

Steroid Role

Hydrocortisone is used as an adjunct in severe allergic reactions and for patients with adrenal insufficiency under stress. It acts slowly, over hours.

It does not replace adrenaline in anaphylaxis.

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

Steroids support but do not replace.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about hydrocortisone in emergencies?

Steroids support but do not replace.

salbutamol-for-bronchospasm.title: Salbutamol for bronchospasm
salbutamol-for-bronchospasm.caption: Salbutamol relaxes airway muscle in wheeze and bronchospasm.
salbutamol-for-bronchospasm.body:
In short: Salbutamol relaxes airway muscle in wheeze and bronchospasm.

Opening Airways

Salbutamol relaxes airway muscle in wheeze and bronchospasm. It can be given by inhaler, nebuliser or IV in severe cases.

Side effects include fast heartbeat, tremor and low potassium.

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

Wheeze needs a cause check too.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about salbutamol for bronchospasm?

Wheeze needs a cause check too.

crash-trolley-drug-checks.title: Crash trolley drug checks
crash-trolley-drug-checks.caption: A quick list on crash trolley drug checks: Check seals and expiry dates every day; Keep adrenaline, atropine and amiodarone ready.
crash-trolley-drug-checks.body:
In short: A quick list on crash trolley drug checks: Check seals and expiry dates every day; Keep adrenaline, atropine and amiodarone ready.

Crash trolley drug checks

  • Check seals and expiry dates every day
  • Keep adrenaline, atropine and amiodarone ready
  • Have glucose and naloxone accessible
  • Restock and reseal after every use
  • Log each check with a signature

Why it matters

Theatre emergencies leave seconds to act. Staff should know the key rescue drugs, where they are kept and how to prepare them safely.

Remember

A ready trolley saves minutes.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Crash trolley drug checks".

crystalloids-versus-colloids.title: Crystalloids versus colloids
crystalloids-versus-colloids.caption: Crystalloids, such as saline and Ringer's lactate, are salt solutions that spread through body water.
crystalloids-versus-colloids.body:
In short: Crystalloids, such as saline and Ringer's lactate, are salt solutions that spread through body water.

Fluid Types

Crystalloids, such as saline and Ringer's lactate, are salt solutions that spread through body water. Colloids hold larger molecules that stay in the blood longer.

Crystalloids are usually the first choice and are cheaper and widely available.

Why it matters

Almost every theatre patient has IV access and fluids. Safe cannulation, fluid choice and line care prevent infection and harm.

Remember

Crystalloids are the usual first choice.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about crystalloids versus colloids?

Crystalloids are the usual first choice.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

normal-saline-limits.title: Normal saline limits
normal-saline-limits.caption: Normal saline is widely used but large volumes can cause a high chloride acidosis.
normal-saline-limits.body:
In short: Normal saline is widely used but large volumes can cause a high chloride acidosis.

0.9 Percent Sodium Chloride

Normal saline is widely used but large volumes can cause a high chloride acidosis. It also adds sodium and may worsen fluid overload.

Balanced solutions like Ringer's lactate are often preferred for big volumes.

Why it matters

Almost every theatre patient has IV access and fluids. Safe cannulation, fluid choice and line care prevent infection and harm.

Remember

Large saline volumes can acidify.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about normal saline limits?

Large saline volumes can acidify.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

ringer-s-lactate.title: Ringer's lactate
ringer-s-lactate.caption: Ringer's lactate has electrolytes close to plasma levels.
ringer-s-lactate.body:
In short: Ringer's lactate has electrolytes close to plasma levels.

Balanced Solution

Ringer's lactate has electrolytes close to plasma levels. The liver turns its lactate into bicarbonate.

It is commonly used in surgery and resuscitation. Do not run it with blood in the same line, because the calcium can cause clotting.

Why it matters

Almost every theatre patient has IV access and fluids. Safe cannulation, fluid choice and line care prevent infection and harm.

Remember

Never mix with blood in one line.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about ringer's lactate?

Never mix with blood in one line.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

choosing-a-cannula-site.title: Choosing a cannula site
choosing-a-cannula-site.caption: Choose a straight, soft, visible vein, usually on the forearm or back of the hand.
choosing-a-cannula-site.body:
In short: Choose a straight, soft, visible vein, usually on the forearm or back of the hand.

Vein Selection

Choose a straight, soft, visible vein, usually on the forearm or back of the hand. Avoid joints, bruised areas, infected skin and limbs with fistulas or lymph node surgery.

Start distally so higher sites remain available.

Why it matters

Almost every theatre patient has IV access and fluids. Safe cannulation, fluid choice and line care prevent infection and harm.

Remember

Start low, keep options open.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about choosing a cannula site?

Start low, keep options open.

cannula-sizes-and-colours.title: Cannula sizes and colours
cannula-sizes-and-colours.caption: A quick list on cannula sizes and colours: 14G orange: very fast flow; 16G grey: fast flow, large volumes.
cannula-sizes-and-colours.body:
In short: A quick list on cannula sizes and colours: 14G orange: very fast flow; 16G grey: fast flow, large volumes.

Cannula sizes and colours

  • 14G orange: very fast flow
  • 16G grey: fast flow, large volumes
  • 18G green: general adult use
  • 20G pink: routine adult use
  • 22G blue and 24G yellow: small veins, children

Why it matters

Almost every theatre patient has IV access and fluids. Safe cannulation, fluid choice and line care prevent infection and harm.

Remember

Bigger vein, bigger cannula.

recognising-phlebitis.title: Recognising phlebitis
recognising-phlebitis.caption: Phlebitis shows as pain, redness, warmth or a hard cord along the vein near the cannula.
recognising-phlebitis.body:
In short: Phlebitis shows as pain, redness, warmth or a hard cord along the vein near the cannula.

Vein Inflammation

Phlebitis shows as pain, redness, warmth or a hard cord along the vein near the cannula. Stop infusions, remove the cannula and document.

Use a visual score chart, and check the site at least once a shift.

Why it matters

Almost every theatre patient has IV access and fluids. Safe cannulation, fluid choice and line care prevent infection and harm.

Remember

Remove the cannula at the first sign.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about recognising phlebitis?

Remove the cannula at the first sign.

infiltration-and-extravasation.title: Infiltration and extravasation
infiltration-and-extravasation.caption: If fluid or drug escapes into the surrounding tissue, the site becomes swollen, cold and painful.
infiltration-and-extravasation.body:
In short: If fluid or drug escapes into the surrounding tissue, the site becomes swollen, cold and painful.

Leaking Fluid

If fluid or drug escapes into the surrounding tissue, the site becomes swollen, cold and painful. Some drugs damage tissue badly.

Stop the infusion, leave the cannula in to aspirate if protocol says so, elevate the limb and report.

Why it matters

Almost every theatre patient has IV access and fluids. Safe cannulation, fluid choice and line care prevent infection and harm.

Remember

Stop the drip at the first swelling.

Check yourself

preventing-air-in-iv-lines.title: Preventing air in IV lines
preventing-air-in-iv-lines.caption: Large amounts of air entering a vein can cause serious harm.
preventing-air-in-iv-lines.body:

Air Embolism

Large amounts of air entering a vein can cause serious harm. Prime all giving sets, remove bubbles from syringes, and never let a bag run dry.

Use an air-eliminating filter where available.

Why it matters

Almost every theatre patient has IV access and fluids. Safe cannulation, fluid choice and line care prevent infection and harm.

Remember

Prime the line and watch the bag.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about preventing air in iv lines?

Prime the line and watch the bag.

aseptic-cannula-care.title: Aseptic cannula care
aseptic-cannula-care.caption: Clean your hands, clean the skin, and use a no-touch technique when inserting a cannula.
aseptic-cannula-care.body:
In short: Clean your hands, clean the skin, and use a no-touch technique when inserting a cannula.

Clean Technique

Clean your hands, clean the skin, and use a no-touch technique when inserting a cannula. Cover with a clear dressing so the site is visible.

Scrub the hub before each use, and remove cannulas that are no longer needed.

Why it matters

Almost every theatre patient has IV access and fluids. Safe cannulation, fluid choice and line care prevent infection and harm.

Remember

Scrub the hub before every access.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about aseptic cannula care?

Scrub the hub before every access.

storing-refrigerated-drugs.title: Storing refrigerated drugs
storing-refrigerated-drugs.caption: Many medicines, such as insulin and some muscle relaxants, are stored at about 2 to 8 degrees Celsius.
storing-refrigerated-drugs.body:
In short: Many medicines, such as insulin and some muscle relaxants, are stored at about 2 to 8 degrees Celsius.

Cold Storage

Many medicines, such as insulin and some muscle relaxants, are stored at about 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Check the label for the right range.

Use a thermometer, record temperatures daily, and never keep food in the drug fridge.

Why it matters

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Remember

Check and chart the fridge daily.

Check yourself

Check and chart the fridge daily.

controlled-drug-storage.caption: Opioids and other controlled drugs are kept in a locked cupboard, with keys held by an authorised person.
controlled-drug-storage.body:
In short: Opioids and other controlled drugs are kept in a locked cupboard, with keys held by an authorised person.

Locked Up

Opioids and other controlled drugs are kept in a locked cupboard, with keys held by an authorised person. Use a register to record every receipt, issue and wastage.

Count stock regularly and report discrepancies at once. Follow local regulations.

Why it matters

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Remember

Count it, sign it, lock it.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about controlled drug storage?

Count it, sign it, lock it.

light-sensitive-medicines.title: Light-sensitive medicines
light-sensitive-medicines.caption: Some drugs break down in light.
light-sensitive-medicines.body:

Protect From Light

Some drugs break down in light. They are packed in dark ampoules or boxes, and may need covering during infusion.

Keep them in their original packaging until use, and follow label instructions.

Why it matters

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Remember

Leave it in its box until needed.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about light-sensitive medicines?

Leave it in its box until needed.

expiry-dates-and-opened-vials.caption: Never use a drug past its expiry date.
expiry-dates-and-opened-vials.body:
In short: Never use a drug past its expiry date.

Check Before Use

Never use a drug past its expiry date. Once a vial or ampoule is opened, its stored life is much shorter, and some must be used immediately.

Label opened containers with date and time, and discard according to policy.

Why it matters

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Remember

Opened means a clock is ticking.

Opened means a clock is ticking.

suxamethonium-storage.title: Suxamethonium storage
suxamethonium-storage.caption: Suxamethonium loses potency at room temperature and is usually stored in a fridge.
suxamethonium-storage.body:
In short: Suxamethonium loses potency at room temperature and is usually stored in a fridge.

Heat Sensitive

Suxamethonium loses potency at room temperature and is usually stored in a fridge. Label guidance varies between brands.

Keep a small supply in theatre with a record of how long it has been out of the fridge.

Why it matters

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Remember

Check how long it has been warm.

Check how long it has been warm.

the-cold-chain.caption: The cold chain keeps vaccines, insulin and some other products within temperature limits from manufacture to use.
the-cold-chain.body:
In short: The cold chain keeps vaccines, insulin and some other products within temperature limits from manufacture to use.

From Store To Patient

The cold chain keeps vaccines, insulin and some other products within temperature limits from manufacture to use. A break can ruin potency even if the drug looks normal.

Use cool boxes with monitors and never freeze items unless allowed.

Why it matters

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Remember

A broken chain cannot be seen.

A broken chain cannot be seen.

multi-dose-vial-rules.caption: Multi-dose vials can carry contamination if used carelessly.
multi-dose-vial-rules.body:
In short: Multi-dose vials can carry contamination if used carelessly.

Shared Risk

Multi-dose vials can carry contamination if used carelessly. Use a fresh sterile needle and syringe every time, wipe the stopper, and date the vial.

Never use a vial for more than one patient where single-patient use is advised.

Why it matters

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Remember

One patient, one needle, one syringe.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about multi-dose vial rules?

One patient, one needle, one syringe.

storing-oxytocin-and-ergometrine.caption: Oxytocin and ergometrine are often kept cold, and heat can weaken them.
storing-oxytocin-and-ergometrine.body:
In short: Oxytocin and ergometrine are often kept cold, and heat can weaken them.

Obstetric Drugs

Oxytocin and ergometrine are often kept cold, and heat can weaken them. Some preparations tolerate warmer conditions, so read the label.

These drugs are vital in postpartum bleeding, so check stock and supplies regularly.

Why it matters

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Remember

Weak oxytocin means more bleeding.

Weak oxytocin means more bleeding.

separating-look-alike-stock.caption: Store similar-looking or similar-sounding drugs apart.
separating-look-alike-stock.body:

Shelf Layout

Store similar-looking or similar-sounding drugs apart. Store concentrated electrolytes, such as potassium chloride, in a separate locked area.

Clear labels and tall-man lettering help to avoid picking the wrong ampoule.

Why it matters

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Remember

Separate dangerous look-alikes.

Check yourself

Separate dangerous look-alikes.

Drugs lose strength or become dangerous when stored wrongly. Good storage and security protect patients and prevent loss or theft.

Routine checks prevent big problems.

recognising-anaphylaxis.title: Recognising anaphylaxis
recognising-anaphylaxis.caption: A quick list on recognising anaphylaxis: Sudden skin flushing, hives or swelling; Wheeze or trouble breathing.
recognising-anaphylaxis.body:
In short: A quick list on recognising anaphylaxis: Sudden skin flushing, hives or swelling; Wheeze or trouble breathing.

Recognising anaphylaxis

  • Sudden skin flushing, hives or swelling
  • Wheeze or trouble breathing
  • Low blood pressure and fast pulse
  • Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat
  • Raise the alarm and give adrenaline

Why it matters

Reactions to drugs and materials can be sudden and life-threatening. Early recognition, treatment and reporting save lives.

Remember

Under anaesthesia, low pressure may be first.

Check yourself

Sudden skin flushing, hives or swelling; Wheeze or trouble breathing; Low blood pressure and fast pulse; Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat; Raise the alarm and give adrenaline.

side-effect-versus-allergy.title: Side effect versus allergy
side-effect-versus-allergy.caption: A side effect, like nausea after morphine, is a known and often dose-related effect.
side-effect-versus-allergy.body:
In short: A side effect, like nausea after morphine, is a known and often dose-related effect.

Know The Difference

A side effect, like nausea after morphine, is a known and often dose-related effect. An allergy involves the immune system and can be serious, even after a small dose.

Record the reaction accurately so future care is safe.

Why it matters

Reactions to drugs and materials can be sudden and life-threatening. Early recognition, treatment and reporting save lives.

Remember

Describe what happened, not just a label.

Check yourself

Describe what happened, not just a label.

malignant-hyperthermia-warning-signs.body:

Malignant hyperthermia warning signs

  • Fast heart rate and muscle stiffness
  • Rapidly climbing temperature
  • Stop triggering agents and call for help
  • Give dantrolene as per protocol

Reactions to drugs and materials can be sudden and life-threatening. Early recognition, treatment and reporting save lives.

Remember

High carbon dioxide is an early clue.

post-operative-nausea-and-vomiting.title: Post-operative nausea and vomiting

post-operative-nausea-and-vomiting.body:

Ponv

PONV is more likely in women, non-smokers, those with past PONV or motion sickness, and after opioids. Anti-sickness drugs can be combined.

Adequate fluids, good pain control and avoiding triggers help.

Why it matters

Reactions to drugs and materials can be sudden and life-threatening. Early recognition, treatment and reporting save lives.

Identify risk and treat early.

Identify risk and treat early.

opioid-related-itching.title: Opioid-related itching
opioid-related-itching.caption: Itching, especially of the face, is common after spinal or epidural opioids.
opioid-related-itching.body:
In short: Itching, especially of the face, is common after spinal or epidural opioids.

Pruritus

Itching, especially of the face, is common after spinal or epidural opioids. It is usually not a true allergy.

Check for hives or breathing trouble to rule out allergy. Treatment depends on severity and local protocol.

Why it matters

Reactions to drugs and materials can be sudden and life-threatening. Early recognition, treatment and reporting save lives.

Remember

Itch alone is rarely allergy.

chlorhexidine-allergy.title: Chlorhexidine allergy
chlorhexidine-allergy.caption: Chlorhexidine is common in skin prep, lubricants and some line coatings.
chlorhexidine-allergy.body:

Skin Prep Risk

Chlorhexidine is common in skin prep, lubricants and some line coatings. Rarely, it triggers severe allergic reactions.

If a patient has a known allergy, use an alternative antiseptic and check line and catheter products.

Why it matters

Reactions to drugs and materials can be sudden and life-threatening. Early recognition, treatment and reporting save lives.

Remember

Check hidden chlorhexidine sources.

Check hidden chlorhexidine sources.

Speak Up

Report any suspected drug reaction through your hospital or national pharmacovigilance system. Include the drug, dose, timing, symptoms and outcome.

Reporting helps spot patterns and protects other patients.

Why it matters

Reactions to drugs and materials can be sudden and life-threatening. Early recognition, treatment and reporting save lives.

Remember

Report even the minor reactions.

documenting-drug-allergies.caption: A quick list on documenting drug allergies: Name the drug involved; Describe the reaction and its timing.

Documenting drug allergies

Reactions to drugs and materials can be sudden and life-threatening. Early recognition, treatment and reporting save lives.

Write it where everyone can see.

post-spinal-headache.title: Post-spinal headache
post-spinal-headache.caption: A headache that worsens when sitting or standing and eases when lying flat may follow a dural puncture.
post-spinal-headache.body:
In short: A headache that worsens when sitting or standing and eases when lying flat may follow a dural puncture.

After A Spinal

A headache that worsens when sitting or standing and eases when lying flat may follow a dural puncture. It can come with neck stiffness or ringing in the ears.

Report it to the anaesthetist. Fluids, rest and simple analgesia help, and some patients need further treatment.

Why it matters

Reactions to drugs and materials can be sudden and life-threatening. Early recognition, treatment and reporting save lives.

Remember

Worse upright, better flat.

Check yourself

Worse upright, better flat.

the-five-rights.caption: A quick list on the five rights: Right patient; Right drug.

The five rights

  • Right drug
  • Right dose
  • Right route
  • Right time

Medication errors are among the most preventable harms in theatre. Habits like checking, labelling and pausing catch mistakes before they reach the patient.

Remember

Check all five, every time.

Right patient; Right drug; Right dose; Right route; Right time.

look-alike-sound-alike-drugs.caption: Some drug names look or sound alike, such as hydralazine and hydroxyzine.
look-alike-sound-alike-drugs.body:
In short: Some drug names look or sound alike, such as hydralazine and hydroxyzine.

Confusing Names

Some drug names look or sound alike, such as hydralazine and hydroxyzine. Mix-ups cause serious harm.

Read the full label, say names aloud, use tall-man lettering where available, and store similar drugs apart.

Why it matters

Medication errors are among the most preventable harms in theatre. Habits like checking, labelling and pausing catch mistakes before they reach the patient.

Remember

Read the label, never the position.

Read the label, never the position.

independent-double-checks.caption: For high-risk drugs such as insulin, heparin, opioids and potassium, two people should check independently.
independent-double-checks.body:

Two Pairs Of Eyes

For high-risk drugs such as insulin, heparin, opioids and potassium, two people should check independently. Each person checks the drug, dose and patient on their own.

A rushed signature is not a check.

Why it matters

Medication errors are among the most preventable harms in theatre. Habits like checking, labelling and pausing catch mistakes before they reach the patient.

Remember

Check independently, not by copying.

labelling-syringes.title: Labelling syringes

labelling-syringes.body:
In short: Label every syringe drawn up outside of immediate use, with drug name, strength and date.

Every Syringe

Label every syringe drawn up outside of immediate use, with drug name, strength and date. Use standard colour codes where your service applies them.

Never give a drug from an unlabelled syringe. Discard it and start again.

Why it matters

Medication errors are among the most preventable harms in theatre. Habits like checking, labelling and pausing catch mistakes before they reach the patient.

Remember

No label, no injection.

verbal-orders-in-theatre.title: Verbal orders in theatre
verbal-orders-in-theatre.caption: In emergencies, verbal orders are sometimes unavoidable.

Close The Loop

In emergencies, verbal orders are sometimes unavoidable. Repeat the drug, dose and route back, and wait for confirmation before giving it.

Write the order down as soon as possible and have the prescriber sign.

Why it matters

Medication errors are among the most preventable harms in theatre. Habits like checking, labelling and pausing catch mistakes before they reach the patient.

Remember

Read back every verbal order.

High-alert medicines

decimal-point-errors.caption: A misplaced decimal point can mean ten times too much.
decimal-point-errors.body:

Ten-Fold Errors

A misplaced decimal point can mean ten times too much. Write 0.5 mg with a leading zero, never .5 mg, and avoid trailing zeros such as 5.0 mg.

Where possible, write units in full and double check calculations.

Why it matters

Medication errors are among the most preventable harms in theatre. Habits like checking, labelling and pausing catch mistakes before they reach the patient.

Remember

Always write the leading zero.

Check yourself

Always write the leading zero.

calculating-weight-based-doses.title: Calculating weight-based doses
calculating-weight-based-doses.caption: Many doses, especially in children, depend on weight.
calculating-weight-based-doses.body:
In short: Many doses, especially in children, depend on weight.

Do The Maths

Many doses, especially in children, depend on weight. Use an accurately measured or estimated weight, and calculate in the same units.

Check the answer makes sense, and have a second person verify it.

Why it matters

Medication errors are among the most preventable harms in theatre. Habits like checking, labelling and pausing catch mistakes before they reach the patient.

Remember

If it looks odd, check again.

Check yourself

If it looks odd, check again.

Avoid Mix-Ups

Draw up, label and use one drug at a time where possible, and never have unlabelled syringes on the tray together. Clear away used ampoules promptly.

Keep the work area tidy to reduce confusion.

Why it matters

Medication errors are among the most preventable harms in theatre. Habits like checking, labelling and pausing catch mistakes before they reach the patient.

Remember

Tidy tray, safer patient.

Check yourself

Tidy tray, safer patient.

The Last Check

Before injecting, stop and re-read the label, the patient identity and the allergy status. Distractions are a common cause of error.

Do not interrupt a colleague who is preparing a drug. If you are unsure, ask.

Why it matters

Medication errors are among the most preventable harms in theatre. Habits like checking, labelling and pausing catch mistakes before they reach the patient.

Remember

Pause, read, then push.

Pause, read, then push.

group-and-screen-versus-crossmatch.body:

Which Test

Group and screen identifies the blood group and checks for antibodies. Crossmatch tests donor blood directly against the patient's blood, so a unit is reserved.

The test chosen depends on likely blood loss and local policy.

Transfusion saves lives but carries risks, especially identification errors. Understanding products, compatibility and checks keeps patients safe.

Match the test to the risk.

Match the test to the risk.

  • Group AB plasma: usually safe for all
  • Group A patients: receive A or O red cells
  • Group B patients: receive B or O red cells
  • Group AB patients: receive any red cell group

Red cells and plasma follow opposite rules.

Group O red cells: can go to most patients; Group AB plasma: usually safe for all; Group A patients: receive A or O red cells; Group B patients: receive B or O red cells; Group AB patients: receive any red cell group.

bedside-identity-check.title: Bedside identity check
bedside-identity-check.caption: Before transfusion, two trained staff check the patient's identity against the wristband, request form and blood unit label.
bedside-identity-check.body:
In short: Before transfusion, two trained staff check the patient's identity against the wristband, request form and blood unit label.

The Last Safeguard

Before transfusion, two trained staff check the patient's identity against the wristband, request form and blood unit label. Confirm the group, unit number and expiry date.

Most fatal transfusion errors involve wrong patient or wrong blood.

Why it matters

Transfusion saves lives but carries risks, especially identification errors. Understanding products, compatibility and checks keeps patients safe.

Remember

Wrong-blood errors begin with ID.

Oxygen Carriers

Packed red cells increase oxygen-carrying capacity. They are given for significant blood loss or symptomatic anaemia, usually guided by clinical state and haemoglobin.

Use a blood giving set with a filter, and follow your local time limits for each unit.

Why it matters

Transfusion saves lives but carries risks, especially identification errors. Understanding products, compatibility and checks keeps patients safe.

Remember

Transfuse the patient, not the number.

Transfuse the patient, not the number.

fresh-frozen-plasma.caption: Fresh frozen plasma contains clotting factors and is used when bleeding comes with abnormal clotting.
fresh-frozen-plasma.body:
In short: Fresh frozen plasma contains clotting factors and is used when bleeding comes with abnormal clotting.

Clotting Factors

Fresh frozen plasma contains clotting factors and is used when bleeding comes with abnormal clotting. It is stored frozen and thawed before use, so plan ahead.

It must be group compatible and should be used promptly after thawing.

Why it matters

Transfusion saves lives but carries risks, especially identification errors. Understanding products, compatibility and checks keeps patients safe.

Remember

Thaw time must be planned.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about fresh frozen plasma?

Thaw time must be planned.

platelet-transfusion.caption: Platelets are given when counts are low or function is poor and there is bleeding or an invasive procedure planned.
platelet-transfusion.body:
In short: Platelets are given when counts are low or function is poor and there is bleeding or an invasive procedure planned.

Platelets

Platelets are given when counts are low or function is poor and there is bleeding or an invasive procedure planned. They are stored at room temperature with gentle agitation.

They have a short shelf life, so avoid waste.

Why it matters

Transfusion saves lives but carries risks, especially identification errors. Understanding products, compatibility and checks keeps patients safe.

Remember

Platelets never go in the fridge.

Platelets never go in the fridge.

cryoprecipitate.caption: Cryoprecipitate is rich in fibrinogen, a key clotting protein.
cryoprecipitate.body:
In short: Cryoprecipitate is rich in fibrinogen, a key clotting protein.

Fibrinogen Source

Cryoprecipitate is rich in fibrinogen, a key clotting protein. It is used when fibrinogen is low, such as in major haemorrhage or some obstetric bleeding.

It is stored frozen and must be thawed before use.

Why it matters

Transfusion saves lives but carries risks, especially identification errors. Understanding products, compatibility and checks keeps patients safe.

Remember

Low fibrinogen needs cryoprecipitate.

Low fibrinogen needs cryoprecipitate.

Suspected transfusion reaction

  • Stop the transfusion immediately
  • Keep the cannula open with saline
  • Recheck patient identity and unit details
  • Call a doctor and monitor vital signs
  • Return the unit and report per protocol

Why it matters

Transfusion saves lives but carries risks, especially identification errors. Understanding products, compatibility and checks keeps patients safe.

Remember

Stop first, then investigate.

blood-storage-and-handling.caption: Red cells are stored in a monitored blood fridge, typically at 2 to 6 degrees Celsius.
blood-storage-and-handling.body:
In short: Red cells are stored in a monitored blood fridge, typically at 2 to 6 degrees Celsius.

Keep It Cold

Red cells are stored in a monitored blood fridge, typically at 2 to 6 degrees Celsius. Do not store them in ward fridges.

If a unit is out of controlled storage beyond your local time limit, return it and report. Never refreeze or reheat carelessly.

Why it matters

Transfusion saves lives but carries risks, especially identification errors. Understanding products, compatibility and checks keeps patients safe.

Remember

Collect blood only when ready.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about blood storage and handling?

Collect blood only when ready.

massive-transfusion-and-warming.title: Massive transfusion and warming
massive-transfusion-and-warming.caption: In major haemorrhage, a massive transfusion protocol delivers red cells, plasma and platelets in set ratios.
massive-transfusion-and-warming.body:
In short: In major haemorrhage, a massive transfusion protocol delivers red cells, plasma and platelets in set ratios.

Big Bleeds

In major haemorrhage, a massive transfusion protocol delivers red cells, plasma and platelets in set ratios. Cold blood given quickly can cause hypothermia and affect clotting.

Use a blood warmer, and watch for low calcium and high potassium.

Why it matters

Transfusion saves lives but carries risks, especially identification errors. Understanding products, compatibility and checks keeps patients safe.

Remember

Warm the blood, watch calcium.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about massive transfusion and warming?

Warm the blood, watch calcium.

informed-consent-basics.caption: Consent is valid when the patient has capacity, receives clear information and agrees freely.
informed-consent-basics.body:

Consent

Consent is valid when the patient has capacity, receives clear information and agrees freely. The surgeon or doctor usually obtains it, but you must check the form is signed before the patient enters theatre.

If anything is missing, stop and report.

Why it matters

Theatre staff care for people at their most vulnerable. Knowing consent, confidentiality, records and professional limits protects patients and keeps your own practice safe.

Remember

No valid consent, no procedure.

No valid consent, no procedure.

Four pillars of ethics

  • Beneficence: act in the patient's best interest

Theatre staff care for people at their most vulnerable. Knowing consent, confidentiality, records and professional limits protects patients and keeps your own practice safe.

Four pillars guide hard decisions.

patients-who-lack-capacity.caption: Capacity is decision-specific and can change.
patients-who-lack-capacity.body:
In short: Capacity is decision-specific and can change.

Deciding For Others

Capacity is decision-specific and can change. An adult may lack capacity because of illness, drugs or unconsciousness.

In an emergency, the team acts in the patient's best interest, often following local protocol. Otherwise, a relative or legal guardian is involved as policy requires.

Why it matters

Theatre staff care for people at their most vulnerable. Knowing consent, confidentiality, records and professional limits protects patients and keeps your own practice safe.

Remember

Assume capacity until shown otherwise.

Assume capacity until shown otherwise.

documenting-honestly.caption: Write notes at the time, in ink, with date, time, signature and name.
documenting-honestly.body:
In short: Write notes at the time, in ink, with date, time, signature and name.

Records

Write notes at the time, in ink, with date, time, signature and name. Record facts, not opinions or blame.

Never alter an entry quietly. A correction should be a single line through the error, signed and dated, so it stays readable.

Why it matters

Theatre staff care for people at their most vulnerable. Knowing consent, confidentiality, records and professional limits protects patients and keeps your own practice safe.

Remember

If it is not written, it did not happen.

Check yourself

If it is not written, it did not happen.

professional-boundaries.caption: Patients are vulnerable, especially when sedated or anaesthetised.
professional-boundaries.body:
In short: Patients are vulnerable, especially when sedated or anaesthetised.

Stay Professional

Patients are vulnerable, especially when sedated or anaesthetised. Do not accept expensive gifts, form personal relationships with patients, or use their situation for personal gain.

Keep dignity first: expose only what the procedure needs.

Why it matters

Theatre staff care for people at their most vulnerable. Knowing consent, confidentiality, records and professional limits protects patients and keeps your own practice safe.

Remember

Dignity is part of safe care.

Check yourself

Dignity is part of safe care.

duty-to-report-errors.body:
In short: Mistakes and near misses should be reported promptly through the incident system.

Open And Honest

Mistakes and near misses should be reported promptly through the incident system. The aim is learning and prevention, not punishment.

If harm occurred, the patient is usually told honestly by the responsible clinician. Hiding errors makes them repeat.

Why it matters

Theatre staff care for people at their most vulnerable. Knowing consent, confidentiality, records and professional limits protects patients and keeps your own practice safe.

Remember

Report it so it never repeats.

Report it so it never repeats.

Scope of practice

  • Never perform tasks beyond your level to please

Respect And Traceability

Specimens belong to the patient's record. Label them clearly in the right container with correct name, site and date, and hand them over as policy requires.

Removed tissue or limbs are treated with respect and disposed of lawfully, following local rules and any wishes of the patient.

Why it matters

Theatre staff care for people at their most vulnerable. Knowing consent, confidentiality, records and professional limits protects patients and keeps your own practice safe.

Remember

Wrong label, wrong diagnosis.

Patient Choice

A patient with capacity may refuse treatment even if the team disagrees. Make sure the person understands the risks, document the discussion, and inform the senior clinician.

Refusal of one treatment does not mean refusal of all care. Keep treating them with respect.

Workplaces

Graduates often work in public and private hospitals, mission hospitals, day-surgery units and specialised centres. Some join emergency, sterilising or endoscopy departments.

Opportunities also exist in training, supply companies and non-governmental health programmes.

Zones

Theatres are usually arranged in zones: unrestricted, semi-restricted and restricted. Each has dress and movement rules.

Learn where scrub sinks, emergency exits, oxygen cut-offs, fire equipment and the sterile store are before your first case.

Attachment turns classroom knowledge into real skill. How you prepare, ask, and respond to feedback strongly affects what you learn and how teams see you.

asking-questions-well.body:
In short: Ask at a quiet moment, not in the middle of a critical step.

Smart Asking

Ask at a quiet moment, not in the middle of a critical step. Try first to find the answer yourself, then ask clearly what you tried.

If a task seems unsafe or unclear, ask before acting. No sensible supervisor minds a question that protects the patient.

Why it matters

Attachment turns classroom knowledge into real skill. How you prepare, ask, and respond to feedback strongly affects what you learn and how teams see you.

Ask before you guess.

Watch With Purpose

Before the case, read about the procedure and the instruments. During it, note the steps, the roles of each team member and the count routine.

Afterwards, write down what you learned and what to review. Stay out of sterile areas if you are not scrubbed.

Why it matters

Attachment turns classroom knowledge into real skill. How you prepare, ask, and respond to feedback strongly affects what you learn and how teams see you.

Prepare, observe, reflect.

Feedback

Supervisors differ in style, but all want safe, reliable students. Accept feedback calmly, thank them and apply it.

If you disagree, discuss it respectfully later. Ask them to sign your logbook promptly while the case is fresh.

Why it matters

Attachment turns classroom knowledge into real skill. How you prepare, ask, and respond to feedback strongly affects what you learn and how teams see you.

Own It

Everyone errs while learning. Tell your supervisor immediately if you contaminate a field, drop an instrument or miscount.

Honesty lets the team fix the problem safely. Concealing it can harm a patient and damage your trust.

Why it matters

Attachment turns classroom knowledge into real skill. How you prepare, ask, and respond to feedback strongly affects what you learn and how teams see you.

coping-with-a-heavy-list.caption: Busy lists mean long standing and little rest.
coping-with-a-heavy-list.body:

Long Days

Busy lists mean long standing and little rest. Eat before you start, drink water when you can and wear comfortable shoes.

Speak up if you feel faint. A fainting student is a risk to themselves and to the sterile field.

Why it matters

Attachment turns classroom knowledge into real skill. How you prepare, ask, and respond to feedback strongly affects what you learn and how teams see you.

Remember

Fainting is a safety issue, not shame.

Check yourself

Fainting is a safety issue, not shame.

seeing-difficult-situations.body:

Emotional Exposure

You may meet severe trauma, death or distressed families. These moments can affect you even if you seem fine.

Talk with a trusted supervisor or peer afterwards. Following your institution's support routes is a sign of professionalism.

Why it matters

Attachment turns classroom knowledge into real skill. How you prepare, ask, and respond to feedback strongly affects what you learn and how teams see you.

Remember

Debrief; do not carry it alone.

Debrief; do not carry it alone.

ending-an-attachment-well.title: Ending an attachment well
ending-an-attachment-well.caption: Before leaving, check that all your cases are signed, return borrowed items and thank the team.

Finishing Strong

Before leaving, check that all your cases are signed, return borrowed items and thank the team.

Ask for feedback and, where appropriate, a reference. Good closures create future opportunities and show maturity.

Why it matters

Attachment turns classroom knowledge into real skill. How you prepare, ask, and respond to feedback strongly affects what you learn and how teams see you.

Remember

Leave the place better than you found it.

Leave the place better than you found it.

why-logbooks-matter.title: Why logbooks matter
why-logbooks-matter.caption: A logbook proves what you have done, not just what you know.
why-logbooks-matter.body:
In short: A logbook proves what you have done, not just what you know.

Evidence Of Learning

A logbook proves what you have done, not just what you know. Assessors and employers use it to judge your exposure and progress.

It also shows gaps, so you can seek cases you have not yet seen.

Why it matters

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Remember

Logbook equals your clinical CV.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about why logbooks matter?

Logbook equals your clinical CV.

what-to-record-for-each-case.title: What to record for each case
what-to-record-for-each-case.caption: A quick list on what to record for each case: Date and department; Procedure and your role (observed or assisted).

In short: A quick list on what to record for each case: Date and department; Procedure and your role (observed or assisted).

What to record for each case

  • Date and department
  • Procedure and your role (observed or assisted)
  • Patient identifier without the name
  • What you learned or did well
  • Supervisor name and signature

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Same fields, every case.

Date and department; Procedure and your role (observed or assisted); Patient identifier without the name; What you learned or did well; Supervisor name and signature.

protecting-patient-identity.title: Protecting patient identity
protecting-patient-identity.caption: Do not write patient names, phone numbers or full addresses in a logbook or personal notes.
protecting-patient-identity.body:
In short: Do not write patient names, phone numbers or full addresses in a logbook or personal notes.

Anonymise

Do not write patient names, phone numbers or full addresses in a logbook or personal notes. Use a code or hospital number only if your institution permits it.

Logbooks can be lost or shared, and confidentiality still applies.

Why it matters

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Remember

Learn from cases, not from names.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about protecting patient identity?

Learn from cases, not from names.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

record-the-same-day.title: Record the same day
record-the-same-day.caption: Write entries on the day while details are fresh.
record-the-same-day.body:
In short: Write entries on the day while details are fresh.

Timely Entries

Write entries on the day while details are fresh. Waiting a week leads to vague notes and invented memories.

Set aside five minutes after shift. Late entries are harder to defend if a supervisor questions them.

Why it matters

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Remember

Five minutes today saves hours later.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about record the same day?

Five minutes today saves hours later.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

observed-assisted-performed.title: Observed, assisted, performed
observed-assisted-performed.caption: A quick list on observed, assisted, performed: Observed: watched without taking part; Assisted: helped under direct supervision.
observed-assisted-performed.body:
In short: A quick list on observed, assisted, performed: Observed: watched without taking part; Assisted: helped under direct supervision.

Observed, assisted, performed

  • Observed: watched without taking part
  • Assisted: helped under direct supervision
  • Performed: did it with supervisor present
  • Independent: only when formally allowed
  • Label your level honestly each time

Why it matters

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Remember

Never overstate your role.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Observed, assisted, performed".

Observed: watched without taking part; Assisted: helped under direct supervision; Performed: did it with supervisor present; Independent: only when formally allowed; Label your level honestly each time.

reflective-entries.title: Reflective entries
reflective-entries.caption: A short reflection turns activity into learning.
reflective-entries.body:
In short: A short reflection turns activity into learning.

Think It Through

A short reflection turns activity into learning. Ask: what happened, what went well, what would I change, what do I need to read?

A few honest lines are better than long, copied text.

Why it matters

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Remember

Reflect: describe, analyse, plan.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about reflective entries?

Reflect: describe, analyse, plan.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

getting-signatures.title: Getting signatures
getting-signatures.caption: An unsigned entry may not count.
getting-signatures.body:
In short: An unsigned entry may not count.

Verification

An unsigned entry may not count. Ask your supervisor to sign during or soon after the case.

Never sign for them or copy a signature. Forgery can end a training career and is treated seriously.

Why it matters

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Remember

Never forge a signature.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about getting signatures?

Never forge a signature.

tracking-your-numbers.title: Tracking your numbers
tracking-your-numbers.caption: Programmes often set minimum exposure for case types or skills.
tracking-your-numbers.body:
In short: Programmes often set minimum exposure for case types or skills.

Competency Targets

Programmes often set minimum exposure for case types or skills. Keep a simple tally page at the front of your logbook.

Review it monthly with your tutor so you can request missing experience before the deadline.

Why it matters

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Remember

Count monthly, not at the end.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tracking your numbers?

Count monthly, not at the end.

keeping-the-logbook-safe.title: Keeping the logbook safe
keeping-the-logbook-safe.caption: A quick list on keeping the logbook safe: Keep it in a clean, dry, waterproof cover; Do not leave it in clinical areas.
keeping-the-logbook-safe.body:
In short: A quick list on keeping the logbook safe: Keep it in a clean, dry, waterproof cover; Do not leave it in clinical areas.

Keeping the logbook safe

  • Keep it in a clean, dry, waterproof cover
  • Do not leave it in clinical areas
  • Photograph or scan pages for backup
  • Write legibly in permanent ink
  • Bring it to every tutor meeting

Why it matters

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Remember

Losing it can mean repeating cases.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Keeping the logbook safe".

Keep it in a clean, dry, waterproof cover; Do not leave it in clinical areas; Photograph or scan pages for backup; Write legibly in permanent ink; Bring it to every tutor meeting.

correcting-an-entry.title: Correcting an entry
correcting-an-entry.caption: If you make an error, draw one line through it, write the correction and initial it with the date.
correcting-an-entry.body:
In short: If you make an error, draw one line through it, write the correction and initial it with the date.

Fix Cleanly

If you make an error, draw one line through it, write the correction and initial it with the date. Do not use correction fluid or scribble.

The original should still be readable, which shows honesty and good record practice.

Why it matters

Your logbook is formal proof of clinical experience. Accurate, timely, confidential entries support assessment, registration and future job applications.

Remember

One line, initial, date.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about correcting an entry?

One line, initial, date.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

making-a-realistic-timetable.title: Making a realistic timetable
making-a-realistic-timetable.caption: List fixed commitments first: classes, attachment, travel and chores.
making-a-realistic-timetable.body:
In short: List fixed commitments first: classes, attachment, travel and chores.

Plan Your Week

List fixed commitments first: classes, attachment, travel and chores. Then place study blocks in the remaining time and include rest.

Be specific: 'Revise sterilisation methods, 40 minutes' beats 'study'. Adjust the plan weekly when life changes.

Why it matters

Theatre courses need practical memory and clear understanding. Good methods make revision efficient and reduce exam stress.

Remember

Plan the week, then follow the plan.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about making a realistic timetable?

Plan the week, then follow the plan.

active-recall.title: Active recall
active-recall.caption: Reading again feels easy but builds weak memory.
active-recall.body:
In short: Reading again feels easy but builds weak memory.

Test Yourself

Reading again feels easy but builds weak memory. Close the notes and try to write or say what you remember, then check.

Use questions, flashcards or explain it to a friend. Mistakes show you what to review.

Why it matters

Theatre courses need practical memory and clear understanding. Good methods make revision efficient and reduce exam stress.

Remember

Retrieval beats rereading.

Check yourself

Retrieval beats rereading.

spaced-revision.title: Spaced revision
spaced-revision.caption: A quick list on spaced revision: Review within one day of learning; Review again after a few days.
spaced-revision.body:

Spaced revision

  • Review within one day of learning
  • Review again after a few days
  • Then again after a week or two
  • Shorten sessions; repeat more often
  • Use short notes for each review

Why it matters

Theatre courses need practical memory and clear understanding. Good methods make revision efficient and reduce exam stress.

Remember

Spacing makes memory last.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Spaced revision".

Review within one day of learning; Review again after a few days; Then again after a week or two; Shorten sessions; repeat more often; Use short notes for each review.

making-useful-notes.title: Making useful notes
making-useful-notes.caption: Write in your own words, using headings, short lines and simple diagrams.
making-useful-notes.body:

Note-Taking

Write in your own words, using headings, short lines and simple diagrams. Leave space to add details later.

After class, tidy the notes and mark what you do not understand. Copying the slides word for word teaches little.

Why it matters

Theatre courses need practical memory and clear understanding. Good methods make revision efficient and reduce exam stress.

Remember

Own words, own diagrams.

Own words, own diagrams.

mnemonics-that-work.title: Mnemonics that work

mnemonics-that-work.body:

Memory Aids

A mnemonic turns a list into a phrase or picture. Making your own is stronger than copying one.

Keep them short and link to meaning. Always check that the facts behind the mnemonic are correct and current.

Own mnemonics stick best.

group-study-done-well.title: Group study done well
group-study-done-well.caption: A quick list on group study done well: Choose two to five serious people; Set a topic and time limit beforehand.
group-study-done-well.body:

Group study done well

  • Set a topic and time limit beforehand
  • Take turns to teach each topic
  • Quiz each other with exam-style questions
  • Stop when chat replaces study

Teaching others tests your own gaps.

Choose two to five serious people; Set a topic and time limit beforehand; Take turns to teach each topic; Quiz each other with exam-style questions; Stop when chat replaces study.

preparing-for-exam-day.title: Preparing for exam day
preparing-for-exam-day.caption: Sleep properly, eat a light meal and arrive early with all permitted items.
preparing-for-exam-day.body:
In short: Sleep properly, eat a light meal and arrive early with all permitted items.

Before The Paper

Sleep properly, eat a light meal and arrive early with all permitted items. Avoid new material the night before.

Read each question carefully and plan your time. Answer easy items first, then return to harder ones.

Why it matters

Theatre courses need practical memory and clear understanding. Good methods make revision efficient and reduce exam stress.

Remember

Calm preparation beats late cramming.

Check yourself

Calm preparation beats late cramming.

reading-a-question-stem.title: Reading a question stem
reading-a-question-stem.caption: Underline the command word: list, describe, explain, compare.
reading-a-question-stem.body:
In short: Underline the command word: list, describe, explain, compare.

Exam Technique

Underline the command word: list, describe, explain, compare. Each asks for different depth.

In multiple-choice questions, watch for words such as 'except' and 'first'. Answer what is asked, not what you hoped to see.

Why it matters

Theatre courses need practical memory and clear understanding. Good methods make revision efficient and reduce exam stress.

Remember

Answer the exact question set.

Answer the exact question set.

avoiding-distraction.title: Avoiding distraction
avoiding-distraction.caption: Study in a quiet place, phone silent and out of reach.
avoiding-distraction.body:
In short: Study in a quiet place, phone silent and out of reach.

Focus

Study in a quiet place, phone silent and out of reach. Work in short focused blocks of about twenty-five to fifty minutes, then take a brief break.

When you slip, simply restart. Perfect discipline is not required, only returning to the task.

Why it matters

Theatre courses need practical memory and clear understanding. Good methods make revision efficient and reduce exam stress.

Remember

Silence the phone, not your goals.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about avoiding distraction?

Silence the phone, not your goals.

researching-the-employer.title: Researching the employer
researching-the-employer.caption: Learn what the hospital offers, its size, specialties and values.
researching-the-employer.body:
In short: Learn what the hospital offers, its size, specialties and values.

Do Your Homework

Learn what the hospital offers, its size, specialties and values. Read the job advert carefully and match your skills to it.

Prepare a question or two about training and teamwork. Employers notice who bothered to find out.

Why it matters

A good interview shows safety awareness, teamwork and reliability as well as knowledge. Preparation helps you present your real strengths clearly.

Remember

Know the place before you apply.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about researching the employer?

Know the place before you apply.

preparing-your-documents.caption: A quick list on preparing your documents: Clean, updated CV with no gaps unexplained; Certified copies of certificates.

Preparing your documents

  • Certified copies of certificates
  • Identity document and licence proof
  • Referee names and contact details
  • Place everything in one neat folder

Why it matters

A good interview shows safety awareness, teamwork and reliability as well as knowledge. Preparation helps you present your real strengths clearly.

Remember

Neat papers show organised habits.

Clean, updated CV with no gaps unexplained; Certified copies of certificates; Identity document and licence proof; Referee names and contact details; Place everything in one neat folder.

dressing-and-arriving.title: Dressing and arriving
dressing-and-arriving.caption: Dress neatly and modestly in clean, plain clothing suited to a health setting.
dressing-and-arriving.body:
In short: Dress neatly and modestly in clean, plain clothing suited to a health setting.

First Impression

Dress neatly and modestly in clean, plain clothing suited to a health setting. Plan your route and arrive well before your time.

Switch off your phone. Greet everyone politely, because reception staff may also give feedback.

Why it matters

A good interview shows safety awareness, teamwork and reliability as well as knowledge. Preparation helps you present your real strengths clearly.

Remember

Be early, neat and polite.

Be early, neat and polite.

answering-with-star.title: Answering with STAR
answering-with-star.caption: A quick list on answering with star: Situation: set the scene briefly; Task: say what you had to do.
answering-with-star.body:
In short: A quick list on answering with star: Situation: set the scene briefly; Task: say what you had to do.

Answering with STAR

  • Situation: set the scene briefly
  • Task: say what you had to do
  • Action: explain exactly what you did
  • Result: share the outcome and lesson
  • Keep it under two minutes

Why it matters

A good interview shows safety awareness, teamwork and reliability as well as knowledge. Preparation helps you present your real strengths clearly.

Remember

Real stories beat vague claims.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Answering with STAR".

Situation: set the scene briefly; Task: say what you had to do; Action: explain exactly what you did; Result: share the outcome and lesson; Keep it under two minutes.

tell-me-about-yourself.title: Tell me about yourself
tell-me-about-yourself.caption: Give a short summary: who you are, what you trained in, key experience and why you want this role.
tell-me-about-yourself.body:
In short: Give a short summary: who you are, what you trained in, key experience and why you want this role.

Opening Answer

Give a short summary: who you are, what you trained in, key experience and why you want this role. Aim for about a minute.

Do not read your CV aloud or share unrelated personal troubles. End by linking your strengths to the job.

Why it matters

A good interview shows safety awareness, teamwork and reliability as well as knowledge. Preparation helps you present your real strengths clearly.

Remember

Present, past, future in one minute.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about tell me about yourself?

Present, past, future in one minute.

talking-about-weaknesses.title: Talking about weaknesses
talking-about-weaknesses.caption: Choose a genuine, work-relevant weakness and explain how you are improving it.
talking-about-weaknesses.body:
In short: Choose a genuine, work-relevant weakness and explain how you are improving it.

Honest Growth

Choose a genuine, work-relevant weakness and explain how you are improving it. For example, hesitating to speak up, and now practising clear communication.

Avoid pretending you have none, or choosing a serious safety flaw.

Why it matters

A good interview shows safety awareness, teamwork and reliability as well as knowledge. Preparation helps you present your real strengths clearly.

Remember

Name it, then show progress.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about talking about weaknesses?

Name it, then show progress.

scenario-questions-in-theatre.title: Scenario questions in theatre
scenario-questions-in-theatre.caption: Panels may ask what you would do if the count is wrong or an instrument falls.
scenario-questions-in-theatre.body:
In short: Panels may ask what you would do if the count is wrong or an instrument falls.

Safety First

Panels may ask what you would do if the count is wrong or an instrument falls. Answer calmly with safe steps: stop, tell the team, follow protocol, document.

Showing you value patient safety matters more than a perfect answer.

Why it matters

A good interview shows safety awareness, teamwork and reliability as well as knowledge. Preparation helps you present your real strengths clearly.

Remember

Safety beats speed in your answer.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about scenario questions in theatre?

Safety beats speed in your answer.

Study aid only. Practice varies, so follow your hospital's protocol and your supervisor's instructions.

body-language.title: Body language
body-language.caption: A quick list on body language: Greet with a steady, friendly voice; Sit upright and keep hands relaxed.
body-language.body:

Body language

  • Greet with a steady, friendly voice
  • Sit upright and keep hands relaxed
  • Make natural eye contact with the panel
  • Listen fully before you answer
  • Smile when it is genuine

Why it matters

A good interview shows safety awareness, teamwork and reliability as well as knowledge. Preparation helps you present your real strengths clearly.

Remember

Calm presence builds trust.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Body language".

Greet with a steady, friendly voice; Sit upright and keep hands relaxed; Make natural eye contact with the panel; Listen fully before you answer; Smile when it is genuine.

asking-and-following-up.title: Asking and following up
asking-and-following-up.caption: When asked if you have questions, ask something useful: induction, supervision, training or shift patterns.
asking-and-following-up.body:
In short: When asked if you have questions, ask something useful: induction, supervision, training or shift patterns.

Close Well

When asked if you have questions, ask something useful: induction, supervision, training or shift patterns. Avoid asking only about pay and leave.

Thank the panel and, if appropriate, send a short thank-you message. Accept outcomes graciously.

Why it matters

A good interview shows safety awareness, teamwork and reliability as well as knowledge. Preparation helps you present your real strengths clearly.

Remember

Thank them, whatever the result.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about asking and following up?

Thank them, whatever the result.

leading-without-a-title.title: Leading without a title
leading-without-a-title.caption: Leadership is not only for managers.
leading-without-a-title.body:
In short: Leadership is not only for managers.

Everyday Leadership

Leadership is not only for managers. Anyone can set an example by being reliable, speaking up about safety and helping a struggling colleague.

Students lead by preparing well and keeping standards high even when nobody is watching.

Why it matters

Theatre depends on clear decisions, fair delegation and high standards. Leadership skills help at any level, even before you hold a senior post.

Remember

Lead by example.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about leading without a title?

Lead by example.

setting-standards.title: Setting standards
setting-standards.caption: A team copies what its leader tolerates.
setting-standards.body:
In short: A team copies what its leader tolerates.

Culture

A team copies what its leader tolerates. If shortcuts in hand hygiene or counts are ignored, they spread.

Good leaders model correct practice, explain why it matters and correct lapses kindly but firmly.

Why it matters

Theatre depends on clear decisions, fair delegation and high standards. Leadership skills help at any level, even before you hold a senior post.

Remember

What you allow becomes the norm.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about setting standards?

What you allow becomes the norm.

delegating-safely.title: Delegating safely
delegating-safely.caption: A quick list on delegating safely: Pick someone with the right skills; Explain the task and the expected result.
delegating-safely.body:
In short: A quick list on delegating safely: Pick someone with the right skills; Explain the task and the expected result.

Delegating safely

  • Pick someone with the right skills
  • Explain the task and the expected result
  • Check understanding before they begin
  • Offer support but avoid micromanaging
  • Stay accountable for the outcome

Why it matters

Theatre depends on clear decisions, fair delegation and high standards. Leadership skills help at any level, even before you hold a senior post.

Remember

Delegation does not mean abandonment.

Check yourself

List the points covered under "Delegating safely".

Pick someone with the right skills; Explain the task and the expected result; Check understanding before they begin; Offer support but avoid micromanaging; Stay accountable for the outcome.

making-decisions-under-pressure.title: Making decisions under pressure
making-decisions-under-pressure.caption: In an emergency, gather the key facts quickly, state the plan aloud and assign clear tasks.
making-decisions-under-pressure.body:
In short: In an emergency, gather the key facts quickly, state the plan aloud and assign clear tasks.

Calm Decisions

In an emergency, gather the key facts quickly, state the plan aloud and assign clear tasks. Revisit the plan if the situation changes.

Staying calm helps others think. Review the decision afterwards without blame.

Why it matters

Theatre depends on clear decisions, fair delegation and high standards. Leadership skills help at any level, even before you hold a senior post.

Remember

Pause, plan, then act.

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about making decisions under pressure?

Pause, plan, then act.

giving-feedback.title: Giving feedback
giving-feedback.caption: Give feedback soon, in private and about specific behaviour, not character.
giving-feedback.body:
In short: Give feedback soon, in private and about specific behaviour, not character.

Constructive

Give feedback soon, in private and about specific behaviour, not character. Say what went well, what to improve and how.

Surgery is a team activity, and most errors involve communication rather than technical skill. Good teamwork keeps patients safe and workplaces pleasant.

A team that respects all members communicates better and makes fewer errors.

Some people are tense or abrupt under pressure. Remain calm, focus on the task and avoid arguing in front of the patient.

If behaviour is abusive or unsafe, report it later through the proper route. Safety concerns must never be silenced.

Surgery is a team activity, and most errors involve communication rather than technical skill. Good teamwork keeps patients safe and workplaces pleasant.

Theatre work is physically and emotionally demanding. Protecting your body, mind and health keeps you safe and able to care for patients for years.

Health workers are exposed to blood and respiratory infections. Hepatitis B vaccination, with antibody check, is widely recommended for those working with blood. Other vaccines depend on local policy.

Theatre work is physically and emotionally demanding. Protecting your body, mind and health keeps you safe and able to care for patients for years.

Regular sleep, meals, movement and time with people you trust protect against stress. During a tense moment, slow breathing can steady you.

Seek professional help if stress affects mood, sleep or safety. Asking for help is a strength.

Theatre work is physically and emotionally demanding. Protecting your body, mind and health keeps you safe and able to care for patients for years.

night-duty-and-fatigue.body:

Tired staff make more mistakes. On nights, eat light meals, take short breaks when possible and avoid heavy caffeine late in the shift.

Travel home safely. If you are too tired to work safely, tell your supervisor.

Theatre work is physically and emotionally demanding. Protecting your body, mind and health keeps you safe and able to care for patients for years.

Theatre staff may meet X-rays, anaesthetic gases, disinfectants and surgical smoke. Use lead aprons, keep distance, ensure ventilation and use extraction where provided.

Follow dosimeter and handling rules. Report concerns early.

Theatre work is physically and emotionally demanding. Protecting your body, mind and health keeps you safe and able to care for patients for years.

Emotional Aftercare

Losing a patient or seeing severe injury can leave you shaken. Feelings such as sadness or difficulty sleeping are normal for a while.

Talk to a colleague, supervisor or counsellor. If symptoms persist or worsen, seek professional help.

Why it matters

Theatre work is physically and emotionally demanding. Protecting your body, mind and health keeps you safe and able to care for patients for years.

Talking helps; silence hurts.

Boundaries

Long hours and emergencies can swallow personal time. Protect rest days, hobbies, faith or community and family connections.

Learn to say no to extra duties when exhausted, and discuss workload with your supervisor early.

Theatre work is physically and emotionally demanding. Protecting your body, mind and health keeps you safe and able to care for patients for years.

why-research-matters.caption: Many theatre practices, such as skin preparation and warming, are improved by research.
why-research-matters.body:
In short: Many theatre practices, such as skin preparation and warming, are improved by research.

Evidence-Based Care

Many theatre practices, such as skin preparation and warming, are improved by research. Studies test whether a method truly helps or harms.

Even as a student, you can read research critically and ask whether your practice is based on evidence or habit.

Why it matters

Understanding research helps you judge claims, improve practice and complete required projects. Even simple studies need clear questions, ethics and honest methods.

Remember

Ask: what is the evidence?

Check yourself

What is the main thing to remember about why research matters?

Ask: what is the evidence?

forming-a-research-question.title: Forming a research question
forming-a-research-question.caption: A good question is clear, focused and answerable.
forming-a-research-question.body:
In short: A good question is clear, focused and answerable.

Start Small

A good question is clear, focused and answerable. A format such as PICO helps: patient group, intervention, comparison and outcome.

Avoid broad topics like 'infection'. Narrow it, for example to one practice in one setting.

Why it matters

Understanding research helps you judge claims, improve practice and complete required projects. Even simple studies need clear questions, ethics and honest methods.

Remember

Narrow questions give clear answers.

Narrow questions give clear answers.

Types of study

  • Cross-sectional: a snapshot at one time
  • Case-control: compares cases with controls
  • Cohort: follows groups over time
  • Randomised trial: allocates by chance

Why it matters

Understanding research helps you judge claims, improve practice and complete required projects. Even simple studies need clear questions, ethics and honest methods.

Search Smart

Use journals, textbooks, guidelines and respected health bodies, and search databases through your library. Check the author, date and whether claims are supported.

Be cautious with social media, advertisements and unreferenced websites. Prefer current sources.

Why it matters

Understanding research helps you judge claims, improve practice and complete required projects. Even simple studies need clear questions, ethics and honest methods.

research-ethics.caption: Studies with people need ethical approval, voluntary informed consent and protection of privacy.
research-ethics.body:
